items.body: A fall in the number of enforcement files can have several causes, and none of them on its own describes the situation of households. A file can be discontinued while the claim remains unpaid; a shorter debt-relief period does not say how many people actually enter the process. New proceedings can still be opened while the overall stock is falling, and a lower average per person can be produced by deleting old cases, not by paying them off. 1. Three curves that look like one Imagine an inter-ministerial meeting on “improving the debt situation”. The finance minister reads a press release from the Chamber of Court Executors and sees that in 2024 more than 700 thousand ongoing enforcement cases disappeared. The justice minister notes that from 1 October 2024 debt relief lasts three years, not five. A mayor from the Ústí region says that in his municipality people still work off the books. A debt counsellor reports a queue that has not shortened. The president of the Chamber insists that discontinuing unsuccessful proceedings is legitimate. A sociologist shows that the number of unique persons in enforcement fell by tens of thousands, not by hundreds of thousands. At the meeting, the word “improvement” hides several indicators. The finance minister watches the files in the Central Register of Enforcement (CEE), justice watches the length of the insolvency process, the mayor the return to a legal wage, the counsellor the capacity of services, the Chamber the state of the register, and the sociologist the number of people instead of the number of proceedings. Each of these indicators can be correct, but their meanings must not be swapped. A year-on-year fall in files is not evidence that household incomes have risen. It can come from repayment, discontinuation for lack of assets, insolvency, deletion of low-value or unsuccessful proceedings, an extraordinary legal scheme, or a change in the new inflow. Before we interpret the fall, we have to name the unit: a file, a person, a claim, or a completed debt relief. Each series answers a different question, and their year-on-year changes cannot be placed on one axis without conversion. A file is not a debtor. A debtor is not discharged. Debt relief is not a return to a legal wage. And a fall in the register is not repayment. — Jiný Kontext What we know so far about three-year debt relief We know: from October 2024 the standard three-year period applies, and in 2025 the number of authorised debt-relief cases rose. [5] [8] [9] We do not know: the first cohort under the new rules could not yet finish the full three-year cycle in 2026, so we have neither its final discharge rate nor a reliable figure for a return to insured employment. The number of authorised entries must therefore not be presented as the number of people successfully discharged. 2. The fall in files can happen in five different ways The “number of enforcement cases” column is the stock of the register, not the sum of debts paid. It falls by several routes, and two equally large year-on-year changes can therefore mean different things for households. Five layers of one number Claim: a legal duty to pay a debt. It exists whether or not enforcement is running. Enforcement title and application: a state-authorised attempt to recover a specific claim by force. Record in the CEE: an entry for a proceeding, including proceedings interrupted by insolvency or deferred. Discontinuation or fulfilment: the file ends because something was recovered, or because recovery stopped. Debt relief and discharge: a court process at the end of which the debtor may be exempted from paying claims that remain unsatisfied. The claim determines what the debtor owes. It is not the only actor. The court executor can discontinue the file under Section 55 of the Enforcement Code without the creditor receiving the principal. The insolvency court can suspend recovery even though the CEE still lists the person. After the conditions of debt relief are met, the court may exempt the debtor from paying claims that remain unsatisfied; as a rule the claim does not legally disappear, but it cannot ordinarily be enforced against the discharged debtor. A new application can put the same person back into the statistics. A self-employed natural person can sit in a different column from an employee. This is where the first error of public comparisons appears. The headline announces a fall in enforcement cases, but in reality it compares the number of files with the number of people, or the number of people with the number of principals recovered. An honest comparison must state not only the year, but also the unit, the population, whether it is the stock as of 31 December or the flow of newly opened proceedings, and whether the CEE includes latent files. The reason for the fall has to be traced in the data that follow. A fall in files without a similar fall in persons may be linked to the discontinuation of old proceedings; a fall in persons without figures on debt relief does not show what happened to them next. Even a higher number of debt-relief cases does not, by itself, prove a return to insured work. The headline “enforcement cases are down” therefore needs a breakdown by reason and by unit. Illustrative diagram: The same person can, in another column, with another title and another way of ending, produce a different fall. 3. Statistics must also show why the case ended Readers usually look for the indicator with the largest year-on-year fall. That is reasonable, but incomplete. Equally important is what the error looks like, whether it can be recognised, how much it costs to correct, and whether the result is reversible. Discontinuing a fruitless file relieves the court. It is a cheap error if we read it as housekeeping. It is an expensive error if we read it as people getting richer. A recovered principal can be checked in the yields. A deletion for lack of assets will not appear in the yields. In its press release of 17 July 2025 the Chamber of Court Executors itself says that the fall is linked mainly to the discontinuation of unsuccessful enforcement cases, not to an improving financial situation of the population. That is a professional body’s view of its own data, not an audit of principals recovered. It does show, however, that even an exact percentage can measure something other than what the headline reads. [1] Type of failure What it looks like How to test it What limits the harm Confusing the unit A fall in files is read as a fall in people Compare the stock of proceedings and the stock of unique persons in the same period A mandatory pair of numbers in every release Confusing flow and stock Fewer running files are read as fewer new debts Separate newly opened proceedings from the registered remainder Publish both series side by side Confusing an ending with fulfilment Discontinuation is read as payment Ask how many endings recovered the principal A statement of yields, not only the number of closed files Confusing the register with activity An entry in the CEE is read as a wage deduction in progress Separate latent files (insolvency, deferral) A methodological note on every table In the assessment it is not the largest fall that decides, but its reason. Deleting an unsuccessful file can be legitimate management of the register; it must not be presented as satisfaction of the creditor. Likewise, a lower average of proceedings per person does not prove that people have returned to a legal payslip. For each series it is therefore important to know why it ended, whether the person returned to a legal income, and the effect on contributions. A smaller year-on-year fall, accompanied by the share of claims actually recovered, can carry more information for public policy than a large deletion without that structure. 4. The number of files does not describe the state of households The Chamber’s statistics are needed because they replace part of impression with a repeatable register. The problem begins when one number starts to stand for the whole health of households. The Chamber publishes the stock as of 31 December and as of mid-year, the number of newly opened proceedings, the average per person and several frequency bands. In the methodological notes on the open data it also recalls that the CEE includes latent enforcement cases that cannot be carried out because of insolvency. [2] [3] [22] Every table contains hidden decisions. Does it cover natural persons including the self-employed, or legal persons as well? Is it a stock or a flow? Is a file counted when debt relief is already running? Is the district of permanent residence measured, or the seat of the executor? The answer to any of these questions can change the order on the map. What must accompany a year-on-year fall The exact unit: a proceeding, or a unique natural person. The moment of measurement and whether it is a stock or a flow of newly opened proceedings. Whether the series includes latent files in insolvency. The reason it ended: recovery, discontinuation for lack of assets, a low-value case, debt relief. Regional and age distribution, not only the national average. An overall ranking of “improvement” tells us less than a table with a precisely defined unit. A smaller audit sample of files with a reason for ending and the debtor’s later status can reveal what the aggregate hides; without a representative sample, however, it does not estimate the whole system. 5. Compare proceedings, not headlines The market in interpretations can be described without a false podium of winners. The map below does not say which report is generally first. It shows the object around which each reading builds its argument, what kind of context it brings, and which failure the reader should look for while reading. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Reading Main object What to check Typical reason for the choice Headline about a fall in files Stock of proceedings in the CEE Share of discontinuations vs. recoveries Quick proof that “enforcement cases are down” Headline about a fall in persons Unique natural persons Pace relative to files, band 1 vs. 10+ Proof that the population of debtors is shrinking Headline about debt relief Authorised debt-relief cases in the period Comparison with the target group, not only year-on-year Proof that a second chance has opened Headline about the grey economy Contributions and declared wages Whether it is an estimate or an administrative series Proof that the deduction is pushing work off the books Headline about the region District share of persons in enforcement Age, one vs. multiple, availability of advice Proof that the Czech average says nothing about Most The table does not judge the quality of the institution or of the register as a whole. It recalls that the individual series have different definitions and that an amendment can change their meaning. The reader can then check whether the headline matches the actual unit and the reason for the change. How to read the diagram: The size of the elements is not a ranking of success. The diagram separates the state of the register, the fate of the claim, the number of people and the return to the legal economy. 6. Discontinuation: the file disappears, the claim does not In 2024, according to the Chamber, more than 910 thousand unsuccessful enforcement cases were discontinued. That is the flow of closed proceedings in a calendar year, not the number of people who stopped owing money. The Chamber links this to a systematic review of cases with no realistic chance of recovery. From the creditor’s point of view it often means the loss of a chance to obtain performance through enforcement, not certainty that the debt has vanished. [1] The legal regime is narrower than the word “end” sounds. Discontinuation under Section 55 of the Enforcement Code ends the specific enforcement proceeding; by itself it does not automatically mean that the claim has been fulfilled. Whether the claim still exists and can be enforced depends on the reason for discontinuation, limitation, any insolvency proceeding and the other circumstances of the case. Section 55 alone is therefore not enough to assert that the claim always continues to bear interest or can be recovered again in the same way. [7] In earlier years other tools also helped to clear the archive, and they must not be piled together with 2024. Low-value enforcement cases with a principal of up to CZK 1 500 could be discontinued from 2022; the Chamber then estimated hundreds of thousands of closed proceedings. Milostivé léto (Mercy Summer) allowed public-law debts to be settled by paying the principal without accessories; these were time-limited schemes with a different logic from fruitless recovery. The tools cleared part of the agenda. They lifted different burdens from the debtor: sometimes the accessories, sometimes only the enforcement order. [16] [17] What needs to be tested The first test concerns the reason for the ending. Of the 910 thousand discontinuations in 2024, how many recovered the principal, how many were for lack of assets, how many for another reason? The public press release does not give that breakdown. The second concerns the person: how many unique people lost all their files, and how many only some of them? The third concerns return: how many discontinued claims reappear at a collection agency or in a new application? Without these three numbers, 910 thousand is an exact figure about office work, not about household debt relief. For the courts this clean-up can be decisive. An overloaded apparatus would otherwise chase files from which nothing can be taken. For public debate, however, the sentence “enforcement cases are down” is not enough. It needs the type of ending, the owner of the remaining claim, and the line beyond which a person may return to a payslip without the deduction taking the entire remainder. 7. Multiple cases are not the same as fewer debtors The core of the Czech debt agenda is not a person with one unpaid fine. The core is concurrence. That is a reasonable reading of the data, but only if we keep the definition. According to the Chamber, as of 31 December 2024 some 614 721 natural persons, including the self-employed, faced enforcement. A year earlier the figure was 645 724. The fall is 31 003 persons, less than five percent. In the same period the number of proceedings fell from 4 059 035 to 3 350 486. The average per person fell from 6.28 to 5.43. Persons with one enforcement case numbered 143 587, almost the same as in 2023 (143 614). Persons with ten or more proceedings fell from 123 426 to 83 691; as of 30 June 2025 the Chamber listed 93 139 of them again. These are stocks in the CEE, not the number of people who repaid the debt. [1] [3] PAQ Research reports that at the beginning of August 2025 about 450 thousand people — roughly five percent of residents aged 15 and over — were in multiple enforcement, defined as at least two proceedings. Almost 400 thousand persons had at least three enforcement cases; according to the same text the average debt of that group exceeded one million crowns. This is an estimate tied to the Chamber’s open data and to a date other than the year-end stock of 2024. It is not the same number as 614 721 persons with all enforcement cases. [6] Imagine Martin. This is not a report, but an illustration of the difference between a file and a person. He had eight enforcement cases, and in 2024 the executors discontinued his five oldest unsuccessful proceedings. In the file statistics that is a sharp fall, but three active enforcement cases remained. His deduction cannot be read from gross wages alone: the calculation depends on net income, dependants, priority claims and other statutory parameters. Five files disappeared; from the public total we cannot tell how his motivation for legal employment changed. [23] It does not follow that the fall in persons is an illusion. It follows that 31 thousand unique people in 2024 is a different story from 708 549 proceedings. The first may be partly debt relief, partly death, partly a move into insolvency, partly deletion of the last file of a person who had ten. The second is mainly work on the archive. 8. The grey economy is a side account, not a footnote A deduction from a legal wage can reduce part of the extra net income a debtor gains from higher official earnings. It is not true, however, that everything above the basic non-attachable amount is taken automatically: the remainder of the wage is split into thirds up to a statutory ceiling, and only the part above a further set limit is deducted without restriction; the result also depends on the type of claim and on dependants. [23] For some debtors this design can weaken the incentive to declare all income, but the extent of work off the books cannot be inferred from the deduction formula itself. In a survey from March to May 2025 among 506 people in intractable debt — weighted to represent the population of persons in enforcement according to Chamber data from March 2025 — PAQ Research found that 55% of households in the sample live below the income-poverty line. In the CZSO Living Conditions survey (EU-SILC) for 2024 the at-risk-of-income-poverty rate in the whole population was 9.5%. That is a relative indicator, suitable for comparing groups inside one country, not for an international ranking of poverty. Half of the debtor sample showed screening signs of at least moderate depression or anxiety; in the general population of the same comparison the figure was 17%. Screening is not a medical diagnosis. [6] [10] The estimate of a fiscal shortfall is a weaker layer. In an interview for Czech Radio, Daniel Prokop gave a conservative estimate of a loss of around 12 billion crowns a year in unpaid contributions from people in multiple enforcement. The National Economic Council of the Government worked with an interval of 5 to 12 billion crowns and a population of 140 to 200 thousand people who limit declared income. These are model intervals, not a line in the state final account. The Czech Social Security Administration does not publish a series called “return from the grey economy after discontinuation of fruitless enforcement”. Without that series, a fall in files cannot be read as a rise in insurance contributions. [18] [19] For municipalities in the districts of Most, Ústí nad Labem and Chomutov, which the Chamber repeatedly lists as areas with the highest share of persons in enforcement, this layer is practical. The Czech average will not tell them how many local wages are visible. It will only tell them that their district sits at the top of the map. [1] [12] 9. Three-year debt relief: a shorter period is not a shorter path From 1 October 2024 the amendment to the Insolvency Act No. 252/2024 Coll. is in force. The standard debt-relief period for natural persons fell from five years to three. The amendment implements Directive (EU) 2019/1023 on preventive restructuring and a second chance. It also removed the requirement to repay at least 30% of the debt as an automatic gate to discharge. That is a change of rule. It is not automatically a change of behaviour. [8] [9] [11] Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext InsolCentrum calculated that from 1 October 2024 to 31 March 2025 some 12 041 natural persons entered insolvency proceedings, both self-employed and not. In 80% of cases the courts had authorised debt relief by the cut-off. Six months after the amendment of 1 June 2019, some 21 646 natural persons entered. The difference is 44%. This compares two six-month windows after two different amendments; it is not proof that three-year debt relief “does not work”. It shows that a shorter period by itself did not produce the rush that part of the debate expected. [4] For the whole of 2025, according to the same source, the courts authorised debt relief for 22 770 persons, 13% more year-on-year. There were 25 336 insolvency applications, 9% more year-on-year. As of 31 December 2025 some 90 950 persons were in debt relief. In earlier years, according to PAQ, about 20 thousand persons a year entered debt relief. The figure 22 770 is an increase, not coverage of a group of hundreds of thousands with multiple enforcement cases. [5] [6] How to read the insolvency rise The first test is the denominator. The 22 770 authorised debt-relief cases in 2025 should be divided by the population for which the tool is meant, not by the population of all residents. The second is a comparison of windows: 2019 had a different starting line, different information and a different 30% threshold. The third is the result at the end of three years, which we do not yet have in 2026. Authorised debt relief is not discharge. Discharge is not an insured job. After the amendment there was therefore no jump comparable to the first half-year after the 2019 change; for the whole of 2025, however, the number of authorised debt-relief cases rose year-on-year. From these two comparisons one can say that the length of the process is not the only barrier to entry. One cannot tell from them how many people will in the end complete three-year debt relief successfully, nor whether the amendment will reduce the number of persons in enforcement in the long run. 10. Information about debt relief is not the same as entry In the same spring 2025 survey PAQ found that 45% of those in intractable debt do not know the key reason to enter debt relief: that at the end of a successful process the remaining unpaid debt is forgiven. More than 40% do not even roughly know the basic rules, or have not heard of debt relief. Two thirds do not know that from October 2024 the 30% condition no longer applies. Two thirds fear that they would not manage the instalments in the long run. 57% do not know that non-profit organisations offer to prepare the application free of charge. This is a sample of 506 respondents, not a census of all 614 721 persons in the CEE. [6] Willingness is higher than intention. More than 60% of the sample declared a hypothetical interest. Only 14% thought entry in the next year very likely. Fifteen percent of those interested said they would not manage even the minimum instalment. 76% said they would let an automatically prepared application be filed; some of them would still fail the conditions. This is not proof that people “do not want to work”. It is the result of one weighted survey of informational, income and psychological barriers, not a measurement of everyone in enforcement. [6] Debt counselling was used by 22% of the sample, the internet as a source of information by 46%, and family or acquaintances by 37%. [6] A shortening of the period that does not pass through these channels may remain, for some people, only a change in the Collection of Laws. Insolvency courts also assess whether the debtor meets statutory duties; a shorter period does not cancel that check. A change of length alone therefore cannot be judged on the assumption that it will automatically bring everyone with several enforcement cases into debt relief. 11. The non-attachable amount is not a switch for work Wage deduction is designed so that the debtor keeps a legally protected part of income. Its amount changes with legal parameters, net wages, dependants and the type of claim. After the non-attachable amount is subtracted, part of the remainder is split into thirds up to a set ceiling; only the part above the threshold of full attachability is deducted without restriction. A higher official wage therefore usually raises the deduction, but the simple rule “everything above the minimum goes to creditors” does not apply. [23] Protection of the non-attachable amount prevents the deduction from taking the entire income. At the same time, in some income situations it can reduce the net gain from a higher official wage. Whether a particular person then moves into work off the books also depends on the size of the debt, the type of claims, the family, the job offer and the risk of a sanction; such behaviour cannot be predicted from the formula itself. The Ombudsman returns repeatedly to the practice of deductions and to the reading of the non-attachable minimum; that is oversight of application, not a substitute for insolvency. [14] [23] Before assessing the deduction Find out how many concurrent proceedings per person remain after the archive has been cleared. Separate maintenance — in 2024 the Chamber recorded 4 400 newly opened enforcement cases for maintenance, of which 3 780 were for a minor child — from consumer debt. Maintenance has a different legitimacy and a different policy. Do not mix it with a microloan. And do not judge only the size of the deduction: record whether after it there is still a reason to sign a contract. [1] CNB supervision of consumer credit targets providers and new credit contracts; by itself it does not delete old files in the CEE. The Responsible Lending Index of People in Need evaluates the present supply of loans, not the stock of historical enforcement cases. Both layers are useful, but they measure a different part of the problem. [15] [20] 12. How to read numbers from press releases Before the Chamber’s open data, the reader had to trust the summary. With the table the reader checks something harder: whether the column measures proceedings or persons, whether the period fits, whether latent files are sitting in the average, and whether the conclusion really follows from the cell to which it is attached. The number is a navigation to the evidence. It is not automatic evidence. A fall of more than 700 thousand proceedings in 2024, a fall of 31 thousand registered persons and 12 041 entries into insolvency in the six months after the amendment describe three different movements. The summary conclusion “Czechia has been discharged” does not follow from them without figures on the reasons for ending. The half-year flow of 256 479 newly opened proceedings in the first half of 2025 is also not proof that the new inflow has stopped: the annual number was 460 573 in 2024 and 461 592 in 2023. The difference between those two years looks more like stagnation at a high level. [1] A four-step check of the number Existence: the figure is in a primary table of the Chamber, InsolCentrum or the CZSO. Unit: a proceeding, a person, an application, an authorised debt-relief case. Support: a specific cell supports a specific sentence. Scope: the population, period, definition and the caveat about latent files all fit. The most reliable procedure therefore separates searching from writing. First comes a table of claims, primary sources and limits. Only then the headline. If the reason why 910 thousand discontinuations ended cannot be opened, the claim is not upgraded to “paid off” merely because the number is large. Three tests of the fall The first is about the unit: did proceedings fall, or persons? The second is about the reason: did it fall by recovery, or by discontinuation? The third is about contradiction: in the same window, did newly opened proceedings or entries into debt relief rise in a way that would explain the fall differently? A product that announces the fall a day earlier need not be better if a month later no one can find out why it fell in that particular way. 13. The price of a file is the price of the raw material, not the price of the result Justice uses several cost languages at once. The executor bills the costs of the proceeding. The creditor writes off the principal. The state counts contributions that did not arrive. The municipality counts benefits and lost purchasing power. The debtor counts what remains after the deduction. A direct comparison of “how many files disappeared” without knowledge of these accounts misleads. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Cheap deletion of a fruitless file can be economically useful for an overloaded office. The same deletion can be expensive if it is read as proof that counselling is no longer needed. Debt relief with an insolvency administrator can be disproportionate for one manageable claim. It can be useful for a person with many proceedings if the statutory conditions are met and a stable legal income becomes possible. The real price of an accepted result Clearing the archive + recovered principal + contributions from a declared wage + the cost of counselling + the price of a misread statistic + future new proceedings. The result is cheap only when it passes a check of the unit and can be used to decide. Not when one column falls. The costs also include fluctuation. If the same person, after five files are discontinued, returns with the third that remains, the average price of a “resolved debtor” is not the price of one deletion. If the system exhausts counselling capacity at the peak, the cost is waiting. If automatic conclusions are tied tightly to a press release, the cost is also a later correction. It is therefore useful to measure the price per accepted output , not the price per file. Accepted means that a person’s status has changed — repayment, discharge, an insured job — and that this can be verified. That metric can reverse a ranking that looked clear from a year-on-year percentage. An IDEA study at CERGE-EI on the link between enforcement and voting behaviour in municipalities in 2001–2017 recalls that a file has costs outside the courts; it is an analysis up to 2017, not a verdict on the 2024 data. [21] 14. What to choose as an indicator Before reading the headline it is necessary to choose the question and the matching control series. The table below does not rank “truths”; it shows pairs of indicators that must be compared in the same period, population and definition of an ending. Need First series Decisive test Unacceptable shortcut Whether the courts are being cleared Stock and flow of proceedings in the CEE Share of discontinuations vs. recoveries Celebrate every fall in files Whether there are fewer debtors Unique natural persons Pace relative to files, band 1 and 10+ Mistake the average per person for a fall in people Whether a second chance is opening Authorised debt-relief cases per year Denominator: the target group, not the whole CR Read +13% as the end of the crisis Whether wages are returning to the books Contributions, insured jobs Linking the person after discontinuation to a wage Rely on an estimate of billions without a series Whether the region is diverging District map Age, multiple cases, availability of advice The national average as a local diagnosis Whether the market is not feeding new debts Newly opened proceedings, CNB supervision The credit segment, not only the total Declare stagnation the end of the inflow Maintenance, public-law debt and consumer credit need separate readings in the Czech context; one CEE number does not join their mechanisms. The check should include different districts and persons with one proceeding and with several, and it must allow the conclusion that the public source is not enough for the question asked. One indicator can track the archive, another people, debt relief and contributions. That division is useful if the definitions are clear, the series are not added without conversion, and the closing sentence states which of them it rests on. 15. A short audit that says more than a year-on-year percentage A short reader’s audit can show, before publication, whether one column can carry the intended headline. It looks for a swap of file for person, stock for flow and discontinuation for repayment, and it asks whether the newsroom or the office can correct it. Fourteen days from impression to table Days 1–2: Write 20 to 40 real questions: file, person, new application, debt relief, contribution, district. Days 3–4: Prepare the same period, the same population and an anonymous scoring sheet. Days 5–7: Open each important series in the primary source and keep a register of swapped units. Days 8–10: Check latent files, the reason for ending, age and the frequency band. Days 11–12: Calculate how much of the fall you can assign to recovery, discontinuation and insolvency. Day 13: Run stress tests: contradictory series, an incomplete reason for ending, an old district average. Day 14: Decide which column may enter the headline, document the caveat and set a date for the next review. If possible the assessor should not know which narrative the number is meant to support. For files, watch the reason for ending. For persons, the pace relative to proceedings. For debt relief, the denominator. For an estimate of the grey economy, whether an administrative series exists. Each failure is classified: a confabulation of the unit, an omission of latent files, an error of period, or a conclusion the cell did not carry. The series should be compared to the same cut-off day and on the same population. If one includes latent files and the other does not, it is a comparison of different statistics, and that limit must be stated. The pilot should also have exclusion conditions. For example: the single sentence “people got richer” without a share of recovery, the use of a half-year flow as an annual stock, or the impossibility of opening the CEE methodology. A high year-on-year percentage must not override an error whose impact the reader cannot accept. The result of the audit should be a rule of use: which unit may enter the headline, what does not follow from it, who checks the methodology and when the conclusion is revised. Amendments, deduction tariffs and the definition of the CEE change, so every comparison must have a date. 16. A new inflow is not the same as the old stock In 2023 some 461 592 enforcement cases were opened, in 2024 460 573. The difference is 1 019 proceedings. In the first half of 2025 the Chamber recorded 256 479 opened proceedings. That is a flow. It is not proof that the stock of 3.16 million files as of 30 June 2025 is “only dying off”. The stock can fall by deletion and at the same time fill with new applications at a pace that, for the whole of 2024, stayed above 450 thousand. [1] Some of the new proceedings are maintenance, some public-law claims, some consumer credit. Without that cut one cannot say whether CNB regulation “worked”, or whether only the creditor changed. The Indebtedness Map of the Institute for the Prevention and Resolution of Over-indebtedness, which continues the older Map of Enforcement, shows the distribution down to municipalities. A nationwide flow will not replace it. A municipality with a high share of persons in enforcement may have a low flow of new applications, or the reverse. Those are two different policies: clearing the stock and braking the inflow. [12] The average age of a debtor in the Chamber’s data rose from 46.2 years in 2023 to 46.8 in 2024 and to 47 years in the first half of 2025. That is the average of registered persons, not proof that poverty is ageing. Without an age pyramid of newly opened proceedings we cannot tell whether younger people enter the CEE less often, or older people remain in the stock. [1] Stock and inflow should therefore be taken on deliberately: both series, a cut by creditor, and a test of whether the reason for the fall in the stock still holds when the inflow has not fallen. 17. A fall in the register does not yet change the debtor’s decision The first generation of debt amendments sold the discontinuation of low-value cases. The next sold Mercy Summer. The next sold three-year debt relief. Today’s press releases sell something larger: the impression that the CEE curve is the state of society. The contest is therefore not only about the best clean-up of files. It is about the debtor’s working context. About whether the person will sign a contract, whether the deduction leaves a reason for a declared wage, whether a counselling office can be found, and whether after five proceedings are deleted three remain — enough for the person to behave the same. The more comfortable it is to read one column, the higher the price of a mistake can be. Automatic narratives are hard to export back into the methodology. Clearing the archive can have a substantial judicial benefit; it must not be mistaken for repayment of debts. Assessment needs a stable definition of the unit, a documented reason for ending, and a way to separate the person from the file. A useful indicator is not the one with the largest fall or the highest number of discontinuations. Its unit must match the question asked, and any mistakes should be visible, correctable and acknowledged in the headline . The moment the CEE only counts files, we are cleaning a register. The moment we assemble from the fall a report about people getting richer, about a return to work and about the end of debts, we are also assembling a new structure of responsibility for reading. And then the question is no longer: “By how much did enforcement cases fall?” Before assessing the fall it is therefore necessary to find out: Which column fell, for what reason, who will see it in time, and who will bear the cost if we read a file as a resolved life? — Jiný Kontext

items.title: Air quality in Czechia: Are we measuring where people breathe?
items.subtitle: The average urban exposure indicator for fine particles in Czechia has fallen by more than half from the baseline period, and in 2024 stations with sufficient data met the annual EU PM2.5 limit. Specific traffic sites and areas loaded with benzo[a]pyrene nevertheless have a different profile from the national average, and many measured values remain above WHO health-based guidelines. The country average is therefore not an estimate of every person’s dose.

items.body: A figure on air quality has meaning only with the substance, the place, the period and the reference value. The national average may fall while a traffic site remains loaded. A station may measure accurately yet not represent the street where a person moves; a spatial model in turn may fail to distinguish a school from the neighbouring arterial road. Meeting an EU limit is moreover not the same as reaching the stricter WHO guideline. 1. Two standards, one air Imagine a ministerial meeting on air. An official holds a table from the European Environment Agency: the average urban exposure indicator for PM2.5 in Czechia fell from 26.6 µg/m3 in 2009–2011 to 12.2 µg/m3 in 2023, that is by 54.1 per cent. [1] A meteorologist from the Czech Hydrometeorological Institute adds that in 2024 the annual PM2.5 limit was not exceeded at any station with sufficient data, for the second time in the history of measurement since 2005. [3] A pulmonologist objects that the WHO annual guideline for PM2.5 is 5 µg/m3 and that 12.2 µg/m3 is still a 2.4-fold multiple. [2] The mayor of a valley municipality shows a winter morning when smoke from chimneys lies in the basin, while the nearest station reports a good index. A Prague councillor shows Legerova: annual average NO2 36.7 µg/m3, under the current EU limit of 40, but almost four times the WHO guideline. [11] [2] The word “clean” here conceals several different assessments. The official tracks a legal limit, the meteorologist the representativeness of the network, the doctor a health-derived WHO guideline, the mayor a local inversion and the councillor a traffic site. Each yardstick has a different spatial and legal meaning. Meeting the annual PM2.5 limit is valid information about a legislative assessment, not a complete description of exposure. A conclusion for the public must also state the health guideline, the station type, the substance tracked and whether the figure represents a park, a traffic street or a valley with local heating. When comparing, it is first necessary to determine whether we are assessing a long-term trend, a particular street, a modelled area or the relationship to the WHO guideline. A background station, a street canyon and a kilometre-scale model are not interchangeable sources for the same question. A station measures a point. A person breathes a route. An average of points is not the air in the lungs. — Jiný Kontext What measurements and models show — and what we do not know from them We know: Stations describe concentration at a particular place and time; models fill the space between them. Station type, interval and model resolution determine for which comparison the figure is usable. [3] One may assume: a well-validated model will capture a spatial trend even where no station stands. We do not know without local measurement or a more detailed model: the precise concentration on a particular pavement, an individual’s personal dose, or every short peak in a street. 2. What determines the meaning of one concentration An index in an app is the result of a choice of substance, station, time interval, aggregation and comparison value. Two apps can therefore, even from the same source, create a different message, and the same figure may be suitable for an annual trend but unsuitable for today’s street. Five layers of one air-quality figure Substance and metric: PM2.5, PM10, NO2, benzo[a]pyrene; annual average, daily maximum, population-weighted exposure. Place of measurement: background, traffic or industrial station; inlet height; distance from the roadway and chimneys. Time: an hour of inversion, the heating season, an annual average, a three-year AEI indicator. Aggregation: a point, a 1 km square, a region, a state, an urban population. Reference value: the current EU limit, the limit from 2030, the WHO guideline, unit carcinogenic risk. The CHMI network is the basis of official assessment, but an app may choose a station of a type that does not match the user’s location, and a spatial model may smooth a local contrast. The yearbook for 2024 at the same time reports meeting of the annual PM2.5 limit at assessed stations and 7.3 per cent of inhabitants on 1.3 per cent of the territory with above-limit benzo[a]pyrene. [3] A general judgment of “clean air” without the name of the substance thus joins two different findings. Without this cut, in a contradiction one does not know where to reach. If the national average has fallen and winter in a valley has remained dirty, spatial selection may have failed, not the laboratory. If a station by a road reports high NO2 and a park three hundred metres away does not, that is not fraud. It is the geography of emissions. If the EU limit holds and the WHO does not, we are not comparing cleanliness. We are comparing two different contracts. Illustrative scheme: The chain between the lungs and a press release runs through substance, station, interval, aggregation and threshold. A break in any link changes the meaning of the number without the measurement itself changing. 3. A report must name its blind spot Readers usually look for the report with the highest share of limits met. That is reasonable, but incomplete. Equally important is what the place the report does not see looks like, whether it can be recognised, how much overlooking it costs, and whether it is a reversible peak or a season in a valley. For 2022 the EEA estimated in Czechia 6 884 premature deaths attributable to PM2.5 against 13 100 in 2005, a fall of 48 per cent. [5] This is a health-risk assessment according to the WHO Europe methodology, not a clinical diagnosis of an individual and not proof that under the EU limit the risk disappears. The decline is real. Zero is not. Type of failure What it looks like How to test it What limits the harm Confusion of references An EU limit met, a higher value than the WHO guideline Compare the same concentration with both values Separate legislation from the health guideline Failure of place A background station representing a canyon or a basin Station type, distance, inlet height Traffic and local measurement Failure of time An annual average hiding inversion weeks Daily and hourly series in the heating season A smog warning system Failure of substance Clean PM2.5, high benzo[a]pyrene Track PAHs and local stoves, not only dust Fuel, boiler, combustion control Political assessment therefore cannot stop at nationwide meeting of limits. It must also show situations that the network or the model distinguishes more poorly. Mountain background, a traffic canyon and a municipality with local stoves have different sources and different groups of inhabitants, and one average will not split their exposure. When assessing the network, besides technical quality it is necessary to watch the visibility of local extremes, time resolution and the representation of vulnerable groups. A clearly labelled station type may carry more information for a local decision than a smooth spatial map that does not distinguish a street contrast. 4. An ambient average does not describe every place Indicators are needed because they replace part of impressions with a repeatable series. The problem arises the moment one number begins to stand for all the air. The EEA builds the Average Exposure Indicator on a three-year average of urban background stations. At the same time it thereby defines what it does not measure: a traffic hot-spot, a village inversion, an hourly peak, or benzo[a]pyrene. [1] Every test contains hidden decisions. Which stations enter the average? What type? What period? What threshold? The answer to any of these questions can change the sentence in a press release. In 2024 the CHMI defined areas with exceedance of ambient limits excluding ozone on 1.3 per cent of the territory, where approximately 7.4 per cent of inhabitants live; after including ozone 1.4 per cent of the territory and 7.5 per cent of inhabitants. The delineation is driven primarily by benzo[a]pyrene. Annual PM2.5 and NO2 at stations did not exceed the limits. [3] What must accompany a claim of clean air The precise substance, metric and unit. Station type and its representativeness, not only the name of the municipality. The period: hour, day, year, three-year AEI. The threshold: EU now, EU 2030, WHO 2021. Known gaps in the network: small settlements, valleys, breathing height. For a local decision a map that distinguishes station type and sources in the municipality is useful. A short winter campaign can capture an inversion episode, but it is not representative as an annual average. The national indicator and local measurement therefore complement each other; each describes a different scale. 5. Compare stations, not slogans about clean air The network can be described without a false podium of winners. The following map does not say who “is right about the air”. It shows what kind of work the individual layers do, what context they bring and which failure the reader should look for on purpose. Layer Main working position What to check Typical reason for use CHMI urban background A city average outside a canyon Whether it is not being passed off as a street A long-term trend Traffic station An artery, a canyon, a junction Inlet height and distance from the roadway NO2 and dust from traffic Industrial station Steelworks, chemicals, a site What has changed on the site A local source, not a “region” CAMx / EMEP / CAMS model Coverage of white spots Resolution and input emissions A spatial map, not a microclimate Community sensor Density in the municipality Calibration against a reference A signal, not an official limit The table does not judge the quality of measurement. It shows for what purpose different types of stations and models serve. A background figure should therefore not by itself be used as an estimate of a child’s exposure in a traffic canyon. The best figure on air is determined by the price of its blind spot. A decision joins impact, the chance of detection, the reversibility of a peak and who bears the consequences. Neither the position nor the size of elements in the scheme expresses a score; the scheme shows questions that must be answered together. How to read the scheme: Background, traffic, industry, model and sensor provide different cuts of the same air. Their figures can be combined only with a statement of space, time and method. 6. An EU limit is not a WHO guideline value Air-quality assessment uses two different references. An EU limit is a legally enforceable value. A WHO guideline is a health-derived value for population protection, not a boundary below which risk is automatically zero. Directive 2024/2881, effective from 10 December 2024, sets for 2030 an annual limit PM2.5 10 µg/m3 and NO2 20 µg/m3; until then the previous values of 25 and 40 are used. The target value for benzo[a]pyrene remains 1.0 ng/m3. [8] In 2021 the WHO recommended annual AQG of 5 µg/m3 for PM2.5, 15 µg/m3 for PM10 and 10 µg/m3 for NO2. [2] Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Substance Annual EU limit (until 2030 / from 2030) WHO 2021 guideline What the number can say in Czechia PM2.5 25 / 10 µg/m3 5 µg/m3 AEI 12.2 µg/m3 (2023) is under the old limit, 2.4× above WHO [1] [2] PM10 40 / 20 µg/m3 15 µg/m3 Annual limits at stations in 2024 met; daily exceedance on 0.003% of the territory [3] NO2 40 / 20 µg/m3 10 µg/m3 Stations met the 2024 limits; traffic arteries remain well above WHO [3] [10] Benzo[a]pyrene 1.0 ng/m3 0.12 ng/m3 as a reference risk level 7.3% of inhabitants on above-limit territory (2024) [3] [21] If a state report notes that limits are being met, that means meeting of a legislative standard. It does not mean reaching the value that the WHO recommends for long-term exposure, nor zero health risk. It does not follow that the CHMI measures badly. A legal limit and a health guideline have a different function. For benzo[a]pyrene the distinction is still more important. The value 0.12 ng/m3 is not a “WHO limit” in the same sense as the annual AQG for PM2.5. It is a reference concentration derived from unit carcinogenic risk in older European WHO materials; the new EU directive uses it in the assessment system. [21] [8] Comparing 1.0 against 0.12 therefore does not place two equally standing limits side by side. According to the EEA overview, in the assessed year still about 95 per cent of the EU urban population was exposed to a PM2.5 average above 5 µg/m3. [6] Czechia is not an exception in that. Meeting of an EU limit can therefore occur earlier than reaching of the WHO guideline value. 7. A background park is not a street canyon The state ambient-monitoring network is technically advanced. Its placement is governed by rules of representativeness, not by the aim of measuring every junction. Urban background stations represent a broader urban background outside the immediate influence of a particular source; traffic stations, for example Legerova in Prague and Českobratrská in Ostrava, track loaded roads. [3] [11] The network therefore does not by itself give a point measurement for every municipality, street or valley. In 2024 the CHMI measured NO2 with passive samplers in streets and by schools in Prague and Ostrava. In Prague the campaign had at 11 of 17 traffic sites an estimate of the annual average higher than 40 µg/m3. It reported the highest values for upper Ječná by Sokolská at 58 µg/m3, V Holešovičkách 57.3 µg/m3 and Plzeňská 57.2 µg/m3. At background sites by schools — in courtyards or development approximately 100 metres from an artery — concentrations were 2.2 times to 2.5 times lower; they nevertheless moved at the level of the future limit of 20 µg/m3 or above it. The deviation of the passive samplers from the reference method was 3.7 per cent at Legerova and 9.1 per cent at Českobratrská. [10] These are results of a measurement campaign, not in themselves a legal evaluation of the whole Prague network nor a measurement of every municipality. That is not proof that background stations lie. It is proof that they measure different air. Anyone who takes a park as a proxy for a canyon does not make an error in chemistry. They make an error in geography. Personal exposure is also affected by height, a person’s movement, distance from the roadway and time spent in the place. From the figure of one stationary station it is therefore not possible, without more data, to derive the precise dose of a child in a pram or of an adult pedestrian. This is not an error of the station, but a difference between ambient measurement of a locality and personal exposure. 8. Model resolution has its limits Because it is not possible to measure on every corner, the CHMI supplements stations with modelling and uses various model inputs; the European context is also provided by EMEP and Copernicus CAMS. [15] [16] Spatial resolution differs among products and tasks. A spatial model may describe an area or a trend well, but without a sufficiently fine grid and suitable inputs it may fail to distinguish the contrast between an arterial road, a school and a courtyard, or the flow in a street canyon. The CHMI says this openly for benzo[a]pyrene: the estimate of fields has among the mapped substances the greatest uncertainty, among other reasons because more extensive measurement in small settlements that would represent the influence of local stoves is missing. Station rotation is therefore used so that over several years more localities are measured. [3] That is an honest limit. It is not a reason to throw the model away. It is a reason not to read a kilometre map as a street. What needs to be tested The first test concerns resolution: what grid, what emissions, what weather. The second concerns validation: where the model sits on a station and where it diverges. The third concerns use. A model is good for delineating areas and trends. It is bad as the sole proof that a particular crossing by a school is “in order” because the square has the colour of the limit. With a large corpus of data, for a particular local decision a suitably placed station with a clearly stated type may be more useful than a smooth map of a whole region. A nationwide map has a different purpose: it shows spatial differences, but it can smooth the contrast of one street. From the map itself one cannot infer an intention to hide something. 9. Benzo(a)pyrene: a household chimney is not a power-plant chimney According to the national emission inventory, the household sector — heating, water heating and cooking — was in 2023 the dominant emission source of several tracked substances: it accounted for 96.6 per cent of benzo[a]pyrene emissions, 81.3 per cent of PM2.5 and 63.7 per cent of PM10. Public energy was a significant source of arsenic and SO2, traffic of NOx emissions. [3] An emission share for the whole republic does not, however, itself determine local concentration, personal exposure or the source’s share of toxicity and health burden. The burning of coal and unsuitable wood in older boilers produces polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Benzo[a]pyrene binds to fine particles and IARC classifies it as carcinogenic to humans. [19] [20] Studies in the Moravian-Silesian region linked exposure to a mixture of dust and PAHs with biomarkers of genotoxicity; these are particular samples and periods, not proof that every municipality in the republic carries the same risk. [12] Long-term PM2.5 cohorts show a relationship to mortality even at concentrations under older limits; Pope and colleagues summarise more than 25 years of these studies. [13] At the industrial station Ostrava-Radvanice ZÚ the annual average of benzo[a]pyrene fell from 5.2 ng/m3 in 2023 to 1.6 ng/m3 in 2024 after the curtailment of primary steel production at Liberty Ostrava. In 2025 provisionally 1.3 ng/m3. [4] The decline is real and is tied to a particular source. It is not proof that local stoves in the agglomeration have disappeared. On the contrary: the CHMI states that local heating has long accounted for more than 95 per cent of nationwide benzo[a]pyrene emissions. [4] The curtailment of primary steel production can explain part of the change at a particular industrial station, not automatically the development of the whole agglomeration. Local stoves and other sources must be assessed separately; neither an emission inventory nor a single station by itself documents their local contribution in every basin. 10. Ostravsko and Legerova fail differently Aggregated statistics erase hotspots because they add up different mechanisms. The Ostrava–Karviná–Frýdek-Místek agglomeration remains according to the CHMI the most loaded area in the long term; in 2024, 80 per cent of its inhabitants were exposed to above-limit concentrations. [3] Above-limit here is driven primarily by benzo[a]pyrene, not annual PM2.5 at stations. That is important: the same percentage could in another city mean traffic. Here it means a mixture of steelworks, stoves and transboundary background. Prague has a different profile. The annual NO2 average at the station Prague 2-Legerova of 36.7 µg/m3 remains under the valid limit of 40 µg/m3, but above the WHO guideline of 10 µg/m3. [11] [2] The passive campaign showed still higher values at some traffic sites. [10] For their interpretation it is necessary to distinguish traffic emissions, urban background and local flow conditions; the concentration itself will not determine each source’s share. Two similar indexes can mean different air. Index 2 in a park and index 2 in an app that draws from the park while you stand on an arterial road are not the same measurement. They are the same number transferred to the wrong place. Two similar indexes can mean different air Take two illustrations, not a report. Locality A: an official station in a hospital grounds on a rise, greenery, background type. The index reports very good quality. Locality B, two kilometres as the crow flies: a housing estate in a valley, a junction, family houses with boilers. During a winter inversion the PM2.5 concentration here can exceed the background several-fold; the order of inversion peaks in basins with solid fuels is known from campaigns and from rotating stations, not from the year-round average of every municipality. [3] Parents in B open an app linked to A and walk with a pram in the belief that they are breathing the same thing. The error is not in sensor A. The error is in the transfer of representativeness. Two kilometres on a map are not two kilometres in the air when a hill and an inversion lie between them. 11. An app must show where it takes the figure from Before the smartphone a person had to trust a window and a nose. With an index they check something more complicated: whether the source exists, whether it is the right type of station, whether it speaks of the same hour and whether the conclusion “you may air the room” really follows from the point the app used. An index is navigation to a measurement. It is not automatic proof about a street. The republic’s annual average, a background-station figure and an hourly peak in a canyon can all be correct, but they relate to a different space and time. A recommendation to run along an arterial road therefore cannot rest on a nationwide or background figure without local measurement. A four-step check of the index Existence: where the number is from, which station, which ID. Type: background, traffic, industry, model, or a community sensor. Support: does the interval fit — now, today, this year? Scope: does the place fit the place where you breathe. The community network Sensor.Community densifies the map with cheap PM sensors. [14] It is a useful signal of the gradient between streets. It is not an official ambient limit. Calibration, humidity and placement on a balcony change the number. A research product is good when it shortens the path to a check, not when it replaces the check. 12. The yearbook describes a trend, not a personal dose The CHMI yearbook for 2024 is sober: concentrations of most substances are falling, PM2.5 and PM10 at stations did not exceed the limits, benzo[a]pyrene and ozone did so on part of the network. The year was extraordinarily above-normal in temperature, an average of 10.3 °C, a deviation of +2.0 °C from the 1991–2020 normal; a warmer heating period reduces fuel consumption. Emissions are also falling. In the Ostrava region the curtailment of Liberty showed. [3] All of this is true of what the yearbook measures. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext For a local reading further figures also matter: according to the yearbook, 80 per cent of inhabitants of the O/K/F-M agglomeration lived in areas with exceedance of at least one ambient limit and 7.3 per cent of the republic’s inhabitants on territory with above-limit benzo[a]pyrene. [3] The Prague passive campaign moreover measured at part of the traffic sites estimates of the annual NO2 average above the numerical level of the valid limit; the campaign itself, however, does not replace a legal assessment of the station network. [10] Act No. 201/2012 Coll. imposes limits, information and a smog warning system. [9] The new directive will from 2030 add harder numbers and a stronger right to information. [8] Neither the act nor the directive will turn a background station into a measurement of a pram. They change the state’s duty. They do not change the physics of dispersion. A long series is like a long context for a model: the whole republic fits into it. It does not follow that every sentence in the series is used equally. The decisive paragraph may lie in the chapter on benzo[a]pyrene, while the headline cites PM2.5. 13. Who remains outside the average The question “has the average fallen?” is important, but narrow. An organisation must also know who remains in the tail of the distribution: children by an artery, households with a class 1 and 2 boiler, an estate under an inversion, an industrial quarter downwind. The average may fall because the middle has been cleaned, while the tail holds the toxicity. The EEA states that Czechia is on the path to the target of reducing premature deaths attributable to PM2.5 by 55 per cent by 2030 against 2005; the decline to 2022 was 48 per cent. [5] The target is population-level. It does not describe whether the gain has been evenly distributed between a park and a basin. It does not follow that the average is worthless. It follows that fairness of exposure is a different metric from meeting a limit. In the European Union a legal shift is added. Directive 2024/2881 brings limits closer to WHO guidelines, but does not reach them: PM2.5 10 against 5 µg/m3 and NO2 20 against 10 µg/m3. [8] [2] The WHO guideline value has remained stricter. Czechia can therefore in 2030 meet the new EU limits and at the same time be above the AQG; both figures answer a different question. Local assessment should besides the average contain station type, fuel, traffic, inversions and places where vulnerable groups stay. Only this combination will show whom the nationwide trend represents well and whom it does not. 14. The price of a limit is not the price of health Public policy uses several languages at once. A press release tracks meeting of a limit, a health assessment population risk, a municipality emission sources and traffic policy the operation in the streets. The claim “we are clean because the limit was met” therefore, without stating the substance, the place and the reference value, says too little. A national average will not quantify the health impact of local hotspots. In 2024, 7.3 per cent of inhabitants lived on territory with above-limit benzo[a]pyrene and the Legerova station reported NO2 close to the valid limit. [3] [11] The choice of measures therefore requires knowledge of the substance, the place and the source; from the concentration in one street one cannot without source analysis determine whether traffic, heating or their combination decides. The conclusion is more complete when, besides meeting of a legal limit, it also states a comparison with the WHO guideline and the limits of spatial representativeness. Such a reading can change the order of priorities: a region with a low background and local hotspots is not the same as a region with an evenly distributed concentration, even if they have a similar average. Costs also include fluctuation. The warm winter of 2024 improved the figures through weather and through emissions. [3] If the same policy rests on a single warm year, average cleanliness is not a property of the boilers. It is a property of February. If an app draws from a park, the cost is false calm in a canyon. It is therefore useful to assess measures by the change of concentration and exposure in the place affected, not only by meeting of a limit at one station. For that the substance, the place, the time and the chosen reference value must all fit. 15. What to watch according to where you live First it is necessary to determine the type of place and a suitable data source. The following table is not a ranking of cities; it shows when to compare an official station with a local signal in the same period and when their difference requires further measurement. Need First figures Decisive test Unacceptable shortcut Trend of the republic AEI, CHMI yearbook The same substance, the same station type, the same threshold “It has fallen, therefore it is safe” Street and school Traffic station, passive NO2 Distance from the roadway, height, peak hour A park as a proxy for a canyon A valley municipality Rotating stations, sensors, fuel Inversion, boiler type, wood moisture Nationwide PM2.5 as a verdict on a basin O/K/F-M agglomeration BaP, industry, stoves Separate the steelworks from the stove One report on “Ostravsko” Personal airing Station + wind + time Where the app takes the point from An index without a station ID In Czech conditions it is necessary to verify the heating season separately. Summer ozone, winter combustion and the traffic peak have different mechanisms. A foreign ranking of cities will not show the fuel in a particular municipality, and sometimes the right conclusion is that the nearest station does not represent the given place. Some cities need more layers. One for the trend, a second for arteries, a third for boilers. That is not a failure of standardisation. It is the same decision as using a different thermometer in a boiler room and a different one on the square. The condition is that the division is intelligible and that data are not translated unchecked from a park into a canyon. 16. A short test that says more than a national average A first local check can be started even before the next yearbook. It does not determine definitive health risk; it verifies the data source, the station type and situations in which the national average may not represent the municipality. Fourteen days from impression to map Days 1–2: Find the nearest CHMI station, its type, ID and distance. Days 3–4: Compare the annual average with the EU limit, the 2030 limit and WHO. Days 5–7: In the heating season track daily PM2.5; evaluate benzo[a]pyrene from available longer-term measurements and the yearbook, because an ordinary daily figure is usually not available. Days 8–10: Check fuel in the surroundings and the traffic artery; separate the boiler from the exhaust. Days 11–12: If you use a sensor, compare it with a reference station, not with feelings. Day 13: Stress test: inversion, calm, Friday afternoon, Sunday heating. Day 14: Write down the limits: what the number measures, what it does not, when to open it again. Three tests of local exposure The first is spatial: is the station background, traffic, or industrial, and how far does it lie from the place where you breathe? The second is a threshold: are you comparing 25, 10, or 5 µg/m3 for PM2.5? The third is about substance: does clean dust fail to address a problem that benzo[a]pyrene holds? A product that answers a minute earlier need not be better if, an hour later, nobody can find out which station it used. Before you open a window according to an app Find the station ID, not only the colour. Separate the annual average from today’s hour. In a winter valley do not take an urban park as a proxy. By a school look for NO2 and traffic, not only PM. With boilers look for benzo[a]pyrene and fuel, not only “PM2.5 met”. A comparison requires the same week, substance and reference value. A model map and a direct measurement are different products; their difference must be stated expressly. When testing the place itself it is on the contrary advisable to unify the source or method. A local check should end with a rule of use: which station represents which place, what the average is for, what the municipality must measure in addition and when it will revise the result. Weather, fuel and traffic change, so the conclusion needs a date. 17. An average can conceal uneven exposure The first generation of air reports sold desulphurisation. The next generation met PM limits. Today’s yearbooks sell something larger: the impression that the republic as a whole breathes the same thing. That is why the contest is not only for a lower microgram. It is a contest over which layer may speak for all the others. The smoother the average that arises, the higher the price of overlooking can be. Basins fit poorly into the AEI. Canyons fit poorly into a background station. Boilers fit poorly into a headline about PM2.5. People cease to distinguish their own street from a map in which it has been smoothed away. The average remains important: it documents a fall in the urban PM2.5 exposure indicator of 54.1 per cent between the baseline period 2009–2011 and 2023. [1] Local use must, however, add to it station type, fuel, traffic and a procedure for inversion situations. The usefulness of a figure is determined neither by the lowest value nor the prettiest colour in an app. Resolution must match the question posed and its blind spots should be visible, named and taken into account in the decision . The moment we read a yearbook, we choose a trend. The moment we open a window above boilers according to an index or send children to an arterial road, we also choose a new structure of responsibility. And then the question is no longer: “Is the average air in the republic clean?” When reading an average we should therefore ask: Who remains outside its resolution, and by which legal or health reference are we assessing the result? — Jiný Kontext

items.title: Housing, heat-pump and electric-vehicle subsidies: Who checks that they actually work?
items.subtitle: The state and the Union have allocated tens of billions to insulation, boilers and electric mobility. Press releases often cite the number of applications and devices, while energy or climate impact requires a different kind of evaluation. In an audit of apartment buildings for 2015–2020, reported savings reached, according to the NKÚ, about 41 per cent of the plan for IROP and 13.5 per cent for the NZÚ sub-programme; these figures cannot automatically be applied to all of today’s subsidy programmes.
