items.body: Choosing a voice assistant for a child is not only a contest in correct answers. It depends on the topic, the age, the privacy settings, the way the product reacts, and whether the child has room to challenge the answer. A fluent voice can be a useful interface, but fluency itself confirms neither truth nor pedagogical suitability. What we know / What we do not know What we know: Voice systems can err, process children’s data, and by their fluency raise trust in an answer. On sensitive topics, verification by an adult and a clear privacy setting are therefore appropriate. What we do not know: From the studies cited one cannot derive a single long-term effect on all children, nor claim that every assistant reacts in the same way. The result depends on age, topic, product, settings and the way it is used. 1. A child’s question and a machine’s answer are not the same Picture the kitchen of a Czech household. One parent wants a voice assistant because the child asks questions in the car and that parent is driving. The other would rather switch the speaker off, because they dislike a five-year-old giving orders to a stranger’s voice. The teacher would be glad if children stopped handing in essays that sound the same. School IT wants an account with supervision. A grandparent sees a miracle: at last someone answers “why”. The child itself only wants to know why the leaves fall, and does not want to wait. At first glance this is a dispute about technology. In fact each person is describing a different problem. One parent compares hands on the steering wheel. The other describes the tone in which the child learns to speak to people. The teacher describes the authenticity of the assignment. The school describes permissions and data. The grandparent describes the availability of an answer. The child describes the cost of waiting. A product can succeed in a quiz and at the same time be unsuitable for sensitive children’s questions. A household therefore has to separate factual accuracy, the manner of the reply, privacy, the possibility of parental control, room for a further question, and the seriousness of a possible error. A brand is worth comparing only after the task has been named. A factual query, language practice, a sensitive conversation and mere playback of content have different risks and require a different degree of supervision. A voice is not a teacher. An answer is not a dialogue. Fluency is not certainty. And the patience of a machine is not upbringing. — Jiný Kontext From a child’s question to a stored answer An illustrative chain between child, device, account and recording. From a child’s question to a stored answer Child Device Account Recording Answer JINÝ KONTEXT Illustrative diagram: The chain shows the path of the voice; it does not measure screen time or rate a particular product. 2. What happens between the question and the answer When a calm sentence comes out of the speaker, it is easy to form the impression that “the assistant said it”. But the result usually arises in a chain. Each layer can raise the quality, lower it, or change the type of error. Two products with the same base therefore need not answer in the same way, and the same product can behave differently according to the account, the mode, and whether an adult is standing with the child. Five layers of one voice answer Base model: language ability, knowledge, typical limits and a leaning toward certainty. Mode: a quick answer, a child’s profile, search, limits on length. Working setup: system instructions, history, the “personality” of the voice, a control loop. Sources and tools: the web, an encyclopedia, a household account, connected applications. Governance and responsibility: who owns the account, what is recorded, who may continue the question. The base model determines an important part of the abilities, but it is not the only actor. An application can insert a child filter before the question, attach a history, shorten the answer, or, conversely, deliver it in a tone that sounds like infallibility. The same question in the car, in the kitchen and alone in a room is not the same exercise. This is where the first error of the public debate is born. A headline announces a contest between a human and a machine, but in fact it compares two different chains: a tired parent at 21:40 and a product with endless capacity. Or, conversely, it measures that an assistant can list photosynthesis and then presents the result as a verdict on upbringing. An honest comparison has to state not only the brand, but also the age of the child, the presence of an adult, the type of question, the tools that are switched on, and the method of control. This layering is not an academic detail. It determines where to turn when something fails. If the answer did not know yesterday’s weather, the web may have been missing. If it overlooked that the child was asking out of fear, the context failed. If it delivered certainty where “I don’t know” would have been enough, the problem is in the tone. The sentence “AI got it wrong” is the beginning of a diagnosis, not its end. Illustrative scheme: The same model can, in another mode, with another adult and another question, create a different habit. 3. The best assistant is the one whose error the child can bear In children’s use, beside factual accuracy, the type of error and the chance to correct it quickly matter. A wrong date in a quiz has a different impact from a self-assured answer to a sensitive question. Pronunciation can be practised again; the long-term effect of frequent ready-made answers is, however, uncertain without longitudinal data and must not be presented as a proven cause of behaviour. In its recommendation on generative AI in education, UNESCO stresses that tools should serve learning, not replace it, and recommends human supervision especially with children. [11] Risk does not grow only with the frequency of error. It also grows when a calm voice tempts disproportionate trust. Type of failure What it looks like How to test it What limits the harm False certainty A fluent answer without “I don’t know” Questions where the source is not enough A required “how do you know”; the presence of an adult Omission A correct fact; a condition or a feeling is missing A check with “and what if?” Asking further together Error of context The machine hears the words, not the reason for the question The same question with an adult and without one Asking together, not the smart speaker alone Linguistic shortcut Orders instead of a conversation A recording of the child’s tone toward people An adult modelling politeness That also changes the question we are asking. We are not asking only which assistant will answer best on average. We are asking which one will fail in a way that the household can catch. Creative play can bear more obvious nonsense; on health, school or personal distress the cost of hidden certainty is higher, and the answer deserves verification by an adult. With a small child it is especially important not to read fluency as evidence. A practical assessment should include whether the system will admit uncertainty, what permissions it has, and whether a parent can set or later check the use. A product with a lower quiz score can be more suitable in a particular household if these limits work better. 4. What the Mini-Census says and what it does not Data on children and technology are needed, because they replace part of impression. The problem begins at the moment when one percentage starts to stand for the whole of upbringing. Almost 84 thousand pupils aged 9–15 from 5.5 thousand classes and 1.1 thousand schools took part in the Mini-Census of the Czech Statistical Office in 2025. It is an educational project of ČSÚ, not a random sample of the whole population of children in the Czech Republic. A press release stated that nine out of ten children had already used tools of artificial intelligence at some point; a more detailed text in Statistika a My put the same survey at 87 percent of pupils and 3 percent who do not know what it is. The difference is in rounding and in the age groups: among nine-year-olds more than half had used AI, among fifteen-year-olds essentially everyone. [1] [2] Only 2 percent of respondents did not have their own mobile phone. According to the ČSÚ summary, less than a quarter of all participating children already owned one before starting primary school. Among today’s fifteen-year-olds it was 15 percent, among today’s nine-year-olds 33 percent. A fifth of children spend more than five hours a day on the internet. [1] [2] Indicator (Mini-Census 2025, pupils aged 9–15) Value What the number does not measure Pupils who have already used AI 87 % The quality of use; the presence of an adult ČSÚ press summary “nine out of ten” The exact interval by age A phone before Year 1 less than a quarter Whether it was a voice assistant A phone before primary school among nine-year-olds 33 % The same cohort as among 15-year-olds Online more than 5 hours a day 20 % The share of voice versus a screen The IRTIS survey of Masaryk University from May and June 2025 asked 2 607 children and adolescents aged 9–17 at 99 schools. They used generative AI most often for an essay or a paper (42 percent) and for a summary of a longer text (39 percent); 29.5 percent ask AI for a recommendation of what to do, watch, listen to or buy. This is a different population, a different tool and a different method from the Mini-Census. [3] Five facts without which a percentage is only an advertising number The exact age, the school and the method of selection. Whether it was voice, text, or “some AI”. Whether the child answered alone, or with a teacher in the room. The period of collection and the wording of the question. What the child counts as “use”. A public indicator helps one to understand that voice and AI are not a matter only of secondary school. A decision about upbringing has to be made by other work: observation of whether another question follows the answer, or silence. A child stands in several circles at once Phone, account, recording and adult oversight enter the same interaction. A child stands in several circles at once Phone Account Recording Adult Child JINÝ KONTEXT Interpretive diagram: Position and size do not express burden; the diagram connects places the speaker hides. 5. Compare modes of use, not mascots The table splits voice modes by the task they are meant to perform in the household and by the failure that a family test is meant to catch. It does not determine a universal ranking of brands. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Mode Main operating stance What to check in a week Typical reason for the choice Voice on a parent’s phone A quick fact, navigation, a timer Whether the child asks alone; the tone of orders The hands are busy Smart speaker A household hub, music, weather Recording, profiles, night use Comfort of the room Child’s account Filters, limits, supervision What the filter lets through and what it withholds Lower content risk School AI An essay, a summary, an explanation Whether a procedure remained, or only the text An assignment that can be described Asking together An adult hears the question and the answer Whether a second question arises Upbringing, not a fact The rows are not a judgment on brands. The same vendor offers several modes, and each can change within a few months. The map is meant to prevent another error: that a family buys an excellent model in a mode that cannot see the child, cannot say “I don’t know”, or locks the child into a habit from which it is later hard to walk away. How to read the scheme: Neither the position nor the size of the elements expresses a score. The diagram separates the content of the answer, the tone of the interaction, the permissions of the product and parental control. 6. Fluency is not infallibility. It is acoustic authority When choosing whom to trust, a child can orient itself by eye contact, intonation, facial expression and the reactions of those around it. Voice output lacks part of these cues, and fluency can work as a signal of authority. The degree of trust, however, differs by age, situation and the child’s experience. In a paper on children’s interactions with voice search, Lovato and Piper described questions, repairs and communication failures. These are observations of particular interactions, not evidence that every child treats the assistant as a teacher, or that every product deliberately closes the question. The study supports the need to watch whether a particular mode allows a follow-up question and admits uncertainty. [4] In a review of smart speakers and children, Common Sense Media describes a device that enters household life as a voice that is always available: music, questions, purchases, jokes. At the same time it points to privacy and to the fact that children may not understand when recording is on. [7] That is a property of a particular mode, not an automatic property of every telephone. What needs to be tested The first trial concerns tone. Ask a question to which there is no single sentence, and watch whether the assistant admits uncertainty. The second concerns repair: state a knowingly wrong assumption and watch whether the machine corrects it or nods along. The third concerns the source: can one tell from the answer where the claim came from? A product that answers a second earlier need not be better if a minute later nobody knows why it answered in that way. For a parent who wants one broad service, integration can be decisive. For upbringing the sentence “we have Siri” is not enough. One needs to know the account, the filter, the recording, the presence of an adult, and the boundary beyond which a human has to take the answer further. 7. Language without emotion is not politeness Human dialogue is two-way. When a child asks an insensitive question or uses an aggressive tone, an adult can react with a change of expression, a pause or an explanation. Some products or modes that have been studied answer an order and a request in a similar way, or with a scripted reaction; others already distinguish tone and politeness. The behaviour has to be checked on the particular version. [7] Beneteau and colleagues analysed communication breakdowns in which children shortened sentences, repeated commands or raised their voice. [5] Druga and Ko followed family patterns around smart devices. [6] These are particular households and recordings, not evidence of long-term damage to language. The results show a possible risk that repeated instrumental commands will narrow the room for negotiating meaning; the size and duration of the effect cannot be determined from them. A pleasant voice can hide the same old problem A well-intoned sentence acts as a sign of understanding. It is not automatically one. On a question about school, guilt or fear one has to check especially whether the system mistook a child’s thesis for a dictionary definition, omitted an inconvenient exception, or fused two different meanings into a smooth but empty sentence. The quality of the wording lowers the cost of listening. At the same time it can raise the cost of discovering that the question was left untouched. Sherry Turkle described the same logic outside voice assistants: a technology that simulates a conversation can reduce the appetite for undergoing the discomfort of a real conversation. [10] The book is not an experiment on Siri. It is a warning that patience without a relationship is not the same as a relationship. An answer is not a dialogue A fluent voice and shared follow-up questions belong to different exercises. An answer is not a dialogue Answer Dialogue Voice Fluency Question Oversight Space JINÝ KONTEXT Interpretive diagram: The sides are not an impact study; they separate a finished answer from the space in which a child may ask again. 8. The gap between the question and the answer is a learning space Part of learning arises in the formulation of a hypothesis, the search for a source and the follow-up questions that come after. An immediate answer can shorten this space if no check or further question follows it; by itself, however, it does not necessarily end the process of learning. A possible risk is the crowding-out of time in which a child bears uncertainty, formulates a hypothesis and looks for connections. The sources cited here do not provide longitudinal evidence that a voice assistant itself causes impatience or permanently weakens this skill. It is a hypothesis that can be watched in a particular family by the questions that follow and by checking together. An illustration, not a report. A seven-year-old asks the speaker: “Why are some people mean?” The assistant offers a shortened definition. The child switches the device off. The question was closed; the fear from a school situation remained. The same question to a father can start twenty minutes about what happened at break. The information is secondary. What is primary is that someone heard the reason for the question. A machine can supply data. It can also end the process before the data are enough. The difference is not in the botany of leaves. It is in whether a second sentence follows the first. 9. The 5 C framework: screen time is the wrong unit In its 2019 recommendations for children under five, the World Health Organization does not treat voice assistants as a separate product. It treats movement, sedentary behaviour and sleep. This is a narrow age frame, not a manual for Siri. There is still a useful distinction in it: measuring only minutes in front of a screen is not enough if sleep, movement and a relationship are being lost. [8] Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext In the policy statement Digital Ecosystems, Children, and Adolescents (Pediatrics, 2026), the American Academy of Pediatrics leaves simple minute limits and moves to a digital ecosystem. It recommends the 5 C framework: Child, Content, Calm, Crowding out, Communication. Artificial intelligence is mentioned in the text as a phenomenon that has yet to receive a separate statement. [9] This is a clinical recommendation for families and paediatricians in the USA, not a law for Czech households. It does show, however, that the unit is not the brand, but the mode. Five C’s in the practice of voice Child: age, temperament, whether the child can already separate a voice from a person. Content: a fact, a game, an order, or a question about guilt and fear. Calm: whether the voice is not replacing falling asleep and the regulation of emotion. Crowding out: what has given way — a book, movement, a conversation, boredom. Communication: whether the child asks together with an adult. A voice assistant can be a useful tool. For small children and sensitive topics the recommended safe mode is the presence of an adult who verifies the answer and develops it. That is not an empirically necessary condition of every use, nor a legal requirement. 10. How to check a finished answer Before a voice assistant, a child had to check whether an adult knew. With an assistant it checks something more complicated: whether the sentence fits the question, whether it is complete, whether it is more certain than it may be, and whether it was even worth asking alone. A citation from an encyclopedia is navigation toward evidence. It is not automatic evidence. One answer can combine three true sentences into a false conclusion. The first describes leaves, the second autumn, the third “because the tree wants to”. Each part sounds right, but the synthesis is anthropomorphic. At other times the system uses a good dictionary on a question that did not want a dictionary. The child asked about a classmate’s meanness. It received a definition of antisocial behaviour. A four-step check of a child’s answer Existence: the claim can be verified. Authority: the source is appropriate for the given age. Support: the sentence really answers the question that was asked. Scope: it fits that this is a fact, not a relationship, fear or morality. On a sensitive child’s question a jointly formulated question and a source that can be looked up should come first. A fluently spoken answer must not become certainty if its support cannot be opened or does not agree with the source. A system is good when it shortens the path to a check, not when it replaces the check. For the weather a quick answer may be enough. On a question about people the last step has to be taken by a human who hears the child. 11. The patience of a machine is not the memory of a dialogue A great willingness to answer fifty times is often translated into the sentence “the assistant has a patience that a parent does not”. Technically a system can accept fifty repetitions. It does not follow that the fiftieth repetition is learning. It can be a loop in which the child learns that the world has no right to say “enough now”. The memory of the product is another layer. It can keep a name, a favourite song, past questions. That helps continuity. It also creates a risk of an outdated assumption: that the child is still five, that it is still afraid of the dark, that it still lives at grandmother’s. The system can “remember” a context that no longer holds. The documentation of particular large models describes a context window as information available for a given interaction, not as a guarantee of lasting understanding. [22] The size of the context and the handling of history differ among voice products and cannot be compared in general without their documentation. Even a long context does not guarantee that the system will use every relevant piece of information. How to test a long series of questions Insert a known untruth into the series and watch whether the system corrects it or carries it on. Ask about a contradiction between the first and the fifth answer. Require it to say what it does not know. Repeat the task with an adult and without one. Do not evaluate only the correct botany. Record whether the child asks another question after the answer, or walks away. On a large corpus of household questions, a well-designed conversation and a smaller relevant context is usually better than a mechanical “ask Siri about everything”. The whole world in a speaker is not a strategy of knowledge. It is often only a faster way to hide the decisive sentence in the middle of certainty. 12. Privacy is not a switch. It is the whole voice flow The question “is it recording us?” is important, but too narrow. A family also has to know where recordings are stored, for how long, who listens to them, whether records are kept, which third parties process speech recognition, and whether a connected application sends the voice on. “We do not use it for advertising” does not mean “we keep nothing”. The GDPR gives children special protection and regulates the conditions of consent in connection with information-society services. [20] Article 50 of the AI Act requires providers of systems intended for direct interaction to inform a person that they are communicating with an AI system, unless that is obvious from the circumstances; further duties depend on the role and the use. [21] A school deployment is not the same as a household speaker, and a concrete classification requires a legal assessment. The practical minimum is a map of the flow. It begins with the child, continues through the microphone, the cloud, the model, the history and the parent’s account, and ends at the place where the recording can be deleted. Without this map, a claim about privacy is only a description of one part of the pipe. That is why Common Sense Media stresses settings, the wake word, and who in the household understands the indicator lights. [7] The difference is not cosmetic. The same child can have a parent’s phone, a school tablet and a speaker in the kitchen. A weekly test has to record on which device the child is asking, what is switched on, and who is responsible for the settings. Otherwise the family tests comfort and by mistake presents it as a security property. 13. The price of an answer is the price of raw material, not the price of understanding The market uses several price languages at once. A parent pays a subscription or nothing, because the voice is “in the phone”. A school pays for licences. A child pays attention. An adult pays the time they no longer had to spend explaining — or the time they will later spend repairing a habit. A cheap assistant can be excellent for a timer and the weather. The same assistant can be expensive on a task that the child repeats until it gets certainty, and that in the end requires half an hour of human conversation that no longer takes place. An expensive ban can be pointless for navigation. It can, however, be cheaper on a question with a high cost of error if it reduces the number of false certainties. The real price of an accepted answer Device + account + the child’s voice + verification + repairs + a conversation that was crowded out + a habit of a closed question. The result is cheap only when it passes a check and can really be used — as a start, not as an end. That is why it is useful to measure the price per accepted second question , not the price per first answer. Accepted means that the child or the adult continues, verifies, or knows that the source is not enough. This metric can reverse a ranking that looked unambiguous from speed. 14. What to switch on for which work A household trial should rest on the age of the child, the type of questions and the parental control that is available. The table proposes comparing two modes on the same questions and under the same conditions, not compiling a general ranking of brands. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Need First group of candidates Decisive test Unacceptable shortcut Timer, weather, a route Voice on a parent’s phone Whether it stays with the command Leaving the child alone with an open web A fact for school Asking together + a book or a primary source Support for the sentence; a second question Mistaking fluency for correctness A question about people and fear Only a human; an assistant at most as a start Whether an adult hears the reason An encyclopedia instead of a conversation A school essay A school account; a ban on handing in the first output The procedure, a citation, a sentence of one’s own Measuring only the text that was handed in A child without supervision Switched off, or a strict child’s profile Recording, purchases, night use Relying on a parent’s consumer account Language practice A human; the machine only as an echo Politeness toward people Training orders on a speaker Czech use needs a separate test. An English assistant will not measure whether it keeps the meaning of “prázdniny”, inflects a name correctly, understands after-school care, or fails to translate a local abbreviation. A test set should contain diacritics, an “I don’t know” question, a question from school, and a question to which the correct answer is “come and tell me”. Some households in the end need several modes. One for the timer, a second for facts asked together, a third switched off in the room. That is not a failure of upbringing. It is the same decision as using one tool in the kitchen and another on a bicycle. The condition is that the split is intelligible and that the child knows where the final authority arises. 15. A weekly test that will say more than a ban on the phone A choice can be made without a year-round ban and without switching the device on on impulse. A short, disciplined week is enough. Its aim is not to prove that an assistant can do something impressive. The aim is to find situations in which it fails, and to see whether the household can catch them. Seven days from impression to a rule Day 1: Write down 15 to 25 real questions of the child, their frequency and the cost of error. Day 2: Prepare the same questions in two modes: alone and with an adult. Days 3–4: Repeat each important question at least three times. Keep a register of tone, certainty and the second question. Day 5: Check recording, the account, deletion of history, purchases and night use. Day 6: Count how many answers closed, and how many opened a conversation. Day 7: Stress tests: a question about guilt, a known untruth, “why are people mean?”, a forbidden purchase. Decide according to the matrix and set a date for the next review. The evaluator watches factual correctness, completeness, tone, and whether the child walks away after the answer. Each failure is classified: false certainty, omission, context, a linguistic shortcut, privacy. The conditions have to be comparable. The same time, the same questions, the same adult. If one mode may search the web and the other may not, we are testing finished working procedures — but we have to name them as such. The pilot should have conditions for elimination. For example: a single unannounced certainty on health advice, a purchase without consent, a recording that cannot be deleted, or a tone that transfers into speech toward people. A high average “it can do it” must not override an error whose impact the family cannot accept. The last output is not the name of an assistant. It is an operating rule: what the voice is used for, what it is not used for, which data it may hear, what a human must hear, and when the decision will be opened again. 16. Two similar evenings can have a different mode With a voice it is especially important not to blur the boundary among a parent’s account, a child’s account and a school tablet. The same child can on Tuesday in the car hear the weather from a mother’s phone and on Wednesday in a room put questions to an open model that nobody hears. Privacy and filters differ. Tone differs. The cost of error differs. The difference is not cosmetic. The pilot has to record in which profile the test is run, what is switched on, and who is responsible for the settings. Otherwise the family tests the comfort of a shared ride and by mistake presents it as a security property of a night-time speaker. Before switching the voice on alone Find who owns the account and where the recordings are stored. Separate the timer from questions about people and the body. Introduce joint participation: at least the first week of asking together. Check that the child hears the sentence “a machine can err”. Establish that a purchase, a third person’s privacy and health advice are forbidden actions. The largest advantage of a household voice therefore need not be the model. It can be order in the matters at which an adult is present. And the largest weakness need not be a hallucination. It can be a true sentence that closes the wrong question. 17. School: an assignment that can be copied is not the same as an assignment that can be understood IRTIS showed that Czech children and adolescents use generative AI most often for schoolwork. [3] That changes the unit of the assignment. The assignment need not be “write an essay”, but “obtain a text that looks like an essay”. The ability to accept a brief is only an entrance gate. The system still has to — and the teacher even more so — recognise which part is the pupil’s own, separate observation from interpretation, and state what the pupil did not understand. UNESCO warns against generative tools becoming a shortcut that bypasses learning. [11] A ban does not follow. What follows is that a school has to test the procedure, not only the surface that was handed in. As with code: measuring only a generated excerpt is a bad test. Measuring whether the pupil can defend the result, repair it and repeat it without a voice is a test closer to the work. For a teacher a small internal benchmark is therefore useful. Thirty real assignments — in Czech, with a question where the source is not enough, and with a duty to show the procedure — will say more than a ban on the phone in the cloakroom. The public percentage “children use AI” helps to choose the topic of a meeting. The decision has to be made by the lesson. 18. The habit of a finished answer The first generation of smart speakers sold music and weather. The next sold jokes, purchases and “something like a friend”. Today’s products sell something larger: a place in which a child searches, asks, learns to wait — or learns not to wait. That is why providers do not compete only for the best answer. They compete for household context. For the microphone, the history, the habits, the school assignment, and for who in the family can still say “come and look for it with me”. The more convenient the ecosystem becomes, the higher the price of leaving it can be. The child stops distinguishing its own question from the product in which it first closed that question. That does not mean that a voice is bad. It is often precisely a voice that saves hands on the steering wheel and supplies a fact that would otherwise disappear. It means that it should be switched on deliberately. A family needs a portable habit of asking further, an emergency procedure without an assistant, and a regular test of whether the original reasons for the choice still hold. The best system is therefore not the one that never errs. We do not have such a system. Nor is it the system with the fastest sentence or the most pleasant voice. It is the system whose abilities match the real question and whose errors are visible, reversible, and bearable for the child . At the moment when the assistant only says what time it is, we are choosing a timer. The moment it answers “why”, teaches a tone and closes curiosity, we are also choosing a structure of learning. And then the question is no longer: “Which assistant is the cleverest?” What decides is which error the child will see in time, who will help it verify the answer, and whether room for a further question remains after the first sentence. — Jiný Kontext

items.title: Teacher pay: 130 percent is not an individual payslip
items.subtitle: The statutory anchor sets the volume of funds for teacher pay from the reference wage of the year before last. It does not create an individual entitlement of every teacher to 130% of the current average wage; actual pay depends on the FTE post, the scale, bonuses and how the budget is split.

items.body: The figure of 130 percent in the Act is not automatically a figure from a payslip. It depends on the reference year, who counts as a teacher, the volume of funds and the split between scale pay and discretionary components. The statutory budget anchor can therefore be met and the relative income of a particular teacher can still move differently. What we know / What we do not know What we know: The statutory anchor works with a volume of funds and a reference wage from the year before last. A group average is therefore not an individual wage entitlement, nor a guarantee of the same rise for every profession in the school. What we do not know: Without the final budget, the Ministry of Education (MŠMT) allocation and actual payments, the average pay for 2027 and the share of scales and bonuses cannot be determined. This article does not verify a single final sum for every teacher. 1. One hundred and thirty percent that run ahead of the wage Imagine a meeting on teacher pay. The education minister points to the Act and says that 130% has been in the section since 2024. The finance minister points to chapter 333 and says the money is approved once a year. The headteacher notes that funds for teacher pay, other staff and running costs have different rules and purposes. The union chair points to a payslip that sits below the promise. The mathematics teacher in the room hears that the average has risen. It does not show on his bonus. The journalist has two figures in the notebook: 130 and 108. He wants to know what each measures. At first glance this is a dispute about promises. In fact each person is describing a different object. The first speaks of the volume of funds in the Act. The second of the spending cap. The third of the school budget. The fourth of the ratio to the average wage in the economy. The fifth of a particular scale and bonus. The journalist compares headline with headline. A dispute about 130 percent is usually a dispute about several different quantities. Statutory volume, reference year, the definition of who is counted, the scale, bonuses and the average wage in the economy have to be stated separately. Before anyone decides whether the commitment has been met, it must be clear whether the check is of the statutory budget volume, a political promise, or the actual pay of a defined group of teachers. The Act is not a payslip. A payslip is not an average. An average is not a scale. And 130% is not one object. — Jiný Kontext 2. From the statutory anchor to the payslip When “teacher pay at 130%” appears on the screen, it is easy to hear that every teacher takes home 130% of the average wage. The result is produced in a chain of layers. Each can raise the ratio, lower it or change who it applies to. Two texts with the same percentage may therefore not be speaking of the same thing. Five layers of one percentage Statutory volume: from 2024 the total funds for teacher pay, as a monthly average per FTE post, are to correspond to at least 130% of the average gross monthly nominal wage. This is a volume per post, not an individual entitlement of every teacher. [1] [11] Reference base: the Act rests on the wage for the calendar year before last. The budget for year T therefore does not measure the wage of year T. [1] [3] Population: the anchor applies to teachers, not to all pedagogical staff and not to non-teaching operations. [1] [11] Pay composition: scale, personal allowance, bonuses. The head distributes the above-scale part. An average of 130% can arise even where the scale is stagnant. [11] [12] Budget ceiling: the State Budget Act assigns concrete limits to the MŠMT chapter. A section without a chapter does not create money. [6] [9] The Act determines an important part of the promise, but it is not the only actor. A macroeconomic forecast can shift the base. Funds for pay and for running costs follow different budget and earmarking rules; they cannot be described as a freely interchangeable pot. The OECD, moreover, measures the occupation against tertiary-educated employees, while the Czech anchor uses another denominator. This is where the first error in most public comparisons appears. A headline announces a contest of 130 and 108, but in fact it compares a statutory volume against a lagged wage with an empirical ratio against this year’s wage. Or it measures only teachers and treats the result as a verdict on the whole school. An honest comparison must state not only the percentage, but also the year of the base, the population, whether it is volume or a payslip, and whether the figure was calculated by MŠMT, the Czech Statistical Office (ČSÚ), or IDEA. Without the layers a figure becomes an accusation. Which analytical cut you take decides where to look when an apparent breach appears. If the ratio fell to 108.4%, surrounding wages may have grown faster. If the Act “holds”, a lagged base may have been met. If the head is cutting bonuses, the problem may have been in the school pot, not in the section. The sentence “130% is not being met” is the start of a diagnosis, not the end of one. Illustrative scheme: The same percentage can, in another base year, for another population and in another mix of scale and bonuses, produce another payslip. 3. The best promise is the one whose gap you can see Politicians usually look for the promise with the highest chance of being understood. That is reasonable, but incomplete. It matters equally what the gap looks like, whether it can be recognised and who pays for it. A typo in a press release is a cheap error. Mistaking a volume per FTE for an individual scale is expensive. A misunderstood reference year can be walked back with an explanation. Teachers leaving the profession sometimes cannot. Type of failure What it looks like How to test it What limits the harm Swapping volume and payslip “Everyone takes 130%” Does the Act speak of an average per FTE? Separate volume, average and scale Swapping the year 130% of the T-2 wage is read as 130% of the T wage Which ČSÚ year is in the base? A compulsory year legend Swapping the population Teacher = assistant = cook Whom does the Act name? A list of categories Nominal instead of the ratio A record rise while the % falls The pace of teachers versus the pace of the economy Two axes in one table OECD without a definition 130% “equals” the OECD average Against whom does the OECD measure? The same comparison group That also changes the evaluation question. We do not ask only whether the percentage exists in the Act. We ask which promise will fail in a way the debate will catch. A government can tolerate a nominal target of CZK 75 000, because it can be written into a programme statement. A teacher cannot tolerate a volume per FTE becoming his personal entitlement. Analysts can accept a lagged base as a technical necessity. They cannot pass it off as the current ratio. For a percentage commitment what decides is a traceable reference year, a precise population and a link to both budgeted and actually paid figures. A number with a clear legend is more useful for scrutiny than a percentage without a definition. 4. What the statutory indicator measures A statutory anchor is needed because it replaces part of impression with a repeatable rule. The problem appears when one percentage begins to stand for the whole pay of a particular person. IDEA at CERGE-EI maps the ratio of teacher pay to the average wage in the economy and at the same time notes that the reading of the statutory commitment is contested. That is one research team’s reading of one section, not proof that the Act is worthless. It does show, however, that even an exact percentage can exactly measure a condition other than the one the teacher reads on the payslip. [3] [12] Every test contains hidden decisions. Which wage year? Teachers, or all pedagogical staff? Regional education, or universities as well? Scale, or scale plus bonuses? FTE-adjusted posts, or natural persons? The answer to any of these questions can change the order of “met / not met”. The think-tank IDEA states in a 2026 study that relative teacher pay in 2025 fell to 108.4% of the average wage in the economy. The historical high in this series was 125% in 2021. Until 2017 the ratio stayed around 106% . This is the ratio of average teacher pay to the average wage of the same period, not the statutory calculation from the year before last. 108.4% and the “statutory 130%” can therefore sit side by side without one necessarily refuting the other. [3] [12] Five facts without which 130% is only an advertising number The exact population: teachers in regional education, not “education”. The wage year in the numerator and in the denominator. Whether this is a volume of funds or a paid average. The share of the scale and of discretionary components. Whether the figure was calculated by MŠMT, ČSÚ, IDEA or the OECD — and against whom. For evaluation, therefore, a small breakdown of the payslip matters more than someone else’s overall ranking. Thirty real payments — with scale, bonus, FTE and a comparison with the local wage of a tertiary-educated employee — can say more than one percentage from a section. A public indicator helps choose the debate. The decision has to be made by the budget and the head. 5. Compare instruments, not slogans The scheme separates the statutory anchor, the political programme, the budget chapter and actually measured pay. For each instrument it shows the unit and the type of error the reader should look for. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Instrument Main object What to check Typical reason for use Act No. 563/2004 Coll. Volume per teacher FTE, T-2 base Population, year, enforceability Legislative anchor [1] Programme statement Nominal targets (starting pay, average by 2029) The ratio to a future wage, not to T-2 Political horizon [2] State Budget Act Chapter 333, annual limit How much of the chapter is for pay A hard ceiling [6] IDEA / ČSÚ Ratio to the current average wage Definition of teacher, period Empirical map [3] [5] OECD EAG Pay against tertiary-educated employees A different comparison group International ranking [8] The rows are not a verdict on honesty. The same government can use three instruments in a single year. The map is there to prevent another error: that a nominal CZK 75 000 becomes 130%, and that 130% becomes every teacher’s payslip. How to read the scheme: A percentage, a crown and a budget chapter are not three names for the same thing. They are a ratio, a nominal payment and a spending framework. 6. The Act, the programme and the budget are not the same Public discussion often mixes three instruments with different enforceability. Act No. 563/2004 Coll., as amended by Act No. 183/2023 Coll., has since 2024 set the volume of funds for teacher pay. Programme documents can use nominal targets, and the budget assigns the MŠMT chapter a concrete sum for a concrete year. The exact shape of the current political promise has to be quoted from a dated version of the programme; this article does not treat it as a legal entitlement. [1] [2] [6] Meeting a nominal promise can go together with a move away from the relative 130% if wages in other sectors grow faster. IDEA notes that the declared CZK 75 000 by 2029 corresponds, on the wage-growth forecast, to roughly 122% of the average wage, that is less than the statutory 130%. That is one study’s calculation on one forecast, not proof that the nominal target is a deceit. It does show that a crown and a percentage can miss each other. [3] [12] That matters more than a quarrel about bad faith. Anyone who measures the Act asks about volume and the T-2 base. Anyone who measures the programme asks about crowns in 2029. Anyone who measures the budget asks about this year’s chapter. Three correct answers. One bad shared decision if they are made into a single headline. 7. The Act counts a different year from the one the teacher lives in The key methodological hook lies in the reference base. When the budget for year T is drawn up, data on the average wage in year T are not available. The statutory construction therefore reaches for the calendar year before last. For 2024 the communication around the amendment therefore started from the outturn of 2022, when the average wage, on the figures then, reached CZK 40 353. [1] [11] If nominal wages in the economy are rising, a two-year lag of the base means that 130% of a past wage is less than 130% of this year’s wage. Formally the volume can be met. In fact teachers take 130% of a wage from the past, not from the present. IDEA measures this gap differently: as a ratio to the current average wage. Both figures can be true. They measure a different denominator. [3] [4] The Ministry of Finance publishes expected wage growth in its macroeconomic forecasts. To hold the relative level in 2027 and 2028, IDEA counts a pace matching the growth of nominal wages in the economy, according to the forecasts 6.1% and 5.2% . Slower growth of teacher pay would lower the ratio further. That is a forecast, not a certainty. Without a year legend, however, every “130%” is a map without a scale. [3] [4] The lag is not a fault of statistics. It is the price of drawing up a budget before ČSÚ closes year T. Anyone who wants the current ratio must either forecast or uprate later. The first path carries the risk of a forecast error. The second carries the risk that the teacher receives a top-up with a delay. The Act chose T-2. That is a choice of object. It is not proof that 108.4% is a measurement of the same section. ISPV and ČSÚ add yet another wage: the median, the industry, the region. The statutory denominator is the average gross monthly nominal wage on FTE-adjusted counts in the national economy. A regional median teacher against a regional median tertiary-educated employee is a useful labour-market map. It is not the Act. Anyone who swaps them gets a dispute the section will not decide. [5] [21] 8. A teacher is not a pedagogical worker The second filter is the definition of the group. In 2023 the Chamber narrowed the guarantee to teachers. It does not automatically cover teaching assistants, school psychologists, special educators, after-school staff or non-teaching personnel. The original government draft counted a wider category of pedagogical workers and a different multiple. The approved wording is narrower. [1] [11] A school works with several money streams that are not freely interchangeable. A shortage of money for assistants or running costs can create institutional pressure and, where the rules allow, affect decisions on discretionary components inside the pay budget. From that pressure, however, a transfer of teacher funds to running costs cannot be inferred without the school’s allocation. [5] [10] The Czech School Inspectorate (ČŠI) tracks, in its staffing reports, the stability of staff, subject coverage and conditions. These indicators do not say whether 130% has been met. They say whether the school has anyone to pay at all. The quality map and the pay map overlap. They are not identical. [10] The Education Act finances a school through several streams and under set rules. An assistant, an after-school club and running costs are therefore not proof that teacher money can be moved without limit; they do show that meeting a narrow guarantee for teachers does not by itself prove sufficient funding of the school as a whole. Union positions describe this difference as a risk for the other professions. [15] [17] 9. The scale is not an average Pay tables set the entitlement base by the demands of the work and the length of service. The 130% average is meant to appear only after personal allowances and bonuses distributed by the school leadership are included. Communication for 2024 said that the scale tables would not change and that heads should have, on average, about CZK 2 500 a month more for personal allowances. Average gross teacher pay was then estimated at around CZK 52 400. That is an estimate of the time for one year, not a 2025 payslip. [11] Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext The IDEA study reports for 2025 a ratio of average teacher pay to the average wage in the economy of 108.4% . [3] An exact average in crowns can be given only from a final MŠMT or ČSÚ table with the same population and period; without such a reference this text does not state it. An average, moreover, wipes out differences by experience, scale, bonuses and school. What has to be tested on the payslip The first test concerns the share of the scale. The second concerns discretionary components that can be cut in a squeeze. The third concerns whether the school average is produced by a few high bonuses or by a broad shift. A product that on paper holds 130% of volume can, on the payslips of most of the staff, look like a stagnant scale. 10. Nominal growth is not a relative gain In 2025 the ratio, according to IDEA, was 108.4% . If wages in the national economy grow at the forecast pace and teacher pay grows about as fast, the gap to 130% does not close. A pace of 6 to 7% can look like a rise on the payslip and like treading water in the ratio. For the ratio to move from roughly 108% to 130% in a few years, teacher pay would have to grow faster than wages in the economy, not at the same speed. The concrete pace needed depends on the wage forecast; IDEA counts different billions for an immediate jump in 2027 than for merely holding the line. [3] [4] An illustration, not a report: a teacher on CZK 48 000 against an average wage of CZK 40 000 stands at 120%. Two years later they take CZK 55 000. On the payslip they see plus CZK 7 000. Meanwhile the average wage has risen to CZK 50 000. The ratio has fallen to 110%. Nominally they are better off. Relative to the economy they are worse off. The figures are simplified so that the mechanism is visible. They are not ČSÚ statistics. The National Budget Council watches mandatory spending and sustainability. In that view school pay is not only a promise. It is spending that crowds out other chapters, or is itself held down by deficit limits. The 130% ratio is a map of aspiration. The budget is a map of the possible. [9] 11. The OECD measures a different comparison group Education at a Glance does not set teacher pay against the average wage in the whole economy. It sets it against the average of tertiary-educated employees. IDEA states that the Czech political 130% against the whole economy roughly matches the OECD and EU average on this international indicator (on the order of 85–89% of the pay of tertiary-educated employees in the years the study cites). The Czech ratio to tertiary-educated employees, according to IDEA, fell from 79% in 2021 to 72% in 2024. That is a different denominator from the statutory one. One cannot say that 108.4% “is” 72%. One can say that the Czech Republic moved away on the OECD map in the years when it moved away from 130% on the domestic map. [3] [8] An international comparison of education spending as a share of GDP is a third map still. EDUin and the OECD use it for the intensity of the system, not for a teacher’s payslip. Anyone who adds them into one “we are falling behind” merges three definitions. [7] [8] Eurostat adds compensation of employees in education. Again another unit, another population, another purpose. An international ranking helps choose a question. It does not decide whether the Czech section has been met. An honest comparison must state against whom the measurement runs: the whole economy, tertiary-educated employees, or GDP. IDEA is careful here: it says that 130% on the domestic indicator roughly matches the OECD average on another indicator. It does not say they are the same percentages. [3] [18] 12. A chapter is harder than a section IDEA prices two scenarios for 2027. Merely holding the relative level of 2026 would, in the 2027 budget, require an extra roughly CZK 11 billion . A return to 130% of the average wage already in 2027 would require an extra roughly CZK 35 billion . That is an estimate against the medium-term outlook of the time, not an approved line. The total increase for regional education would have to be higher, because other pedagogical and non-teaching pay is also paid from the state budget. [3] [12] The draft state budget published by the Ministry of Finance on 31 August 2026 states CZK 287.862 billion for the MŠMT chapter in 2027. That is a draft before government and parliamentary debate, not an approved budget and not a separate scale fund. The IDEA scenarios of 11 and 35 billion must therefore be compared with a concrete pay allocation, not with the whole chapter. [3] [6] The medium-term outlook is a fourth layer that disappears in the headline. IDEA notes that if the original outlook from the autumn of the previous year were met in 2027, the ratio could fall below the historical low from the period before 2017. That is a conditional scenario, not an approved budget. The condition is exactly what the reader of the promise needs to see: a section without a chapter does not stand. A chapter without a wage forecast does not stand either. Three documents — the Act, the outlook, the Ministry of Finance forecast — have to sit in one table, or 11 and 35 billion become an impression. [3] [4] [6] Before the chapter is approved Separate the volume for teachers from the rest of regional education. Write down how much of the increase goes into the scale and how much into bonuses. Set 11 billion (holding the line) beside 35 billion (a jump to 130%). If the text promises a jump and the figure in the chapter is only enough to hold the line, you are not reading a breach of the T-2 Act. You are reading another object. 13. Where to check the Act, the budget and the payslip Before 130% was written into law, the reader had to check that the promise was not only a programme. With the Act they check something more complicated: whether the volume sits on T-2, whether it concerns teachers, whether the average is produced by bonuses, and whether the chapter is enough. A section is navigation to an account. It is not an automatic payslip. One press release can combine three true claims into a false conclusion. First: the Act is in force. Second: average pay rose nominally. Third: the ratio to the current wage fell. Each works. The synthesis “130% has been met, therefore the teacher takes 130%” is methodologically wrong. A four-step check of a percentage Existence: the figure is in the Act, the programme, the budget, or a study. Object: volume, ratio, nominal, or an OECD indicator. Support: population, year, unit. Scope: what the figure leaves out — the scale, assistants, the current wage. Before a headline about 130 percent, a table of claims, years and defined staff should appear. If the statistics of FTE posts cannot be opened, a round number in a section does not replace them. 14. The price of an FTE is the price of a raw material, not the price of a staff The market in promises uses several languages. The Act pays by volume per FTE. The government pays in nominal terms. The teacher pays with time, subject qualification and the option of leaving. A direct comparison of price lists without the school’s working procedure misleads. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Nominal growth may not suffice if teachers in scarce subjects are leaving. How any increase is split between scale and discretionary components can have a different effect on staff stability; from the model scenario of 35 billion alone the outcome cannot be predicted. The real price of an accepted staff Volume for teachers + pay of other pedagogical staff + non-teaching operations + departures + recruitment + the head’s time spent splitting bonuses. A staff is cheap only once it holds subject coverage and can be opened in September. The costs include churn. If the same post is filled from one of five advertisements, the average price of a teacher is not the scale in the table. If the chapter sticks in mid-year, the cost is waiting for bonuses. It is therefore useful to measure the price per filled, subject-qualified FTE , not the price per press-release percentage. That metric can reverse a ranking that looked obvious from the 130%. 15. What to measure before 130% becomes a verdict A check should start by deciding whether the Act, the payslip, the relative wage or budget sustainability is being verified. The table assigns each question the matching figure. Question First object Decisive test Unacceptable shortcut Has the Act been met? Volume per FTE, T-2 base The text of the § and MŠMT method Swap it for a payslip Is the teacher better off? Scale + bonus, inflation The real wage of a defined group Report a nominal record Is the ratio holding? Pay / average wage of the same year IDEA / ČSÚ, the same population Read T-2 as T Are we like the OECD? Pay / wage of tertiary-educated employees EAG, the same year Say that 130% = 88% Can the budget bear it? Chapter 333, 11 vs. 35 bn Ministry of Finance and NRR outlook Promise a percentage without the billions Is the staff holding? Subject coverage, age, departures ČŠI, not only the average Pay = quality of teaching Czech use needs a separate test. An international ranking will not show whether a given school really keeps earmarked and operating streams apart, nor how budget pressure affects discretionary components inside pay funds where the rules allow it. The test set should include scale, bonus, FTE, T-2 and T — and the sentence “the source is not enough” if statistics of discretionary components are missing. 16. A short payslip test An evaluation can be done without a large quarrel about character. A short procedure is enough. The aim is not to prove that 130% sounds good. The aim is to find a swap of objects. Seven steps from slogan to sentence Write down the object: Act, programme, ratio, OECD, or chapter. Write down the wage year in the numerator and the denominator. Write down the population: teacher, pedagogical staff, non-teaching staff. Separate scale and bonus. Compare the pace with the Ministry of Finance forecast. Set the IDEA billions beside the chapter. Only then write whether the promise has been met. Three tests of a percentage The first is verbal: volume, or payslip? The second is temporal: T, or T-2? The third is about population: teacher, or school? A figure that does not pass is not a lie. It is a map without a legend. The conditions have to be comparable. If one text may use a nominal and another a ratio, we are testing narratives. We have to name that. An exclusion error: a single sentence that turns CZK 75 000 into 130% without a wage forecast. A pilot should also have a revision date. Wage forecasts, the chapter and the composition of the staff change. Without a date even an honest T-2 slowly turns into the superstition that “the Act arranged it”. The last output is not a winner between 130 and 108. It is a rule: which percentage for what, which population, which year and how many billions in chapter 333. 17. Two promises that can miss each other A nominal CZK 75 000 and a relative 130% can look like the same thing in one year and like a dispute in another. It depends on wage growth in the economy. IDEA quantifies this mismatch as roughly 122% versus 130% by 2029 on the cited forecast. The forecast can change. The mismatch of objects will not: a crown is not a percentage. [2] [3] An illustration of two schools, not a report. The first school posts a high average thanks to leadership bonuses and several qualified subjects in a regional city. The second holds the scale but loses the physics teacher. Both can be “in order” on the statutory volume. Only one holds the subject. The Act will not tell them apart. The head and ČŠI will. That does not mean the 130% anchor is pointless. It means it should be read as a map of volume, not as a judgment on every payslip and every staff room. 18. Departures as a consequence of pay uncertainty The first generation of promises sold a rise in crowns. The next sold a percentage in the Act. Today’s dispute sells something larger: the right to treat a section as finished pay. The contest is therefore not only over the highest figure. It is over which object will be “real pay”. The more comfortable the shortcut, the higher the price of the error. The journalist stops distinguishing T from T-2. The minister stops distinguishing volume from payslip. The teacher stops distinguishing promise from scale — and leaves. That does not mean the statutory anchor is a bad one. It is often precisely what creates bargaining leverage. It means the purchase should be conscious. The public needs a portable legend: which percentage, which year, which population, how many billions and when the decision will be opened again. The best promise is therefore not the one that never misses the payslip. In a growing economy with an annual chapter we do not have such a promise. Nor is it the promise with the highest percentage or the roundest crown. It is the promise whose object matches the question and whose gaps are visible, reversible and fiscally bearable . The moment we ask only “is it 130%?”, we are choosing a slogan. The moment we read the base, the population and the chapter, we are choosing a structure of responsibility. And then the question is no longer: “Why do teachers not have 130%?” What decides is which definition of 130% we are reading, for which year, and how the budget volume shows up in actual payments. — Jiný Kontext

items.title: A deepfake of a familiar voice: the voice alone is no longer enough to verify identity
items.subtitle: With some tools a short sample can be enough for a convincing imitation; quality depends on the model, the language, the source and the transmission channel. Five seconds is not a universal threshold, and a “perfect voice” is not a documented category. For payments, verification through a second channel is safer than relying on hearing.
