items.body: The proposed deficit of CZK 389 billion sits below the psychological line of four hundred billion, but CZK 79 billion above the approved plan for 2026. The cash deficit, the general-government balance and the structural balance are different indicators. Meeting one European threshold does not by itself prove that nominal debt, or the cost of servicing it, is falling. At 11:00 on 31 August 2026 the Ministry of Finance published the draft state budget for 2027 . It reports revenue of CZK 2 189.1738 billion, expenditure of CZK 2 578.1738 billion and a deficit of CZK 389 billion. Act No. 38/2026 Coll. approved a deficit of CZK 310 billion for 2026, so the proposal assumes a year-on-year increase of CZK 79 billion. The ministry has submitted the document to the government; the figure may change in government and parliamentary debate. How is a budget narrative produced, what do four different deficits measure, and what happens to the spending framework when defence becomes an exception? What we know / What we don't know What we know: The Ministry of Finance proposal of 31 August 2026 works with a deficit of CZK 389 billion, revenue of CZK 2 189.1738 billion and expenditure of CZK 2 578.1738 billion. Against the approved deficit for 2026, the proposal is CZK 79 billion higher. What we don't know: We do not know the final shape after government and parliamentary debate, nor the actual outturn for 2027. The ministry’s claims about growth, savings or the effect of spending are assumptions in the proposal, not a measured result. 1. A ceiling under which the direction can still deepen Imagine the meeting after the 2027 budget proposal is published. The finance minister puts a deficit of CZK 389 billion on the table. The chair of the National Budget Council points to the fiscal-responsibility rules. The defence minister recalls the statutory share of two percent of GDP and the European defence clause. The coalition talks about investment, the opposition about stalled consolidation. The journalist has, side by side, the crisis year 2021, the approved plan for 2026 and the proposal for 2027. What can actually be compared? At first glance this is an argument about discipline. In fact each person is describing a different object. The first is talking about a psychological threshold below which the deficit still “fits”. The second, about the structural balance and the spending framework. The third, about the defence chapter and NATO methodology. The fourth, about visible spending. The fifth, about the year-on-year direction. The journalist is comparing one headline with another. The same proposal can meet one threshold and worsen another indicator. The phrase “responsible deficit” therefore needs a legend: the cash balance of the state budget, the general-government balance, the structural balance, the statutory spending framework and the cost of servicing the debt. So the first distinction that matters is not who is cheating. It is which column is being read . Otherwise we set the treasury, Maastricht, the cycle, an exemption and interest next to one another and are surprised that each figure wins a different contest. A ceiling is not a direction. It is a choice of reference point. Below four hundred billion can be true — and a deepening at the same time. — Jiný Kontext A deficit is a remainder, not a grade An illustrative path from revenue and spending to the spending frame and debt service. A deficit is a remainder, not a grade Revenue Spending Deficit Frame Interest JINÝ KONTEXT Illustrative diagram: The chain shows accounting layers; it is not a moral score or a breakdown of a specific budget act. 2. Five different pictures of the budget balance When “deficit” appears in a headline, it is easy to imagine a single invoice from the state. The result is produced in a chain. Each layer can raise the amount, lower it, or merely move it out of sight. Two sentences about the same year therefore need not be a quarrel. They can be two views of the same chain. Five layers of one deficit State-budget cash deficit: the difference between revenue and expenditure of the state treasury, in koruna. Act No. 38/2026 Coll. set it at 310 billion koruna for 2026, with revenue of 2 117.8 billion and expenditure of 2 427.8 billion. [1] It measures the flow in one chapter of the state. It does not measure regions, municipalities or health insurers. General-government balance: ESA 2010, the notification to the European Commission, the ratio to GDP. It includes the wider public sector. It can differ from the cash deficit by accruals, capital injections and units outside the state budget. [12] Structural balance: the deficit adjusted for the cycle and one-off measures. On the 2026 proposal the National Budget Council reported the Ministry of Finance estimate of 2.2% of GDP and its own estimate of up to 2.5% of GDP. Both figures exceeded the legal limit then in force for that year. This is an estimate, not a cash balance. [4] Statutory spending framework: the ceiling under Act No. 23/2017 Coll. and its amendments. It says how much spending counts toward the limit. It does not say how much the state will actually spend if part of the spending drops out of the cap. [3] [4] Financing need and debt service: how much must be borrowed and how much the interest costs. After the 2026 budget act took effect, the ministry put the total financing need at 737.8 billion koruna, about 8.2% of GDP. That is not the same thing as a deficit of 310 billion. It also includes repayments of old debt. [9] The basic treasury sets an important part of the debate, but it is not the only actor. A government can formally keep the EU ratio to GDP and still raise nominal borrowing. It can show compliance with the framework because the content of the framework has changed. It can talk about investment while the item that builds nothing grows fastest: interest. Public debate often compares figures from different accounting layers. Every comparison must therefore state the year, distinguish a proposal from an approved plan and from outturn, separate the cash balance from ESA, and explain the effect of the defence exemption. The proposal raises the cash deficit from the planned 310 billion in 2026 to 389 billion in 2027. At the same time the ministry reports the sector balance, after the European defence clause, at −2.8% of GDP. Both figures can be true, because they measure different objects; neither by itself proves the “responsibility” of the budget. Illustrative diagram: The same year can, in another layer, with another anchor and another exemption, produce another story. 3. The best deficit is the one whose error you can afford The lowest number in a headline is not, by itself, the safest budget. The type of error, how easy it is to spot, and the cost of correcting it all have to be named. A badly rounded headline can be fixed quickly; a badly chosen reference base can hide a year-on-year deterioration. A debt-service trajectory and a legally anchored exemption are also harder to change than a single press sentence. Risk does not rise only with the size of the deficit. The proposed 389 billion is a documented figure, but it does not by itself answer the question of the structural balance, of financing, or of future debt service. Type of failure What it looks like How to test it What limits the harm Anchor error The same amount read as consolidation and as expansion Ask: against which year, plan, or outturn? A mandatory year-on-year plan–plan and outturn–outturn table Layer error Cash is passed off as Maastricht, and the reverse Separate the state budget (SR), ESA, the structural balance and the framework One sentence with every figure: what it measures, what it does not Exemption error Compliance with a limit after an item is taken out Calculate the deficit with the exemption and without it A visible column “taken out of the framework” Duration error A one-off outlay that becomes a trajectory Ask whether the exemption ends or is extended An end date for the clause and a plan after it That also changes the reader’s question. We are not asking only which number is lower. We are asking which error in our reading we will catch. A voter can tolerate ten arguments about billions, because one direction is easy to see. A state accountant cannot tolerate a single hidden change in what counts toward the limit. An economist can accept a higher deficit if it is cyclical and temporary. An economist cannot accept it if it is structural and masked by an anchor from the covid year. Beside the nominal ceiling it is necessary to watch whether the layers can be traced, how easily an outlay can be reversed, and what it will do to debt service. A clearly broken-down proposal may be more readable for scrutiny than a lower number without explanation. 4. What the deficit alone does not explain A public balance is needed because it replaces part of impression with a repeatable series of numbers. The problem begins when one figure starts to stand for the whole of fiscal policy. The Ministry of Finance, the Czech Statistical Office and the National Budget Council measure different objects. None of them measures “responsibility”. That is a judgment, not an indicator. [4] [12] Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Every figure contains hidden decisions. Is it a plan, or outturn? The state budget, or general government? With EU projects, or without them? With defence spending above two percent of GDP, or without it? In which year’s prices, and in which GDP estimate? The answer to any of these questions can change the tone. Five facts without which a deficit is only an advertising number The exact unit: SR cash, ESA, the structural balance, or the framework. The period and status: a proposal, an approved act, a cash outturn, a notification. The population: central government, or the whole of general government. What is taken out: EU funds, defence, one-off operations. The known limit of the indicator: the cycle estimate, a GDP revision, NATO methodology versus ESA. For buying political calm, therefore, a small internal table matters more than someone else’s overall ranking of the “worst deficit in history”. Eight real rows — with real chapters, Czech koruna, approved exemptions and actual debt service — can say more than a thousand comparisons with a year that will not be repeated. A public ceiling helps choose candidates for the headline. The decision has to be made by work with the layers. That is not proof that ceilings are worthless. The point is that even an exact percentage can measure a defective condition exactly. Act No. 38/2026 Coll. sets 310 billion exactly. It does not say whether 310 billion is consolidation. It says what flow of the state treasury parliament approved for one year. [1] One word, several balances Cash, the government sector, the cycle and an exception answer different questions. One word, several balances Cash ESA Cycle Exception Balance JINÝ KONTEXT Interpretive diagram: Elements express neither a share nor a score; they show that a deficit is not a single state invoice. 5. Compare accounts, not headlines The table ranks fiscal statements by the account they come from: the treasury, ESA, the structural balance, the spending framework or the debt. For each it shows the context and the swap that has to be caught in the reading. Account Main working position What to check in the proposal Typical reason for the choice SR cash deficit Headlines, the Chamber, cash outturn Plan versus outturn, EU adjustment One intelligible figure in koruna SVI / ESA balance Notification, Maastricht, Eurostat Units outside the SR, accruals Comparison with three percent of GDP Structural balance Medium-term plan, NRR Output-gap estimate, one-off items Direction after adjustment for the cycle Spending framework Act No. 23/2017 Coll. What is inside the limit and what has dropped out Compliance with the national rule Debt service Chapter 396 Year-on-year growth of interest, maturity The price of past deficits in the present Defence exemption NEC, national amendment Volume taken out of the framework, end date Compliance with a limit after the limit has changed The rows are not a verdict on the quality of a government. The same cabinet offers several figures in one workbook, and each of them can change by amendment within a few months. The map is meant to prevent a different error: that the public buys an excellent ceiling in an account that cannot see its question, cannot finish it safely, or locks it into an exemption that is later hard to leave. How to read the diagram: The position or size of the elements does not express a score. The diagram separates the cash balance, the European indicators, the spending framework and debt service. 6. A cash deficit is not a sector balance The domestic debate lives off the treasury. The state-budget act is intelligible: revenue, expenditure, deficit, debt cover. Act No. 38/2026 Coll. covers a deficit of 310 billion koruna and an increase in the balances of state financial-asset accounts by a change in the stock of state debt of 313.6 billion koruna. That is the flow of one accounting unit in one calendar year. [1] The European debate lives off ESA 2010. The general-government balance includes the state budget, but also local government, health insurers and other units classified as government. Accrual accounting can move an outlay into a different year from the one in which it left the treasury. A capital injection can look like expenditure in one methodology and like a financial operation in another. [12] [15] When a government official argues that the deficit complies with EU rules, the official may be telling the truth about the SVI balance. That does nothing to refute the fact that the central government’s cash debt is rising in nominal terms. Nor the reverse: a deep cash deficit need not automatically mean a breach of the Maastricht ratio if GDP in the denominator is growing, or if part of the flow is not ESA expenditure. What has to be tested The first test concerns the unit. The same year in the treasury and in the notification is not the same experiment. The second concerns the adjustment: for 2025 the Ministry of Finance reported a cash deficit of 290.7 billion koruna and, after adjustment for EU projects and financial mechanisms, 249.9 billion. Both figures are true. They measure a different object. The first rose by 19.3 billion year on year against 2024. The second fell by 38.9 billion year on year. Whoever picks only one picks a story. [2] The third test concerns plan versus outturn. The 2025 deficit exceeded the approved plan of 241 billion by 49.7 billion koruna. The figure 290.7 is therefore not evidence that “the plan is holding”. It is evidence that the treasury ended somewhere other than the act. That does not diminish the importance of the outturn. It reduces the right to claim that the approved balance is the same object as the balance achieved. [2] [19] For a reader who wants one sentence, cash may be decisive. For a reader who wants a European comparison, the sentence “we have 310 billion” is not enough. That reader needs ESA, the GDP estimate, the exemption, and whether the figure is a proposal or a notification. 7. History measures a different question from a plan The path of the state-budget cash balance in recent years shows the band in which the Czech treasury is moving. It is not the pre-covid band of tens of billions. It is a band of hundreds. Year SR balance Type of figure What the number measures — and what it does not 2019 −28.5 bn CZK Outturn A pre-pandemic year. It does not measure today’s debt service or the defence commitment. 2020 −367.4 bn CZK Outturn The first pandemic year. A one-off shock, not a new “normal” written into law. 2021 −419.7 bn CZK Outturn The historical peak of the SR cash deficit. A poor anchor for a year without a lockdown. 2022 −360.4 bn CZK Outturn The energy crisis and the war. It measures a crisis flow, not a structural target. 2023 −288.5 bn CZK Outturn The start of the consolidation package. Still hundreds, not tens. 2024 −271.4 bn CZK Outturn The fifth-deepest deficit since the Czech Republic was founded; the best since the pandemic. Both sentences can be true. [18] 2025 −290.7 bn CZK Outturn A year-on-year worsening of 19.3 bn against 2024; 49.7 bn above the plan of 241 bn. [2] 2026 −310.0 bn CZK Approved plan Act No. 38/2026 Coll. Not outturn. Not ESA. [1] 2027 −389.0 bn CZK MoF proposal of 31. 8. 2026 Submitted to the government; neither an approved act nor outturn. Year-on-year +79 bn against the 2026 plan. [22] The table shows that deficits around 270 to 310 billion koruna have become the operating band of the Czech state, not an exceptional crisis episode. That is not proof that “everyone is stealing”. It is a description of the level at which the debate now moves. Whoever takes 2021 as the anchor gets a story of reassurance. Whoever takes 2019 gets a story of a break. Whoever takes the approved plan for 2026 gets the year-on-year direction. The data are identical. The tone depends on which row you put in the foreground. The figure of 419.7 billion for 2021 measures the cash result of a crisis year. It does not say whether a proposal of 389 billion in 2027 is consolidation. The relevant plan comparison shows an increase against the approved 310 billion for 2026; the actual results of both years will be known only after they have ended. A ceiling is not a direction The headline threshold and the year-on-year movement belong to different readings of the same draft. A ceiling is not a direction Ceiling Direction Threshold Headline Plan Interest Remainder JINÝ KONTEXT Interpretive diagram: The sides are not a moral grade; they separate a psychological ceiling from the direction of the balance. 8. An escape clause does not change the spending. It changes its visibility Spending on a tank, a radar or ammunition is spending whether or not it counts toward the national limit. An escape clause does not change the physical delivery. It changes which part of the account appears in the rule. At European level the defence escape clause allows a temporary deviation from the net-expenditure path. In the 2027 proposal the Ministry of Finance says it is not using the domestic backup escape clause, but in the European assessment it applies COFOG defence spending of CZK 70 billion: after that is taken into account it reports a balance of −2.8% of GDP, without it −3.5% of GDP. [7] [8] [22] The spending does not disappear from the cash budget; the clause changes the compliance assessment, while the effect on financing depends on the whole budget. The National Budget Council said in 2025 that the European Commission’s illustrative projections, which assume linear use of the full flexibility through 2028, point to a deficit in 2028 up to 1.3% of GDP higher than if net expenditure had grown along the original path. The Council also stressed that the European clause does not by itself repeal the national fiscal-responsibility act. It is a Council recommendation on the EU framework. It is not an automatic breach of the debt brake. [5] [4] Three tests of an escape clause The first is legal: which norm is being cited — Regulation 2024/1263, a Council recommendation, or Act No. 23/2017 Coll.? The second is about volume: how many billions are taken out, in which year and against which GDP forecast? The third is about time: does the flexibility end in 2028, or is the national exemption stretched further? A product that “meets the rule” a minute earlier need not be better if, a year later, no one can tell what still counted toward the rule. In a security situation the clause may be strategically justified. It allows higher defence spending without the same consequence in the assessment of a chosen European rule; by itself it does not prove the cause of the whole cash deficit, nor the economic return on the spending. 9. Defence: the exception that became architecture Since 2023 the Czech Republic has had Act No. 177/2023 Coll., which requires the government, in the draft state budget, to set defence spending at least at 2% of nominal GDP according to the forecast in the budget strategy. That is not a promise from a press conference. It is a statutory share. It is calculated from the forecast, not from later revised GDP. Final recognition in NATO methodology arrives with a lag and may differ from the sum of the Ministry of Defence chapter. [13] Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext The executive summary of the 2026 state budget puts total defence spending in all chapters at 184.6 billion koruna. On the January macroeconomic forecast that was 2.06% of GDP, on the April forecast 2.1% of GDP. Year on year these outlays in all chapters rise by 23.9 billion. The figure of 184.6 billion is therefore not “the MoD chapter”. It is the sum of the items that count toward defence. The defence chapter itself is lower. Whoever swaps them manufactures an argument about tens of billions that is an argument about definitions. [11] At national level the law allows certain defence spending to be treated outside the ordinary path of the spending frameworks. [3] [5] The exact scope and duration have to be read in the current wording of the act and in the proposal tables; this article, without a further primary source, does not set a horizon into the thirties. The spending remains spending; what changes is its treatment in the rule. That is an important distinction. Defence investment can be legitimate and strategically necessary. At the same time it can worsen the cash deficit and debt service. Both sentences can be true. Whoever infers from the first that the second is slander is mixing a security aim with a fiscal layer. Whoever infers from the second that the first is unnecessary is mixing an account with a threat. Before reading the defence chapter, therefore, “how much does it cost” is not enough. It is necessary to know whether the figure is 2% or a band above it, whether it is calculated from the January or the April GDP forecast, whether NATO will recognise the same items, and whether the amount fits the framework only because the framework dropped the amount. 10. A law adapted to the budget. Not the other way around On the draft state budget for 2026 the National Budget Council said that the binding deficit limit under the fiscal-responsibility rules act is 246 billion koruna and that the proposal with a deficit of 310 billion exceeds that ceiling by 64 billion. According to the Council this was the first case, for as long as the act has been in force, in which the government proposal itself was ex ante in explicit conflict with the maximum statutory limits. The Ministry of Finance rejected the mismatch by pointing to the European escape clause and the precedence of EU law in application. That is a dispute about the hierarchy of norms. It is not a dispute about whether 310 is larger than 246. [4] In its opinion on public finances in 2025 the Council also warned that the present setting of tax and spending policies does not secure the consolidation path after 2026, and that in an unchanged-policy scenario the structural deficit will already in 2027 be higher than the act assumes — even after additional defence spending with the exemption is subtracted. That is one institution’s projection, not the cash result for 2027. It does, however, say something that a ceiling of “under 400” does not: the direction after the election year is not automatically a continuation of consolidation. [5] By shifting spending frameworks and creating exemptions, the political representation makes legal room so that it need not proceed to further cuts or tax changes. That is not necessarily a breach of the law in the criminal sense. The point is that the law can adapt to the government’s budgetary needs, not only the budget to the law . That is legitimate work for parliament. It is also why the sentence “we kept the rules” requires a question: which rules, in which wording, after which amendment. As of 31 August 2026 there is an official Ministry of Finance proposal with a deficit of CZK 389 billion. [22] It is not an independent audit, an approved act or an accounting fact. On compliance with national rules and on the consolidation direction it is therefore necessary to read, beside the proposal, the current NRR opinions and the later changes in debate. 11. How to check a claim about the deficit After the proposal was published, 389 billion is no longer a mere political corridor. The reader has to check that it is a proposal submitted to the government, not an act or an outturn, and whether the claim uses the cash deficit, the sector balance or a structural indicator. One press conference can join three true figures into a false conclusion: the outturn of 419.7 billion in 2021, the approved plan of 310 billion in 2026 and the proposal of 389 billion in 2027. The synthesis “we are consolidating because we are under four hundred” does not stand as a year-on-year plan comparison; against 2026 the proposal deepens by 79 billion. A four-step check of a budget statement Existence: the figure is in an act, in the cash outturn, or only in a sentence. Authority: the source is primary for that layer — the Ministry of Finance, the Czech Statistical Office, the NRR, Eurostat. Support: a specific passage actually supports the specific sentence about direction. Scope: the year, the unit, the adjustment, the exemption and whether it is a plan all fit. The most reliable working method therefore separates searching from writing. First a table of claims, primary sources and limits is built. Only then the headline. For every figure, the population, the period, the indicator measured and the uncertainty are recorded. If the source cannot be opened or the passage cannot be found, a claim is not promoted to a fact merely because it is worded calmly. A budget statement is good when it shortens the path to a check, not when it replaces the check. For a low-risk question a quick sentence about the ceiling may suffice. For an act that will bind borrowing for the next year, the last step has to be taken by a person who understands the layer. 12. Debt service is not a one-off item Chapter 396 – State Debt, under Act No. 218/2000 Coll., gathers the revenue and expenditure tied to managing the liquidity of the state treasury and managing the state debt. The administrator is the Ministry of Finance. It is mostly interest on government bonds and loans taken, not an “accounting operation” that could be postponed without a price. [10] [14] The executive summary of the 2026 budget puts spending on servicing the state debt at 110.0 billion koruna, 10.0 billion more year on year. The figure measures budgeted interest and related spending, not the principal or the future rate on refinancing. Debt service is a contractually and market-wise hard-to-postpone flow, but not a category that can, without qualification, be labelled a “mandatory expenditure” in the same sense as statutory benefits. [11] By the end of 2025, according to the finance minister’s public figure, state debt had risen to 3.678 trillion koruna. That is a stock, not a deficit. The 2025 deficit of 290.7 billion is a flow that feeds into the stock, but is not identical with it. Whoever adds them into one sentence about a “four trillion deficit” is mixing a stock and a flow. [19] [2] The illustration is simple. Each further year with a deficit around 300 billion koruna adds principal that will have to be rolled over later. Even if the next deficit returned to zero, the interest on the principal already there would not disappear. A ceiling of “under 400” can therefore be true in 2027 and still leave in chapter 396 a bill that will be visible in 2030. That is not a forecast of rates. It is the mechanics of a bond. 13. The price of the raw material is not the price of the result The market uses several fiscal languages at once. Politics pays with a visible ceiling. The treasury pays with a cash flow. The market pays with the bond yield. The European Commission pays with a net-expenditure path. A direct comparison of price lists without knowing the layer therefore misleads. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext A cheap deficit in a headline can be economically excellent if it is cyclical, temporary and covered by growth. The same figure can be expensive if it repeats, if defence has dropped out of the framework, and if chapter 396 is growing by ten billion a year. An expensive deficit in a covid year can be useless as an anchor for 2027. It can still be useful as a warning of how far the treasury can go. The real price of an adopted budget Cash deficit + spending taken out + interest + refinancing + the price of postponing consolidation + dependence on the exemption. The result can be judged only once the treasury deficit, the ESA balance and debt service have been explained against one another. The same number cannot be demanded: each metric has a different definition. The cost also includes volatility. If the same ceiling is defended only thanks to the anchor year 2021, the average price of truthfulness is not the price of one press briefing. If the system slows at a peak of maturities, or exhausts the market’s willingness, the cost is the yield. If the exemptions are tightly bound to one reading of EU law, the cost is also a future dispute with the NRR. It is therefore useful to measure the price of the direction taken , not the price of the headline. For the 389 billion proposal that means describing the year-on-year change, the defence clause, the financing and the uncertainty before the act is passed. 14. What to read in the proposal before a verdict is reached The budget workbook should be read according to the specific question and the accounting layer. The table shows where to compare plan with outturn and the cash balance with ESA methodology, without mixing years or units. Need First place in the workbook The decisive test Unacceptable shortcut Year-on-year direction SR deficit 2027 versus the 2026 act The same unit, plan versus plan The 2021 anchor EU compliance SVI balance and the net-expenditure path ESA, GDP, NEC “We are under 3%, done” Compliance with national law The framework under 23/2017 Coll. The volume of defence taken out Citing the framework after an amendment as if it were the original The price of the past Chapter 396 Year-on-year growth of interest A deficit without interest Investment versus operations Capital versus current spending What is one-off Calling every outlay an investment Defence The sum of all chapters, not only the MoD The GDP forecast, NATO methodology Passing 184.6 bn off as the MoD chapter For Czech use a separate anchor test is required. An English commentary on the Stability Pact will not measure whether the sentence “under 400 billion” in Czech means a ceiling or a promise. The test set should include the 2026 plan, the 2025 outturn, the covid record, budgeted debt service and the CZK 70 billion of COFOG defence spending stated in the 2027 proposal. It should also include a sentence in which the right answer is “the source is not enough”. Some readers finally need more figures. One for the treasury, a second for ESA, a third for interest and a fourth for defence taken out. That is not a failure of clarity. It is the same decision as using one account for a household and another for a firm. The condition is that the split is intelligible, that the figures do not cross unchecked, and that people know where final authority arises — in the Chamber, in a notification, or in a press sentence. After the proposal is published and before the act is passed Separate the Ministry of Finance proposal from an act approved by the government and parliament. Write down the year-on-year difference against the 310 billion of 2026. Establish the volume of defence in all chapters and the volume above 2% of GDP. Open chapter 396 and its year-on-year change. Check whether the structural estimate cites the Ministry of Finance or the NRR. 15. From a ministry proposal to an approved act A position on the proposal can be chosen without a six-month seminar and without impulsive agreement with the headline. A short, disciplined reading pilot is enough. Its aim is not to prove that the government can do something impressive. Its aim is to find situations in which a sentence about the ceiling fails, and to see whether we can catch them. A fortnight’s check of the proposal Days 1–2: Write down the layers: cash, ESA, the structural balance, the framework, interest. Days 3–4: Prepare the same anchors — 2019, 2021, 2025, 2026 — and forbid mixing plan with outturn. Days 5–7: Repeat every important statement three times: with the ceiling, with the direction, with the exemption. Days 8–10: Check the clauses, the volume of spending taken out, the end date and chapter 396. Days 11–12: Calculate the price of the direction taken, including interest, not only the price of the headline. Day 13: Stress tests: the covid anchor, the EU adjustment, defence above 2% of GDP, the absence of an act. Day 14: Document the limits and set the next review after the government decision and after submission to the Chamber. If possible the assessor should not begin with the sentence they want to confirm. On cash they follow the flow. On ESA, the support in the notification. On the framework, the content of the limit. On defence, the definition of the chapters. On interest, the year-on-year change. Each failure is classified: anchor, layer, exemption, duration, or a missing source. The conditions have to be comparable. The same year, the same unit, the same status of the proposal. If one statement may use 2021 and another 2026, we are testing rhetoric, which may be entirely proper — but we have to name it as such. If we want to test consolidation, we have to unify the anchor on plan–plan. The pilot should also have elimination conditions. For example: a single swap of plan and outturn in the decisive sentence, the use of the covid record as proof of discipline, or an inability to trace how much defence dropped out of the framework. A high average score for intelligibility must not override an error whose impact the reader cannot accept. The last output is not merely agreement with the ceiling. It is an operating rule: what the figure is used for, what it is not, which layer may enter the headline, what must stay in the table, and when the decision will be opened again. Acts, forecasts and clauses change. Without a revision date even a good ceiling gradually turns into a state superstition. 16. Maastricht under three percent is not consolidation The deficit-to-GDP ratio is a useful map. The Maastricht threshold of 3% of GDP is a procedural threshold, not a thermometer of virtue. It can be met by growth in the denominator, a one-off receipt, a shift of spending outside the sector, or an actual cut in the flow. Whoever announces “we are meeting Maastricht” has announced compliance with one threshold. They have not announced that the cash deficit has fallen year on year. They have not announced that debt service is falling. They have not announced that the structural balance is heading toward one percent of GDP, as the national act speaks of it. [8] [3] [6] In 2025 the NRR recalled the long-term importance of the structural balance and doubted that, without further measures, the national fiscal rules would be met in 2027. [6] [5] That opinion predates the Ministry of Finance proposal of 31 August 2026 and is not an assessment of it. It has to be updated against the new proposal, which is not yet an act or an outturn. OECD and Eurostat international comparisons help only where the definition fits. The Czech ESA deficit cannot, without reservation, be set beside a neighbouring country’s cash deficit. Even the debt-to-GDP ratio does not measure interest-rate risk at a short maturity. When the definition fits badly, it is more honest to say so than to manufacture a ranking. Consolidation is the direction after adjustment for the cycle, one-off operations and exemptions. A ceiling is the upper bound of one year. They can meet. They need not. A sentence that swaps them is not a lie about the amount. It is a mistake about the question. 17. The price of the exemption in later budgets The first generation of budget debates sold an absolute figure in billions. The next generation sold a ratio to GDP. Today’s workbooks sell something larger: a place in which part of the spending becomes invisible to the rule that was meant to constrain it. Governments therefore compete not only for the lowest deficit. They compete for the reference base. For which year is the anchor, which layer enters the headline, which clause is activated and which interest is postponed into a chapter that no one applauds. The more comfortable the ceiling that arises, the higher the price of leaving the exemption can be. Frameworks are hard to put back, consolidation automatics rely on the original act, and people stop distinguishing their own rule from the amendment in which they rewrote it. That does not mean a defence exemption is a bad thing. Precisely that exemption can create the greatest benefit in a security situation. It means it should be bought consciously. The public needs a portable table of layers, a visible column of spending taken out, a way to compare plan with plan, and an emergency reading procedure without a headline. The best deficit is therefore not the one that is never deep. After a pandemic, a war and an act on two percent of GDP for defence, we do not have such a year. Nor is it the deficit with the lowest number, the longest ceiling or the largest number of references to Maastricht. It is the deficit whose layers match the real question and whose errors are visible, reversible and economically bearable . At the moment 389 billion is published, we are reading a ministry proposal. Only government and parliamentary debate can turn it into an approved budget; later outturn will show the fact. At the same time the framework, the defence clause and the refinancing of the debt have to be watched. What decides is against which year the proposal deepens, which spending changes the fiscal assessment, and how that feeds through into financing and interest. — Jiný Kontext

items.title: One benefit merged four calculations. The effects differ by household
items.subtitle: An internal analysis by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs, described by ČTK on 3 June 2026, reported lower calculated support for 57 % of the 155 500 households included in the recalculation. According to the same calculation, almost a fifth of the 128 400 households monitored would remain below the living minimum after housing costs. This is not a long-term record of payments actually made, nor a complete map of poverty.

items.body: One application promises less paperwork, but it does not say how much the household will have left. The form may be shorter and the calculation stricter. Digital filing may speed up the case, while the assets test decides before the components are added up. A district housing cap refines the geography and at the same time draws borders that the real rental market need not respect. Act No. 151/2025 Coll. introduced the state social assistance benefit — in the media the unified benefit — and replaced the housing allowance, the housing supplement, the subsistence allowance and the child allowance. It took effect for new applicants on 1 October 2025. Act No. 35/2026 Coll. moved the transition of existing recipients to 1 July 2026; under the interim timetable the first payment under the new calculation was due in August for July, but this article has no operational data on whether every payment was actually delivered. From 1 October 2026 the housing-component calculation changes: instead of three bands by municipality size, 77 district caps apply. [1] [2] [5] How exactly does the new algorithm combine four logics, what do the first ministerial recalculations measure, and why is a map of districts not a map of the market? What we know / What we do not know What we know: The state social assistance benefit merged four earlier benefits. An internal MPSV recalculation, reported by ČTK on 3 June 2026, described lower calculated support for 57 % of the 155 500 households in the analysed set. The publicly cited report is not a complete data table. What we do not know: The recalculation does not show the long-term effect on all households, the number of successful remedies, or actual behaviour after the rules changed. Without the consolidated wording and specific figures, an individual entitlement cannot be calculated. 1. Four logics that look like one benefit Imagine a meeting about the “unified benefit” at the labour ministry. The minister points to one form and says the trek between allowance, supplement, subsistence and child benefit is over. A Labour Office official points to the queue of applications and to the assets test that stops a file because of a second car. An MPSV statistician lays on the table a recalculation of transferred households and says the amount fell for most of them. A mayor from a district with expensive rents asks for a higher cap. A mayor from a district with a thin rental market asks that his median not be calculated from five contracts. The single mother is not in the room. She wants to know how much she will have left after rent. At first glance this is a dispute about generosity. In fact each person is describing a different object. The first speaks of the number of proceedings. The second speaks of procedural capacity and the assets test. The third speaks of the year-on-year difference in a specific sample. The fourth speaks of the level of eligible rent. The fifth speaks of how robust the percentile is. The applicant measures the balance after actual housing costs. Each person at the meeting can describe their part of the system exactly without describing the outcome for the household. The slogan “one benefit, less bureaucracy” is therefore not enough. Simplicity has to be split into the size of the components, the map of caps, the assets filter, the offset of earnings, the capacity of the office and the chance to correct an error. Any assessment of the reform must first decide whether it is comparing the form, the calculation, the district cap, or the balance after housing. Without that choice, different quantities sit side by side. The form is not a benefit. A benefit is not a situation. A district is not a market. And a drop in a sample is not a map of poverty. — Jiný Kontext 2. How four components produce the final amount When a single sum appears in the account, it is easy to think the “unified benefit” calculated it. The result is built in a chain. Each layer can raise help, cut it, or change the kind of error. Two households with the same income may therefore not receive the same amount. The same act can behave differently by district, by the number of cars, and by whether the household is in the vulnerable category. Four layers of one calculation Benefit components: the act combines one to four components — housing, subsistence, child and work bonus. A household need not be entitled to all of them. One application is therefore not one entitlement. [1] Cap and percentile: eligible housing costs are capped. Until September 2026 by three municipality sizes. From 1 October 2026 by district, from data on the rents of benefit recipients; for ordinary households the 50th percentile, for vulnerable households the 75th percentile. What is measured is rent in a sample of recipients, not market listings for the whole district. [5] [6] Tests and offset: income, assets, number of cars, a further residential property. The filter can stop the file before the components are added up. [1] [8] Administration and channel: the Jenda electronic zone, assisted filing, deadlines, appeals, Labour Office capacity. An error in layer 4 can look like an error in layer 1. [3] The basic formula decides an important part of the amount, but it is not the only actor. According to a ČTK report, in 2026 the president signed a change that widens the vulnerable category of single parents from care of children under seven to children under fifteen; for any concrete decision the effective consolidated wording must be checked. Such a change can alter the percentile used without changing the rent. District borders change the cap, and the number of registered cars can change whether the assets condition is met. [5] This is where the first error in public comparisons appears. A headline announces a fight between a “more generous versus a stingier benefit”, but in fact it compares two households with a different district, a different percentile basket and a different assets filter. Or it measures only a shorter form and treats the result as a verdict on poverty. An honest comparison must state not only the name of the benefit but also the month of the calculation, the district, the size of the household, whether it is a vulnerable category, what was offset from income, and whether it was a new application or a transfer. This map of layers is not decoration on the form. It tells you where to turn when something fails. If the amount did not cover the rent, the cap may have failed. If the application fell, the car test may have failed. If the payment arrived late, office capacity may have failed. The sentence “the unified benefit failed” is the start of a diagnosis, not its end. Illustrative diagram: The same act can, in a different district, with a different percentile basket and a different assets filter, produce a different balance after rent. 3. The best benefit is the one whose error a household can bear The average amount alone does not show how the system treats an error. It is necessary to know whether the household will see it, what remedy the law allows, and whether the correction will arrive before the rent is due. A week’s delay in payment can be decisive when rent is due on the first. A jump in the cap between neighbouring districts cannot be repaired by changing the form alone. Proof that a vehicle has been scrapped can correct a wrong input; loss of housing is much harder for administrative proceedings to undo. Risk does not grow only with how often amounts are cut. It also grows when a smooth form invites undue trust that “one benefit” means “the same protection”. Type of failure What it looks like How to test it What limits the harm Merger error Four risks in one calculation, a non-linear response to income Compare the components separately, not only the total A mandatory breakdown of components on the decision Sample error A percentile from a thin rental market The number of contracts in the district and size category A minimum sample, smoothing, a year-on-year cap on the jump Filter error Rejection after a wrong figure on assets Check the legal category, ownership and the number of vehicles or properties A request to complete the file, instruction, and a remedy within the limits of the law Channel error Digital filing the household does not complete The share of assisted filings, appeals, delays A personal channel, capacity, a temporary payment That also changes the question of assessment. We are not only asking which benefit pays more on average. We ask which one fails in a way the household and the office can catch. An analyst may tolerate ten model deviations, because one methodological error is easy to see. A family with children cannot tolerate a single month below the living minimum after rent is paid. An office may accept a more complex formula if the decision breaks the components down. It cannot accept rejecting a file with no path to a correction. Beside the amount of support, the readability of the decision, the chance of a lawful remedy and the effect of delay on housing must be assessed. A clear breakdown of components and instruction on the remedy may matter more to the household than a national average with no explanation. 4. What the ministerial recalculation of 57 percent shows On 3 June 2026 ČTK published figures from an internal MPSV analysis that recalculated the entitlement of existing recipients under the new rules. This is a numerical trace before the first August payments to transferred households, not an observation of amounts actually paid. The analysis does not measure new applicants, the SILC population or the long-term path of poverty. [7] Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext According to the ČTK report, lower support came out for 57 % of the 155 500 households included in the recalculation. In the monitored set of 128 400 households, after actual housing costs were counted, almost a fifth would remain below the living-minimum line. ČTK obtained the figures from MPSV; the publicly cited article does not contain a complete table or a methodological file from which all results could be recalculated independently. The numbers therefore describe a ministerial model recalculation, not an audit of the August payments. [7] Every such figure contains methodological choices. Which recipients did the analysis include? How did it set the comparison amount of the old benefits? How did it capture actual housing costs and the work bonus? Without a published table and methodology these questions cannot be closed from the ČTK article. Five facts without which a percentage is only an advertising number The exact population: households included in the recalculation, new applicants, or all households below the threshold. The period: the date of the recalculation and the comparison period, not automatically the month of payment. The unit: household, not person; the amount before rent, or after it. The source: a ministerial recalculation, SILC, or a Labour Office audit. The known limit: the full table is not public, the method is uncertain, and the rules may still change. For an assessment of the reform, a small internal audit of the components therefore matters more than someone else’s catch-all slogan “the unified benefit failed”. Thirty real files — with actual rents, a Czech district, an assets test and the actual balance after energy — can say more than a thousand comments on the form. A public percentage helps choose the question. The decision has to be made from the file. 5. Compare logics, not forms The old system rested on four benefits with different philosophies. The housing allowance tested the ratio of costs to income in state social support. The housing supplement covered the poorest people in material need. The subsistence allowance held a safety net. The child allowance supported families with dependent children. Act No. 117/1995 Coll. and Act No. 111/2006 Coll. kept these logics apart. Separation was confusing. It was also insurance: the failure of one benefit did not bring down the other three. [12] [13] The new act fused them into one proceeding with four components. That is an administrative gain. It is not automatically a gain for every hardship. The housing component behaves like a capped rent. The subsistence component like a minimum. The child component like conditional support. The work bonus like a correction of the earnings offset. One change in income can trigger all four at once. Original benefit What it tested What became of it in DSSP Typical failure after the merger Housing allowance Costs / income, municipal cap Housing component; from 1. 10. 2026 a district cap A jump in the percentile, a different data basket Housing supplement Material need, the actual shortfall Part of the same ceiling Loss of a “last resort” above the cap Subsistence allowance Basic needs Subsistence component The income offset pulls housing down as well Child allowance Family, income threshold Child component A different threshold, different age bands The rows are not nostalgia for chaos. The same state offers fewer proceedings and more mathematics. The map is there to prevent another error: a family buying an excellent form in a product that does not see its rent, cannot safely top the rent up, or locks it into a district that is later hard to leave. How to read the diagram: The columns are not a set of accounts; they separate the number of applications from the balance after rent. 6. Four benefits, four risks The housing allowance could fail because a municipal cap did not match the rent beyond the town. The supplement could fail by arriving late. Subsistence could fail through a hard offset. The child allowance could fail at a threshold that dropped a family after a small rise in wages. The unified benefit does not add these risks to zero. It moves them into one algorithm that responds non-linearly to a change in income. That is why a cut in bureaucracy can be true and a worse balance can be true as well. The first measures the number of filings. The second measures the result in crowns. Act No. 151/2025 Coll. allows both, because they are different layers. Anyone who infers from the first that the second is slander confuses the channel with the benefit. [1] The living minimum and the subsistence minimum, which the components refer to, have their own Act No. 110/2006 Coll. A change in those amounts can change the result of the benefit without changing the form. The specific amount and the date it takes effect must therefore be taken from the valid and effective wording of the regulation; neither a calculator nor a press release replaces the legal text. [14] What needs to be tested The first test concerns the breakdown. The same total without a breakdown of components is not the same experiment as an amount with four lines. The second concerns the rollout: an existing recipient with a deferred transfer to July 2026 is not the same as a new applicant from October 2025. The third concerns housing: rent of 16 000 crowns in a district with a high percentile basket is not the same as 16 000 in a district where the office calculates from five contracts. The act may be the same. The result is not. 7. A ministerial sample is not all poverty The set of 155 500 households included in the internal recalculation is large, but it is not a picture of all Czech poverty. It does not include all new applicants, nor households that never apply for the benefit at all. The share of 57 % therefore describes the result of one specific ministerial analysis, not the population at risk of income poverty according to SILC. [7] [15] Almost a fifth of the 128 400 households monitored remaining below the living minimum after actual housing costs is a figure for a modelled balance, not for an average benefit. Without the full table we do not know how the results split among types of household, districts and levels of rent. [7] In the SILC survey the Czech Statistical Office measures income and living conditions with a different definition of the household, a different period and a different poverty threshold. It cannot, without reservation, verify the June ministerial recalculation, nor refute it. These are two different statistical questions. [15] That does not mean the ministerial number is useless. It means the sentence “for most people, help fell” needs a rider: which majority, in which month, against what total and after what costs. Without the rider it is a headline. With the rider it is a map for an audit. 8. A district is not a market. It is a statistical basket Three bands by municipality size were crude. A municipality near Prague shared a logic with a municipality in the Bruntál area if both stayed under 70 000 inhabitants. Prague and Brno had their own category. In 2026 Lidovky published the then table of normative rent: a one-person household from 7 580 crowns in a municipality of up to 69 999 inhabitants to 12 831 crowns in Prague and Brno. The figures measure the legal ceiling, not the rent paid. From October 2026 this crudeness gives way to 77 districts, Prague as one district. [10] [8] PAQ Research pointed out that MPSV calculates the rent cap from the rents of existing recipients of the housing component, not from the wider CZSO market. For households that are not vulnerable, from the median; for vulnerable households, from the 75th percentile, plus the statutory amount for costs tied to using the flat. In a small district and a rare household size there may be few contracts. A percentile from a small sample is unstable. A year-on-year jump can arrive without any movement in listings. That is not proof that a district map is worse than three bands. It is proof that a finer map needs more robust data. [6] An illustration, not a report: two single mothers eight kilometres apart may, at a similar rent, have a different eligible amount if they fall into different district baskets. Without the effective official values the specific difference in crowns cannot be stated honestly. Model amounts from the public debate are not official statistics, and before a practical calculation the valid regulation or the MPSV notice for the period must be opened. [6] [10] A district border is administrative. The labour market and commuting do not respect it. The algorithm does. That is the price of geographic fairness calculated from a basket, not from travel time. 9. An assets test is not a guarantee of fairness The act limits a further property intended for housing and the number of passenger cars by the number of adult members of the household. The aim is clear: the benefit is not meant to underwrite a well-off household with a second flat and a fleet of cars. The tool is cruder than the aim. A rural family with two old cars needed for shifts and an immobile wreck waiting for ecological disposal can look the same as a speculator. The system reads the count, not the value. [1] [8] Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext The legal text sets the assets filter, but the sources cited with this article do not, as of 31 August 2026, contain a separate public Labour Office statistic on applications rejected only because of a vehicle, nor a breakdown of the appeals that followed. From that it cannot be inferred that the filter is flawless or that it is harmful across the board; both claims would need administrative data. [1] [17] Before the filter is switched on Separate the second property from the car, and the car from the wreck. Check in the act how the given assets and ownership are counted for the test. Document the current registration status and respond to any request from the office within the set deadline. Check whether a rejection states the reason, or only “does not meet the conditions”. Watch the appeals: how many of them return to payment. An assets test can strengthen public control of how the benefit is targeted, and at the same time create borderline cases. Without data on the reasons for rejection it is not possible to say which of these effects prevails in practice. 10. A work bonus is not the same as net earnings The act adds a bonus to the benefit for work activity and does not offset employment income in full. The aim is to remove the trap in which every crown earned disappears from the benefit. The mechanism is a correction of the offset, not a guarantee that net income after levies, deductions and rent will rise. [1] [3] Analyses of work incentives can show that the combination of levies, a fall in the benefit and other deductions creates a high effective burden for some households. They are not, by themselves, an evaluation of the effect of the Czech benefit after launch. A claim of a mass move into legal work would need follow-up administrative data and a comparable control group. [9] [11] An enforcement deduction and the calculation of the benefit are different legal mechanisms. For a particular household, the rise in disposable income may therefore be smaller than the work bonus itself. Without an individual calculation it cannot be said that the bonus will always raise the net balance, nor that a deduction will always wipe it out. The sources cited with the article as of 31 August 2026 do not contain a public causal evaluation of how many households increased their hours because of the work bonus. Such an assessment would need a longer time series, employment data and a suitable comparison. Until then the work bonus is a described mechanism, not a proven exit from the shadow economy. 11. Where the calculation is checked after the merger Before the merger an applicant could receive several decisions for different benefits. After the merger one decision is checked, with several components, a district basket and assets conditions. The practical question is whether the cap used, the input data and the income offset are right. One decision can combine three true inputs into a wrong balance. The rent is real. The district is correct. The income is reported. A synthesis below the living minimum after rent may still be the result of a ceiling, not of fraud. At other times the system uses a sound median from a small sample. Or it cites a vulnerable category that will shift in October, while the file still runs under September rules. A four-step check of the payment Existence: the decision arrived and breaks down the components. Authority: the cap is from the valid MPSV notice for the given quarter. Support: the specific rent and income actually entered the specific line. Scope: the district, household size, vulnerability, assets and month fit. The most reliable working method therefore separates the search from the argument about the reform. First the table: old payment, new payment, rent, energy, balance, reason for the difference. Only then a verdict on the “unified benefit”. If a line cannot be opened, a claim does not become a fact merely because the form was one. 12. One application is not one situation The Jenda client zone and assisted filing at the Labour Office are a channel. The act says the benefit can be applied for electronically or in person. The channel measures access to the proceeding. It does not measure the amount of a component. A household without a bank identity, without data and without time to appeal may have the same entitlement and a worse channel. That is an old inequality in a new interface. [3] Older recommendations of the Public Defender of Rights on the Labour Office’s application practice point to risks around documents, deadlines, instruction and the language of decisions. They are not, however, statistics of payments or a direct evaluation of the rollout of the new benefit; for that, files and remedies have to be tracked separately. [17] Office capacity is another layer. Act No. 35/2026 Coll. postponed the transition of existing recipients and preserved a temporary continuity of the original payments. The wording of the act itself does not prove a single political motive for the shift, nor the scale of any operational trouble in August. Delay in a proceeding would be a problem of administration, not by itself proof of a flawed formula. [2] Two similar files may have a different channel. One household files in Jenda with a bank identity in an evening. The other waits for assisted filing, brings proof of the rent and of the car, and leaves with a case number. The act is the same. The time to payment is not. Anyone who measures the reform only by the number of clicks measures the channel of the winners of digital access. They do not measure the household for which the office is the last public counter. 13. The price of the form is not the price of the result The market in reforms uses several languages at once. A politician pays by the number of benefits. An office pays by the number of operations. A household pays with the balance after rent. The state pays through the MPSV budget chapter. A direct comparison of “four applications versus one” without knowing the balance therefore misleads. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Cheaper administration can be economically excellent for processing a hundred thousand files. The same reform can be expensive for a household that appeals three times, uses assisted filing and in the end needs extraordinary immediate assistance. The more expensive old supplement may have been unnecessary for duplicates. It may have been cheaper for a one-off shortfall that the new ceiling will not recognise. The real price of a payment received Components + the balance after rent and energy + time to file + an appeal + the price of losing housing + a future jump in the percentile. The result is cheap only when it has passed the month from which the rent is paid and can be defended with a breakdown of the components. It is therefore useful to measure the price per accepted balance , not the price per application. Accepted means the payment met a predetermined minimum after housing, passed a check and did not cause the later loss of the flat. This metric can reverse an order that looked obvious from the form. 14. What to read in the decision before the verdict The decision has to be read according to the kind of hardship and the specific mechanism of the calculation. The table shows in which part of the file to look for the first verifiable figure. Need First place in the file Decisive test Unacceptable shortcut Balance after housing Housing component versus actual rent Cap, district, percentile The average benefit in the Czech Republic Food and basic needs Subsistence component versus the living minimum Income offset “One benefit is enough” Children Child component, age, vulnerability Threshold and age band A single average for all families Work Work bonus and net wage after deductions Enforcement, levies Bonus = motivation Assets Number of cars, a further property Legal category, ownership and count Every car is abuse Channel Jenda versus assisted filing Delay, appeal Digitisation = access For Czech use a separate district test is needed. A national average will not measure whether the system preserves the weight of rent in the Central Bohemian Region, classifies vulnerability correctly, distinguishes a municipality near Prague from a municipality near the border, or translates “district” into a market that does not exist. The test set should include diacritics in an address, two cars, an inheritance, a small sample of contracts, and a file in which the right answer is “the source is not enough”. Three tests of a decision after the transition The first is comparative: what was the sum of the old benefits in the same month last year, cleaned of the change in rent? The second is residual: what is left after the actual rent and energy prepayments? The third is procedural: did the decision meet the deadline, and can the component that decided the amount be read from it? A product that pays a day earlier need not be better if, a month later, no one can find out why it paid exactly that much. 15. A short household audit An assessment can be done without waiting for SILC 2027 and without an impulsive verdict from a single payment. A short, disciplined audit is enough. Its aim is not to prove that the reform can do something impressive. The aim is to find situations in which the algorithm fails, and to see whether the household and the office can catch them. Fourteen days from an impression to a figure Days 1–2: List 20 to 40 real files, their district, rent, number of cars and the cost of an error. Days 3–4: Prepare the same inputs before and after October 2026, the mandatory points and an anonymous sheet. Days 5–7: Repeat each important type of household three times — with a percentile jump, with a filter, with a bonus. Days 8–10: Check Jenda, assisted filing, appeals, deadlines and whether the breakdown is intelligible. Days 11–12: Calculate the balance after rent, including energy and deductions. Day 13: Stress tests: a small sample in a district, a wreck, a child between 7 and 15 years, an incomplete entry. Day 14: Decide by the matrix, document the limits and set a date for the next review after the October caps are published. If possible the evaluator should not know whether the case is a “winner” or a “loser” from a press conference. For the amount they watch whether the components are factually right. For housing, the support for the percentile. For the filter, whether it can be reversed. For the channel, the number of human interventions. Each failure is classified: merger, sample, filter, channel, or a missing source. The pilot should also have conditions for exclusion. For example: a single unannounced stop of payment without instruction, use of a forbidden percentile from an empty basket, or an inability to trace from which rent the 50th percentile was calculated. A high average score for digitisation must not outweigh an error whose effect the household cannot accept. 16. Digitisation is not a benefit. It is a channel The public-administration portal describes the benefit as a tool for covering basic needs, housing costs and the raising of children, with a bonus for work. An application is possible online or with assistance. That is a description of the entry. It is not a description of the balance. Anyone who swaps “it can be applied for on a phone” for “help has improved” has bought a channel and issued it as a benefit. [3] The OECD compares social systems and work incentives across countries. Comparison helps only where the definitions of household, offset and housing fit. The Czech unified benefit, with a district percentile basket from recipients’ rents, is not the same as a Canadian or Danish model with a different market. When the definitions fit badly, it is more honest to say so. [18] One application saves time for programmers and for some officials. If the formula misses a specific hardship, a system appears that is smooth in the channel and blind on the ground. The quality of a net is not known by how easily a form is filled in. It is known by whether it catches a person in the month when a notice to quit the tenancy is a threat. 17. The district cap as a long-term risk The first generation of social policy sold the number of benefits. The next sold targeting. Today’s reform sells something larger: a place in which four hardships are added up in one algorithm and geography becomes a parameter of the calculation. So the contest is not only over the amount of help. It is over the data basket from which the percentile is calculated, the definition of vulnerability, the number of cars and the habit of applying once. The more convenient the form that appears, the higher the price of leaving the map of 77 districts. Files, automatic rules and expectations are hard to return to four acts. People stop distinguishing their own hardship from the product in which the state calculated it. That does not mean the merger is wrong. It is precisely the merger that can cut friction. It means it should be bought with open eyes. The state needs a portable breakdown of components, a documented percentile, a way to repair the filter and an emergency procedure when the basket in a district runs dry. The best benefit is therefore not the one that never short-changes anyone. We do not have such a system with four logics merged. Nor is it the benefit with the shortest form, the highest average or the largest number of districts. It is the benefit whose components match the real hardship and whose errors are visible, reversible and bearable in the month the rent is due . The moment the state is only merging forms, it is choosing a channel. The moment it reads rent from a basket of recipients, filters cars and prepares the October percentiles, it is also choosing a new map of fairness. And then the question is no longer: “Is one benefit simpler?” In a check, what matters is which hardship the formula misses, how the district entered the result, and whether the error can be corrected before the rent is due. — Jiný Kontext

items.title: What the government’s first pension amendment of July 2026 actually contained
items.subtitle: In its policy statement the government coalition pledged to cap the retirement age at 65 and to return to indexation by half of real-wage growth. The public summary of the first amendment approved by the government on 20 July 2026 describes an earlier spread of the age supplement from age 80 and an increase in the percentage assessment for work in retirement. The cap at 65 is not in it, and according to a ČTK report the return to half of wages dropped out of the bill.
