items.body: A pension reform and a partial amendment are not synonyms. A headline may announce government approval while the bill does not contain a cap at 65. An age supplement may be part of the first phase, indexation by half of real-wage growth may drop out of it, and the increase for work may have its first practical effect only in 2028. Andrej Babiš’s government approved a policy statement on 5 January 2026: the retirement age will be capped at 65 and the indexation formula with inflation and half of real-wage growth will be restored. On 20 July 2026 the government approved an amendment to Act No. 155/1995 Coll. on pension insurance. Public summaries by ČTK and the labour ministry describe an age increase from 80 and automatic raising of the percentage assessment for work from 2028. ČTK reported that the return to half of wages dropped out of the bill after comments from the Ministry of Finance; MPSV places the cap at 65 in the second phase. [1] [3] [4] [18] How does a reform become a shift in the timing of a supplement, what do 2.6 billion koruna in 2027 measure, and why is postponement not the same as fulfilment? What we know / What we do not know What we know: The policy statement promises a cap at 65 and half of real-wage growth. The official MPSV summary of 20 July 2026 describes, in the first amendment, age supplements, work in retirement and payments abroad; a separate MPSV page places the cap at 65 in the second phase. ČTK described the dropping of half of wages. On 3 August 2026 the Office of the Government still spoke of age bonuses and the increase for work as a proposal. [1] [3] [4] [18] [19] What we do not know: This article does not have as its basis a definitive Chamber wording with a print number and all sections. It therefore assesses the publicly documented content of the bill as of 20 July 2026, not the final form after parliamentary changes. Budget figures are scenarios quoted by ČTK, not certain future spending. 1. A pledge the amendment need not carry Imagine a July meeting on the “pension amendment”. The labour minister puts the supplement from age 80 on the table and says that seniors at a high age will get the money sooner. The finance minister points to a long-term projection and says that the cap at 65 and half of wages do not belong in this text. The prime minister promises a second wave and a mention of Brussels. A coalition deputy hears that the government is dealing with pensions. An opposition deputy hears that the January pledge has vanished. The journalist in the room has two sentences in the notebook: “The government approved a pension amendment” and “we will cap the age at 65”. He wants to know which one holds. At first glance this is a dispute about the word reform. In fact each person describes a different object. The first speaks about an age increase in the percentage assessment. The second speaks about the balance of the pension account in the 50s of this century. The third speaks about the legislative calendar. The fourth speaks about political delivery. The fifth speaks about a missing section. The journalist compares the headline with the policy statement. Participants in the debate may therefore speak truthfully about different parts of the bill and still leave the public without an answer as to which programme points actually became sections. The term “pension reform” here covers several separate topics: retirement age, the indexation formula, arduous occupations, work in retirement and the age supplement. Scrutiny therefore begins with the question of which pledge entered the bill and later the law in force . A programme, a government bill, an explanatory memorandum and a valid act have different legal weight. A programme is not a law. A headline is not a section. A supplement is not an age cap. And postponement to 2028 is not fulfilment in 2026. — Jiný Kontext 2. From programme to effect several steps remain When “pension amendment” appears in a headline, it is easy to get the impression that the system has changed. The result, however, is produced in a chain. Each layer can fulfil, postpone or merely rename a pledge. Two documents on the same topic therefore need not say the same thing. Five layers of one pension verdict Policy statement: a political document of 5 January 2026. It promises a cap at 65, half of real-wage growth, age indexation from 80, arduous occupations and support for work in retirement. It is not a statute. It does not change the assessment. [1] Government bill amending Act No. 155/1995 Coll.: a bill approved by the government on 20 July 2026. In its public summary MPSV lists the age supplement, work in retirement and payments abroad; it places the cap at 65 in the second phase. ČTK reported that half of wages dropped out of the bill after finance comments. [3] [4] [18] Effect: the age increase from 1 January 2027. Automatic raising for work first in January 2028, the relevant period of work from September 2026. A calendar is not a headline. [5] [6] Fiscal layer: the explanatory memorandum and projections. ČTK, on government approval, stated that annual spending on both measures contained would, on the mildest scenario, grow from 2027 to 2060 from 2.6 billion koruna to 60.8 billion. This is a scenario for this amendment, not the price of the cap at 65. [3] Administration and responsibility: ČSSZ, automatic recalculation for employees, an application for the self-employed, a second wave promised for later. Who bears the bill depends on the date, not on the name of the act. The basic pledge determines an important part of the debate, but it is not the only input. The government can approve a bill without a cap at 65, keep the 6.5 % insurance discount and at the same time propose an increase in the percentage assessment for further work. The label “first wave” itself shows that this is not the whole programme. A comparison must therefore state the date, the stage of the legislative process, the content of the bill, the intended effect and the points expressly postponed. The individual steps make it possible to determine exactly what has changed. A supplement from age 80 documents an age change, but by itself says nothing about the retirement age. The indexation formula in force cannot be inferred from the programme. The sentence “the government approved a pension amendment” therefore does not yet describe the content or the effect of all pledged points. Illustrative diagram: The same word reform can, in a different layer, with a different effective date and a different missing section, produce a different impact. 3. Check also the points that are missing from the bill A visible supplement is easier to check than a provision that is missing from the bill. A five-hundred-koruna amount at eighty has a concrete sum and a date. A missing cap at 65 appears only when the programme, the bill and the retirement age in force are compared. A postponed point remains exposed to further political change. The risk does not grow only with the absence of a pledge. It also grows when a grand title invites undue confidence that the headline has replaced the section. Type of failure What it looks like How to test it What limits the harm Title error “Reform” for a parametric shift Compare programme and section line by line A table of pledge / text / effect Cap error A supplement from 80 is read as a cap at 65 Open the retirement age in 155/1995 Coll. One sentence: what the amendment does not change Calendar error Effect in 2027 is read as indexation in 2027 The date as of which January indexation is set Separate the age supplement and the wage formula Account error 2.6 bn is read as the price of the whole programme The scenario for both measures contained versus the dropped items Two columns: in the text / outside the text This also changes the reader’s question. We do not ask only whether the amendment “gives something”. We ask which gap in our reading we will catch. An eighty-year-old woman may tolerate that the cap at 65 is not her question. A forty-year-old man cannot tolerate that the headline answered this question for him. A state accountant may accept 2.6 billion in 2027. He cannot accept them as proof that half of wages is settled. Public assessment must, besides the changes contained, also show the missing points, their expected date and the impact on different cohorts. An accurate description of a more modest bill is more useful than a broad title that conceals its limits. 4. What a headline does not say about a section A news headline summarises a government decision, not the entire pension system. On 20 July 2026 ČTK described approval of a bill raising pensions after eighty and for work in retirement, and the dropping of a return to higher indexation. [3] From this report it does not follow either that all programme points have been fulfilled, or that the bill brings no change at all. Every headline contains hidden decisions. Does it cite the programme, or the bill? Does it speak about 80 years, or about 65? About 2027, or 2028? About ČSSZ, or about Brussels? The answer to any of these questions can change the order of blame and credit. Five facts without which “reform” is only an advertising word The exact document: programme, government bill, Chamber print, or the act in force. The date: 5 January, 20 July, 1 January 2027, 1 January 2028. The population: seniors 80+, working pensioners, cohorts heading towards 67, arduous occupations. What the text changes and what it expressly does not change. The fiscal scenario: to which measures the 2.6 billion relate. For buying political calm, therefore, a small internal table matters more than a foreign overall slogan. Five real rows — with actual sections, Czech effective dates and a real gap — can say more than a thousand debates about “betrayal of pensioners”. A public headline helps select candidates for a sentence. The decision must be made by work with the text. That is not proof that press conferences have no value. It is an audit of one specific government day carried out by public agencies, not proof that pledges have no value. It does show, however, that even the precise date of 20 July may precisely change only part of the question the programme opened in January. 5. Compare sections, not pledges The following comparison does not assess who is generally fairer to seniors. It shows what type of information individual documents contain and what, conversely, cannot be inferred from them. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Document Main working position What to verify Typical reason for the choice Programme 5. 1. 2026 Political commitment Cap 65, 1/2 of wages, occupations One intelligible sentence for voters Government amendment 20. 7. 2026 Sections of 155/1995 Coll. What is in the text and what is missing What the Chamber actually receives Act 155/1995 Coll. in force Retirement age, indexation 1/3 The trajectory towards 67 The state that holds until it is changed Explanatory memorandum / ČTK Fiscal scenarios 2.6 bn for what; 2–102 bn for what The price of what is contained, not the price of the pledge Print 50 (10th term) A different bill, different sponsors It is not the government wave of July Do not confuse an opposition print with a government one The rows are not a verdict on honesty. The same government offers several documents in one year and each of them may change during reading in the Chamber. The map is meant to prevent a different error: that a voter buys an excellent headline in a product that does not see his retirement age, cannot change it safely, or locks it into a “second wave” from which it is later hard to exit. Interpretive diagram: The position of the documents does not express a score; it shows questions that must be answered together. 6. A policy statement is not a statute The government’s text of 5 January 2026, in the chapter on pensions, promises capping the retirement age at 65 and restoring an indexation formula that takes account of living costs and half of real-wage growth. It further promises age indexation from 80, an adjustment of arduous occupations and an increase in the pension for work. It is a document that the government sends to the Chamber with a request for confidence. It is not an amendment. It has no effect. It does not change the ČSSZ assessment. [1] [2] That does not diminish its importance. It diminishes the warrant for claiming that approval of any pension amendment is automatically fulfilment of the January sentences. A programme may be fulfilled in several steps. It may be fulfilled in part. It may be postponed with a reference to fiscal rules and the European Commission. Each of these options is politically defensible. None of them turns a headline into a section. In May 2026 Lidovky described that the MPSV bill then contained only some points of the programme and that the cap, arduous occupations and pillars were to come later, with effect from 1 January 2028. Between May and 20 July, half of wages also disappeared from the bill. The trail is therefore double: something never entered the first wave at all, and something dropped out of it during comments. To confuse both for a single “betrayal” is inaccurate. To separate both is the reader’s work. [7] [3] 7. The age supplement: earlier payment of the same cap The most visible change in the July bill is an adjustment of the monthly pension amount after a set age is reached. The existing rule raises the monthly pension by 1 000 koruna on reaching 85 and by a further 2 000 koruna on reaching 100. From 1 January 2027 the bill spreads the same resulting monthly level of increase: by 500 koruna on reaching 80, 85, 90 and 95 and by 1 000 koruna on reaching 100. These are not one-off amounts paid out, nor a “lifetime sum” of 3 000 koruna; each increase feeds into the next monthly pension payment. [3] [5] [18] ČTK reported an estimate that the addition by age would in 2027 cost nominally 2.6 billion koruna. The sum would grow gradually: in 2029 three billion, in 2035 then 3.8 billion, by mid-century 4.8 billion, in 2060 then 6.4 billion. This is a projection for this measure, in the then prices of the scenario, not a ČSSZ audit. It does not measure the average pension. It does not measure whether 500 koruna at 80 is “dignity”. It measures the budgetary flow of the age step. [3] The mechanism mainly changes the timing and the path of the monthly increase. A person who reaches one hundred is, under the bill, to have against the basic pension the same resulting monthly level of increase of 3 000 koruna as under the existing age steps, but receives part of the increase earlier. It is not a lifetime maximum of money paid out. Anyone who adds the amounts into the sentence “pensions will rise by three thousand extra” confuses the monthly level after the age is reached with a one-off or lifetime amount. How to read the age supplement Separate three numbers. The first is the monthly step: 500 or 1 000 koruna after a specific age is reached. The second is the resulting monthly level of increase of 3 000 koruna at 100. The third is the estimated annual budgetary flow of 2.6 billion koruna in 2027, which ČTK relates to the age measure, not to the dropped half of wages. Anyone who adds them into one sentence about “reform” produces an amount that none of these figures means. An illustration, not a report: Mrs Marie is 79. A headline about supplements for seniors is concrete for her. At 80 she may receive 500 koruna a month. Mr Tomáš is 42. He reads the same headline and may gain the impression that the retirement age has stopped. For him nothing about 65 changes in this amendment. One title, two populations, two objects. 8. Work in retirement is not an insurance discount Since 2025 a 6.5 % discount on social insurance has applied to working old-age pensioners. From the first automatic recalculation in January 2028 the July bill is to raise the percentage assessment of the pension by 1.5 % for every 365 days of gainful activity; we do not use public government and ministry summaries here to derive a more precise calculation base, which the section wording must confirm. The discount is to remain. For employees ČSSZ is to carry out the increase automatically; the self-employed are, according to the summary, to proceed by an application tied to the statement of income and expenditure. [3] [18] [19] The relevant period of work is to be counted already from September 2026, or from a later month according to promulgation of the act. The first automatic raising of pensions is to come in January 2028. Minister Juchelka argued that it had been wrongly assumed that people would set aside the money from the discount. Raising the assessment is to ensure more money in old age. That is a hypothesis about behaviour, not a measurement of household savings. [3] [5] The catch is in the calendar. Postponement to 2028 means that real fulfilment is borne only by the budget of a later period. That may be legislatively rational: the rules of January indexation and recalculation have their deadlines. It is also a political shift of the bill. Anyone who announces “we will reward work in retirement” in 2026 has announced an intention. He has not announced that the assessment rose in 2026. Two similar accounts may therefore have a different regime. An employee with a monthly ČSSZ report gets the automatic. A self-employed person with a statement of income must apply. The 6.5 % discount flows into net pay now. The 1.5 percent flows into the assessment later. Anyone who adds them into an “immediate reward for work” mixes the wage flow with the pension flow. The law may hold both. A headline must not present both as the same moment. The previous regime until the end of 2024 raised the pension for work in a different way. The proposed 1.5 % for 365 days from the first recalculation in 2028 is a new parameter beside the retained discount. The old regime, the discount effective from 2025 and the proposed increase must therefore not be added into one sentence about a “return of the old times”. 9. What dropped out is not a trifle in an annex A return to half of real-wage growth instead of a third was explicit in the policy statement. In the comment procedure the Ministry of Finance wanted more precise calculations and opposed inclusion in this amendment. ČTK quoted that annual spending would, according to the labour ministry, rise from 2029 to 2060 from two billion koruna to 102 billion. This is a long projection for the dropped measure, not the deficit of 2027. Government politicians said that the step, like the cap at 65, would come in a further amendment. [3] [4] Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext A cap at 65 would abolish the mechanism in force of gradually raising the age towards 67 for younger cohorts, which a previous amendment brought into the act. As late as 11 February 2026 Minister Juchelka in the Chamber still placed the cap in the first wave. In March he was already speaking of a second wave with arduous occupations. In June on Czech Television he said there was no need to hurry. On 20 July the government approved the first amendment without the cap. The trail is public. It is not proof of bad intent. It is proof of a change of calendar. [4] [8] Arduous occupations are also not in the July text. The programme promised them. In May MPSV placed them in a later wave. Anyone who reads “pension amendment” as protection for a welder or a nurse is reading a document that is not in this wave. The gap is empirical: it is missing from the text. An assessment of intent is political. Separating both is again the reader’s work. [7] [1] 10. Demography is not a press conference In the Report on the Long-Term Sustainability of Public Finances 2025 the National Budget Council described that the “small” and “large” pension reforms of previous years — tightening of early pensions, reducing the share of real wages from a half to a third, gradual raising of the age towards 67 and adjustment of the replacement ratio — improve the balance of the pension system in the worst years, at the turn of the 50s and 60s of this century, by roughly two percentage points of GDP. Without these measures, according to the council, the deficit of the pension system in that period would reach almost 4 % of GDP. With the sum of the reforms the projection heads towards the 1.5 % of GDP boundary. This is an NRR projection, not the treasury of 2026. It does not measure fairness to today’s eighty-year-olds. It measures the path of the account. [9] Abolishing the path towards 67 and returning to a cap at 65 would shift the long-term account towards a more costly variant. In publicly available materials located as of 30 August 2026 we did not find a separate methodologically described dataset from which the precise billions “extra in 2050” quoted from an individual government slide could be verified. We therefore keep to the NRR projection: it works with percentages of GDP in the period when the departure of large cohorts culminates, not with the account for a 500 koruna supplement. Mixing the 2.6 billion of 2027 with this long-term path would join two different calculations. CZSO population projections show ageing and the dependency ratio. ČSSZ pension statistics show counts and average assessments as of 31 December. Neither of these sources measures whether 65 is “fair”. They measure population and payments. Policy may read various conclusions from them. The data read from them only what they measure. [10] [11] The European Commission in the Ageing Report sets Czech paths beside other member states. The comparison holds only where the definitions of statutory age, early departure and the replacement ratio fit. When they do not fit, the ranking misleads. [12] 11. A postponed pledge is checked in another phase Before the July approval a voter had to watch whether the government would “do something about pensions”. After approval he watches something more complicated: whether the headline fits the section, whether the effect fits the year, and whether the second wave has a date, or only an adjective. The pledge was not cancelled by a press conference. It moved into the gap between documents. One report can combine three true sentences into a false conclusion. The government approved the amendment. Eighty-year-olds will get 500 koruna. The programme promised 65. Each sentence works. The synthesis “they fulfilled the pension reform” is methodologically wrong. At other times 2.6 billion is quoted as the price of the “whole reform”, even though the scenario belongs to both measures contained, not to the dropped half of wages. Or the 6.5 % discount, which already applies, is quoted as if the July text had brought it. A four-step check of a pension statement Existence: the sentence is in the programme, in the bill, or only in the headline. Authority: primary is the government text and the act, not a paraphrase. Support: a concrete passage supports a concrete pledge. Scope: the population, the effective date and the fiscal scenario fit. The most reliable procedure separates searching from writing. First a table of pledges and gaps. Only then a dispute about betrayal. If a section cannot be opened, a claim is not promoted to fulfilment merely because the government “sat”. 12. Postponement is not repeal. It is a different account A second wave may come. It may contain the cap at 65, arduous occupations and half of wages. It may contain only a part. It may not come. The state as of 20 July 2026 is: a first wave without these points, a public promise of later, a mention of alignment with fiscal rules and with the Commission. Postponement is a political technology. It is not an accounting zero. It moves the conflict into another year, to another majority and to another notification cycle. [4] [8] Before the second wave Write down which three points of the programme are missing from the first wave: the cap at 65, half of wages, arduous occupations. For each, demand an effective date, a fiscal scenario and whether it is a pledge or a section. Until a date is missing, it is honest to say “postponed”, not “settled”. A second wave without a calendar is a headline. It is not a statute. In 2024 the Constitutional Court assessed the previous pension amendment No. 270/2023 Coll. That is a different print, a different Chamber, a different dispute about indexation. The number 270 in the Collection from 2023 must not become the automatic address of the July bill of 2026. As of 25 July 2026 the Chamber system, for the pension insurance act in the 10th term, recorded primarily deputies’ print 50 — a bill by a group of deputies from December 2025 on shortening the insurance period and indexing the child-raising increment, to which the government gave a negative opinion. The government July amendment may have received a number in the register later; as of the date of writing this text it is not honest to present the old 270/2023 or print 50 as “that” government wave. These are three objects. [13] [14] Postponing the indexation formula to a practical effect in 2028 — even if half of wages returned to the text — shows the same calendar mechanics. The rules of January indexation are set with a lag. Effect from 1 January 2027 therefore need not catch indexation in 2027. That is a legislative detail that changes the year of the account. It is not a trifle in a footnote. [15] 13. The price of a parameter is not the price of a pledge The market uses several price languages at once. A senior pays with a visible five-hundred-koruna amount. The labour minister pays with a scenario of 2.6 to 60.8 billion for both measures contained. The finance minister pays with the absence of 2 to 102 billion for half of wages. The demographer pays with percentages of GDP in the 50s of this century. A direct comparison of these price lists without the layer misleads. [3] [9] Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext A cheap supplement of 500 koruna may be economically excellent as targeted support for a high age. The same amendment may be expensive as a substitute for an unfulfilled age cap, if it is read that way. An expensive return to half of wages may be unnecessary in a year of high inflation. It may be cheaper as fulfilment of a pledge, if it reduces the number of further amendments and disputes about confidence. The real price of the adopted text Measures contained + measures postponed + the calendar of the account + the price of the demographic path + the price of mistaking a headline for a law. The result is cheap only when it passes a check of gaps and can be defended with the same content in the programme and in the section. It is therefore useful to measure the price of an accepted pledge , not the price of a headline. Accepted means that the measure is in the text, has a date and does not serve as a screen for an item that is not in the text. 14. What to read in the bill before a verdict falls Reasonable reading does not begin with the word reform, but with the kind of pledge and the control mechanism. Need First place in the text Decisive test Unacceptable shortcut Fulfilment of the programme A table of pledge / section Cap 65 and 1/2 of wages “They approved an amendment” Income of eighty-year-olds Age steps 500 / 1 000 Kč Cap 3 000 Kč, date 1. 1. 2027 “Three thousand extra as of today” Work in retirement 1.5 % and the 6.5 % discount Effect 2028, self-employed versus employees “Already this year” Retirement age 155/1995 Coll. in force The trajectory towards 67 A headline about seniors The long account NRR, Ageing Report % of GDP in the 50s of this century, not 2.6 bn One number for everything Arduous occupations Whether they are in the text at all Does the second wave have a date? Silence = fulfilment For Czech use a separate generation test is necessary. An English Ageing Report will not measure whether a headline in Czech promises 65 to an eighty-year-old woman. The test set should contain the January programme, ČTK of 20 July, the retirement age in force, 2.6 billion with the reservation of a scenario, and a file in which the correct answer is “it is not in this wave”. What needs to be tested The first test concerns the title. The same word reform in the programme and in the amendment is not an identical experiment. The second concerns the calendar: 2027 for the supplement is not 2028 for work. The third concerns dropped items: whether they have a date of a second wave, or only a promise. A product that adds to a senior a month earlier need not be fulfilment of a pledge that concerned the retirement age. 15. Fourteen days from headline to section A position on the amendment can be assembled without waiting for 2050 and without impulsive agreement with a briefing. A short reading pilot is enough. The aim is not to prove that the government can add to seniors. The aim is to find the gaps in which the headline fails. Days 1–2: List the pledges of the programme and the rows of the July bill. Days 3–4: Separate the populations: 80+, working pensioners, cohorts towards 67, arduous occupations. Days 5–7: Mark each pledge: in the text / dropped / never entered / postponed. Days 8–10: Verify effect, the 2.6 bn scenario, the 2–102 bn scenario and what they belong to. Days 11–12: Open the retirement age in force and the NRR on 1.5 % versus 4 % of GDP. Day 13: Stress: confusion of print 50, confusion of 270/2023 Coll., confusion of the 6.5 % discount for a novelty. Day 14: Write down the reading rule and the date of the next review — after the Chamber, not after X. The pilot should have elimination conditions. For example: a single sentence that turns a 500 koruna supplement into a cap at 65, or the use of 2.6 billion as the price of the dropped indexation. A high average score of “the government approved something” must not override a gap whose impact the reader cannot accept. 16. Two prints, two amendments, two questions The Chamber of the 10th term sees in parallel deputies’ print 50 on pension insurance and the government wave of 20 July. The first shortens the insurance period and reaches for the child-raising increment. The second walks in age steps and work in retirement. The government expressed a negative opinion on print 50. Anyone who adds them into a “pension reform 2026” produces an object that is not in the register. [14] Act No. 270/2023 Coll. is an amendment from the previous term on indexation, later assessed by the Constitutional Court. The number can mislead, because media shortcuts and the memory of public debate easily join distinct documents. The July bill of 2026 must therefore be labelled as a government bill until the Chamber publishes its print number, and the number 270 left to the amendment of 2023. [13] OECD pension surveys show that parametric adjustments — age, indexation, work in retirement — are common and that they are often delivered in parts. Partiality is therefore not a Czech aberration. A Czech aberration would be to present a part as the whole of the programme of 5 January. [16] Analyses by IDEA at CERGE-EI describe that a shift of age and a change of indexation land differently by cohort, sex and the amount of the pension. [17] They do not thereby automatically assess the July bill. They do, however, recall the difference of target groups: a supplement from 80 aims at today’s high age, a cap at 65 at future retirement, and the indexation formula at the whole set of pensions paid. A bill containing only the first point may be a substantive change, but it does not thereby fulfil the whole programme. 17. Postponement changes political responsibility In pension policy it is not only the parameter that decides, but also the order of legislative steps. A pledge moved to a later phase may be deliberated in a different political situation than a bill approved today. The contest is therefore not only for the highest supplement. The contest is over which pledge enters the first wave, which the second, and which remains in the programme as an anchor. The more comfortable the headline that arises, the higher the price of leaving the impression that 65 is done. Cohorts, ČSSZ automatics and expectations are hard to reverse. People stop distinguishing their own entitlement from the product in which the government announced it. An age supplement may bring an earlier increase to people at a high age. Its benefit must not, however, conceal that the retirement-age cap and the indexation formula remained outside the first phase. The public therefore needs an overview of points contained and postponed, their legislative status and dates. A bill cannot be assessed by the breadth of its title or the number of pledges in a press sentence. What can be checked is whether its sections correspond to a specific measure and whether the missing points are visible, dated and politically acknowledged . At the moment when the government is merely adding 500 koruna at eighty, it is choosing a parameter. At the moment when it postpones the age cap, drops half of wages and transfers the account for work to 2028, it is also choosing a new structure of responsibility among generations. And then the question is no longer: “Did the government approve a pension amendment?” Let us ask: Which pledge already has a section and an effective date, which remains in a further phase, and which so far exists only in a political message? — Jiný Kontext

items.title: The October elections will take place without the new ISSV
items.subtitle: In October 2026 municipal councils and one third of the Senate are elected. The election administration information system, which was to carry candidate registration and the assembling of commissions, is by statute to be used only for elections held after 31 December 2027. The voter in the booth will not notice the change. The office will.

items.body: A paper ballot paper, an electronic candidate list and a cyber audit belong in different parts of the electoral process. October voting can take place according to the law even if the new agenda system is postponed. A valid candidate list, in turn, says nothing by itself about the strength of competition in a municipality, and a Chamber model does not describe the election of a mayor or a senator. What we know / What we do not know What we know: Act No. 108/2026 Coll. postponed the use of selected parts of electoral legislation linked to ISSV to elections held after 31 December 2027. The Ministry of the Interior states expressly that the municipal and Senate elections of 9 and 10 October 2026 will take place according to the existing procedures. On 26 August the CZSO published a continuously updated register of candidates and lists. [3] [4] [6] What we do not know: The public sources used in the article do not contain an independent final audit of ISSV readiness, nor complete data on the costs of postponement for individual offices. From the postponement itself it therefore cannot be inferred that the system was dangerous, nor that the existing procedures are without risk. 1. The ballot box and the agenda system are not the same Imagine an August meeting at the ministry. The election official wants paper and a data mailbox, because he knows them from previous elections and can stop a defective list on them. The system supplier wants live ISSV operation, because Act No. 88/2024 Coll. counted on it and postponement looks like an admission of inability. The cyber specialist wants postponement, because widespread testing, training and emergency procedures for an outage are not finished. The mayor of a small municipality wants calm: his secretary has no capacity to learn a new interface in the weeks when candidate lists are being filed. A commentator wants a “digital state”, because he regards paper as backwardness. A political scientist wants to warn against reading the mood of the Chamber from 22 552 municipal lists. At first glance this is a dispute about modernity. In reality each person is describing a different problem. The official compares a known procedure and judicial review. The supplier the timetable of the act. The cyber specialist resilience against attack and outage. The mayor the capacity of one office. The commentator a visible symbol. The political scientist the electoral system. Each participant in the meeting is judging a different part of the operation, so the mere date in the Collection does not prove the readiness of the whole chain. Under the label “digital elections” equality and secrecy of the vote, candidate registration, the staffing of commissions, audit, training, a fallback procedure and an error in a fixed statutory deadline are mixed together. First it is necessary to determine which part of election administration is being judged . Constitutional guarantees, the registration agenda, technical resilience and political commentary use different criteria. Elections are not software. Software is not a constitutional guarantee. And postponement is not proof that the vote is in danger. — Jiný Kontext 2. How the administration of the October elections is assembled When a citizen receives an envelope and ballot papers on Friday afternoon, it is easy to form the impression that “elections work”. The result, however, arises in a chain. Each layer can raise quality, lower it, or change the type of error. The same vote can be constitutionally in order and correctly exhausting. The same system can be usable in a laboratory test and not in the August peak of registrations. Five layers of one vote Constitutional framework: equality, secrecy, universality, judicial review and independent determination of the result. The electoral act of the given type: a municipality, the Senate and the Chamber do not measure the same contest. Agenda administration: filing of lists, verification of residence and age, staffing of commissions, methodology, training. Technical carrier: paper, a data mailbox, a portal, the population register, transmission to the CZSO. Reading of the result: statistics, commentary, a poll, and substitution of a municipality for the state. The Constitution and the electoral acts determine what is permitted. They do not, however, carry lists to the office or assemble a commission at midnight. Act No. 88/2024 Coll. on election administration was to transfer part of this work into an information system. Act No. 108/2026 Coll., promulgated on 25 June 2026 and effective from 26 June, postponed this applicability to elections held after 31 December 2027. [2] [3] [4] The Ministry of the Interior stated expressly that the October elections to municipalities and the Senate will run according to procedures known from previous elections. [4] This is not a theoretical dispute. The cut of layers determines where to turn when something fails. If a voter does not receive a ballot paper, polling-station logistics failed. If an office does not finish registration, the agenda failed, not the booth. If a portal falls during the deadline, the carrier failed — and it can also pull in a constitutional dispute about who was allowed to stand. The sentence “the elections failed” is the beginning of a diagnosis, not its end. Illustrative diagram: The same vote can, in a different layer, with a different carrier and a different reading of the result, mean a different dispute. Comparing the booth with the portal is the same error as comparing an engine with a timetable. A vote is produced across the whole admin chain An illustrative sequence from the constitution through the agenda and its carrier to how results are read. A vote is produced across the whole admin chain Constitution Statute Agenda Carrier Reading JINÝ KONTEXT Illustrative diagram: The chain separates the ballot box from the agenda system; it does not rate the delay or a particular office. 3. Which errors in election administration can still be corrected The benefit of digitalisation cannot be separated from the consequences of a specific error. A typing error in an agent’s form can be corrected within the deadline, but an outage of the portal on the last day of filing can hit the right to stand. An incorrectly recorded commission member can be replaced more easily than a registration of lists that has been challenged across the board. The Venice Commission, in the Code of Good Practice in Electoral Matters, proceeds from the point that elections are to be organised by impartial bodies and that rules are to be stable, intelligible and known in time. [11] OSCE/ODIHR in the handbook on observing election administration translates the same into operational language: administration is not only polling day, it is the whole cycle from registration to results. [12] It does not follow that paper is a virtue. It follows that a new carrier is judged by the type of failure, not by a date in a contract. Type of failure What it looks like How to test it What limits the harm Outage of the carrier The portal does not work in the filing deadline A fallback channel, a load test, a blackout Paper and a data mailbox with a known procedure Registration error A defective list passes or a valid one does not A check against the register, a deadline for correction, a court Review, a protocol, the same rule for all Commission error Members are missing, training is missing A pool of substitutes, a practice record CZSO and MoI methodology, a limited scope of the agent Reading error A municipality is read as the Chamber Separate the system, the constituency, turnout Do not combine incommensurable contests This also changes the question of postponement. We do not ask only whether the software “already knows a form”. We ask which system will fail in a way that the state will catch within the deadline. A creative team may tolerate ten unusable ideas. Election administration cannot tolerate a single unannounced outage on a day when the law counts hours. A slower agenda with a clear trail may better bear the guarantee of the vote than a timetable winner without a way back. The government commissioner for digitalisation, Lukáš Klučka, put it without ornament in June 2026: launch the system on time and risk problems that could undermine the course of the elections, or postpone it. The ministry chose the second variant. [5] This is a justification of one specific proposal of one institution, not proof that every IT postponement is a virtue. It does, however, show that the price of an error here is not aesthetic. It is constitutional. 4. What registration numbers say — and what they do not Numbers from a closed registration procedure are needed because they replace part of impressions with a count. The problem arises at the moment when one number begins to represent the whole of politics. On 26 August 2026 the Czech Statistical Office published the registers of candidates and lists for the elections of 9 and 10 October 2026. The registers are still updated until polling day according to the instructions of registration offices; this is not an election result. [6] [7] As of the date of publication the CZSO stated: 22 552 candidate lists were registered for municipal councils. Voting is to take place in 14 553 permanent polling districts ; in 5 021 of them Senate elections concurrently. In 1 842 municipalities voters will choose candidates of only one electoral party. In 3 municipalities the municipal elections will not take place, because a list was not filed or the number of candidates was insufficient. 154 candidates registered for the Senate (120 men, 34 women). Czech Television added that this is the lowest number since 1998; the CZSO itself does not present the comparison with 1998 in the cited registration report as a main figure, so this is a journalistic reading of a series, not a separate statement of the office. [6] [8] Each figure contains a hidden decision. A list is not the same as a mandate. One list in the municipality of Kateřinice in the Vsetín area, where the CZSO recorded 30 lists of one candidate each, is not the same as 24 lists in Prague with 1 060 candidates. [6] Senate constituency 27 Praha 1 with nine candidates is not the same as constituency 48 Rychnov nad Kněžnou with two. [6] [8] The number of 1 842 municipalities with a single party does not measure “the end of democracy”. It measures in how many municipalities a contest of more lists did not arise this time. It does not follow that elections there are invalid. It follows that the role of voting is different: confirmation of representation, not a choice between camps. Five facts without which a registration number is only a headline The exact type of election, the date registration closed, and whether it is a state as of an update. The unit: list, candidate, municipality, polling district, constituency. The size of the municipality and the number of council members being elected. Whether it is a single list, or an absence of elections. What the number does not measure: turnout, preferences, a Chamber majority. For the purchase of a political story, therefore, a small map of municipalities matters more than a foreign nationwide ranking of parties. Twenty real municipalities — with one list, with thirty lists, with a drop-out of candidates — will say more about October than one column in the Chamber. 5. Compare agendas, not the words of digitalisation The market in state systems can be described without a false ranking of winners. The following map does not say who is modern. It shows around what work the individual layers build a product, what kind of context they bring, and which failure the buyer — here the state — should deliberately look for during a trial. The state of functions changes; what decides is the current act, the methodology and the concrete account of the agenda. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Agenda Main working position What to verify before live operation Typical reason for the choice The citizen’s vote Paper, envelope, commission, CZSO Secrecy, counting, protocol ISSV did not introduce e-voting Filing of lists Paper and a data mailbox at the registration office Deadline, defects, ROB, court A known procedure after postponement Commissions Manual delegation by municipalities Substitutes, training, record A digital pool only after 2027 ISSV Portal, validation, coordination Test, cyber, blackout, training Less friction in registration Reading of results The CZSO’s encrypted programme Separation of types of election Do not mix a municipality and the Chamber The rows are not a judgment on the quality of officials. The same state offers more than one agenda and each may behave differently during a single electoral cycle. The map is meant to prevent a different error: that an excellent portal is bought in a product that will not bear the August peak, or that postponement is read as a challenge to the vote. Interpretive diagram: The position of the elements does not express a score. The scheme shows questions that must be answered together: the impact of an error, detection, reversibility, responsibility. Elections are not a software purchase Paper, ISSV, commissions and audit belong to administration, not to the booth. Elections are not a software purchase Paper ISSV Commission Audit Admin JINÝ KONTEXT Interpretive diagram: Elements do not express readiness; they connect places that the phrase digital elections mixes together. 6. ISSV: an advantage that is not bought with a date in the act Act No. 88/2024 Coll. on election administration introduced common rules of state administration of elections and with them the election administration information system. The act took effect on 1 January 2026. [2] The system was to enable electronic filing for agents, verify data against registers and coordinate the staffing of commissions. That is practical value that a pure test of “it knows a form” does not capture. Removing friction between the registry office, the population register and the list of commission members is work, not a slogan. Universality, however, also creates a new requirement. The user must know whether he is just using live operation, a practice mode, a fallback channel, or paper. Act No. 108/2026 Coll. postponed the applicability of key parts linked to ISSV to elections held after 31 December 2027. The Ministry of the Interior added that the system should first be used at the regular election of the president of the republic. [3] [4] [5] This is the plan of one institution in one press justification, not a constitutional certainty that in 2028 nothing will fail any longer. ISSV was not alone in the June package. The Ministry of the Interior proposed a shift also for the registry information system and for the electronic system for drafting legal rules. For all three projects it stated obstacles that the original timetables did not fully take into account. [5] It does not follow that three postponements prove the same thing. It follows that the state this time compared a deadline with resilience, not a deadline with prestige. What needs to be tested The first test concerns load in a real deadline: thousands of concurrent filings, not ten practice ones. The second concerns an outage: a blackout, DDoS, an identity outage, an outage of the link to the population register. The third concerns people: whether an official at an authorised municipal office can return a defect, print a document and switch to paper without the deadline collapsing. The fourth concerns the law: whether the procedure on failure of the carrier is in a decree in advance, not in a press release. For an individual who wants “an online candidate list at last”, integration may be decisive. For the organisation of the state the sentence “we have ISSV” is not enough. It needs to know the version, the owner of the data, the fallback channel, training, audit and the boundary beyond which a person must approve the result. 7. Postponement does not change the vote. It changes the work that prepares it For the voter, the booth does not change on 9 and 10 October 2026. The president of the republic called the elections by Decision No. 117/2026 Coll. Voting on the territory of the Czech Republic takes place on Friday from 14.00 to 22.00 and on Saturday from 8.00 to 14.00. [1] [2] A possible second round of the Senate falls on 16 and 17 October 2026. [8] ISSV was not entering this booth. It was not to introduce electronic voting. It was to carry administration. Area October 2026 regime after postponement How it would look with ISSV The citizen’s electoral act Paper ballot papers and envelopes No change in the booth Filing of lists A list or a data mailbox at the office An online form with validation Polling-station commissions Records of delegations at municipalities More central coordination of members Processing of results CZSO programme and procedures An extra administrative layer, not necessarily different counting The source of the comparison is the ministry leaflet for candidates and the information on postponement: candidate lists and applications for registration are not filed through ISSV. [4] [9] According to the ministry’s description, postponement does not change the way in which a voter in October 2026 hands in a paper vote. That by itself does not prove that no dispute about equality or registration can arise; it only means that these questions will be handled through the existing channels. For the state, postponement means that checks of lists, residences and commissions remain with people and with previously used procedures. Imagine two parallel illustrations, not a report. A voter enters a school on Friday at 14:30, receives an envelope, marks her neighbours, drops the envelope in. She has the feeling that the state is holding. The secretary of an authorised office in August copies lists from paper and data mailboxes, verifies data and hunts substitutes for commissions, because the postponed software will not take these acts. Both can be right about their layer. Neither describes the whole machine. 8. Paper is not nostalgia. It is a checkable trail Resistance to paper is often aesthetic. Paper is slow, heavy, repetitive. That is true and it is not the whole truth. A paper list with a stamp and a data mailbox with a delivery receipt give a trail that a court can read. The Supreme Administrative Court and the Constitutional Court have a long series of decisions on registration procedure and on review of elections: the dispute is about a deadline, a defect, equal treatment, not about whether the portal was modern. [16] [17] Digital filing can improve the same trail. It can also lose it in a log that nobody owns, in an interface that falls at night, or in automatic validation that rejects a valid candidate because of an error in the register. “A PDF can be uploaded” does not mean “it is auditable, reversible and intelligible to an agent in a municipality of 400 inhabitants”. Four-step check of the agenda Existence: the filing arrived and has a time stamp. Authority: the office is the one the law designated. Support: a specific defect rests on a specific provision, not on an impression from a screen. Scope: correction is possible within the deadline and the same for all. The most reliable working procedure therefore separates a new carrier from new law. First a table of acts, deadlines and fallback channels arises. Only then is paper switched off. For every automatic rejection it is recorded who will correct it. If the source cannot be opened or a passage of the act cannot be found, a claim is not promoted to a fact merely because the system formulated it neatly. Digitising administration is not e-voting Agenda work, a delay and a secret ballot are different objects. Digitising administration is not e-voting Admin Vote ISSV Delay Ballot Secrecy Split JINÝ KONTEXT Interpretive diagram: The sides are not a verdict on modernity; they separate office work from the act in the booth. 9. Cyber resilience is not a stamp. It is the whole flow The question “is the system secure?” is important, but too narrow. An organisation must know where identity runs, how long filings are kept, who has access to the population register, which third parties process hosting, and whether an outage of electricity or the network has a regime written in advance. “It passed a penetration test” — if such a test existed and were published — would still not mean “it will bear the day of the deadline”. A public audit of specific ISSV pentests as of June 2026 is missing from open sources as a separate document with a result; the ministry spoke of the need to finish widespread testing, strengthen cyber security, train users and prepare procedures for extraordinary events including a blackout. [5] Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext NÚKIB, in the summary report on the state of cyber security for 2023, describes pressure on the supply chain, geopolitically motivated attacks and the need for exercises. [13] Act No. 264/2025 Coll. on cyber security, effective from 1 November 2025, sets duties for providers of regulated services and a framework for managing cyber risks. [14] From the public materials of this article, however, it cannot be determined which specific parts, and in what regime, apply to ISSV. A reference to the act is therefore not proof that ISSV has the same legal regime as another critical service; it only supports the requirement to describe assets, suppliers and emergency procedures. The practical minimum is a map. It begins with the agent, continues with the office, identity, the register, hosting, the log, a backup, and ends at the place where a filing can be restored or paper accepted. Without this map a claim of resilience is a description of one part of the pipe. The cited SAI audit conclusion from 2008 on the Integrated State Treasury System described problems of timetable and management in another state IT agenda. [15] It is not an audit of ISSV, and one older conclusion does not authorise a claim that the same failure occurred here as well. It serves only as a reminder that a deadline, responsibility and a fallback procedure should be separate items in an audit. 10. Digitalisation of administration is not electronic voting Part of the public debate hears “election administration information system” as “we will vote on the phone”. The election administration act and the ministry materials do not support this substitution. ISSV was to administer candidate lists and commissions. It was not to replace the ballot box. [2] [4] [9] International standards add a second distinction. The Venice Commission and ODIHR assess electronic voting as a particularly sensitive change: transparency of counting, verifiability, trust. [11] [12] The Czech postponement of ISSV does not belong in this category. It belongs in the category that ODIHR describes as election administration: registration, logistics, training, continuity. To mix these two debates is to buy fear of e-voting for a decision that did not address e-voting. Postponement should equally not be mixed with illegitimacy. October 2026 runs according to electoral acts that courts can read: Act No. 491/2001 Coll. on elections to municipal councils and Act No. 247/1995 Coll. on elections to Parliament, as amended, and, in the scope unaffected by the postponement, also the election administration act. [2] [9] [10] Postponement changes the carrier of the agenda. It does not change the right to vote. For a European organisation that is digitalising registers, the placement of the system and the emergency regime may be more important than the last per cent in a project Gantt chart. “It can be launched on the deadline” does not mean “it is a finished electoral state”. Operation needs people, methodology, backups and a person who understands when to return to paper. A single identity outage can turn digital registration into non-registration. 11. A Chamber model does not measure a municipality. Nor the Senate In the pre-election period another substitution of objects regularly appears. Commentary takes a nationwide model for the Chamber of Deputies and reads October from it. That is honest only when the model claims that it measures a hypothetical Chamber. It is not honest when a forecast of mayors and senators arises from it. This is a crude misunderstanding of commensurability, not a dispute about which agency is decent. Chamber of Deputies: a proportional system, party brands, an electoral threshold. The act on elections to Parliament provides that only parties that exceed a set threshold are considered in the scrutiny; for a single party that is five per cent of the total valid votes. [10] Senate: 27 single-member constituencies in the given cycle, a two-round majority system, specific names, a second round, different turnout. The list of constituencies for 9 and 10 October 2026 was published by the Ministry of the Interior. [8] Municipalities: thousands of separate contests, accumulation of votes, associations of independents, coalitions that do not exist in a nationwide model. The political-science literature on Czech municipal elections repeatedly shows the strength of local lists and the weakness of reading a municipality as a mini-Chamber. [19] [20] Converting Chamber preferences into a gain of Senate seats or mayors is the same error as choosing company software according to a test the firm never runs. A nationwide trend can influence a local election. It is not identical with it. Three tests of political reading The first is systemic: which electoral act, which unit, which round? The second is about population: who is a voter in a municipality of 400 inhabitants and who is a respondent of a nationwide telephone poll? The third is temporal: the registration state from August is not the result from October. A product that answers a day earlier need not be better if a week later nobody can find out why it answered just so. 12. After postponement, different places are checked Before postponement it was checked whether the software would make August. After postponement it is checked whether paper and a data mailbox will bear the same agenda without a loss of equality. The act is navigation to a procedure. It is not automatic proof that the procedure will work. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext One amendment can combine three true sentences into an untrue conclusion. First: ISSV is being postponed. Second: elections are being held. Third: digitalisation is a priority of the state. Each sentence works, but the synthesis “the state has given up on elections” is methodologically wrong. At other times commentary uses a high-quality secondary text on cyber matters, even though a primary ministry leaflet is available on lists being filed the old way. [4] [9] The Constitution in Art. 102 provides that councils are elected for four years and elections are held at a time tied to the end of the term. [18] That is why October 2026 is not an optional project milestone. It is a calendar against which software either makes it, or must get out of the way. Postponement is in this sense an admission that the calendar is harder than a Gantt chart. Before switching on an enterprise assistant, over-shared folders are looked for in another field. Before switching on an election portal the same is looked for in another language: public test accounts, unfinished training, a missing owner of a document, substitution of search for an action that changes registration. The greatest advantage of digital administration need not be speed. It may be order in the data. The greatest weakness need not be an outage. It may be a true automatic rejection based on a figure that was true two years ago. 13. The price of a deadline is the price of a raw material, not the price of a result The market in state IT uses several price languages at once. A project pays milestones. An act pays dates. An office pays night shifts. A voter pays with trust that he does not know he is spending. A direct comparison of “we made the deadline” without knowledge of the working procedure therefore misleads. A cheap postponement can be economically excellent if it prevents a constitutional dispute. The same postponement can be expensive if it is repeated in two years with the same justification and nobody counts the human work of August 2026. Expensive live operation can be unnecessary for an agenda that paper will bear. It can be cheaper for a decision with a high price of error if it reduces the number of unsuccessful filings and checking work — but only when it can prove that with a test, not a slide. The true price of the accepted result Legislative deadline + development + tests + training + human checking + corrections + the price of a challenge + interruption of work + future migration. The result is cheap only when it passes polling day and can be defended in court. On the postponement proposal the ministry stated that postponement does not represent an increase in the financial costs of building the system. [5] That is a claim about a project budget item. It does not measure night work of secretaries, court disputes about registration, or the price of losing the 2028 deadline if postponement were repeated. It is one column of the bill, not TCO. It is therefore useful to measure the price by an accepted registration and an accepted polling-station record , not the price by a milestone. Accepted means that the act fulfilled the law, passed a check and did not cause a subsequent correction on a day when it is already impossible. 14. What to launch for which agenda A reasonable choice does not begin with the logo of a system, but with the type of work and the checking mechanism. The following recommendations are not a ranking of products. They are a signpost to a first pilot. In each category it makes sense to choose two regimes and compare them on the same data, in the same language and with the same budget of time. Need First group of candidates Decisive test Unacceptable shortcut A fair vote in the booth A verified paper procedure, commissions, CZSO Secrecy, counting, protocol Substitute ISSV for e-voting Registration of lists 2026 Paper and a data mailbox according to the MoI leaflet Deadlines, defects, court disputes Launch a portal without a fallback Commissions Manual delegation + methodology Staffing, training, record Assume that “someone will meet” Live ISSV after 2027 A portal + a paper brake Load, cyber, blackout, training Trust a date in the Collection without exercises Reading of October Separate maps of municipality, Senate, Chamber Unit, round, turnout Read a mayor from Kantar For Czech use a separate test of a small municipality is necessary. Prague City Hall will not measure whether the system preserves the meaning of a petition in a municipality where the agent is at the same time a firefighter and an accountant. The test set should contain a defective list, a coincidence of deadlines, a network outage and a text in which the correct answer is “the filing is returned for correction”. Some teams finally need more than one regime. One for registration, a second for commissions, a third for counting, a fourth for fallback. That is not a failure of digitalisation. It is the same decision as using a different tool for accounting and a different one for printing ballot papers. The condition is that the division is intelligible, data do not pass unchecked, and people know where final authority arises. 15. A short audit that will say more than a strategy The choice can be made without a six-year programme and without the impulse “launch because the act promised”. A short, disciplined audit before the presidential elections to which the ministry ties ISSV is enough. Its aim is not to prove that the portal can do something impressive. The aim is to find situations in which it fails, and to see whether administration can catch them. Fourteen days from impression to a decision on live operation Days 1–2: Write down 20 to 40 real acts of registration and commissions, their frequency, the price of an error and current time. Days 3–4: Prepare the same inputs, mandatory points and an anonymous scoring sheet. Days 5–7: Repeat every important act at least three times and keep a register of errors. Days 8–10: Verify the fallback channel, permissions, export, logs, deletion and a return to paper. Days 11–12: Calculate the price of an accepted act including checking and interruption of work. Day 13: Stress: a blackout, a contradictory register, an incomplete filing, an old figure, a forbidden action. Day 14: Decide according to the matrix, document the limits and set the date of the next review. Before live deployment in the cycle after 2027 Find a fallback channel that an official can use without training from the previous night. Determine the owner and the validity date of decisive data in the register. Separate search from actions that change registration. Introduce audit, approval and a trial group of municipalities, not only the centre. Verify that the agent sees from which state and version of a decision he is drawing. If possible the assessor should not know which regime created the act. For registration he watches lawfulness, completeness and the quantity of corrections. For commissions staffing and the record. For an outage the time to paper. Each failure is classified: carrier, register, permission, training, deadline. The pilot should also have elimination conditions. For example: a single unannounced loss of a filing, use of a forbidden figure, inability to export a record, or a situation in which the office does not know whether a list arrived. A high average score of an exercise should not override an error whose impact administration cannot accept. The last output is not only the name of the winning supplier. It is an operating rule: what the system is used for, what not, which data it may see, what a person must approve, how the result is verified and when the decision is opened again. Acts, tariffs and threats change. Without a review date even a good postponement gradually turns into a state superstition. 16. The most expensive thing can be lost trust in the next deadline ISSV is not to be only an electronic form. It is to connect the filing of candidate lists, data for commissions and an audit trail in a process whose statutory deadlines cannot be shifted at will. The contest is therefore not only about the best screen. It is about electoral context. About registers, permissions, methodologies, the habits of offices. The more comfortable the ecosystem that arises, the higher the exit price can be. Automata rely on proprietary steps and people stop distinguishing their own procedure from the product in which they built it. Integration can simplify the work of offices substantially, but it must preserve portable data and filings, a documented interface, a fallback procedure without a portal, and a regular test of readiness. The quality of a system is not decided by the number of modules nor by a timetable in a presentation. What decides is whether it covers the real agenda, whether an error can be found and corrected in time, and whether the fallback procedure protects electoral rights. The moment software only prints a list, the state is choosing an aid. The moment it reads the population register, decides on a candidate list and prepares a commission, it is also choosing a new structure of responsibility. And then the question is no longer: “When will we finally launch ISSV?” Let us ask: Which error will we see in time, who can correct it, and who will bear its price — the voter, the office, or the next deadline? — Jiný Kontext

items.title: Kantar estimates electoral support. One point is not the vote of the whole Czech Republic
items.subtitle: Television graphics show a point. The agency states a statistical error around it. A headline sometimes keeps the point and discards the uncertainty. An estimate for a defined population then becomes an overly certain judgment about the entire country.
