items.body: A house, an email, photos in the cloud and a seed phrase in a drawer are not interchangeable items from the point of view of inheritance. A notary can transfer a flat, but cannot technically transfer a password. The law can include a right in the estate, while a platform contract binds the account to a particular person. The GDPR does not itself apply to the data of the deceased, and without a key, a custodian or a legal title what remains of the cloud may be only a request to support. What we know / What we do not know What we know: Section 1475 of the Civil Code defines the estate as the entire property of the deceased, and Recital 27 GDPR leaves rules for the data of the deceased to the Member States. [1] [2] Google, Apple, Meta and Microsoft at the same time publish their own procedures for inactive or deceased users; we checked their status as of 31 August 2026. [4] [5] [6] [7] [21] What we do not know: This article is not a complete survey of all Czech court decisions, nor legal advice for a particular estate. It cannot be guaranteed in advance that a Czech resolution will open a foreign account, that a written wish will overcome contractual terms or the rights of third persons, or that today’s platform procedure will remain unchanged. For property, disputes or sensitive communication, verification with a notary or a lawyer and in the service’s current help pages is appropriate. 1. A cloud the notary does not see Picture probate proceedings in a district town. The notary wants to list the estate: a flat, a car, an account at a Czech bank, a share in a firm. The son asks for access to his father’s Google account, because the tax documents and ten years of family photographs are there. The daughter wants Facebook frozen as a memorial and WhatsApp left alone. The family’s lawyer cites the Civil Code and says that the estate comprises the entire property. The platform’s lawyer, who is not in the room and answers only from a support form, replies that the account is bound to a person, that private messages of third persons cannot be released and that without a custodian set in advance the data will after a time be deleted. The custodian of the cryptocurrency wallet, who is also not in the room, does not exist. There is only a seed phrase that the father told no one. At first glance this is a dispute about the decency of firms. In fact each person is describing a different object. The notary measures property rights that can be valued and recorded. The son measures practical access to a file. The daughter measures piety. The lawyer measures the Czech norm. The platform measures a contractual term, encryption and the American stored-communications statute. Cryptocurrency measures possession of a key. The family, the notary and the platform can thus each be solving a different part of the same problem. A death certificate that is enough for some property steps need not open a communications account. “Digital inheritance” is therefore only a shared name for different claims and obstacles: money, a licence, a memory, someone else’s secret, an encryption key and the rules for an inactive account. First it is therefore necessary to name what is actually to be handed on . A house, a personal licence, a letter from a third person and a safe without a combination are subject to different rules; there is no one universal procedure for them. An account is not a thing. A licence is not ownership. And a notarial resolution is not a password to the cloud. — Jiný Kontext 2. What altogether makes up a digital estate When it is said that after a person “data remained”, it is easy to form the impression that there is one box and one key. The result, however, arises in a chain. Each layer can give the heir something, take something away, or change the kind of loss. Two accounts with the same provider therefore need not end the same way. The same person may have a personal Gmail, a work Workspace and a telephone to which verification SMS messages arrive — and each of these trails lives in a different regime. Five layers of one digital estate Economic property: balances, claims, domains, monetised channels, tokens, codes for restoring a wallet. Licensed content: e-books, films, games, cloud subscriptions. The user often did not buy a thing, but a non-exclusive right to use an account. Personal archives: photographs, documents, unfinished texts, phone backups. Confidential communication: emails, chats, voice messages — including third persons who spoke with the deceased. Identity and administration: login, second factor, an estate contact, the contractual regime, the seat of the provider, the deletion period. The basic account determines an important part of the trail, but it is not the only actor. An application can encrypt data so that even the operator cannot read them. A company administrator can after an employee’s death close the account before the family manages to ask. The same photo can lie in iCloud, in Google Photos and on an SD card. The same message can be on a device, in a backup and in a service that may remove the account or the data after its published period of inactivity. The precise period depends on the service, the type of account and the current terms. This is precisely where the first error of public debate arises. A headline announces a contest of heirs with a corporation, but in fact it compares two entirely different things: a right to an estate and the ability to open a box. Or, conversely, it adds photos, chats and bitcoins into one “digital property” and expects one procedure. An honest comparison must state not only the service, but also the type of account, whether a custodian was set, whether data exist outside the cloud, whether it is someone else’s communication and whether a person holds the key, or only an algorithm. This is not a dispute about a password. The cut of the layers determines where to turn in a loss. If photos disappeared, the inactivity manager may have failed. If bitcoin disappeared, a paper with a seed phrase may have failed. If the platform refused a chat, a statute on the secrecy of messages may have held. The sentence “the firm will give us nothing” is the start of a diagnosis, not its end. 3. An estate is not the same as access to an account Czech inheritance law works with the transfer of property. Digital services work with the identity of the user. These two logics meet only sometimes. Property can be valued, listed and transferred. Access is a technical state: you know the password, you have the telephone, you can confirm an SMS, the platform recognises you as the designated custodian. One can inherit a claim against a bank and at the same time not have the password to internet banking — the bank, however, has a statutory duty to deal with the heirs. Conversely one can know the password to Instagram and still not have the right to go on using the account, because the terms forbid it and logging in as the dead person is a breach of contract. The difference is sharper for things that nobody “holds” apart from the key. Bitcoin continues to exist on the network. Without a seed phrase it is, however, economically dead in the same way as a safe whose combination nobody knows. The law is not enough here, because there is no one to sue for the release of the content. The network has no notary. The difference is still sharper for communication. An heir may have a legitimate interest in finding an invoice in an email. The same email contains letters of people who spoke with the deceased in the trust that the addressee, not his son, would read them. A platform that refuses to release an entire mailbox need not merely be stubborn. It may be protecting third persons. It may also be covering its own operational convenience. Both things can look the same. They are not the same. That is why the sentence “data are inherited” is a dangerous shortcut. Some data behave like a thing. Some like a loan. Some like someone else’s letter. Some like a lock for which the key exists only once. Without this distinction the family asks for everything and the platform refuses everything. Both sides then have the feeling that the other is lying. A notarial resolution is in this dispute a strong paper only where there is an addressee with a duty to perform: a bank, the land registry, a debtor. With a platform that regards itself as a guardian of someone else’s communication, the same resolution is only an attachment to a form. It may be enough for deactivation. It need not be enough for an export. The difference is not recognised from the stamp. It is recognised from the help pages that the deceased did not read in life. 4. Purchased content may be only a personal licence The market in digital content speaks the language of purchase. A button may say “buy a book”, “buy a film” or “buy an album”, but it does not itself say whether the entitlement is transferable to an heir. That must be verified in the current terms of the particular service. A user may have an entitlement to read, listen to or download the content without obtaining transferable ownership comparable to a book on a shelf. For a particular e-book or film the result therefore cannot be determined without the contractual terms, the manner of acquisition and any copy outside the account. Copyright law regulates the transfer of the author’s economic rights to heirs. [15] That does not, however, by itself show that a consumer’s licence to a work purchased in a catalogue is transferred in the same way. These are two different legal situations and the second must be assessed according to the particular contract. The same map misleads for a subscription. A family can pay for months for a cloud that nobody will open any more, because the payment card lives longer than the user. Or, conversely, it loses a terabyte of photographs because the subscription falls and the storage empties after a period. The price list here measures access in life. It does not measure what happens when access disappears. An honest reading of a licence therefore requires four figures without which “purchase” is only an advertising word: whether it is a thing or an entitlement; whether the entitlement is bound to a person; whether a copy exists outside the account; whether the provider has a procedure for heirs, or only for deletion. 5. The Czech code sees property. It does not see a password The Czech Civil Code in Section 1475 proceeds from the principle that the estate comprises the entire property of the deceased — the aggregate of their property rights and duties. The exception is rights and duties bound exclusively to the person, unless they were recognised as a debt or asserted in life. [1] This sentence will carry a flat, a car and a claim. It carries less well an account that according to the terms “is not transferable”, and still less well a password that nobody wrote down. In the cited Czech sources we did not find a special institute of a digital will that would by itself bind a foreign platform to release content against its terms. That is not, however, a claim that such a result cannot be brought by a particular contract, court decision or other legal title. [3] [18] Personality protection does not, moreover, disappear entirely with death. Under Section 82, close persons may defend the human dignity of the deceased. [1] That is a tool against misuse of a name, likeness, reputation. It is not an automatic key to Gmail. It can more readily prevent a profile from becoming a stage than compel a profile to become an archive. The cited Czech legal commentaries distinguish property digital assets, the accounts themselves and practical access to data. The result depends on the nature of the right, the provider’s terms and whether the data exist in a form that can be released. [3] [18] A cryptocurrency asset can be part of the estate and still remain inaccessible without a private key. An email can contain property documents and still remain closed because of other people’s messages. The code is therefore not powerless over everything. It is blind where the subject of the estate is not in the land registry, in a bank or in a safe, but in the relation between a login, a cipher and a foreign contract. The blindness is not recognised at the notary. It is recognised three months later, when support answers with a template. 6. The GDPR protects the living. The dead it leaves to the states Many people mistakenly believe that their digital privacy after death is protected by the European GDPR regulation. The text of the regulation is more sober. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Recital 27 provides that the regulation does not apply to the personal data of deceased persons and that Member States may lay down rules for the processing of such data. [2] That does not mean that the data of the dead are freely available. It means that Union protection of personal data as subject rights ends with death. The further regime depends on national law, on the contract with the provider and on the rights of people whose data remain in the account — addressees, senders, people in photographs. According to the cited sources Czechia has no special statutory regime of a digital will comparable to the French post-mortem directives; what applies in particular are general inheritance law, personality protection, the contract and the rules of the service. [1] [3] [18] France, in the Informatique et Libertés act, allows a person in life to determine directives on the retention, erasure and communication of data after death; the supervisory authority CNIL explains this regime publicly. [14] [22] The difference is not that the French “have the GDPR even after death”. It is a special national arrangement following on from the space that Recital 27 leaves to the Member States. Caution is needed in the opposite direction as well. The absence of the GDPR for the dead does not entitle heirs to ask for everything. In the account live the data of the living. A message that a colleague sent is their communication. A photograph on which a neighbour appears is also their likeness. A provider that refuses a blanket release of a mailbox may rely precisely on these third persons. It may also rely on its own term. The first reason is legal. The second is contractual. Without distinguishing both, the impression arises that “Europe does not protect the data of the dead, therefore it must release them”. Recital 27 did not carry such a sentence. 7. An American wall in front of a Czech resolution A number of large platforms are seated in the United States and apply the federal Stored Communications Act to the content of communication. The act limits when a provider may release the content of a mailbox to someone other than the user. [12] A Czech resolution on an estate is in this text not an automatic consent of the user. An American court and a provider need not read from it an authorisation for a full release of emails. Microsoft, for personal accounts, distinguishes two situations. A user can in advance set OneDrive Digital Legacy: a trusted contact, after verification by a code, a request and a waiting period, obtains read-only access to files on OneDrive. [21] If this tool was not set, Microsoft in its procedure for deceased users describes a formal legal path and does not expressly guarantee the release of content. It also points to the life cycle of inactive accounts. [7] The particular result therefore depends on the prior setting, the type of data and the legal regime. X (formerly Twitter) is still narrower. The official procedure contemplates a request to deactivate a deceased person’s account. Access to the account, the password or an archive of private messages the firm, according to its help pages, does not provide regardless of kinship. [8] The family can therefore let the account disappear. It cannot inherit it as a diary. This wall is not proof that Czech law “does not apply”. It is proof that enforceability runs into a foreign statute, the seat of the defendant and the price of an international dispute. For a mid-sized estate a lawsuit in California is often more expensive than the value of the photographs the family is looking for. The platform knows this. The family finds it out late. American states are in the meantime trying to build a bridge from the other side. The model Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act gives fiduciaries — estate administrators — a framework for access to digital assets, if the state has adopted it. [17] Even that, however, does not automatically open an encrypted chat or erase a conflict with the federal communications statute. It is a map of domestic fiduciary law. It is not a key to a Czech Gmail. 8. Germany inherits the account. France gives directives The comparison shows that the same European Recital 27 does not lead to the same result. The German Federal Court of Justice on 12 July 2018 decided in case III ZR 183/17 that a contract for a user account on a social network passes to the heirs by way of universal succession under Section 1922 BGB. The heirs have a claim to access to the account including the communications content. Telecommunications secrecy, post-mortem personality rights and data protection did not, according to the court, bar this access. A provision on a “memorial state” that in fact made access impossible the court did not recognise as an effective obstacle to inheritance. [13] The analogy was sober: digital letters are not to be inherited differently from paper ones. France took another path. The law for a digital republic and Article 85 of the Informatique et Libertés act allow a person in life to determine what is to happen with their data after death: retain, delete, communicate, appoint an executor. If there is no directive, heirs have more limited entitlements to acts needed for the settlement of the estate and for the protection of memory. [14] [22] The state here does not build an automatic claim to the whole of Facebook. It builds an instruction given in advance. In the cited Czech sources we did not find an equally unambiguous precedent of the BGH type, nor a special regime of French post-mortem directives. That is not proof that no relevant Czech decision exists; a complete case-law survey exceeds this article. For the practical result, therefore, besides the general code, much depends on what the user set in life and what the platform currently allows. An international comparison is not a ranking of civilisation. It is proof that Recital 27 is a beginning, not an end. Whoever reads from it that “in Europe the dead have no data” reads wrongly. Whoever reads from it that a Czech resolution will open iCloud reads equally wrongly. 9. Platform rules determine the practical procedure The operating rules of a service often decide what practical procedure a bereaved person will have available. Tools exist, but they must be set in advance and their possibilities are not identical with inheritance law. Platform Tool in life What an heir usually obtains What they usually do not obtain Google Inactive Account Manager: inactivity of 3, 6, 12 or 18 months, up to 10 contacts Data that the user selected in advance What they did not order to be shared; the account can after long inactivity disappear even without a plan [4] Apple Legacy Contact and an access key Available account data after presentation of the key and a death certificate Keychain data and licensed media; without an access key the result depends on another legal procedure [5] Meta A designated person / memorialisation Administration of a memorial, sometimes deletion Private messages. A memorialised account is a pious state, not a mailbox [6] Microsoft OneDrive Digital Legacy with a trusted contact designated in advance After a code, a request and a waiting period, read-only access to files on OneDrive Outlook, passwords and other services; without a prior setting the release of content is not guaranteed [7] [21] X Nothing Deactivation after verification Access, an archive, private messages [8] The key problem is not that the tools would not exist. It is that they must be switched on in advance. Google describes a plan for the event of inactivity and at the same time a separate policy for long-term inactive personal accounts. [4] Apple requires a Legacy Contact access key and a death certificate; the tool will not, for example, make Keychain data available. [5] Microsoft offers a trusted contact limited access to OneDrive. [21] Meta and X have their own, narrower procedures. [6] [8] Two similar accounts can have a different regime The same person often has a personal Gmail, a work Workspace and an account on a telephone that the firm manages through MDM. A private photo gallery and a work drive are not the same legal subject. A pilot of “what happens after death” must therefore record in which profile it is being tested, who is the administrator of the domain and whether the terms are consumer or enterprise. Otherwise the family tests the help pages for a natural person and by mistake presents them as the regime of an employee account that the IT department will switch off within a week. The practical result is therefore determined not only by the logo of the service, but also by the type of account, its configuration and the current terms. 10. Four kinds of failure that an account can hide A demand that a system “hand data to the family” is too broad. For each item it is necessary to assess whether the loss can be detected in time, remedied and what impact it has. A deleted public post, the only export of a wedding, a lost private key and an unauthorisedly released conversation of someone else represent four different kinds of harm. Type of failure What it looks like How to test it in life What limits the harm Loss of access A password, an SMS code, a blocked telephone Try restoration without a SIM and without the second factor An inactivity manager, emergency access in a password manager, a local backup Loss of a licence “Purchased” content cannot be transferred Read whether it is a licence bound to a person A copy where the law allows it; do not rely on the shop catalogue Loss of a key A wallet without a seed phrase Practise the procedure only with an empty test wallet; restore a production seed only by a verified procedure on trusted hardware or an offline device Separate storage of the phrase, not in the same cloud Interference with other people’s messages An heir reads letters of third persons Separate documents from conversation already in the archive An express instruction as to what to release and what to delete Alongside the possibilities of the platform, what decides is whether the family knows about the account at all, whether data can be exported before the period expires and whether the loss will strike family memory, legal evidence, or irreversible capital. A service with a clearly set contact and a local backup can be more usable for a family than a comfortable cloud without a recovery plan. What decides is whether the bereaved know about the account, understand the official procedure and can react before the currently valid inactivity period. 11. 2FA protects the account; an estate needs recovery Two-factor authentication is an important protection of an account and because of an estate it should not be switched off or weakened. The risk arises when there is no safe and previously tested way of recovery. A bereaved person may know the password, but may not have the original telephone, SIM, backup code or authority to take over the account. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext End-to-end encryption in messengers means that the operator cannot read the content of personal messages. WhatsApp states this expressly; with an optionally end-to-end encrypted backup it moreover cannot restore a lost password or a 64-digit key. [20] Apple, for Legacy Contact, does not make data stored in Keychain available. [5] This is a property of privacy protection that at the same time limits the possibilities of recovery. Cryptocurrencies are a pure form of the same problem. The network does not know the deceased. What is known is only an address and a signature. Whoever holds the key holds the property. Whoever does not hold it has no one to ask for an exception. A notary can here record that “a wallet” was part of the estate. They cannot compel the blockchain to change the mathematics. A right to a thing and possession of a key diverge here more sharply than with a flat. A flat can be opened by a locksmith with a court order. An address on the network a locksmith will not open. Backup codes stored only in a telephone that itself holds the second factor are not independent recovery. The same applies to a seed phrase stored only in an account whose Keychain Legacy Contact will not open. A safe plan therefore separates active login credentials, backup codes and an instruction for the authorised person. Recovery can in life be safely tried on a clean device without the original SIM, but only within the bounds of the service’s terms and without sharing active passwords or private keys. For cryptocurrencies it is safer to verify the procedure on an empty test wallet; a production seed should not be entered into someone else’s device or made available to another person during the trial. An unsuccessful test is a signal to adjust the plan, not a reason to weaken 2FA. 12. A private message is not a family album Family photographs and tax documents are one kind of trail. A chat with a doctor, a lover, a debtor or a friend from military service is another. The first can reasonably be wanted as part of family memory and of proof. The second is correspondence in which the sender need not have counted on an heir reading it. The German BGH accepted the analogy with paper letters and in the given matter decided on the heirs’ access to the account including communication. [13] Meta and X, in their estate procedures, do not make private messages available. [6] [8] For a Czech case the result cannot be derived only from these three examples; it depends on the law, the contract, the kind of data and the particular procedure of the service. An instruction in life can make the family’s wishes clear: an archive of photographs and documents can be backed up and its custodian determined, while for conversations it can be recorded whether the person wishes their retention or erasure. Such an instruction does not, however, by itself transfer other people’s rights, replace the consent of further participants in the communication or necessarily overcome the terms of the service. The secrecy of electronic communications in the Czech Electronic Communications Act protects the confidentiality of communication. [19] It does not itself determine whether and in what scope an heir is to obtain a cloud archive. A written wish can help the bereaved, but the final procedure must respect the law, the contractual terms and the privacy of other people. The separation of albums and conversations can be done cheaply in life: an export of photographs to a disk, a folder of documents, an express ban on reading chat. After death the same separation is expensive or impossible, because the platform sees one account. The notary sees one estate. Neither sees the layers. 13. Necrobots: a memory that starts to answer With generative AI the question of the trail shifts from access to an account to use of the trail. From preserved emails, chats and recordings a system can be built that answers in the style of the deceased. The literature on the so-called digital afterlife and on deathbots notes a double pressure: the dignity of the dead as an informational body and the vulnerability of mourners, who may mistake a simulation for a continuation of the relationship. [11] [16] Öhman and Floridi propose that digital remains not be taken only as capital to be mined. They propose an analogy with human remains in collections: dignity bars their being a mere means of profit. [11] That is not a legal claim in a Czech judicial senate. It is a warning that a consent that can no longer be given cannot be replaced by the fact that the data “technically remained”. The question is therefore not only whether a chatbot helps in grief. It is who may build the model, from what data, with what ban on commerce and with what right of close persons to switch the model off. Section 82 of the Civil Code gives close persons a tool to defend the dignity of the deceased. [1] It does not say whether a simulation of a voice is an interference. It says that the dispute will be conducted over piety, not over the GDPR. The GDPR is silent for the dead. [2] A written instruction can document whether a person wished, or did not wish, posthumous use of voice and texts. It is not, however, an automatic guarantee of enforceability: the maker of the system must, besides the wish of the deceased, deal with the rights of living persons, copyright, contracts and possible personality protection. With a simulation of the deceased the dispute does not concern only access to data, but also piety, consent and the possibility of switching the system off. Recital 27 GDPR does not itself resolve this situation. [2] From the cited sources a comprehensive Czech regime of posthumous avatars cannot be inferred; a particular case would require a separate legal assessment, among other things according to personality protection and the rights of living persons. 14. Two brothers, the same father, the opposite lock The deceased: a father died suddenly. For ten years he documented the life of the family exclusively by telephone. He stored photographs in a cloud with two-factor authentication on a number that after death the operator blocked. Tax PDFs lay in the same account. A bitcoin wallet had a seed phrase in a phone note, not on paper. Facebook had no designated person. Google Inactive Account Manager was not switched on. Brother A knows the password to the email. He does not know the code from the SMS. Password recovery therefore gives him nothing. A login from a new telephone asks for the second factor, which lies in a dead device. Brother B asks the support of the individual services and attaches a Czech death certificate and a resolution on the estate. The result cannot be determined in advance in one sentence: Microsoft without Digital Legacy set describes a formal legal procedure and does not guarantee release, Facebook offers memorialisation without access to private messages, and for a cryptocurrency without a recovery phrase there is no central operator who would replace the key. [6] [7] [12] The result is not a dramatic exception. It is the sum of unset layers. Thousands of photographs and video recordings can disappear after the deletion of an inactive account. Tax documents remain in limbo until the family obtains them from the senders. Bitcoin remains at an address that everyone can see and no one can sign. The two brothers are not, moreover, conducting a dispute about love for their father. They are conducting a dispute about which object they want to open. One wants an album. The other wants a wallet. The platform will open neither, because the father did not open the settings that serve for that. The notary can record that “digital property” was part of the estate. She cannot carry it out of a data centre. 15. What to set before the account falls silent A reasonable preparation does not begin with a list of passwords in a drawer. It begins with a map of the layers and a decision as to which layer is to be handed on, which deleted and which remain unreadable. Passwords in an unsecured file are moreover a risk in life. A password manager with emergency access is something else: the designated person obtains access after a set period, not at once. Need First step Decisive test Unacceptable shortcut Family photos and documents A local backup plus a cloud custodian Recovery on someone else’s computer without your SIM “It is in iCloud, they will somehow give it” A Google / Apple account Inactive Account Manager, Legacy Contact, a safely stored access key The contact knows where the key is and understands the official procedure Only a death certificate without a prior setting Social networks A designated person, or an express order to delete The family knows your choice of piety / erasure The assumption that Facebook “will do it decently” Cryptocurrencies and 2FA Separately and safely stored recovery data A procedure verified on a test account or an empty wallet A production seed in the telephone that holds 2FA Licences and subscriptions A list of what will lapse, the card that goes on paying Cancellation of payments, export where possible The myth that a “purchase” is inherited like a book An AI simulation of a voice A written ban, or written consent Close persons know what they must not upload into a model Silence and a later dispute about piety For Czech use a separate language test is necessary. A death certificate from the registry office is not a “court order” from Microsoft’s help pages. An Apple “Legacy Contact” is not the same as an heir under the code. “Memorialisation” is not an archive. The test set should include diacritics in names, Czech documents, a work versus a personal account and the sentence “the source is not enough”, if the help pages promise only deletion. What needs to be set The first examination concerns the existence of accounts. A family cannot ask for what it does not know about. The second concerns destination: who is the contact, whether they have the key, whether they know that they are it. The third concerns a copy outside a single cloud. The fourth concerns money that has value only with a key. The fifth concerns what, conversely, should not be released. Without the fifth layer, “open everything” is as crude as “delete everything”. Some households ultimately need several regimes. One archive for children, a second ban for social networks, a third safe for keys. That is not a failure of simplicity. It is the same decision as having a different key to the flat and a different one to the safe. The condition is that the division be intelligible and that a single fire, a single SIM and a single cloud not decide everything at once. 16. A test that says more than a death certificate Preparation can be done without a lawyer in California and without the illusion that “it will somehow work out”. A short, disciplined attempt is enough. Its aim is not to prove that platforms are evil. The aim is to find places where access will fail, while the failure can still be repaired. Fourteen days from impression to a plan Days 1–2: Write down services, devices, wallets, subscriptions and what is only in one cloud. Days 3–4: Separate property, licences, archives, other people’s messages and keys. Days 5–7: Switch on the native tools of Google, Apple, Meta or Microsoft according to the service used. Store access and recovery data separately and safely. Days 8–10: Verify the recovery procedure on a test account or an empty wallet; do not enter a production seed or an active password into someone else’s device. Days 11–12: Store the list with a notary or in a safe. Bare passwords in open text do not belong in the list unless the safe protects them. Day 13: Write down what is to be deleted, what memorialised and what must not enter an AI model. Day 14: Tell the designated person that the task belongs to them, and set a date for the next review. Three tests of whether an heir will actually get the data The first is identitary: will the platform recognise the designated person without your SIM? The second is of content: will they get an album, or only the possibility of administering or deleting the account? The third is of time: will the procedure finish before the currently valid inactivity period of the given service? Periods differ by platform and type of account, therefore they should not be replaced by one universal number. The test should verify whether an independent path of recovery exists, not circumvent the second factor. A trial on a test account without the original telephone will show whether backup codes are safely available and whether the designated person understands the official procedure of the service. The last output is not a list of passwords on a slip. It is an operating rule: which trails are handed on, which are deleted, who bears the key, what is pious and what is evidence in a tax proceeding. Accounts, tariffs and help pages change. Without a date of revision even a good plan turns into a family superstition. 17. Photographs and legal supporting documents can both be lost In online accounts today there lie not only memories, but also invoices, contracts, school correspondence, health attachments and data needed for access to property. The loss of an account can therefore strike a family archive and practical proof. Platforms therefore determine not only comfort in life, but also the place where important supporting documents may remain after death. A family can, alongside an album, lose a document for a tax proceeding, a bill for a house or a digital asset. The scale of the topic is shown by CZSO data: in 2025, 7.7 million people aged over 16 used the internet, that is 88 % of this population, and 90 % of households were connected to the network; among senior households it was 60 %. [9] From these numbers, however, it cannot be established how many people actually have an estate contact set or a safe recovery plan. A cloud can keep data that would disappear on a single device. Important documents, however, need a portable backup, a designated authorised person, safely separated recovery data and a clear wish concerning private communication. A safe plan does not automatically hand over the entire account, nor does it delete everything. It separates property, a family archive, licensed content, other people’s communication and access keys and for each part respects the law and the current procedure of the service. At the moment when only a holiday lies in the cloud, we are choosing an album. At the moment when documents, keys and ten years of other people’s messages lie there, we are choosing a structure of accountability. And then the question is no longer: “Will the family inherit our account?” Let us ask: Which trails do we want to hand on, which to delete, who may obtain access to them — and whether for this choice there exists a safe and legally usable procedure? — Jiný Kontext

items.title: What a study says about a medicine’s benefit for a particular patient
items.subtitle: A clinical trial usually compares groups. A decision for a particular person therefore requires, besides the relative effect, baseline risk, absolute benefit, possible harms, duration of treatment and the patient’s preferences.

items.body: A prescription, a relative reduction and the probability of benefit for one patient are three different figures. A study may be methodologically sound, yet its average transfers to a particular person only with regard to diagnosis, baseline risk, other illnesses, concurrent medicines and the follow-up period. A large relative difference may moreover correspond to a small absolute benefit. What matters is to establish for whom we have evidence, which outcome the treatment changes, and how both benefit and possible harms will be monitored . What we know / What we do not know What we know: Randomised trials estimate an average difference between groups, not a certain outcome for an individual. For cardiovascular prevention NICE recommends discussing absolute risk and absolute benefits and harms, and starting a statin after an informed discussion. [5] For depression it distinguishes less and more severe states, offers several treatment options, and when antidepressants are stopped it recommends a gradual dose reduction agreed with the prescribing clinician. [22] What we do not know: Without a diagnosis, examination, a specific product, dose, other medicines and health status, neither a personal benefit nor the cause of a new symptom can be determined. An improvement or a difficulty cannot at a distance be labelled placebo, nocebo or an adverse effect. This text is not a guide to starting, stopping or changing a dose. Safety: Do not change prescribed treatment, or stop it abruptly, on the basis of an article; agree the next step with a doctor or pharmacist. Abrupt withdrawal of antidepressants can trigger even serious discontinuation symptoms. [22] In a severe or rapidly worsening condition, unconsciousness, breathing difficulty, chest pain or an immediate risk of self-harm, call 155 or 112. 1. A prescription that promises more than a study can carry Imagine a morning ward round in a Czech hospital. The cardiologist wants a statin because a patient after a heart attack has a high absolute risk of a further event. The general practitioner hesitates with another person of the same age, an athlete with mildly raised cholesterol, because they do not want to treat a laboratory number. The clinical pharmacologist asks about other tablets, about the liver and about which enzyme even activates the medicine. The nurse reports that patients complain about their muscles and about the package leaflet. The quality manager wants it documented that care is “lege artis”. The patient, who is only half present in the room, wants to hear the sentence: this will protect you . At first glance this is a dispute about whether “statins work”. In fact each person is describing a different object. The cardiologist measures population benefit at high risk. The GP weighs the benefit and burden of primary prevention. The pharmacologist assesses metabolism and interactions. The nurse catches a muscle problem whose cause cannot be determined without clinical assessment. The manager measures a process. The patient needs to understand the degree of uncertainty in plain language. Each member of the round may therefore work with a different, legitimate figure, and a shared conclusion for the patient may still be missing. “Efficacy” is not one unchanging property of a tablet; it includes relative and absolute difference, baseline risk, possible harms, interactions and the clinical importance of the outcome being followed. The first task is therefore to determine which treatment outcome is being assessed : a laboratory change, relief of a symptom, an averted event, or an adverse effect. These outcomes are not interchangeable. A relative miracle may be an absolute drop. The patient does not sit in the study average. They sit in their own body. — Jiný Kontext 2. What an effect estimate is made of When the screen shows “the medicine reduces risk by 30 %”, it is easy to get the impression that the tablet switches the illness off in thirty cases out of a hundred. The result, however, arises in a chain. Each layer may enlarge the benefit, shrink it, or change the type of error. Two patients with the same prescription therefore need not receive the same treatment. The same medicine may behave differently according to baseline risk, the liver, concurrent tablets and whether we are even measuring the right endpoint. Five layers of one effect Molecule and mechanism: what the medicine does in the body if it reaches its target. Population evidence: a randomised trial, the relative and absolute difference against the comparator. [1] [7] The patient’s baseline risk: the same relative reduction gives a different person a different absolute benefit. The fate of the medicine in the body: absorption, enzymes, interactions, age, kidneys, adherence. Context and follow-up: placebo and nocebo, the natural course, monitoring, withdrawal, reporting of harm. [4] [10] The pivotal trial determines an important part of the certainty, but it is not the only input. Expectations can change how a symptom is experienced, yet a new difficulty cannot without examination be attributed to the leaflet rather than the medicine or another cause. The result is also affected by how the patient differs from the study population, by drug interactions, by dose and by the actual pattern of use. This is where the first error of public debate arises. The headline announces a duel of “medicines save lives” and “medicines do not work”. In fact it compares two layers: a relative reduction in an ideal cohort and the absolute benefit in a person at low risk. Or, conversely, it adds relief from the visit, the retreat of a viral illness and the effect of the molecule into one “the medicine worked”. An honest comparison must state not only the name of the active substance, but also the population, the period, the endpoint, the absolute difference and what the study did not measure. Distinguishing these influences determines the next clinical step. When a laboratory value does not change, the clinician addresses, among other things, use, dose, interactions and the biological response. When a difficulty appears, they must assess possible adverse effects as well as other causes; nocebo cannot safely be assumed from timing alone. And the occurrence of an event does not by itself prove that preventive treatment had no population effect. 3. The study average is not the body in the consulting room Randomised controlled trials are an important tool for assessing the efficacy of medicines; the appropriateness of blinding and the further form of the evidence depend on the question and the type of intervention. [15] As early as 1996 Sackett and colleagues recalled that evidence-based medicine links the best available evidence with clinical experience and the patient’s values. [1] The average result of a group is important, but it is not enough for an individual decision. The result of a trial is a difference between groups. The group with the medicine fared, on average, better than the group without it. Inside the average, however, lies heterogeneity that the consulting room does not see until it looks for it: people with a large benefit, people with a small benefit, people with no measurable response, people with harm and no benefit. At the moment of signing the prescription the clinician does not know which of these four groups the particular person belongs to. They know only how groups that resemble the patient in a few baseline features fared — and that often do not resemble them in age, in the number of diagnoses and in the number of other boxes. CONSORT and GRADE therefore require that evidence also be described by its limits: who was included, who was excluded, what the interval of uncertainty was, how serious the outcome was, how direct the analogy to the consulting room is. [13] [14] That is not bureaucracy. It is an admission that statistical significance may be a precise answer to a question this patient did not ask. For a decision the size of the average effect is not enough. One needs to know whether the effect can be monitored for the given indication, how quickly harm can be caught, and whether the aim is relief of a symptom, a laboratory marker, or prevention of a serious event. The choice therefore rests on the whole balance of benefits and risks, not on a single ranking on a poster. 4. Relative and absolute risk can read differently Pharmaceutical communication and media headlines often speak in relative risk reduction . It sounds impressive. Gigerenzer and colleagues showed that patients, journalists and clinicians systematically overestimate this figure if they do not know the baseline risk and the absolute difference. Informed consent then takes place in a fog. [2] A didactic example that is not a citation of one particular study, but the arithmetic of the same illusion: in the group without treatment, 2 people out of 100 have the event being followed (risk 2 %), in the group with the medicine, 1 person out of 100 (risk 1 %). The report sounds: the medicine reduces risk by 50 %. The fact for the person in the waiting room sounds: the absolute reduction is one percentage point . Of a hundred people treated, the event being followed fails to occur in one extra person. Ninety-nine of the others would either not have had the event, or will have it even with the medicine. The relative miracle and the absolute drop are the same data. They differ in the frame. Gigerenzer therefore asks for a different language: absolute risks, natural frequencies, a clear reference class. A “25 % reduction” in screening may mean that one fewer woman dies out of a thousand. Without a denominator the percentage is an advertising word. [2] Welch, Schwartz and Woloshin in their book on overdiagnosis show the same trap in early detection: higher “survival” need not mean a longer life if only the moment at which the illness is named is shifted. [9] An honest figure therefore needs five items, without which “30 % less” is only a poster: which event, which population, which period, which baseline risk, which absolute difference. If a single one is missing, an impression remains. 5. What NNT says and what it does not To get medicine out of the trap of relative figures it uses NNT (number needed to treat) and NNH (number needed to harm). NNT is the reciprocal of the absolute risk reduction: how many people need to be treated for a given period for one of them to gain the benefit being followed. NNH says the same sentence about harm. [2] NNT is not a property of a molecule like a melting point. If baseline risk changes, NNT changes, even if the relative effect remains similar. A person after a heart attack and a healthy person with a mildly off laboratory number therefore cannot share “the NNT of statins” as a single score. They can share the same active substance and receive an entirely different account of benefit and harm. An ideal medicine would have NNT = 1 and an NNH so large that harm vanishes in practice. Real medicine moves in a compromise. In therapies where baseline risk is high, the absolute benefit is usually larger and NNT lower. In prevention in people at low risk, NNT is usually higher: many are treated so that one gains the endpoint being followed. That is not evidence that prevention “does not work”. It is evidence that the account should be read in absolute figures. NNT inherits the limits of the source study: the follow-up period, the selection of the population, the definition of the outcome and the uncertainty of the estimate. Without these items and without knowledge of the patient one cannot derive from it whether treatment is “worth it”. In the consulting room it can help formulate two questions: how many comparable people need to be treated for a given period for one additional benefit, and how often the harm being followed appears. The Cochrane review of statins in primary prevention (Taylor et al., 18 studies, 56 934 participants) reports for all-cause mortality OR 0.86 and for composite cardiovascular events RR 0.75. [3] From these relative measures one cannot, without baseline risk and follow-up time, determine a personal absolute benefit or a universal NNT. Converting OR 0.86 by itself into the slogan “14 % fewer deaths” would moreover mistake an odds ratio for a simple relative risk. 6. Placebo, nocebo and the natural course of illness Why does a person often feel better after a visit and after starting a medicine, even when the absolute benefit of the molecule is not large? Three processes add up in the consulting room and are rarely separated. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext The first is the natural course and regression to the mean . People go to the doctor when a symptom is at its worst. Many acute states recede on their own. A tablet that arrives on the right day takes credit that belongs to time. The second is placebo . It is not “nothing”. Benedetti describes a measurable neurobiology of expectation, ritual and relationship: endogenous opioids, dopamine, conditioned responses. [10] The context of treatment can change the experience of pain and anxiety. It can also confuse the evaluation of a medicine if a study does not separate the context. The third is nocebo : negative expectation can contribute to a real experience of a symptom even without a specific pharmacological mechanism. The same headache, nausea or muscle problem can, however, be caused by the medicine, the illness, an interaction or another state. From a symptom or from its timing one therefore cannot determine the cause at a distance. Suspicion of an adverse effect belongs to clinical assessment and can be reported to SÚKL; a report is a safety signal, not automatic proof of causality. [7] A pleasant improvement can conceal the same old problem Well-timed relief does not by itself prove what share of the change was caused by the specific effect of the medicine, the natural course or the context of care. In acute and fluctuating states it is therefore important to decide in advance what will be assessed and when. That does not, however, justify attributing a persistent or serious symptom to placebo or nocebo without examination. Separating these layers is not cynicism. It is a condition for not betting on a tablet where time will suffice — and conversely for not betting on time where the absolute risk does not allow waiting. 7. Pharmacogenomics: the same tablet, a different liver A registration trial gives an average dose to an average body. Livers are not average. Clopidogrel is a documented example, not a slogan. It is a prodrug: it acts against platelets only after activation by cytochrome P450 enzymes, especially CYP2C19. Mega et al. in the New England Journal of Medicine showed that carriers of at least one reduced-function CYP2C19 allele — in their healthy cohort roughly 30 % — had lower exposure to the active metabolite and weaker platelet inhibition. In a cohort of patients with acute coronary syndrome these carriers had a higher occurrence of cardiovascular events (12.1 % versus 8.0 %) and a higher risk of stent thrombosis. [6] That is not evidence that “genetics refutes EBM”. It is evidence that the study average hides a subgroup for whom the same tablet name is a different chemistry. The share of homozygous slow metabolisers in the European population is lower than the share of all allele carriers; clinically, however, it is enough that the clinician does not know whether they have a carrier in front of them until a test is done or until the effect fails. The same logic applies to other CYP substrates. There is no need to invent that every other antihypertensive has data as hard as clopidogrel. It is enough to know that an identical prescription is not an identical fate of the molecule. Where a validated test exists and where failure costs a stent, genetics is a layer of effect. Where there is no test and the medicine has a wide therapeutic window, genetics is speculation. To confuse the two is to read one study as a law about all livers. 8. Multimorbidity: a trial without the person in the waiting room Clinical trials use inclusion and exclusion criteria, so people with several illnesses and extensive medication may be represented less than in an ordinary consulting room. For a particular patient, therefore, interactions, kidney and liver function, fall risk, frailty and other treatment decide alongside the trial result. One cannot, however, claim without checking that none of their combinations has ever been studied. ÚZIS records consumption of medicines by anatomical-therapeutic groups. [11] The consumption curve says that chronic pharmacotherapy is a mass phenomenon. It does not say whether every combination in the home medicine cabinet was ever tested. SÚKL collects reports of suspected adverse effects. [7] A report is a signal, not automatic proof of causality. Even so it is one of the few maps that sees the person outside the protocol. Welch’s book on overdiagnosis belongs here as a warning about another layer: the more one treats risks rather than illnesses, the more people enter treatment whose absolute benefit is small and whose harm is real. [9] It is not a call to stop medicines after a heart attack. It is a call not to apply the logic of a heart attack to a laboratory deviation in an otherwise fit person. The NNT of one treatment does not by itself capture the overall burden of several products. That must be assessed in a regular medication review, including the indication of each medicine, interactions, duplications and symptoms that may be related to treatment. The Medicines Act and pharmacovigilance rules govern, among other things, the handling of medicines and the reporting of suspected adverse effects. [7] [17] The summary of product characteristics (SPC) describes indications, dosing, contraindications, interactions and known risks of a particular product. [21] In a person with several medicines, however, the combination and health state as a whole must also be assessed. 9. How treatment results can miss the goal The choice of treatment does not rest only on the probability of average benefit. The seriousness of possible harm, the possibility of timely review and the consequences of ineffective or interrupted treatment also decide. Short-term failure of cough relief, occult bleeding and arbitrary interruption of secondary prevention after a heart attack therefore require a different safety procedure. Type of failure What it looks like How to test it What limits the harm Frame illusion A relative 50 % conceals an absolute 1 point Ask for frequencies: how many out of a hundred ARR, NNT, the same period Context illusion Relief from time and placebo is credited to the molecule Compare with the natural course Time, placebo control, a real target Body illusion The study average misses the liver, kidneys, interactions Medication history, possibly genotype Start-stop, review, an estimate of NNH Endpoint illusion A number is treated, not the event that matters Ask which event is meant to fall The endpoint being followed, not only a laboratory shift An error in dose can be acutely dangerous and requires immediate verification with a health professional; its consequences cannot in advance be labelled reversible. The dispatched impression “I am already protected, I can go on smoking” is a different, long-term type of risk. It therefore makes sense to separate a medicine that changes a laboratory marker from a medicine that, in a given group, changed heart attacks and deaths. The first can be a useful tool. It is not automatically the second. 10. Statins: the same sentence, two different accounts Statins show well the difference between relative and absolute benefit. The Cochrane review of primary prevention found in the included studies a fall in total mortality and in cardiovascular events. [3] Current NICE NG238, for people without known cardiovascular disease, works with an estimate of ten-year risk and requires an informed discussion of absolute benefit and harms, preferences, comorbidities, polypharmacy, frailty and life expectancy. [5] This British threshold is not an automatic Czech prescribing rule, but the methodological principle of communicating risk is transferable. It does not follow that “statins are pointless”. It follows that secondary prevention after a previous event and primary prevention in a person without known disease are not one situation. As baseline risk rises, absolute benefit usually rises at the same relative effect. A personal NNT or NNH cannot, however, be determined from age, one LDL figure and a general mention of muscle problems. The Cholesterol Treatment Trialists’ Collaboration, in a meta-analysis of individual data from 28 randomised trials, found a reduction in major vascular events with statin treatment across age groups, with less direct evidence for primary prevention in people older than 75 years. [16] Even this result does not make NNT a universal figure. NICE and European recommendations link the decision to overall risk, the indication and an informed choice, not to a single laboratory column. [5] [18] A precise NNT cannot be calculated from one sentence about cholesterol. It can be calculated only when these are known: the event, the time, the baseline risk, the absolute difference. Anyone who does not have these four figures does not have an NNT. They have an impression. A laboratory fall in LDL is a useful intermediate. It is not the end for which a person takes the medicine. The end is the event they want to avoid. If the consulting room discusses only a laboratory number, it is discussing the dashboard, not the road. 11. Antidepressants: the average depends on the population and the scale Kirsch et al. in PLOS Medicine processed data submitted to the US FDA for the registration of four newer-generation antidepressants, including then unpublished studies. The difference against placebo grew with baseline severity. In milder and moderate states it was small; it reached the conventional threshold of clinical importance only at the upper end of very severe depression. By meta-regression the authors attributed this more to a falling placebo response in the most severe states than to a rising strength of the molecule. [4] Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext That is not evidence that antidepressants “do not work”. Kirsch’s work shows that the average difference against placebo in this set depended on baseline severity and that a change in score is not the same as a certain clinical outcome for a particular person. The studies did not measure whether treatment delayed hospitalisation, and such a conclusion cannot be drawn from them. Cipriani et al., in a network meta-analysis of 21 antidepressants, found that all the medicines examined were in the acute treatment of adults with major depressive disorder more effective than placebo, while they differed in efficacy and acceptability. [20] The results cannot simply be set against Kirsch as a vote: the works have different sets of studies, methods and outcomes followed. NNT cannot honestly be lifted from Kirsch’s work as a single figure for all depressions. The studies measured a severity score, not the share of people cured in a Czech outpatient clinic. Anyone who makes from it a poster “antidepressants are placebo” reads as dishonestly as anyone who turns a relative difference in severe depression into an obligation of a tablet for every sadness. Current NICE, for a new episode of less severe depression, does not recommend an antidepressant routinely as first choice unless it is the informed preference of the patient; for more severe depression it offers several psychological, pharmacological and combined options. [22] The choice depends on clinical assessment, risk, previous response, comorbidities and preferences. The medicine should not be stopped arbitrarily: the dose is usually reduced gradually with the prescribing specialist. [22] 12. Antibiotics where the benefit disappears In a serious bacterial infection, timely antibiotics can be decisive. Against viruses, however, antibiotics have no effect, and in a particular respiratory infection the clinician must assess the diagnosis, severity and the risk of complications. Possible adverse effects and the population risk of resistance remain even when a bacterial benefit is not confirmed. The 2017 Cochrane review of acute bronchitis or acute productive cough in people without underlying lung disease found limited clinical benefit and more adverse effects; the authors also noted little data in frail older people with several illnesses. [19] This result is not a blanket ban on antibiotics. It shows why it is necessary to decide according to the probable cause, the clinical state and the balance of benefits and risks. What decides is the diagnosis and the sensitivity of the pathogen, not a general sentence that antibiotics “work” or “do not work”. A fall in fever during treatment does not by itself prove that the cause was a sensitive bacterium; the clinical course must be assessed by a specialist. NNT makes sense only for a precisely defined population, treatment, outcome and period. For “an antibiotic against a virus” such a figure is not a clinical argument, because a corresponding mechanism of action is missing. 13. Shared decision-making is not a loss of authority Elwyn et al. described a practical model of shared decision-making in three steps: announce that a choice exists; describe the options; help the person say what benefit and harm mean for them. [8] The ethical code of the Czech Medical Chamber places informed consent and the patient’s autonomy at the core of the profession. [12] Neither text portrays the clinician as a statistician with a calculator. It portrays someone who can bear to say the figure. What needs to be said before a prescription is written The conversation should, according to the situation, cover baseline risk, the expected absolute benefit, common and serious harms, reasonable alternatives and a review plan. In preventive treatment one cannot directly know, in an individual, whether a particular event was averted; one can follow, for example, risk factors, the laboratory response, use and safety. Any change or end of treatment is determined by a professional plan, not by a patient’s solo experiment. The sentence “it will cut the risk by half” without a denominator and a time is not enough for an informed choice. The patient should receive understandable absolute figures if they are available for a comparable population, and space to state their priorities. The clinician at the same time explains the seriousness of the indication and the risks of refusing or interrupting treatment. Authority is not lost by this. What is lost is only the authority that stood on a certainty the data did not have. 14. Primary and secondary prevention are not the same situation A person with already proven cardiovascular disease and a person without a known event, in whom future risk is only being estimated, do not enter the same decision. NICE therefore uses, in people without proven disease, an estimate of ten-year risk, while in secondary prevention it does not require a risk calculation for the decision to treat. [5] In neither situation can a personal NNT or NNH be manufactured from a general sentence about statins. For an absolute estimate, data on a comparable population, a specific event and a follow-up period are needed. In an individual, moreover, we do not observe the counterfactual result: if the event does not occur, we do not know whether the medicine prevented it, or whether it would not have occurred without it either. A practical decision should therefore rest on the indication, overall risk, comorbidities, other medicines, possible interactions, expected absolute benefit and the patient’s preferences. New muscle problems or other symptoms should not automatically be labelled nocebo or a reason for unprompted withdrawal; they belong to assessment by the prescribing clinician. [5] 15. What to choose for which treatment A reasonable choice does not start with the name of the molecule. It starts with the kind of work the medicine is meant to do, and with the review the consulting room has available. Need First question Decisive test Unacceptable shortcut Secondary prevention Which event, and over what horizon, does treatment reduce? Clinical guidance, absolute benefit and safety reviews A decision from a single laboratory number alone Primary prevention What is the baseline absolute risk? An informed discussion of benefits, harms and preferences A relative percentage without a denominator Treatment of depression What is the severity, the risk and the patient’s preference? Clinical assessment, recommended options and a review plan An automatic tablet or an automatic refusal of medicine Infection Bacterium, or virus? Mechanism, not fever itself An antibiotic “just in case” Many products Is each medicine still indicated and safe in combination? Medication history and a professional medication review Adding or stopping a product on one’s own Suspicion of genetics Is the medicine a prodrug with a narrow window? A validated test where failure costs an event A gene poster for every antihypertensive For Czech use a separate language test is necessary. A “30 % risk reduction” in a press release is not the same as 30 out of 100 people. A decimal point in an English study is not a decimal comma in a Czech laboratory. “Statistically significant” is not “significant for this life”. A test set should contain: the denominator, the period, the endpoint and the sentence “the source is not enough”, if a leaflet offers only a relative frame. Some people need a combination of pharmacotherapy, lifestyle measures, psychological support or a specialist adjustment of other treatment. Individual interventions should have their own indication and review plan; no prescribed product should be changed without agreement with a specialist. 16. A review plan instead of a universal test There is no safe fourteen-day test for all medicines. The time to onset of effect, the appropriate review and the manner of any discontinuation differ by product and indication. In prevention, moreover, an averted event cannot be observed directly in an individual: the fact that nothing happened in a short period neither confirms nor refutes a long-term benefit. A safe plan arises together with the prescribing specialist and contains: Indication and aim: which symptom, laboratory marker or clinical event the treatment is meant to influence. Baseline state: important values, other medicines, allergies, organ function and risk factors relevant to the given product. Time horizon: when a change can be expected and when a review should take place according to guidance and the SPC. For example NICE, for statins, states a check of lipids and liver transaminases at 2 to 3 months after starting or changing treatment, while for antidepressants it works with other intervals and regular reviews. [5] [22] Safety signals: which problems to raise at a routine review, which to report without delay and for which to call emergency help. Further decisions: who will adjust the dose, change the treatment or plan gradual withdrawal, and on what basis. The patient should not change a prescribed medicine on their own or stop it abruptly. A record of uncertainty: what is documented for a similar group of patients and what we do not yet know in the particular person. Three questions for the follow-up review Can the benefit be expressed in absolute terms for a comparable population and the right time horizon? Does the treatment have a measurable interim target, or is it long-term prevention whose personal counterfactual result we will not see? And does the patient know which symptoms to tell a doctor or pharmacist, and that a suspected adverse effect can also be reported to SÚKL? [7] The review should not prove that a symptom is “only nocebo”, nor experiment with withdrawal. It should compare expected benefit, the actual course, new difficulties and current preferences, and then adjust the plan safely. 17. Uncertainty must be reviewed as one goes Treatment can affect a symptom, a laboratory value or the risk of a future event. None of these results by itself means that overall health risk is “dealt with”. Pharmacotherapy does not replace reviews or other recommended parts of care. The way figures are presented affects the decision. A relative reduction without baseline risk can overstate the benefit; the experience of one patient cannot in turn replace a comparison of groups. Population evidence therefore needs to be joined to the clinical state and preferences of the particular person. A randomised trial is a basic tool for estimating the causal effect of treatment in the study population. [1] [13] For an informed decision one needs to add which event is being followed, what the baseline risk is, the absolute difference, possible harms and a review plan. ÚZIS publishes statistics on medicine consumption in Czechia and SÚKL runs the system for reporting suspected adverse effects. [7] [11] These systems remind us that knowledge of safety continues after registration. In long-term treatment a regular professional review of indication, effect, risks and the patient’s preferences therefore matters. Suitable treatment is not determined by the highest relative percentage. It should match the patient’s indication and risk, have an acceptable balance of benefits and harms and a clear monitoring plan. Some harms, moreover, are not reversible, so wording about safety must not create the opposite impression. Different criteria apply to short-term relief, different ones to the treatment of depression and different ones to the long-term prevention of a heart attack. In every case, however, it must be clear what the treatment changes, how quickly that can be assessed and how possible harms are handled. Let us ask: For whom do we have evidence, how large is the expected absolute benefit, what remains uncertain, and how will the treatment be safely reviewed? — Jiný Kontext

items.title: How to Choose AI by the Mistakes You Can Afford
items.subtitle: AI cannot be ranked honestly in one league table. The choice depends on the job, sources, privacy, costs and the mistakes a user can detect and correct.
