items.body: Section: Technology & AI Author: V Reading Length: ~27 min Sources and further reading: 22 items Topics: digital footprint, GDPR, OSINT, cookies, data brokers, public registers, deindexing SEO / Working Title: What is a digital footprint and what does it reveal about a person? What is a digital footprint, and what does it reveal about a person? The question sounds simple until we notice that we are not assembling one biography. A cookie is not consent to everything. Deindexing is not deletion of a page. An IMEI is not an account, and an account is not the content of messages. And an American list of data brokers is not a Czech file. The following text maps the everyday footprint under the GDPR. It is not court evidence, a forensic chain or a guide to assembling a stranger. 1. Two namesakes, one bar, four different traces Imagine an ordinary lunch in the office. Someone types their name into a search engine and finds an old race result, a social profile, a company entry in a register and an article about a person with the same name. A colleague says the internet knows everything. An accountant objects that it is enough to file a GDPR request and it will be gone. A lawyer recalls the cadastre and ARES. A marketer adds American data-broker catalogues and a number that looks like a definitive map of the market. At first glance this is a dispute about privacy. In fact each person is describing a different layer. The colleague mixes a visible selection of links with a biography. The accountant confuses a right against one controller with deletion of the whole web. The lawyer is talking about the statutory publicity of recorded facts. The marketer is transferring an American registration regime into Europe, where no such single public catalogue exists. That is why they can all be partly right and the sentence “the internet knows everything” still wrong. The first distinction is therefore not whether a trace exists. It exists. It is which trace, with whom, at what time and toward which conclusion it may be used. A trace after your own comment is not the same as a cookie in a browser. An entry in the commercial register is not the same as the contents of a mailbox. And a search result by name is not proof that all displayed records belong to the same person. 2. An everyday footprint has at least six layers The single word “footprint” hides several things. Some are public, others sit with a particular controller. Some we create on purpose, others arise as a side record of traffic. Some have legal weight, others are only a technical joining point. If we do not separate them, we begin to read character from cookies and private life from the cadastre. Six layers of the everyday footprint: Deliberate publication: profiles, comments, photos, public CVs, reviews and posts. In VŠIT 2025, CZSO reports that 15.7% of social-network users aged 16+ in private households had a fully public profile and posts; this is a self-report by network users, not an audit of all their accounts [1] . Account and telemetry: history with Google, Apple, Microsoft, social networks or apps. It is a rich picture of behaviour with one controller. It is not public merely because it exists. Device and network identifiers: IMEI, IMSI, advertising ID, IP address, cookies or fingerprint. The GDPR recalls that online identifiers can, in combination with other data, identify a person [3] . By themselves they are not a biography. Commercial aggregation: data brokers, advertising profiles, people-search services and marketing segments. Their record can be useful for targeting and dangerous for fraud. It is not a register of civil status. Statutory publicity: public registers, collections of deeds, the cadastre of a property, official notice boards. They have weight for the recorded fact. They do not have weight for everything a person does outside the record. Copies, caches and backups: search-engine snippets, forwarded emails, downloaded documents, web archives or stored screenshots. The author need not control them. A forensic chain does not enter here. Seizure of a device, a bit copy, procedural usability and evidence in proceedings belong to another series. Here the subject is the ordinary footprint a person meets when using accounts, websites and public records. It is not a smaller topic. It is a different topic. That is why the question “where am I everywhere” is misleading. A person is not spread across the internet the way text is spread across a page. With one service there is an account, with another an advertising segment, with a third a billing contact, with a fourth a public record and with a fifth only a technical identifier. A map of your own footprint cannot begin by throwing everything into one list. It begins with a table of layers: what I published, what the account controller holds, what the browser holds, what is in a register, what may sit with a broker and what is already a copy outside the original context. A digital footprint is not a biography. It is a set of traces with different weights. — Jiný Kontext From the device to a copy out of context Illustrative layers between device, account, content and a later copy. From the device to a copy out of context Device Account Content Register Copy JINÝ KONTEXT Illustrative diagram: The chain is neither a biography nor forensic proof; it only separates everyday traces. 3. The best map is the one whose gap you can bear With a footprint we are not looking for an all-knowing picture of a person. We are looking for a map that admits its gaps. A good map says what it sees, what it does not see, whom the record belongs to, who administers it and why a stronger conclusion cannot be drawn from it. A bad map folds everything into one person and adds certainty where there is only resemblance. Type of failure How it looks How to test What limits the harm Confusion of layers A cookie or IMEI is read as a biography Separate identifier, account, content and register A map of controllers and data types Confusion of rights Deindexing is passed off as deletion of a website Distinguish the source page and the search engine First the source controller, then the search engine Confusion of geography 750 brokers from the USA are transferred onto Czechia Name the state, the register and the period Do not transfer an American number onto the EU Confusion of publicity The cadastre or ARES is taken as “everything about a person” Ask what fact the record writes down Stay with the recorded role or property Confusion of population A visible profile is passed off as a universal state State the population and the unit of the statistic Read CZSO as self-report, not as a forensic file That is reasonable, but incomplete if the map ends with a list of finds. Each find needs a weight. A public profile can be genuine and still old. A register entry can be accurate and still speak only of a function in a company. A cookie can join visits, but it does not say who sat at a shared computer. A footprint is therefore not judged by the number of items. It is judged by which question it can bear without switching into conjecture. A good map also has a date. Not because everything vanishes quickly, but because different layers age differently. Cookie settings can change after one click. A social profile can stay visible for years even if the author long ago stopped using it. A register entry can have a legal history. A broker’s segment can be derived from an old purchase. Without a date the map becomes a mix of present and past that looks like today’s portrait. 4. A footprint is not a biography. And it is not a verdict A biography has a plot, an author, a timeline and responsibility for the selection. A digital footprint has records. Some are accurate, others outdated. Some arose from your will, others from the running of a service. Some concern you, others a namesake, a company account, a family device or a shared address. That is not a detail. It is the boundary between orientation and a false conclusion. A footprint is also not a verdict. Court evidence must pass other questions: who obtained it, how it was secured, whether it changed, how it relates to the alleged event and whether it can be used in proceedings. An everyday footprint has no such chain. It can be a guide for cleaning your own accounts, for a request to a controller or for better privacy settings. It should not pose as a definitive truth about a person. It does not follow that a footprint is worthless. It follows that it must stay in its weight. When we find an old photograph, we know that a copy of an image exists somewhere. We do not know whether it expresses today’s consent. When we find a company entry, we know something about a legal role at a certain time. We do not thereby know anything about health, a household or everyday movement. The largest error does not arise from one bad item. It arises from correct items joined by a bad sentence. The name fits, the field fits, the city fits, the photograph looks similar. It does not follow that it is the same person. Shared Wi-Fi, a family tablet or a company phone can create a technical record that, if read carelessly, would look more personal than it may. A digital footprint therefore needs a denominator: who is the subject, who is the controller and how we know that the record belongs to them. 5. An IMEI is not an account. An account is not content An IMEI identifies a device, more precisely mobile equipment on the network according to GSMA rules [14] . It is not an account with Google, Apple or a social network. And an account is not automatically the content of messages, photos and documents. In ordinary speech the three words melt into the sentence “the phone knows everything about you”. Technically and legally they are three different traces. A device can be company-owned, shared or sold. An account can be signed in on several devices. Content can sit with another controller, in a backup, in an app with end-to-end encryption or only locally. So when a person checks their own footprint, they should not ask what “the phone knows”. They should ask which identifiers the device has, which accounts are signed in and where the content sits. This distinction is practical. Resetting an advertising ID does not change account history. Signing out of an account does not delete a public comment. Replacing a phone does not cancel a profile with a service. One change can be right, but only for its own layer. Whoever sells it as a cleansing of the whole footprint is selling calm without support. The opposite error holds as well. When a person finds a long list of app permissions on a phone, it does not mean that every app read every piece of content. A permission is a possibility in a certain regime, not an automatic log of everything that happened. It is still a good place for a clean-up. Of your own footprint we ask: which app has access to location, photos, contacts or the microphone, and whether that matches the function for which I use it. The answer need not be large to be useful. Device, identity and inference are not the same A trace links hardware, an account, a name and what is only inferred from them. Device, identity and inference are not the same Device Account Identity Inference Trace JINÝ KONTEXT Interpretive diagram: Position and size do not express evidential weight; the diagram stops a resemblance from becoming a biography. 6. A cookie is not consent to everything A cookie is a small technical record. It can hold a login, a basket, a language, analytics or advertising. Recital 30 of the GDPR states that online identifiers such as an IP address, cookies or RFID can, in combination with other data, identify a natural person [3] . Directive 2002/58/EC, Article 5(3), ties the storing of or access to information in a terminal device to consent, except for what is necessary for a service the user requested [4] . Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext In Guidelines 2/2023 the EDPB reads the technical scope of this rule more broadly than traditional cookies alone; it also reaches similar technologies of access to information on a device [5] . That does not mean every cookie is the same. It means a technical detail in the browser can be personal data if it joins other data and serves to distinguish a person. In VŠIT 2025, CZSO reports that 43% of persons aged 16+ in Czechia said they had changed cookie settings; in the age group 16 to 34 it was 62%, among persons 75+ it was 7% [1] . The figure measures a self-report about a change of settings, not the legal quality of consent and not the actual number of trackers. It does show that part of the population no longer treats the cookie bar as mere website background. What needs to be tested On your own browser it is enough to start simply. Which sites have an exception? Which extension blocks or allows tracking? Which services hold a login? This is not an audit of someone else’s computer. It is a check of your own layer, which has different rules from an account, a phone or a public register. 7. Deindexing is not deletion The right to be forgotten is often shortened in ordinary speech to “they deleted me from Google”. But the judgment of the Court of Justice of the EU in Google Spain, and the practice that followed, aims at search results by name, not at the automatic disappearance of the source page [8] . The later case Google v. CNIL rejected a duty of global deindexing as a general rule of Union law [9] . In its guidelines on the right to be forgotten in search engines, the EDPB distinguishes the role of the search engine and the role of the publisher of the source content [7] . That is the core of the matter. A link can disappear from a European name search while the page remains at the original address. Whoever knows the URL can find it. Another search engine can display it differently. An archive or a copy can live on. A study by a Google team for the period May 2014 to May 2019 reports that Google deindexed 44.5% of requested URLs in requests under the right to be forgotten [10] . This is a historical window of one service and one type of request. It does not measure deletion of the internet, it says nothing about every request today and it is certainly not a promise of a result. It only shows the difference between a request, a search result and source content. Deindexing deletes a link under a name. It does not delete the page. And Article 15 shows one controller, not the internet. — Jiný Kontext 8. A public register is not everything about a person A public register is strong precisely because it is narrow. Act No. 304/2013 Coll. regulates public registers of legal and natural persons and the recording of registered facts [15] . Justice and ARES help verify a company, a role, an entry or a link to business [17] [18] . They are not diaries of private life. Similarly, the cadastre of real estate records rights to property. Section 52 of the Cadastre Act regulates inspection of the cadastre [16] . The practical weight of an entry concerns a plot, a building, a unit or a right. It is not a telephone directory of residents and it should not be used to build a “name, address, contact” procedure about a stranger. For your own footprint a public record has a different sense. A person can look at whether their company, role or property matches reality, whether an old document still sits somewhere and whether the recorded fact is still true. That is a check of your own legal picture. It is not a search into someone else’s privacy. A record is not a biography What is stored and what is inferred from it are different steps. A record is not a biography Record Inference Device Account Profile Name Layer JINÝ KONTEXT Interpretive diagram: The sides are not a profile score; they separate a data record from an inference it need not support. 9. An American broker catalogue is not Czech OSINT In an analysis published in 2025, Privacy Rights Clearinghouse reports that at the beginning of April 2025 it found 750 unique groups of data brokers registered in at least one of five American state registers [22] . The figure is useful if we know what it measures. It is a floor of registrations in the USA, not the number of data brokers in Czechia and not the number of profiles of Czech residents. In the European Union a data broker is governed by the GDPR like any other controller of personal data. That is a strong rule, but it is not a single public catalogue of every firm that trades in data. Whoever transfers the American number into the Czech sentence “there are 750 brokers about you” is making a precise number for the wrong population. In its documentation of App Tracking Transparency, Apple lists sharing data with data brokers as one of the purposes of tracking for which apps ask permission [13] . That is useful for understanding your own device and apps. It is not a list of firms that have a record of you in particular. Again: a trace exists, but its weight depends on the layer, the controller and the geography. 10. One Article 17 request does not delete copies Article 17 GDPR regulates the right to erasure under stated conditions [3] . It is not a magic button. If the controller has published the data, paragraph 2 speaks of reasonable steps to inform other controllers processing those data. It does not say that one email will physically destroy every cache, screenshot, downloaded file and forwarded copy. The time limit is also concrete. Article 12(3) GDPR says that the controller shall provide information on action taken without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request; depending on complexity and the number of requests the period may be extended by up to a further two months [3] . This is a time limit for the controller’s response, not a promise of complete disappearance of a footprint. In VŠIT 2025, CZSO reports that a request to delete data previously provided on the internet was made by 21.2% of persons aged 16+ in Czechia, that is 1,838.7 thousand persons; the figure has a broad definition and also includes situations such as unsubscribing from a newsletter [1] . The number measures people’s behaviour, not the success of erasure and not the extent of copies. The precision of a statistic must not cover the limit of what it actually counts. 11. Sixty-three percent of networks is not a complete profile Social networks are the most visible part of a digital footprint, and that is why they invite exaggeration. In VŠIT 2025, CZSO reports social-network use among 63.2% of persons aged 16+ in private households in Czechia, that is 5,492.6 thousand persons [1] . In 2020 it was 54% and in 2009 it was 5% [1] . That measures the spread of use, not a complete profile of every person. The same source reports that 15.7% of social-network users had a fully public profile and posts, that is 863.9 thousand persons; 79.6% had at least sometimes set privacy and 4.7% did not know the settings [1] . This is a self-report. We do not know from it whether a service profiles a person for advertising, whether someone downloaded a copy or whether a namesake is mixing into search results. The age layer looks different again. Among persons 75+, CZSO reports social-network use of 9.4% [1] . A digital footprint is therefore common, but not universal in the same way for everyone. Whoever says “everyone has a public profile” misses the population. Whoever says “older people have no digital footprint” misses accounts, official records, operators, family devices and copies. 12. Article 15 shows a picture with one controller. Not the whole footprint The right of access under Article 15 GDPR gives a person the possibility to ask a particular controller whether and how it processes their personal data [3] . In Guidelines 01/2022 the EDPB explains how a controller is to fulfil the right of access [6] . That is a strong tool. It is not, however, a statutory “extract of the digital footprint of a citizen of the Czech Republic”. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext When you ask an operator, you get the operator’s picture. When you ask a social network, you get the social network’s picture. When you download data from your own account through Google Takeout, you obtain an export at Google [11] . Each extract has its own structure, time range, exceptions and controller. Only their comparison shows a map. Even then it is not the internet. In VŠIT 2025, CZSO reports that refusal of personal data for advertising purposes at least once in three months was stated by 58.2% of persons aged 16+ in Czechia, that is 5,060.2 thousand persons [1] . Checking the security of a page when entering data was stated by 45.6%, while the chapter text speaks in rounded terms of 46% [1] . A change of access to device location was stated by 52% [1] . All of these figures speak of people’s behaviour. They do not say what individual controllers hold about them. 13. Six months with an operator is a different layer from a cookie The Electronic Communications Act, Section 97(3), works with the retention of traffic and location data for 6 months [19] . These are network metadata, not the content of communication. That is a different layer from a cookie in a browser, an advertising ID on a phone or a profile with a social network. In a press release on decision 30 Cdo 2556/2025 of 8 January 2026, the Supreme Court stated a conclusion on the unlawfulness of blanket retention of electronic-communications data in relation to EU law [20] . This text does not turn that into an article about data retention or police location. It uses it only as a boundary: the same person can have cookies, a public profile, an account with a platform and network metadata with an operator side by side. Each layer has a different purpose and a different regime. A practical error arises when network metadata are added to the general sentence “the phone knows everything”. Metadata are not content. Nor is content always with the operator. And a statutory duty of retention is not a user’s consent to advertising tracking. The rules of one layer cannot be inferred from another. 14. Deliberate publication and a broker differ in weight, not only in visibility A public profile is conspicuous. A broker’s record can be hidden. That invites the conclusion that the first is less serious and the second always more accurate. But visibility and weight are not the same. A public profile can contain a real name and photograph, but also irony, an old job or a namesake. A broker’s record can be extensive, but duplicated, derived and wrongly assigned. Neither layer is a register of civil status. A profile is a statement in the environment of a service. A broker’s segment is a commercial hypothesis over sources that must be known. In both cases one must ask about origin, updating, the controller and the possibility of correction. It does not follow that they are the same. It follows that they deceive differently. For your own footprint that means two kinds of work. The public layer can often be cleaned directly: old profiles, visibility of posts, photographs, captions, linked accounts. The hidden commercial layer can be handled only toward a particular controller, if you know them, or through platform settings, consents, advertising preferences and rights under the GDPR. The feeling that a catalogue exists somewhere is not enough. 15. A copy outlives the author. Recital 27 is a different file A digital footprint does not die at the moment the author deletes a post. Someone may have quoted it, downloaded it, forwarded it or saved it in a backup. A search engine may have had a snippet. An app may have created a preview. A controller may have held a log. This durability is not always ill will. It is a property of a distributed environment in which data are copied for speed, backups, integrations and human convenience. Recital 27 of the GDPR states that it does not apply to the personal data of deceased persons, while Member States may lay down rules for the processing of such data [3] . That is a boundary, not an invitation to a detour. Digital inheritance of accounts after death is another text. Here it is enough to say that a copy can outlive the author’s original intention and their control of the account. That is why it is more cautious to speak of reducing visibility than of absolute erasure. A change of settings, a request to a controller, deindexing and deletion of an account can be the right steps. They are not the same step and they do not have the same result. Cleaning a footprint is gradual work with layers, not a one-off cleansing of the internet. A copy also changes the addressee of a request. With the original service you can ask the controller. With a search engine you can address a search result. With a post that someone else took over, you are already dealing with another controller or a new context. That is inconvenient, but precise. One request to the wrong place can be lawfully handled without a result, because the addressee does not control the layer that bothers the person. That is why, before each step, the map gets a column “who can change it”. 16. A map of your own footprint says more than the sentence that the internet knows everything A practical test should be the reader’s defence. Not a search for a stranger. The aim is to find which layers of your own footprint exist, where they are administered and what follows from them. The moment the test turns into assembling someone else’s address, phone or privacy, it has stopped being hygiene and has become a risk. Three tests of your own footprint The first test is the deliberate layer. In a private window search for your name and your email, that is, data you yourselves enter. Sort the results into “me”, “namesake”, “register”, “news” and “other people’s content”. It is not a file. It is a list of visible finds and confusions. The second test is the account and the browser. Download data from your own account using Google Takeout or a similar export at a service you use [11] . Next to that, look at cookies, site permissions and advertising settings in your own browser. Compare what is public and what only the account controller sees. The third test is the device and the content. On the phone find the advertising ID, app permissions and signed-in accounts. Separate the device identifier, the account and the content of communication. Resetting an identifier is not deletion of messages. Signing out of an account is not deletion of a public page. Each step belongs to its layer. The result of the test should not be a feeling of guilt. It should be a working list. For each item four columns are enough: layer, controller, visibility and a possible step. A public profile has a different step from an old register document. A cookie in the browser has a different step from account history. A copy with someone else has a different step from a post you still hold in your own account. Such a table is less impressive than the sentence “the internet knows everything”. It is, however, usable. What needs to be tested with Article 15 Choose two controllers you know: say your own operator and one platform. Request access under Article 15 GDPR and watch the one-month time limit with a possible extension under Article 12(3) [3] . Read the answer as the picture of one controller, not as a complete footprint. Before a request for erasure and deindexing First find the source. If the problem is on a page, write to the controller of the page. If it is a search result by name, address the search engine; Google offers tools for this, including Results about you [12] . The historical 44.5% of deindexed URLs at Google in the period 2014 to 2019 is not a promise. It is a reminder that the result of a request depends on the law, the content and the controller [10] . The same rule holds for public records. For your own company or your own property, first check whether the recorded fact is correct and current. If it is, it is not an error merely because it is public. If it is not, correction is handled under the rules of the record. This test is not done on a stranger. This article is not a manual for assembling someone’s address from official traces. 17. The question is not what the internet knows about you. It is which layer can bear which conclusion A digital footprint is not one vault, one profile or one verdict. It is a set of records that arise with different controllers and serve different purposes. Some are public. Some are visible only after sign-in. Some are technical. Some have a legal effect. Some are copies that the author no longer controls. The hidden cost is not only a loss of privacy. It is a biography assembled from unlike traces. When a cookie is read as character, a register as privacy and an American list of brokers as Czech reality, a picture arises that looks precise because it has many items. The precision of an item is not the precision of a conclusion. The same caution holds inside a family or a firm. One laptop is used by several people. One phone can be a work phone. One address can serve a whole household. One role in a register can outlive the actual work on a project. A digital footprint is therefore not only a question of privacy. It is a question of attribution. Whoever does not know whom a record belongs to and why it arose should not make a strong sentence from it. The right question is therefore not: “What does the internet know about me?” The right question is: “Which layer of the footprint can bear which conclusion, who administers it and how can I verify or correct it for myself?” At that moment an undefined panic becomes a map. It is not perfect. But it is precise enough that a person does not chase the whole internet and does not begin to assemble someone else’s life from someone else’s traces. Such a map has a second value as well. It teaches you to brake your own interpretation. Once a person has, for themselves, distinguished an account, a cookie, a register and a copy, they more easily use the same distinction in a public debate, a newspaper text or a company decision. The digital footprint then no longer acts as a fog in which anything can be claimed. It becomes a set of limited records. Some require correction. Some require only lower visibility. And some require mainly the sentence: from this, what we would like to say does not yet follow. Related texts in this series On the site, the series A digital footprint is not a verdict — court evidence. This text is an everyday GDPR/OSINT map. items.title: Running out of money to buy is not operational cover
items.subtitle: GIBS described the production of pervitin when a police officer ran out of money to buy it. The court imposed two years with a thirty-month suspension. The headline wrote that it sent him to prison. Three sentences do not add up.

items.body: The question is what happened when a Příbram police officer cooked pervitin — and whether the punishment he received for it was what it should have been. It sounds simple only until we notice that we are not comparing one thing. Running out of money to buy is not operational cover. A trip to Poland for medicines with pseudoephedrine is not a production procedure this text may set out. Two years of punishment are not two years of bars if the court suspended execution. And the headline "to prison" is not GIBS's statement of a suspended sentence. Only when these four things are separated can one read what the District Court in Příbram decided in October 2020 and what, after appeal, the Regional Court in Prague finally imposed on 3 February 2021 — and what still does not follow from that about the whole territorial department [12] [23] . 1. The headline, GIBS and the kitchen see three different acts Imagine a table after a final judgment. A reader holds iDNES of 16 March 2021. The headline says the court sent a police officer to prison for two years for producing pervitin. It is right about the term of two years. It is not right about execution. In the body of the same article GIBS spokesperson Ivana Nguyenová says: two years with a conditional suspension for thirty months, final in February [12] . Next to him sits an inspector. He says the man began to manufacture when he ran out of money to buy, that with another person they went to Poland for tens of packs of medicines with pseudoephedrine, that production ran in January and February 2020 and that the police uncovered it in June. He is right about the act as GIBS published it. He is not measuring the punishment. And this text will not turn his sentence into a recipe [12] . The judge lays down a third file. The basic paragraph of § 283 gives one year to five years or a fine. Two years are inside it. Suspension is possible under § 81, because two do not exceed three. A thirty-month probationary period is longer than the sentence, as § 82 requires. He is right about the corridor. He is not measuring the headline [2] [7] . A service official has a fourth paper: a final conviction for an intentional criminal offence means dismissal from the service relationship. A suspended sentence is not an exception here [8] [22] . At first glance this is a dispute about "whether the police officer walked away for cooking". In fact each person is defending a different object: bars in the headline, a suspension in the judgment, an act in a press release, the end of service in the act on the relationship. That is why they can all be partly right and the shared sentence "for pervitin in uniform one does not go to prison" still wrong. A family that reads the headline is right about the anger. It has the impression that two years mean the door of a cell. GIBS, in the same account, does not move that door into execution. A judge, if he sat at the table, would say that § 81 is a hypothesis about rehabilitation, not a discount for rank. A service official would say that after intent he has no discretion whether to keep the man. He has a duty to dismiss. Four truths. One case. The shared decision "he walked away" is still wrong, because the verb to walk away measures only bars [12] [7] [8] . Running out of money to buy is not operational cover. — Jiný Kontext 2. The case has at least six layers Folders and a newspaper on a table: the headline, the statutory range and the suspension lie in different covers. The word Příbram in this case looks like one scandal. In fact it is a bundle of layers. The first layer is the person and the posting. A member of the Territorial Department Příbram. The account does not name a name. This text does not supply one. A name the public file did not carry does not belong here [12] [1] . The second layer is the act with a substance. GIBS described the production of pervitin and the purchase of medicines with pseudoephedrine in Poland. That is § 283 in an account of production. It is not a map of Czech labs from article 21 and it is not a recipe [2] [12] . The third layer is the motive the inspection said publicly: he began to cook when the money to buy ran out. That is running out of money to buy, not the sentence "he penetrated the milieu". The series holds this distinction against Jakubec, who at court defended a trade after operational work [12] [14] . The fourth layer is time. January and February production 2020, uncovering in June, finality in February 2021, the report in March. Four dates, one act. A March headline is not the day of pronouncement [12] . The fifth layer is the punishment: two years, a thirty-month suspension, a ceiling of "up to five years", two further accused without a published punishment [12] [7] . The sixth layer is the service relationship and the public impression. The law dismisses after a final intentional conviction. Meanwhile the headline sends him to prison. Both layers are real. Neither of them is the other [8] [12] . Uncovering in June 2020 and finality in February 2021 means the case lived in the file for more than half a year after the seizure. That is a time when a service official could have released the man from the performance of duty even before judgment. The account does not carry that expressly for Příbram the way the regional directorate carries it for Rychnov. The text therefore does not assert a release from performance in Příbram. It asserts only the duty after finality. The gap between seizure and judgment is the place where the public most often assembles the sentence "he is still walking in uniform". Without a source that remains a sentence, not a fact [12] [13] . This layering is not an academic detail. It decides whether a sentence about leniency belongs in the file. If we are talking about a motive, we cannot turn it into operational work. If we are talking about two years, we cannot turn them into bars. If we are talking about Territorial Department Příbram, we cannot turn one man into a department. 3. The best reading is the one whose mix-up you can bear An article about a police officer who cooked breaks into five mistakes. Either running out of money becomes cover for a case. Or a trip to Poland becomes a recipe. Or two years become bars. Or "up to five years" becomes a promise the court broke. Or one convict becomes a territorial department. Type of failure What it looks like How to test What limits the harm Want as operational work "He cooked to uncover the market" Read the GIBS sentence about money to buy Do not quote Jakubec into Příbram The act as a recipe Details of a lab Hold that , not how No procedure, no quantities of raw materials Term as execution "Two years to prison" Separate imprisonment and § 81 Read GIBS, not only the headline Ceiling as middle "He should have got five" The basic paragraph of § 283 The upper limit is not an expectation The man as a department "Příbram police cook" One person, two co-accused Do not add to the 76 prosecuted by GIBS 2024 That also changes the question of the part. We are not asking whether production happened. GIBS and the court recognised it by a punishment. We are asking which layer of punishment which sentence can bear. From that it does not follow that production was "only want". It follows that a sentence about leniency must bear the error in the headline before it can bear a dispute about the statutory range. The best reading is the one that survives when it turns out you read the heading instead of Nguyenová. A bad reading is the one that turns a press release into a cookbook and a cookbook into a territorial department. The damage from the first mix-up falls on one man. The damage from the second falls on a corps that is not convicted in the account. 4. Running out of money to buy is not operational cover The inspection's sentence is short and hard. The man manufactured drugs from the moment he ran out of money to buy them. He apparently manufactured the drug several times during January and February 2020 [12] . The point is not that "a police officer must sometimes play the dealer". It is that the public account does not assign the act to a file, to an informant, to an order from a superior. It assigns it to the fact that the money ran out. The series has other parts for operational work. Jakubec said at court he wanted to penetrate the milieu; the judge accepted part as a beginning and refused it as a trade. Vogel's covering of an informant fell at the evidence. Příbram does not belong in these two sentences, because GIBS did not put it there [14] [16] [12] . Anyone who turns the Příbram shortage of money into "everyone who cooks in uniform does it because of a case" is adding three cases into one motive. The law punishes the act. Motive is mitigation or aggravation under § 41 and § 42, not an exchange of the offence definition [6] . 5. A trip to Poland is not a recipe GIBS stated that together with another person they set out by car to Poland, where they bought several tens of packs of medicinal products containing pseudoephedrine. Pseudoephedrine is used to produce pervitin [12] . This paragraph may say that . It must not say how . Article 21 on pervitin in the population holds the same boundary at labs. A part on an official holds it at one flat. Tens of packs are, in the account, a circumstance of purchase, not a list of raw materials to repeat. Anyone who assembled a procedure from a police report would abuse a source against its purpose [12] [2] . Poland is not a geographical ornament here. It is a foreign purchase of a precursor in a medicine, as the inspection described it. It is not proof that "everyone goes to Poland". It is one factual course of one file. The act on addictive substances and the Criminal Code punish unauthorised handling. Pseudoephedrine in a registered medicine is a lawful item in a pharmacy. The moment it becomes a raw material of production, the account is no longer talking about a cold. It is talking about § 283. The boundary this text holds is the same: it may name the medicine and the country of purchase, because GIBS did that. It must not assemble a kitchen procedure from it. Anyone who asked for "more detail, so that it is believable" would be asking exactly for what the public interest must not get from an official — a recipe under the pretext of reportage [18] [2] [12] . GIBS investigated the case because the offender was supposed to be a member. Act No. 341/2011 Coll. gives it a competence that a regional directorate does not have over its own man. That is why the spokesperson in the account is not the Příbram press office, but Nguyenová. Institutional separation is here part of punishment in a wider sense: the corps did not write a judgment to itself [1] [9] . 6. January and February production is not a map of a territorial department Production "several times" in January and February 2020, uncovering in June. The account does not say how many times exactly, how many grams, what purity. Article 21 may carry 184 uncovered labs for the year 2024 as a police picture of the country. This case must not turn two months in one flat into that picture [12] [10] . Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Territorial Department Příbram is the offender's posting. It is not the guilt of colleagues. The account mentions two further accused and is silent about their punishments. That too blocks the sentence "the department cooked". Three charges are not three final judgments and are not a map of the corps. GIBS for the year 2024 prosecuted 76 police members in the whole republic; that is another year, another unit, another report [10] [12] . The timeline has one more practical sense. From the act to finality roughly a year passed. That is not "justice slept". It is not proof of speed either. It is a date without which the March 2021 headline would look like the day of the main hearing. 7. Two co-accused are not two published punishments "Together with him two further people were also charged. What punishments they received, the inspection did not publish." That sentence in iDNES is more honest than half of the crime accounts. It says what the file has and what the public does not have [12] . From that it does not follow that the punishments were not there. It follows that this part must not invent them. It must not turn silence into an acquittal. It must not turn silence into five years. The case has, in public space, one named judgment: two years with a thirty-month suspension for the police officer. The rest is a prosecution about whose punishments we do not know. That is also a test of the series. Where GIBS did not carry a name and a punishment, the text does not supply them from a discussion under the article. A name the reader "would of course know from the region" belongs here no more than an invented term. The series names only where GIBS, a court, ČT or iROZHLAS themselves carried a name. Příbram, at the core of the account, did not carry a name. The part therefore stays with the posting and with the judgment. The two co-accused may be civilians, they may be further members, they may be both. The account did not decide. The sentence "they cooked it under the department" needs exactly that decision. Without it there remains one final punishment for one man and two charges without a public end. That is less than a scandal wants. It is exactly as much as the source can bear. 8. Up to five years is the ceiling of the basic paragraph "Originally the police officer faced up to five years in prison." That is the upper limit of the basic paragraph of § 283 as the account reads it: one year to five years or a fine. It is not the middle. It is not what "was supposed to fall". The court moves between floor and ceiling under § 38 and § 39: where a less intrusive sanction suffices, it must not impose a harsher one; it takes into account the nature of the act, the person, rehabilitation, mitigation and aggravation [2] [5] [12] . Two years are a term above the lower limit and below the upper. Anyone who says "he should have got five because he is a police officer" must bear that a uniform is an aggravating circumstance in § 42 — abuse of position, breach of a special duty — but is not an automatic jump to the ceiling. The ceiling would be there if the act carried a qualification: an organised group, a considerable extent, a child. The public account of Příbram does not name that qualification. This text therefore does not write it into the file [6] [2] . § 38 adds subsidiarity to that: where a less intrusive sanction suffices, a harsher one must not be imposed. A conditional suspension is, in that logic, harsher than a mere ban, and less harsh than execution. A court that chose two years with a suspension is moving inside this sentence of the law, not outside it. A dispute about the "right punishment" is therefore a dispute about whether the reader treats subsidiarity as cowardice or as a rule. The law treats it as a rule expressly [5] [7] . Suspension has one more condition the headline never carried. The court must reasonably believe that execution is not needed to affect the offender so that he leads an orderly life. That is a hypothesis about the future, not a discount for the past. Anyone who disappoints the hypothesis in the probationary period may go to serve the two years. The account is silent on whether the Příbram convict proved himself. Silence is not proof of conduct. Proof of conduct is a decision under § 83 after the period has run, or an order of execution when he does not lead an orderly life [7] . From that it does not follow that five years were forbidden. It follows that the sentence "faced up to" measures the description of an indictment, not a judgment. 9. Two years with a thirty-month suspension is a judgment, not bars The building of the District Court in Příbram, Milínská: the first instance decided in October 2020; the final judgment after appeal was issued by the Regional Court in Prague on 3 February 2021. VitVit, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 . The court building. It is not a kitchen and it is not a recipe. The court first imposed a prison sentence of two years. Only then did it suspend execution for a probationary period of thirty months. It may give a suspension under § 81 because two years do not exceed three and because it reasonably believes that execution is not needed to affect the offender. The probationary period must not be shorter than the sentence; thirty months are longer than twenty-four. Anyone who does not lead an orderly life in the probationary period may have the court order execution [7] [12] . The point is not that "he got a suspended sentence, so nothing". It is that guilt stood, a punishment is measured, the bars are suspended, not cancelled. The Příbram account does not say whether a ban on activity or a fine was added to the punishment. Where GIBS is silent, the article does not invent a ban. It says only what the law knows about suspension in general: if an accessory punishment had been imposed, the suspension would not apply to it [7] . Three years are the ceiling of the statutory device. Příbram is a year lower. Jakubec sits on the ceiling. Rychnov on eighteen months. Comparing them as "who got more bars" is nonsense, because none of them got bars in the judgment at once. Comparing terms as the corridor of § 81 is honest [7] [13] [14] . 10. The headline "to prison" is not the inspection's report iDNES chose: "A court sent a police officer to prison for two years for producing pervitin." The first paragraph under it cites GIBS on a conditional suspension. The clash is not between two newsrooms. It is between a heading and a source in the same text [12] . That is the narrowest distinction of the part. A reader who skims the headline has bars. A reader who finishes Nguyenová has a suspension. The question "was the punishment what it should have been" then breaks according to which of them he treats as the judgment. The law treats the suspension as the judgment. Journalism often treats bars as the judgment, because bars click better. From that it does not follow that a suspended sentence is harsh. It follows that a debate about leniency that begins with a false execution is measuring a different object from the one the court imposed. Part 1 of the series carries this generally. Příbram is the case where it happened most cleanly: the same number, a different verbal aspect. Headline and judgment do not differ here in the length of the punishment. They differ in whether someone is to start serving two years. A reader who wants to punish more may say the suspension was a mistake. He must not say the court sent him to prison if only the heading said that. The first sentence is a dispute about the politics of punishment. The second is a dispute about a fact. This part decides only the second. 11. A suspended sentence for intent is still dismissal from the corps Production under § 283 is an intentional criminal offence. A final conviction is a ground for which a member must be dismissed from the service relationship. The Supreme Administrative Court in 2016 confirmed that this holds even where the conviction is later treated as if the person had not been convicted, because it was an amnesty. A suspended sentence is not a back door into service here [8] [22] [2] . The Příbram account does not carry the sentence "he was dismissed" the way ČT carries it for Jakubec. The absence of a sentence in the newspapers is not the absence of a law. This text therefore does not say it saw the particular man leave a station. It says what the law orders a service official after February 2021. Anyone who measures punishment only by bars leaves out the layer that, for an official, often hurts longer than thirty months of probationary period: the loss of the key. Loss of the key is not the same as a ban on activity. A ban the account would have to name. Dismissal it need not name, because the law carries it after every final intentional conviction. A reader who in March 2021 read only the headline about prison may have had the impression that the man is sitting and the corps will "still see him". The law at that moment no longer had discretion whether it would see him in uniform. It had a duty to take him out of the relationship. The account does not name that duty expressly for Příbram. This text therefore does not read it from the headline. It reads it from § 42 [8] [22] [12] . 12. A uniform is an aggravating circumstance, not an alibi § 42 of the Criminal Code knows as aggravation the breach of a special duty and the abuse of employment, position or function. A police officer who cooks carries both more strongly than a civilian in the next flat. The law knows that. At the same time it knows mitigation: a first sentence, a confession, remorse, the life so far [6] . Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext The public account of Příbram did not carry the senate's reasons. We do not know which side of the list the court weighed more. We know that a term of two years with a suspension is compatible with both: aggravation by a uniform need not mean five years of execution; mitigation by a first sentence need not mean zero. Anyone who assembles from the absence of reasons "the court spared him because he was one of theirs" is speculating. Anyone who assembles "he got the maximum possible on a suspended sentence" is speculating too — the maximum of suspension is three years, not two [7] [12] . The honest sentence is narrower. The uniform was not an alibi here. The act was prosecuted by GIBS, not by a service interview. Guilt stood. A punishment fell. The dispute is about the aspect of bars, not about whether a regime of punishment existed at all. A disciplinary sanction before a service official could run in parallel or precede. 258 files referred to discipline in 2024 — another year — show that the inspection often ends outside a criminal statutory range. Příbram did not end there. It reached an indictment and finality. Anyone who turns a suspended sentence into "they returned him to discipline" misses the instance. Discipline punishes a service delict. The court punished a crime in the basic range, as the account reads it. Both instances can exist in one life. In the public source the criminal one is visible [10] [1] . Article 21 measures pervitin as a population, a lab, a seizure and a death. This part does not assemble those series from a Příbram flat. 184 uncovered labs for the year 2024 are not this flat in 2020. 38.2 thousand in an estimate of risky use is not one member. Prevalence is not added in here. The authority of an official is not added in there. The series holds both maps apart precisely so that a cook in uniform does not become epidemiology and epidemiology the guilt of a department [21] . 13. Section 283 of this account is not section 329 The public description of Příbram is production and the purchase of medicines. It is not the leaking of patrols. It is not a bribe for a burglary. It is not an intervention in records. Rychnov punished § 283 and § 329 with one aggregate. Jakubec punished sale, abuse of authority and a bribe. Pardubice punished a system. Příbram, in the published sentence, punishes a substance. Comparing terms as "for pervitin in uniform one gets a suspended sentence" therefore adds different protected interests [2] [3] [13] [14] [15] . GIBS was created by Act No. 341/2011 Coll. so that criminal offences of members would not be investigated by the same institution. Municipal police is not in this regime. Příbram is the Police of the Czech Republic, therefore GIBS. That is not a trifle. It is why the case has a public inspection spokesperson at all and not only a regional press office [1] [9] . Discipline before a service official is another regime. 258 files referred to discipline in 2024 — another year, another report — are not 258 Příbrams. This case reached a court and finality. It is not "it fizzled out" [10] . 14. What the account does not say about the punishment An honest list of gaps is shorter than a list of impressions and longer than zero. We do not know the public prosecutor's proposal. In Vogel's case the account carries it: a three-year suspended sentence under a headline of "up to ten years". In Příbram it is silent. We do not know whether the accused confessed, regretted, appealed. We do not know a ban on activity. We do not know the punishments of the two co-accused. We do not know gram weight and purity. We do not know whether the court, in the reasons, expressly weighed the uniform [12] [16] . From that it does not follow that the article should fill the gaps with an estimate. It follows that the sentence "the punishment was soft because…" needs exactly these data. Without them there remain the corridor of the law and the clash of the headline. That is not little. It is everything the public source can bear. What needs to be tested Before a sentence about Příbram leaves the table: finality, offence definition, term and suspension, what the headline promised, what GIBS said, what the law on service orders. The sixth mark — the prosecutor's proposal — is missing here. A missing mark is not counted as mitigation for the court. 15. A comparison with Rychnov is not a ranking of leniency Rychnov: eighteen months, four years of probation, 60 thousand, a five-year ban, two misdemeanours. Příbram: two years, thirty months of probation, production, silence about a ban. The term of imprisonment is higher in Příbram. The accessory punishments are more visible in the public Rychnov account. Anyone who turns that into "Příbram was harsher" is measuring only imprisonment. Anyone who turns it into "Rychnov was harsher" is measuring the ban and the money. The law imposes both in one judgment. A ranking on one axis is a map without the other [13] [12] [7] . Jakubec: three years on five years of probation, a ten-year ban, up to ten in the headline, waiver of appeal, public reasons about a trade. That is another paragraph, another concurrence, another mitigation. Adding it with Příbram into the sentence "police officers get a suspended sentence for pervitin" is a truth about the aspect of punishment and a lie about the identity of the act [14] . Vogel is yet another axis: guilt did not stand, the prosecutor still asked for a suspended sentence, the state apologised. Pankrác carries two judgments about guards and a substance in a prison. Neither of these files transfers a Příbram kitchen onto a map of the corps. It transfers only that a conditional suspension for an official in this series is not the exception of one district senate. It is a repeated aspect. A repeated aspect is not proof that "everyone cooks". It is proof that the question of bars returns in these accounts because the law knows suspension for a sentence of up to three years [16] [14] [7] . 16. Three tests before the sentence that he walked away Three tests before a sentence about leniency The first test is the stage. February 2021, finality. Not a charge. Not Domašov. Not an appeal on points of law. A punishment is here [12] . The second test is the aspect. Two years are imposed. Execution is suspended. The headline changed the aspect. Anyone who cites the headline as a judgment is not saying the punishment was mild. He is saying an untruth about bars [12] [7] . The third test is the service one. Intent plus finality. The act on the relationship dismisses. "He walked away" in the sense of "he remained a police officer" would need an exception that § 42(1)(a) does not carry [8] . Before a comparison with a civilian lab A civilian did not carry a service dismissal or GIBS. He did not carry aggravation by position in the same sense. At the same time he may have carried recidivism that the account does not name for the police officer. Without the same paragraph, extent and past, "for the same thing a civilian would go to prison" is a mood, not an audit. The fourth test is motive. The account assigned production to the fact that the money to buy ran out. It did not assign it to a file, to an informant, to an order. The series has other parts for those three. Mixing them into Příbram is convenient, because the reader already knows the word operational. Convenient is not the same as documented [12] [14] [16] . The fifth test is the co-accused. Two further people, punishments unpublished. The sentence "a gang cooked under the department" needs exactly those two numbers that GIBS did not give. Without them there remains one judgment about one member [12] . The dishonest answer assembles running out of money, a headline about prison and a ceiling of five years into one anger. The anger may stay. The unit must not. A practical test that can bear more than a headline has five steps and none of them is a kitchen. Is guilt final? Yes, February 2021. What definition? § 283 in the published sentence about production. What term and whether § 81? Two years, a thirty-month suspension. Does the headline say the same as GIBS? No. What does the law on service say? Dismissal after intent. Anyone who leaves out the fifth step may leave the man in uniform in his mind. The law will not leave him there [12] [7] [8] . 17. The question is not whether he cooked. It is which punishment you are reading A corridor of a district court: the judgment can no longer be rewritten into a headline. The public question with which the part began sounds just. A person with authority who begins to manufacture pervitin because he ran out of money to buy has broken something other than a neighbour without a key to a database. The law knows that. GIBS prosecuted it. The court punished it. The hidden cost is not that a punishment is missing. Two years with a thirty-month suspension in February 2021 finally are there. The hidden cost is when bars are assembled from them that the judgment did not postpone into execution, and from the bars the impression that justice lied to the statutory range. The range promised a ceiling of five years. The judgment gave two with a suspension. The headline gave prison. GIBS gave a suspended sentence. Four sentences. One case. The right question is therefore not whether he cooked. The public source bore that. It is: which punishment you are reading just now — ceiling, term, suspension, sacking, or headline — and which dislike you are willing to bear when it turns out that you read the heading. Part 1 of the series put that question across cases. Příbram is the first where it can be shown on one file, without Domašov and without an appeal on points of law. Guilt is there. A judgment is there. The headline is different from the judgment. The motive in the published sentence is not operational work. A recipe is not here and must not be. Anyone who after this part still reads "two years to prison" is not reading the court. He is reading iDNES over GIBS. The headline promised prison. The judgment suspended execution. The number was the same. — Jiný Kontext Related texts in this series 01 — "Up to five years" is not the sentence imposed 03 — Three grams off duty are not the same as leaking a patrol 21 — Pervitin is not one thing

items.title: A data centre is not the same as “AI” and a watt-hour of a prompt is not the same as a terawatt-hour on the grid.
items.subtitle: The IEA measures data-centre electricity: in 2024 about 1.5 percent of world electricity use. The share of artificial intelligence is smaller, growing faster, and without a year, a definition and a boundary between training, inference and cooling it must not become a simple headline.

headings: 1. Four numbers on one table are not one share of “AI”
2. The electricity of artificial intelligence has at least six layers
3. The best number is the one whose denominator you can bear
4. A data centre is not artificial intelligence
5. 485 TWh and +17 percent is a data-centre bill, not a ChatGPT bill
6. AI-focused centres are growing faster than all data centres
7. Training is not inference
8. 42.4 GWh of one GPT-4 training run is not a global share
9. 0.24 Wh of a prompt is not 415 TWh on the grid
How to test a prompt against the grid
10. Even if ordinary searches were simple AI text, it would still be less than 4 TWh
11. PUE is not the consumption of a model
12. Electricity is not carbon and carbon is not water
13. On-site water is not a total water footprint and Li is not a rebuttal of Google
14. 626,155 pounds of CO2e from 2019 is not ChatGPT in 2026
15. Microsoft’s 37 TWh is a company bill, not the world’s share of artificial intelligence
16. Czech 58 TWh is a country scale. It is not ChatGPT’s bill in Brno
Before a comparison with the Czech Republic
17. The question is not how much “AI” uses. It is which bill, which year and which boundary
