items.body: Section: Technology & AI Author: V Reading time: ~27 min Sources and further reading: 22 items Topics: Google, digital footprint, security, deindexing, GDPR, public registers, own data SEO / working title: What can Google find out about you from a single name? What can Google find out about you from a single name? The question sounds simple only until we notice that we are not comparing one thing. A search result may contain a true record and still belong to a namesake. Deindexing can remove a link while the page remains. The cadastre can show a property and still not be a people-search engine. A European request can change the European version of Search without deleting the same URL from google.com. This text therefore does not ask what “Google knows”. It asks what you will see about yourself in the public layers — and what of that is not a case file. This text is not a guide to tracing another person, an address, a phone number or a place of residence. The tests below are an inventory of your own footprint. The point is not to assemble someone else’s life from registers. The point is to read your own visibility without panic and without false certainty. 1. In a private window your name is typed. Beside it stand someone else’s managing director and an old snippet Before an interview, a job applicant opens a private window and types their own name as they use it in e-mail and on documents. They find an old profile of their own, someone else’s LinkedIn, an article about a namesake, a company listing that has nothing to do with them, and a snippet from a page that has already changed its text. A managing director opens the public register and sees a function recorded by law. A person with a common name finds someone else’s photograph. A reputation office handles hundreds of URLs. A journalist reads an official disclosure. Google ranks links; it is not the publisher of every page. At first glance this is a dispute about what Google can find out about a person. In fact each description is of a different layer. The applicant compares visibility, not the completeness of an identity. The managing director compares the publicity of legal dealings, not a biography. The bearer of a common name compares a string match, not identity. The office compares the volume of URLs in requests, not the average Czech. The journalist compares a statutory disclosure, not a private file. That is why everyone can be partly right and the shared conclusion still wrong. A search result can be unpleasant and still incomplete. It can contain a true fact, but about another person. It can show a public register, but only your role in legal dealings. It can hide a page after deindexing on a name search, while the page still exists. The first rule of a safe inventory is therefore not: find out everything about yourself. It is: sort what you see. Links you published yourself. Official disclosures. News coverage. Obvious namesakes. Outdated snippets. Platforms that have their own visibility settings. Without that sorting we read a mixture as a verdict. A name in Search is not a case file. It is a ranked selection with namesakes and gaps. — Jiný Kontext 2. One name has at least six layers A name in search looks like a simple key. It is not. It is a string of characters that passes through an index, registers, platforms, cache, the right to deindexing and territorial rules. When those layers are mixed, two opposite errors appear. One says: Google knows everything about me. The other says: once I deleted something, nobody will see it any more. Six layers of one own footprint: Index and ranking. Google fetches publicly available URLs, stores information and ranks the results. What is not crawlable need not appear in name results. What is crawlable can appear even against the will of the person shown. Public registers and official disclosures. The public register, the Collection of Deeds, ARES, the insolvency register and other portals have statutory purposes. They are not a CV. Platforms and self-publication. LinkedIn, social networks, company sites, academic databases and old profiles often say more about visibility settings than about what a search engine “knows”. Namesakes and panels. The same name string can merge different people. A Knowledge Panel can attach the wrong context. A match of the name is not identity. Rights against the search engine and the source controller. Deindexing a result on a name search, erasure at the publisher, and the right of access against a controller are different acts [1] [5] [6] [7] . Territory, cache and copies. The European version of the results, google.com outside the EU, the cache, the snippet, another search engine and an archive are not one thing [2] [14] . This layering is not a detail for lawyers. It decides where to turn when something fails. The wrong person in a panel is not the same as a live page. An outdated snippet is not the same as current content. A request to Google is not the same as a request to the publisher. A public register is not the same as a social network. And the cadastre is not a telephone directory of names. Interpretive scheme: One name leads into six layers. The index shows links, the register shows a statutory role, the platform shows a visibility setting, the law addresses a specific controller, territory changes the scope and cache changes the time. 3. The best inventory is the one whose error you see before an outside reader does For your own digital footprint it is not enough to count results. What matters more is knowing which error is likely and how to recognise it. Sometimes the problem is too much visibility. Sometimes it is a mix-up with a namesake. Sometimes an outdated snippet that survived a correction of the page. Sometimes an official fact that someone reads as a private biography. Type of failure What it looks like How to test it on yourself What limits the harm Namesake Someone else’s profile, article or listing under your name In a private window, separate your own links, registers, news and obvious namesakes A string match is not identity Outdated cache The snippet lives on after the page has changed Compare your own URL, the live page and the snippet Ask for a refresh of outdated content [14] Deindexing is not erasure The link disappears on a name search; the source remains After a request, distinguish the result from the live source Two acts: Google and the publisher Territory The European version differs from the result outside the EU Read C-507/17 as a rule of scope, not as a promise of global erasure European measures make circumvention harder; they do not delete the site [2] Register as biography A company function is read as a whole life Check only your own role and the statutory purpose of the disclosure Publicity of legal dealings is not doxxing Public profile The search engine shows more than you want Check the public visibility of your own profile Changes appear with a delay [20] The best inventory is therefore the one that expects an error in advance. It does not ask only how many links sit on the first page. It asks what each link is, whether it belongs to you, whether it is current, who published it, what rights you have against it, and whether its purpose is to inform the public about a role, or about a private life. 4. A search result is a ranked selection. It is not a case file A case file has an originator, rules, a procedural purpose and responsibility. A search result has an index, ranking, snippets, ads, panels and links to other people’s pages. These two things can meet in the same browser, but they are not the same. When a search engine shows a court decision, an article or a register entry, that does not mean it has assembled a complete dossier on a person. CJEU judgment C-131/12 of 13 May 2014 matters precisely because it recognised the special role of a search engine in a search by name. In that processing the search engine operator is a controller of personal data, and under certain conditions the data subject may ask for a link to be removed from the results [1] . The court did not say that Google is the author of every page. It said that ranking and making links available by name has an effect of its own. It does not follow that a search result has the completeness of a police file. It follows that the index can significantly shape what an ordinary reader sees first about a person. That is exactly why an inventory of your own footprint is worth doing. Not because Google knows everything. Because a ranked selection sometimes decides the first impression. 5. A name is not a unique identifier A name is a social tool, not a primary key in a database. Two people can share a name, a similar profession, the same city, an old profile and someone else’s article. A search engine does not see a person the way a family or an office does. It sees strings, links, context and signals of relevance. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext As of September 2026 the dossier does not contain current official frequencies of given names and surnames from the Ministry of the Interior for the 2026 population. There is therefore no figure here for how many namesakes the average person has. The mechanism is more precise: the more common the name, the greater the risk of mix-up; the more public the role and the rarer the combination of name plus field, the easier the assignment; neither of those turns the result into a case file. A Knowledge Panel can look like an authoritative card for a person. That is convenient, but not decisive. The panel can join data that belong to a publicly known person, an organisation or another bearer of the name. If someone else’s card appears next to your name, the first reaction should be neither panic nor the assumption that someone has assembled your identity. It is an assignment error, to be handled through the tools of that service. A safe inventory therefore works with categories, not with guesswork. “This is my profile.” “This is an obvious namesake.” “This is an official role.” “This is an old snippet.” “I do not know.” The last sentence is better than a false link. 6. A public register records you as a function. Not as a biography Czech public registers have a statutory purpose. Act No. 304/2013 Coll. regulates the public registers of legal and natural persons and the disclosure of data related to registered persons and facts [15] . The Ministry of Justice portal or.justice.cz makes the public register and the Collection of Deeds available [16] . ARES of the Ministry of Finance aggregates data on economic entities from selected source registers [17] . If you are a managing director, a member of a body, a co-founder of an association or a natural person in business, you can appear in these systems. That is the publicity of legal dealings, not a narrative of private life. The entry says that a given person has or had a given role in a given entity. It does not say what their character is, where they spend their time or what they think. How to test your own register entry The test belongs only to your own role. If you know you are registered with a given entity, open your entity in or.justice.cz or ARES and note what is disclosed by law. This is not about assembling other people’s registers. It is about understanding what can be visible about you as a person in a role, and why. It does not follow that public registers are a security flaw. It follows that their result must not be read as a biography. Official publicity can be legitimate and still reputationally sensitive if a reader pulls it out of its purpose. 7. The cadastre asks about a parcel. Not about a telephone directory The real-estate cadastre is about properties and rights in them. Act No. 256/2013 Coll. regulates the cadastre and its publicity, including limits on inspection in § 52 [18] . ČÚZK describes the cadastre as a system for recording real estate, not as a service for finding people by name [19] . That distinction matters for the security of your own footprint. If you know your own parcel or the address of a building, you can check what data attach to your property. Free inspection is tied to the property: a territory, a parcel, a building or a title sheet. An ownership overview for the whole territory of the Czech Republic and the collection of deeds have a narrower regime under § 52(2) [18] . This article deliberately does not describe how to join other people’s names to addresses. The safe question is: what is visible for my own property, if I know its identification? It is not: how do I find where another person lives. The difference is not cosmetic. It is the line between a personal inventory and a guide to interfering with privacy. The cadastre can therefore be part of your own inventory, but not as a people-search engine. It is a layer of real-estate records. When someone reads it as a telephone directory, they are reading a different object. 8. Deindexing removes a link on a name search. It does not delete the source Judgment C-131/12 brought a European right, under certain conditions, to ask for a link to be removed from name-search results [1] . GDPR Article 17 regulates the right to erasure, and Article 12(3) sets the period in which the controller informs the data subject about measures: one month from receipt of the request, with a possible extension of a further two months in more complex cases [5] . These are strong rights, but not magic. Deindexing at a search engine means that, if the conditions are met, the link will not appear for a query that contains the name. It does not mean that the publisher deleted the page. It does not mean that the same content is not elsewhere. It does not mean that an official document has lost its statutory purpose. The CJEU in C-136/17 addressed sensitive data and deindexing; the EDPB in its Guidelines 5/2019 describes the balancing with the public interest, for example in journalism, official documents or a public function [4] [6] . ÚOOÚ also reminds us that the right to erasure is not absolute [9] . That matters for expectations. Not every unpleasant result disappears merely because it concerns a person. Before a deindexing request First separate three things: a request to the search engine, a request to the publisher or source controller, and a possible complaint to ÚOOÚ. Google’s form for the European right to privacy protection concerns URLs that relate to you [12] . If you want the content deleted from the source page, you turn to the publisher or the controller. If the controller does not reply, a supervisory authority comes into consideration. The GDPR period is a period for information about measures, not a promise of erasure from the whole internet [5] [8] . Deindexing removes a link. It does not delete the page. — Jiný Kontext 9. European deindexing need not be global Judgment C-507/17 of 24 September 2019 asked whether deindexing must be carried out globally. The CJEU held that Union law does not impose a duty of global deindexing; the search engine operator must apply measures that effectively make it harder for users in the member state to circumvent the deindexing [2] . The CJEU press release recalls the facts: the French CNIL imposed on Google, on 10 March 2016, a fine of 100 000 EUR for refusing global deindexing [3] . Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext The figure of 100 000 EUR measures one sanction by a French authority against Google Inc. in that dispute. It does not measure the success of erasure, it does not say how many results return globally, and it cannot be read as what every user will see. Its role is different: it shows the conflict between national supervision and the global reach of a search engine. For the reader the point is that the result on the European version and the result outside the EU need not be the same. That does not mean the right is worthless. It means that deindexing has a territorial and a technical scope. If we expect “deletion from the whole internet”, we will be disappointed by a right that was not built that way. 10. Cache and snippet can outlive the live page Another common error appears after a page has been corrected or deleted. The live site may already be different, but search results still show an old snippet. That does not mean the publisher is necessarily lying. It means that the search engine may not yet have the current version, or that the preview still holds old text. Google has a procedure for refreshing outdated content in search results [14] . This tool is not a universal erasure. It aims at the situation in which the content on the page has changed or disappeared and the search results still show old information. Again this is about a specific URL and a specific difference between the live page and the result. The practical test on your own footprint is simple. For your own page or profile, compare the live content with the snippet in the result. If they differ, first check whether the change on the site is in fact public. Then deal with refreshing the outdated content. Do not read the cache as the live page, and do not read the live page as proof that Google has already corrected everything. 11. A LinkedIn public profile is a different page from the profile for signed-in users LinkedIn is a good example of the difference between a profile for the platform and a public page for the web. A person can have a rich profile for signed-in users and still limit what an unsigned visitor sees. A search engine usually works with the publicly available version. Looking at your own profile while signed in is therefore not enough. LinkedIn Help describes public-profile settings and states that changes can take weeks to months to appear in search engines [20] . That period measures the expected indexing delay according to the platform, not a guarantee that every search engine will react in the same way. It is a reservation against a quick conclusion: I changed it in the profile, so Google must show it at once. The safe test is again your own. Check public profile visibility on your profile and open the public version without signing in. What an unsigned person sees is closer to what a search engine can index. If you do not want a given item shown publicly, you change it in the platform. If an old snippet holds on in search, you deal with delay and, if needed, outdated content. 12. Results about you looks for your data. It is not a search for other people’s Google describes the Results about you tool as a way for a signed-in user to find and manage results that contain their personal contact details — for example a phone number, an address or an e-mail — if they themselves enter them [13] . The point of the tool is protection of your own data. It is not a service for entering other people’s contacts. What needs to be tested The test has a narrow brief: your own account, your own contact, your own result. If the tool finds a URL with your datum, you handle a specific request under Google’s rules. If it finds nothing, that does not mean there is no footprint on the internet. It means only that the tool, in that mode, did not find the match it is designed to look for. This chapter is a safety brake. An inventory of your own footprint is not OSINT on other people. There is no place in it for procedures that combine another person’s name, address, phone, family and property. If we catch ourselves turning protection of our own footprint into a guide to someone else’s, we have changed the purpose. The boundary of the test is simple: you enter data that belong to you, and you ask for action only on URLs that concern you. 13. The volume of erasure requests does not measure what Google knows about you Figures on the right to be forgotten invite a shortcut. The study by Bertram et al. from 2019 analysed five years of requests at Google, from May 2014 to May 2019. It reports 3.2 million URLs in requests, about 502 000 requesters, and deindexing of 44.5 percent of requested URLs after assessment [11] . Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext These figures measure the volume and outcome of requests at one operator in a given period. They do not measure what Google knows about the average person. They do not measure the number of pages on the internet. They do not measure the number of deleted sources. Nor do they say that 44.5 percent is the probability of success for your request; a specific request depends on the content, the public interest, the role of the person, recency and other criteria [6] . The same study states that 84 percent of requested URLs fell into the category of private individuals, which is the default at Google; at the same time 1 000 requesters, that is 0.2 percent, asked for more than 526 000 URLs, that is 16 percent of all requested URLs [11] . Some of those requesters are offices and reputation services. Again this is not the average Czech. The Google Transparency Report stated, for data from January 2016, as of January 2018, that 1 percent of requesters accounted for about 20 percent of requested URLs, that is 1.4 million URLs [10] . That is a different time window from the Bertram et al. study; the figures do not add up. Surfshark, in a secondary analysis of the dashboard with collection as of 20 February 2025, reports for 2024 about 180 000 requests and more than 800 000 URLs, and the authors note that the interval may not cover the whole calendar year [22] . That too is not a count of deleted pages. A good sentence is therefore not: Google deletes almost half the internet. It is: in a given period and for a given type of request it deindexed a share of URLs after assessment, while the volume of requests is unevenly distributed and does not describe the completeness of an individual footprint. 14. Visibility on networks is not the same as the index in Search The Czech Statistical Office, in the VŠIT 2025 sample survey, for the 2nd quarter and persons 16+ in private households, states that 63.2 percent of persons used social networks, that is 5,492.6 thousand people [21] . That measures the use of social networks. It does not measure what Google indexes. Among network users, according to the same survey, 15.7 percent had a fully public profile and posts, that is 863.9 thousand persons; 79.6 percent said they at least sometimes set privacy, and 4.7 percent do not know the settings [21] . This is a self-report in a sample survey, not a technical audit of indexability. A public post may be available to a search engine, but it need not be. A non-public profile may be less visible, but a screenshot or a quotation elsewhere changes the path. CZSO also states that 21.2 percent of persons 16+ have asked for the deletion of data previously provided on the internet, that is 1,838.7 thousand persons [21] . This figure includes situations other than the right to be forgotten at Google, for example unsubscribing from a newsletter. It is not a statistic of deindexing. Visibility on networks therefore cannot be turned into the simple sentence “Google sees your social networks”. The right question is: which part of my profile is public, what the platform allows search engines, what has already been taken elsewhere, and how long a change takes to appear. 15. The right of access aims at a specific controller. Not at the whole internet GDPR Article 15 gives the data subject the right to obtain from the controller confirmation of whether it processes their personal data, and if so, access to those data and further information [5] . The EDPB in Guidelines 01/2022 sets out how the right of access is to work [7] . ÚOOÚ explains practical questions of processing data on the internet and the reply period [8] . This right is strong, but addressed. We do not write to “the internet”. We write to a specific controller of whom we know or reasonably assume that it processes our data: an employer, a shop, a platform, a club, a website controller. Under Article 12(3) the controller must inform about measures within one month of receiving the request; where needed the period can be extended by a further two months [5] . It does not follow that every footprint disappears from the web in three months. It follows that a specific controller must respond under a specific legal regime. The right of access is there so that you know what a controller processes about you. The right to erasure has conditions and exceptions. Deindexing at a search engine is another layer. Mixing them into one sentence manufactures the wrong expectations. 16. An inventory of your own name says more than the myth of a case file A practical inventory should be short, repeatable and your own. It is not a search for other people. It is not an assembly of addresses, property and family. It is about what you will see about yourself in ordinary public layers and which steps make sense. Three tests of your own footprint The first test is a search for your own name in a private window without signing in. Record the first results in four categories: my own publications, official disclosure or register, news coverage, obvious namesake. Do not add guesses. If you do not know whether a result belongs to you, mark it as uncertain. The second test is your own contact. In a signed-in account use Results about you only with your own e-mail or phone number, which you yourself enter [13] . The aim is to see whether your contact details appear in results and what request can be filed. It is not a tool for other people’s data. The third test is your own public page and your own statutory role. On LinkedIn check public profile visibility and the public version of the profile without signing in [20] . If you are registered in a company, an association or as a person in business, check your entity in the public register or ARES [16] [17] . If you have your own property and know its identification, check the data for that property in the cadastre regime [18] [19] . There is deliberately no procedure here for finding a person’s place of residence. A useful result is not a long list of links. It is a short record in which each line answers four questions. Does the result belong to me, or to a namesake? Is the page live, or is it only a snippet in search? Who is the controller of the source? Which step makes sense: a change to your own profile, a request to refresh outdated content, a deindexing request, a request to the controller, or no action? That record has one advantage. It stops the emotion from the first result becoming a bad procedure. An old public profile is handled in the platform settings. An outdated snippet is handled as outdated content. An official role is not handled with the same request as a blog post. Someone else’s namesake is not deleted from your life by reading them as Google’s mistake. The result should not be a dossier. The result should be a map of visibility: what I published myself, what the state publishes for legal certainty, what a platform displays, what is a namesake and what is an old snippet. Such a map is less exciting than the myth of a case file. It is, however, usable. 17. The hidden cost is a mixture that we read as a verdict The greatest risk of a name search is not only that we find something. It is that we read a mixture as a continuous story. One link is yours, the second belongs to a namesake, the third is an official role, the fourth an old snippet, the fifth an article that has a public interest. The mind easily assembles a person from that. The search engine did not provide a case file. It provided a ranked selection. That is why it makes sense to repeat your own inventory after a change of role, after a publication, after deleting a profile, or before a situation in which the first impression matters. Not so that we live under the dictate of search results. So that we do not confuse three different jobs: repairing our own presentation, asking a controller to intervene, and accepting that some statutory disclosure has a purpose other than our comfort. In security it is tempting to look for a secret procedure. Here ordinary evidence is better. The date of the check. The query you entered. The result that belongs to you. The result that does not. The URL for which you request a change. The controller to whom you write. The reply and the period. Such a record is neither a public profile nor a tracing tool. It is your own working note, which helps when an old snippet shows up again in a month. The question is therefore not what Google will find out about you from a single name. It is: which layer are you reading right now — and whom do you see in it, when a string match is not identity and deindexing is not deletion of a site? A rare name joined to a role that in practice creates an almost unambiguous identity would weaken this thesis. Even there, however, the result would not be a case file. A rule of mandatory global deindexing would also weaken it; C-507/17 does not impose that from Union law [2] . So would a flat free search for a person by name in the cadastre; § 52 of the Cadastre Act sets a narrower regime for the ownership overview [18] . The practical answer is more modest. Search for yourself, sort the layers, repair your own profiles, request deindexing where you have a reason, and do not read other people’s namesakes as part of your story. A name is not a case file. It is the start of an inventory. Related texts in this series What a digital footprint is… — a name in Search is one layer of the footprint, not a whole CV. What does your mobile phone know about you? — an account and a device are a different vault from Google’s index.

items.title: "Up to five years" is not the sentence imposed. A suspended sentence is not an acquittal.
items.subtitle: A statutory range, a headline, a suspended sentence, a ban on activity and dismissal from the corps do not add up to one bowl of justice. The law keeps them apart — and in a prosecution there is not yet anything to compare.

headings: 1. The headline, the prosecutor and the law speak of a different punishment
2. Punishment has at least six layers
3. The best reading is the one whose mix-up you can bear
4. "Faced up to" is the ceiling of the range, not the expected sentence
5. A suspended sentence is not an acquittal. It is a suspension of execution
6. A ban on activity and dismissal from the corps are not a footnote to the headline
7. Seventy-six prosecuted persons are not a map of the corps
8. Příbram: the headline sent him to prison, the judgment suspended execution
9. Rychnov: two acts, one aggregate under the ceiling of a suspended sentence
10. Jakubec: three years on a five-year probationary period is the ceiling of section 81
11. Pardubice: acquittal, then guilt, then an appeal on points of law
12. Vogel: the right punishment was none. The prosecutor still asked for a suspended sentence
13. Pankrác: twenty months against "up to five years"
14. Database checks and Domašov: where there is no guilt, there is nothing to compare with a statutory range
15. Section 283 is not section 329 and is not discipline
What needs to be tested
16. Three tests before you say the punishment was mild
Three tests before a sentence about leniency
17. The question is not whether they deserved it. It is which layer of punishment you are reading

items.body: The question is whether the punishments for police officers and people in positions of power who broke the law — who took, procured or manufactured pervitin, for example — really were what they should have been. It sounds simple only until we notice that we are not comparing one thing. "Up to five years" is not a court's judgment. A suspended sentence is not an acquittal. A ban on activity in a security corps is not a disciplinary interview. And the charging of twenty highway officers from Domašov does not yet have a punishment that can be measured against a statutory range. Only when these four things are separated can one read what the Criminal Code, GIBS and a final judgment actually imposed in the documented cases — and what still does not follow from that about the "right punishment". 1. The headline, the prosecutor and the law speak of a different punishment Imagine a table after the main hearing. A reader holds a news headline: they sent a police officer to prison, he faced five years, he walked away with a suspended sentence. He is right about the anger the headline feeds. He is not measuring the judgment. Next to him sits a public prosecutor. He says he proposed a sentence inside the statutory range and that the court is no more bound by the proposal than it is bound by the headline. He is right about his role. The prosecutor's proposal is public only sometimes — in Miroslav Vogel's case the public account caught it: a three-year suspended sentence and a three-year ban on activity, while the headline carried "up to ten years" [16] [17] . The judge lays down a third file. The Criminal Code tells him in § 38 that where a less intrusive sanction suffices, he must not impose a harsher one. In § 39 it tells him what to take into account: the nature of the act, the person, rehabilitation, mitigation and aggravation. In § 81 it tells him when he may suspend the execution of a prison sentence. He is right about the law. He is not measuring the public impression of justice [5] [7] . The GIBS spokesperson reads a fourth paper: two years with a thirty-month suspension. The headline above the same act writes "to prison". Both cite the same February 2021 in Příbram. They do not say the same sentence [12] . A service official has a fifth paper: the act on the service relationship. A final conviction for an intentional criminal offence means that the member must be dismissed. A suspended sentence is not an exception here. It is still a conviction [8] [22] . At first glance this is a dispute about "whether the punishments were what they should have been". In fact each person is defending a different object: a headline, a proposal, a statutory range, a suspension of execution, the end of a service relationship. That is why they can all be partly right and the shared sentence "the police officer walked away for pervitin" still wrong. So the first rule does not read: trust the harshest number. It reads: write which layer of punishment the sentence is meant to prove. "Up to five years" is not a court's judgment. — Jiný Kontext 2. Punishment has at least six layers A court file and the Criminal Code on a table by the window: the statutory range, the proposal and the judgment lie in different folders. The word punishment looks like one object. In the news, in the pub and at the family table it is used for the statutory range, the proposal, the judgment, the suspended sentence, the ban and the sacking. In fact it is a bundle of layers that do not add up. The first layer is the offence definition. Unlawful production and other handling of narcotic and psychotropic substances under § 283 is not abuse of the authority of an official under § 329 and is not accepting a bribe under § 331. A police officer can fulfil one, two, or all three. Adding them up into the word "pervitin" is the start of a mix-up, not the end of a diagnosis [2] [3] [4] . The second layer is the statutory range. The basic paragraph of § 283 and of § 329 carries, in the public accounts of the cases in this series, an upper limit of five years. A qualified form carries ten, twelve, eighteen — according to the paragraph and according to the year of the wording. "Faced up to" is usually this upper limit as GIBS or the prosecutor described it at the time of indictment. It is not the middle. It is not the median. It is not what "was supposed to fall" [2] [3] . The third layer is the public prosecutor's proposal. Where the public account publishes it, it is usually lower than the headline. In Vogel's case the prosecutor asked for a suspended sentence. The court acquitted. The difference between "up to ten years", "I ask for three suspended" and "no punishment, because guilt did not stand" is the whole case, not a nuance [16] . The fourth layer is the pronouncement of a prison sentence and the decision whether execution will be suspended. Conditional suspension under § 81 is possible only for a sentence not exceeding three years, and only if the court reasonably believes that execution is not needed to affect the offender. Three years here are not "little". They are the ceiling of the statutory device [7] . The fifth layer is punishments beside imprisonment: a ban on activity, a fine, forfeiture of a thing. The law says expressly that permission to suspend does not apply to the execution of the other punishments imposed alongside it. So a ban on work in the corps is not executed "only if the suspended sentence collapses". It is executed now [7] . The sixth layer is the service relationship and the public headline. The act on the service relationship dismisses a member after a final intentional conviction. Meanwhile the headline may write "to prison" even though execution was suspended. Both layers are real. Neither of them is the other [8] [12] . This layering is not an academic detail. It decides whether a sentence about leniency belongs in the file at all. If we are talking about a statutory range, we cannot turn it into the punishment imposed. If we are talking about a suspended sentence, we cannot turn it into zero. If we are talking about a prosecution, we cannot turn it into the proportionality of a judgment that does not yet exist. 3. The best reading is the one whose mix-up you can bear An article about the punishment of a police officer usually breaks into one of five mistakes. Either the upper limit of the statutory range becomes a promise the court "did not keep". Or the suspended sentence becomes an acquittal. Or the probationary period becomes the length of the sentence. Or a GIBS prosecution becomes guilt. Or the 76 prosecuted members of the Police of the Czech Republic for the year 2024 become a map of a corps on pervitin. The table is not a ranking of severity. It is a map of the mix-ups the text has to bear before it assembles a verdict on justice. Type of failure What it looks like How to test What limits the harm Statutory range as judgment "He should have got five years, he got two" Separate the upper limit from the term imposed Read the paragraph of the offence definition, not the headline Suspended sentence as zero "He walked away" Ask whether guilt stood and whether § 81 applies Describe the suspension, the ban and the service relationship Probationary period as imprisonment "He got four years" Distinguish the term of the sentence from the probationary period Do not quote an "X-year suspended sentence" until the account states both Prosecution as guilt Domašov = 20 culprits Stage: charge / indictment / final Do not assess the proportionality of a punishment that is not there 76 as prevalence "The corps takes pervitin" What does GIBS 2024 even count Do not add up prosecutions, drugs and establishment posts That also changes the question of the series. We are not asking which judge was hard enough. We are asking which description of punishment the law can bear. A family that reads "to prison" may be right about disappointment. It is not right about the judgment if GIBS, in the same sentence, says a conditional suspension [12] . 4. "Faced up to" is the ceiling of the range, not the expected sentence A newspaper on a table by the window: a headline can promise prison where the judgment suspended execution. The sentence "faced up to five years" is almost a chorus in the public accounts of this series. Příbram. Rychnov. Pankrác. In Jakubec's case "up to ten". In Vogel's case again "up to ten", even though the prosecutor asked for three suspended. In the foreign-police database-check case "up to ten" for accepting a bribe — at the stage of prosecution [12] [13] [14] [16] [18] [19] . The law promises nothing here. The basic paragraph of § 283 punishes with imprisonment of one year to five years or with a fine. The basic paragraph of § 329 punishes with one year to five years or with a ban on activity. That is the span in which the act moves if it was not charged in a qualified form. The upper limit is a ceiling. The lower limit is a floor. The court moves between them under § 39, according to mitigation and aggravation, according to whether there is concurrence, and according to whether guilt stands at all [2] [3] [5] [6] . As an aggravating circumstance the law expressly knows breach of a special duty and abuse of employment, position or function. A uniform is not mitigation here. It is a circumstance the court must take into account — beside a confession, a first sentence, remorse and the life so far, which the law knows as mitigation. A dispute about the "right punishment" is often a dispute about which of these two lists the reader treats as the only one [6] . From that it does not follow that five years is right and two are wrong. It follows that the sentence "faced up to" measures the ceiling of a description, not the middle of justice. Anyone who turns it into a promise the court broke is not judging the judgment. He is judging a journalistic shortcut. With qualified forms the difference is harder. Ten years in Jakubec's case and in Vogel's case is a different legal position from five years in Příbram. Adding up "faced ten" across cases as proof of soft justice means adding up different ceilings. Ceilings do not add up. 5. A suspended sentence is not an acquittal. It is a suspension of execution An empty chair by a closed door: suspension of execution is not an acquittal of guilt. A suspended sentence is poorly named in Czech. It sounds like "almost nothing". The law sounds different. The court first imposes a prison sentence. Only then, and only if the term does not exceed three years, may it suspend execution. Suspension is not a cancellation of guilt. It is a hypothesis about rehabilitation: that execution is not needed to affect the offender so that he leads an orderly life. The probationary period is one year to five years, not shorter than the suspended sentence itself. Anyone who does not lead an orderly life in the probationary period may have the court order the sentence executed [7] . That is the first distinction a headline about a suspended sentence loses. The second is harder. Permission to suspend does not apply to the other punishments imposed beside imprisonment. A fine is paid. A ban on activity runs. Forfeiture of a thing is executed. The third distinction is a service one: a final intentional conviction is a ground for which a member must be dismissed. The Supreme Administrative Court in 2016 confirmed that this holds even where the conviction is later treated as if the person had not been convicted, because it was an amnesty. The legal fiction "as if he had not been" in the criminal sense does not throw the service relationship wide open [7] [8] [22] . So the point is not that "he got a suspended sentence, so nothing". It is that guilt stood, a punishment was measured, execution of imprisonment was suspended, the accessory punishments run, the service relationship ends in a case of intent. Three years as the ceiling of suspension are a practical test of the whole series. Příbram: two. Rychnov: eighteen months. Jakubec: three — so at the edge of the statutory device. Pankrác, the first guard: twenty months. The second: one year. All publicly described prison sentences on this map fit inside § 81. That is not proof that justice "always gives a suspended sentence". It is proof that in these cases the court chose a term for which the law allows suspension. If it had wanted execution, it could either have declined to suspend a sentence of up to three years, or — if the act would bear it — have gone above three years, where § 81 gives no suspension [7] [12] [13] [14] [18] . From that it does not follow that immediate execution was mandatory. It follows that the question "why not to prison" has an answer in the law: because at a term of up to three years the court may hold that execution is not needed, and in these matters it did. 6. A ban on activity and dismissal from the corps are not a footnote to the headline Public anger concentrates on bars, because bars can be seen. The law on an official often punishes otherwise: it takes the key. For Jakubec the District Court in Kroměříž, beside a three-year sentence with a five-year suspension, pronounced a ten-year ban on activity in the security corps. Rychnov: five years. The Pardubice commissioner according to Novinky: four years with the Police of the Czech Republic, municipal and city police and the security corps. The Pankrác guard: five years with the corps, plus a one-year driving ban, because they caught him behind the wheel under the influence in November. The second guard: three years. These are not footnotes. For a person whose power stood on a service relationship, a ban on activity is a punishment of that power [14] [15] [18] . Dismissal from the service relationship is a still harder layer, because it is not in the discretion of the court in the criminal case. It is in the act on the service relationship. Anyone finally convicted of an intentional criminal offence must be dismissed. The public account sometimes says this in human language — Jakubec "was dismissed from the police because of the case" — and sometimes does not say it at all. The absence of a sentence in the newspapers is not the absence of a law [8] [14] . Here a second mix-up of the question "were the punishments what they should have been" arises. The reader measures months of bars. The law also measures whether the person may return to authority. Ten years of ban in Jakubec's case is longer than the suspended three years and longer than the five-year probationary period. Anyone who says he "only got a suspended sentence" left out the longest number in the judgment [14] . 7. Seventy-six prosecuted persons are not a map of the corps Before the punishments in individual cases start to be read as a diagnosis of the corps, a map is needed that GIBS for the year 2024 can actually carry. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Ekonomický deník on 10 December 2025 cited the inspection's annual report for the government. In all, GIBS prosecuted 129 persons, or notified them of suspicion in shortened preparatory proceedings. That is a drop of 55 persons against the previous year. Among them were 76 police members (a drop of 22), 20 members of the Prison Service, 3 customs officers, 7 police employees, 3 employees of the prison service and 20 civilians. Employees of the customs administration and legal persons did not figure among those prosecuted. Prague 28, the South Moravian Region 17, Vysočina 11, the Hradec Králové Region 3. For the police, intent in 58 cases, negligence in 18. Criminal activity on duty or in working hours was committed by 36 police officers and 8 members of the prison service. Abuse of position was connected with 29 prosecuted police officers and 8 members of the prison service. In corruption, 13 new cases and 26 prosecuted persons, of whom 8 police members [10] . That is prosecution. It is not guilt. It is not a map of pervitin. 29 abuses of position are not 29 labs. Anyone who turns 76 into the sentence "the police take pervitin" is adding a GIBS unit to the unit of article 21 on prevalence in the population. Those two do not add up. Beside punishment the inspection conducted 1,257 files in inquiry; in 258 cases it referred the matter to discipline. It recorded 9,400 submissions outside crime and inquiry. Discipline is not punishment. A submission is not a crime [1] [10] . The Police of the Czech Republic published 46,163 service posts as of 20 September 2024. That is an establishment table, not a count of bodies; fill-rate for the year 2024 is missing from the same information. From 76 and from 46,163 one therefore cannot make a percentage of the "dirty" [21] . The forms of corruption the daily lists from the report are kept separate by the series: database checks, files, smuggling into a prison, a bribe in traffic. Pervitin is one of the substances in individual cases. It is not the denominator of the annual report [10] . 8. Příbram: the headline sent him to prison, the judgment suspended execution The building of the District Court in Příbram on Milínská: the first instance decided in October 2020; the final judgment after appeal was issued by the Regional Court in Prague on 3 February 2021. VitVit, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 . The court building. It is not the scene of the act. The District Court in Příbram decided in October 2020; after appeal the Regional Court in Prague on 3 February 2021 finally convicted a police officer of the Territorial Department Příbram to a prison sentence of two years with a conditional suspension for a probationary period of thirty months. GIBS said this in March through spokesperson Ivana Nguyenová. iDNES built over this information a headline that the court sent the police officer to prison for two years for producing pervitin [12] [23] . The point is not that one of the sources is lying about the term. It is that two years are in the judgment, prison in execution is not, until the suspension collapses. The headline measured the term and stuck prison bars onto it. GIBS measured the term and the suspension. A reader who asks whether the punishment "was what it should have been" often reads the headline. The law reads GIBS. The act as the inspection described it: the man manufactured drugs when he ran out of money to buy them; several times in January and February 2020; with another person they went to Poland for tens of packs of medicines with pseudoephedrine. Originally he faced up to five years. Two other people were charged with him; the inspection did not publish their punishments. This text does not describe a production procedure. It describes that the court recognised production and imposed two years with a suspension [12] . Was that "little"? The basic statutory range of § 283 gives room from one year to five years. Two years are inside it. The suspension is lawful, because two are under three. The thirty-month probationary period is longer than the sentence, as § 82 requires. The public account does not say what the prosecutor proposed. It does not say whether the court, in the reasons, weighed a confession, a first sentence, remorse, or on the contrary abuse of position. Without the reasons one cannot say the court "should have gone to five". One can say that the headline and the judgment parted, and that this parting is itself an answer to the question why the public reads punishments as soft [2] [7] [12] . 9. Rychnov: two acts, one aggregate under the ceiling of a suspended sentence The District Court in Rychnov nad Kněžnou, Svatohavelská: the aggregate of February 2022 punished both acts here. Krvesaj, Wikimedia Commons, public domain. The court building. It is not a map of patrols. The District Court in Rychnov nad Kněžnou found a former police officer of the Territorial Department guilty of unlawful production and other handling of narcotic and psychotropic substances and of abuse of the authority of an official. Punishment: eighteen months of imprisonment with a conditional suspension for four years, a fine of 60 thousand koruna, a ban on activity in the security corps for five years, forfeiture of a thing. Final on 21 February 2022. GIBS published this in April. He faced up to five years [13] . Two acts that do not add up into one word pervitin. Off duty, at least three times from October 2020 to May 2021, he procured for a civilian each time three to three and a half grams of pervitin for roughly ten thousand koruna. On duty, from December 2020 to May 2021, he gave two people without a driving licence information about patrols. At his home they found cannabis, to which the forfeiture applies. The civilian was to use the pervitin, or to distribute it further — GIBS leaves it in this pair. This text does not turn that into a recipe or a map of the market [13] . An aggregate sentence of eighteen months for both misdemeanours is under the ceiling of a suspended sentence. A four-year probationary period is long against eighteen months. A five-year ban is longer than the prison sentence. The fine is executed under § 81(2). Anyone who says "he only got a suspended sentence" must add to the sentence 60 thousand, five years of ban and the fact that leaking patrols is a different protected interest from gram weight. The court punished both with one aggregate. The public often hears only the drug [7] [13] . Was the aggregate "what it should have been"? The account does not contain the prosecutor's proposal or the full reasons. It contains that guilt stood in both offence definitions and that the term stayed in the band where the law allows suspension. That is documented. The sentence "for the patrols and for the pervitin he should have gone to prison" is a politics of punishment. It is not a citation of the file. 10. Jakubec: three years on a five-year probationary period is the ceiling of section 81 Lukáš Jakubec, a former employee of the district station in Bystřice pod Hostýnem, received from the District Court in Kroměříž three years of imprisonment with a five-year suspension and a ten-year ban on activity in the security corps. The public prosecutor and the accused waived appeal. The judgment is final. He faced up to ten years. He confessed in part. At the main hearing he changed his testimony [14] . Three years are the ceiling above which § 81 will not let a suspension through. The court therefore chose the highest term that can still be suspended. The point is not that "always a suspended sentence at the bottom". It is that if it wanted a suspended sentence, it could not go to four unsuspended. If it wanted execution, it could have left the three unsuspended, or — if the act and the paragraph would bear it — have gone higher, where there is no suspension. It chose the edge of the statutory device and with it the longest ordinary probationary period and the longest ban on this map [7] [14] . Judge Hana Machalová said according to ČT that it contributed to the suspended sentence that Jakubec had not been punished before. He had debased the police in the eyes of the public. At first the distribution of pervitin may have helped clarification. Later he made a "trade" of the drugs. That is a public statement of reasons which Příbram and Rychnov did not get in the accounts. It gives the reader what the question "what it should have been" needs: the court weighed mitigation (a first sentence) and aggravation (a trade in uniform) and said why it did not go to execution [14] [6] . His wife Lucie: a one-year sentence with a two-year suspension for handing over pervitin in at least one case. She faced up to five years. She refused to testify. That too is final. Her statutory range is not the range of an official. Adding them into one bowl "a family on pervitin" is a different sentence from the one the file can bear [14] . The defence "to penetrate the milieu" is a thesis this series carries into the part on the informant. Here one distinction is enough: the court partly accepted that sentence as a beginning and refused it as an end. The punishment is therefore not a punishment for having an informant. It is a punishment for the fact that, according to the court, a trade was made of the informant and, on top of that, a bribe of 30 thousand for not dealing with a burglary. Part of the sum was paid according to the judgment. Jakubec denied that at the hearing [14] . Waiving appeal means that the judgment did not go to an appellate court. The question whether it "should have been harsher" therefore had no second instance. That is not proof that the punishment was right. It is proof that none of the parties wanted it reviewed. 11. Pardubice: acquittal, then guilt, then an appeal on points of law A former chief commissioner of the anti-drug department in the Pardubice Region left the appellate regional court, according to Novinky, with a four-year suspended sentence, a fine of 40 thousand koruna and a four-year ban on work with the Police of the Czech Republic, municipal and city police and the security corps. The appellate court confirmed the district court's second verdict. At the first one the district acquitted the indictment on the ground that the act had not happened. The accused filed an appeal on points of law with the Supreme Court [15] . Here the question "was the punishment what it should have been" breaks three times. First: the first instance said the act had not happened. That is not a mild punishment. That is no punishment, because no guilt. Second: the appellate instance assembled guilt and imposed a punishment. Third: an appeal on points of law means that as of the day of the account the judgment is not yet the end of the file. A series that turned Novinky into "he got four and that is little" would be lying about the stage [15] . The second mix-up is the word suspended sentence. Journalism often writes "a four-year suspended sentence" and does not say whether four years mark the term of the prison sentence or the probationary period. In § 81 the law does not allow suspension above three years of term. If four years were the term of imprisonment, the account would be describing something the basic conditional suspension cannot bear — or it would be another statutory device the text does not name. If four years are the probationary period, the term of imprisonment is missing from the account. This article therefore does not cite the number four as a proved term. It cites it as a journalistic shortcut that clouds exactly the question the reader is asking [7] [15] . The core of the act, as the presiding judge Aleš Holík described it according to Novinky, is not a dose in the commissioner's pocket. It is an intervention in the system and the covering of a source: he actively failed to document, he warned, he advised how to testify in a tax matter. The defence sounded like operational tactics. The court said he expected advantages and that the source gave the impression he could go on offending. That is § 329 and a regime of records. It is not article 21 on prevalence. It is not Příbram on a lab [15] . Until the Supreme Court decides publicly, a sentence about the proportionality of the punishment is premature. Prematurity here is a finding, not an excuse. 12. Vogel: the right punishment was none. The prosecutor still asked for a suspended sentence Miroslav Vogel, a senior counsellor of the National Drug Headquarters, was indicted for abuse of authority, favouring, endangering classified information and for extorting the informant Petr Ryžák. Ryžák claimed he manufactured and sold pervitin on Vogel's instruction. The Municipal Court in Prague acquitted on 11 December 2014. Judge Petr Hovorka called the witness unreliable: he began to testify in custody, the motive was in his own criminal proceedings, there were no wiretaps and documents, and some of the indictment's claims even proved, according to the court, to be acts that had not happened. The High Court in Prague confirmed on 12 March 2015. Final on 21 May 2015 [16] . Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Prosecutor Michal Moravský himself proposed acquittal on the extortion. He insisted on the rest and asked for a three-year suspended sentence and a three-year ban on activity. The headline carried up to ten years. The court imposed zero, because guilt did not stand. Anyone who asks whether the punishment "was what it should have been" must first bear this sentence: the right punishment on an acquittal is no punishment. The suspended sentence the prosecutor asked for would have been a punishment without guilt. The court did not give it [16] . The state later apologised for an unlawful criminal prosecution and the Ministry of Justice awarded 295 thousand koruna. iROZHLAS in February 2017 cited the apology of the head of the damages department. Vogel did not return to his original leading post at NPC. A further claim in the order of millions the account later tied to the limitation of the rest. That is not "he walked away thanks to the uniform". It is the bill for an indictment that fell at the evidence [17] . A series without this part would be dishonest. The tabloid sentence "a police officer covered a lab" is exactly the kind of act a reader wants punished most harshly. Here it did not survive the evidence. The question of the mildness of punishment in Vogel's case therefore has no object. The question of the price of a charge has an object. 13. Pankrác: twenty months against "up to five years" Soudní street at Pankrác: a prison and a court side by side. Power behind a wall is a different key from a patrol on the road. ŠJů, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 . The compound, not a smuggling procedure. The Municipal Public Prosecutor's Office in Prague described the act of the first guard of Pankrác Remand Prison as follows: from January to the beginning of November 2023 he enabled persons in remand and serving a sentence access to addictive substances, he secured the substances from persons the prisoners named, and he carried them inside. He handed some over, he kept some as a reward. Thirteen times successfully, four times an attempt, plus 200 tablets with anabolic and other hormonal effect. The final punishment according to Novinky: twenty months of imprisonment with a three-year suspension, a five-year ban on activity in the security corps, a one-year driving ban — because they caught him behind the wheel under the influence in November. He faced up to five years [18] . The second guard: two attempts at smuggling. A one-year sentence with a two-year suspension, a three-year ban on activity. The same account, the same "up to five years" [18] . Power behind a wall is a different key from a patrol on the road. Smuggling into a prison is exactly the form the GIBS report for the year 2024 ranks among the most frequent corruption patterns. The series therefore does not hold it as "another police officer on pervitin". It holds it as a key to a guarded space. The part the guard kept is § 283 in the pocket of an official. The smuggling is abuse of authority and obstruction. The anabolics are a further act. An aggregate of twenty months with a suspension again sits inside § 81. A five-year ban again outlives the suspended sentence [10] [18] [7] . Were twenty months "little" against thirteen smugglings? The account does not contain the prosecutor's proposal. It contains an upper limit of five years, which is the ceiling of the basic paragraph, and a term that is a third to a half of this ceiling, plus a ban and a driving ban. The sentence "he should have sat because it was a prison" is intelligible. It is not a citation of § 39. The law allows suspension here too. The court used it. Anyone who wants to say it was unlawfully mild needs reasons that Novinky do not carry. Anyone who wants to say it was lawful has § 81. Between unlawfulness and dislike sits the whole article. 14. Database checks and Domašov: where there is no guilt, there is nothing to compare with a statutory range On 11 November 2024 GIBS described the prosecution of a member of the Directorate of the Foreign Police Service: in five cases more than 180 persons in a year, on a single day 174 database checks, the period September 2020 to September 2021. In two cases, for 4,000 Kč, seven database checks for a civilian, handed over through a colleague. Prosecution: accepting a bribe, abuse of authority, unauthorised access to a system. The colleague and the civilian as well. They face up to ten, or six, years. That is a charge. It is not a judgment [19] . GIBS and the Regional Public Prosecutor's Office in Brno in 2026 are prosecuting twenty police officers of the Domašov highway department. All twenty for abuse of the authority of an official; ten of them also for accepting a bribe. The statutory ranges in the account: one to five years, for the bribe three to ten. No one in custody. Some filed a complaint against the charge. A service official released them from the performance of duty. The act is from 2022. There is no pervitin in the account. There is no verdict as of the date of this research [20] . The question "were the punishments what they should have been" has no object in these two cases. The question whether the public can wait has an object. The series deliberately does not make them "the tenth dirty police officer". It makes them a measure: the proportionality of a punishment is not counted from a headline and from a statutory range. It is counted from a judgment. Where there is no judgment, what remains is only a ceiling, which again is not a punishment. 15. Section 283 is not section 329 and is not discipline Three regimes melt together in the debate about "a police officer on pervitin", because the public sentence wants them as one. § 283 punishes handling of a substance: production, sale, procuring for another. Příbram, part of Rychnov, Jakubec, part of Pankrác. The unit is the substance and the act with it. A uniform is an aggravating circumstance and sometimes concurrence, not an element of the offence definition [2] [6] . § 329 punishes an official who, with intent to harm or to obtain an unauthorised advantage, exercises authority contrary to a regulation, exceeds it, or fails to fulfil a duty. The Rychnov patrols, the Pardubice system, the database checks, Domašov, part of Pankrác. The unit is the key. The substance may be missing [3] . § 331 punishes a bribe. Jakubec, part of the database checks, part of Domašov. The unit is a counter-value for arranging matters of general interest, for an official in a stricter statutory range [4] . Discipline before a service official is a fourth regime. 258 files referred to discipline in 2024 are not 258 punishments. 9,400 submissions are not 9,400 crimes. GIBS was created by Act No. 341/2011 Coll. so that criminal offences of members of the Police of the Czech Republic, the Prison Service, customs officers and its own inspection would not be investigated by the same institution that commits them. Municipal police is not in this regime. Anyone who turns GIBS into "a police that watches itself" misses the law that placed it beside them for that very reason [1] [10] [9] . The practical consequence for punishments: concurrence of § 283 and § 329 (Rychnov) is not the same as bare § 283 (Příbram in the public account of production) and is not the same as bare § 329 (Domašov at the stage of prosecution). Comparing terms across these lines as proof that "for pervitin in uniform one gets a suspended sentence" means comparing different protected interests. The law does not add them into one statutory range. It adds them into an aggregate in a concrete judgment. What needs to be tested Before a sentence about punishment leaves the table, five marks on paper are enough. The stage. The offence definition and the paragraph. The term of imprisonment and whether § 81. The accessory punishments. Whether the headline says the same as GIBS or the judgment. Anyone who leaves out the fifth mark is measuring iDNES against the law and wondering that it does not fit [12] . 16. Three tests before you say the punishment was mild A notepad and a code: five marks on paper say more than the sentence that he walked away. The opening question has three honest answers and one dishonest one. Three tests before a sentence about leniency The first test is the stage. In Vogel's case the answer is: there should have been no punishment, because guilt fell. In the database checks case and Domašov: one cannot yet measure by a punishment. In Pardubice: an appeal on points of law. Anyone who rates these three lines as "soft justice" is rating an absence. The second test is the legal corridor, not an impression. All final prison sentences on this map for which the account states a term lie between one and three years and were suspended. That is the corridor of § 81, not proof that five years were mandatory. Beside the corridor run bans from three to ten years and fines that do not survive the suspension as zero. Anyone who measures only bars is measuring the narrowest part of the judgment [7] . The third test is the reasons. In Jakubec's case the account carries them: a first sentence, a trade, debasement of the corps, waiver of appeal. In Příbram it carries the clash of headline and GIBS. In Rychnov it carries the concurrence of substance and patrols. In Pankrác it carries the number of smugglings and the driving ban. Where the reasons are missing, the sentence "the court should have gone to the upper limit" is speculation about § 39. Speculation may be political. It must not pose as a citation of the file [5] [14] . The dishonest answer is the one that assembles one anger from the upper limit of a statutory range, from the headline "to prison" and from 76 prosecuted persons. The anger may stay. The unit must not. Before a comparison with a "civilian" dealer there is a fourth distinction this text does not wrap in a false equality. An official carries § 329 and § 42 aggravating circumstances and carries a service dismissal that a civilian does not have. At the same time, in concrete judgments, he carries the mitigation of a first sentence that a civilian recidivist does not have. A comparison "for the same thing a civilian would go to prison" therefore needs the same: the same paragraph, the same extent, the same recidivism, the same concurrence. Without that it is a mood, not an audit. 17. The question is not whether they deserved it. It is which layer of punishment you are reading A corridor of a palace of justice toward morning: punishments are not read from a crowd, they are read from a judgment that no one is rewriting into a headline any more. The public question with which this text began sounds just. A person in a position of power who cooks, procures or smuggles pervitin, or who opens a database for a bribe, has broken something other than a neighbour in a panel block. The law knows that. It has § 329, § 331, the aggravating circumstance of abuse of position and mandatory dismissal. The hidden cost is not that punishments are missing. In Příbram, Rychnov, Kroměříž and at Pankrác the punishments are there and they are final. The hidden cost is when one curve of leniency is assembled from them: the headline promised prison, the statutory range promised five or ten, the judgment gave two with a suspension, so justice failed. In fact the headline promised a thing that the judgment in Příbram did not expressly postpone into bars, but suspended in execution. The statutory range promised a ceiling, not a middle. The judgment gave a term in the corridor where the law allows suspension, and with it a ban that does not survive the suspension as zero. In Vogel's case the ceiling of ten years survived only as the shadow of an indictment that fell. In Domašov the ceiling does not yet have a judgment. The right question is therefore not whether they deserved it. It is: which layer of punishment you are reading just now, which ceiling you have confused with a judgment, and which dislike — bars, a ban, a sacking, an apology by the state — you are willing to bear when it turns out that you added wrongly. A suspended sentence is not an acquittal. It is the suspension of a punishment that has already been imposed. — Jiný Kontext Related texts in this series This part is the frame of the series on power and law. The following texts take individual cases as one distinction, not as another mugshot. Article 21 on pervitin in the population is not added in here: there the unit is prevalence, here the authority of an official and a judgment of punishment. 21 — Pervitin is not one thing 02 — Running out of money to buy is not operational cover 03 — Three grams off duty are not the same as leaking a patrol Power and law series — a map of ten parts

items.title: A leaderboard measures a task. It does not decide whom you may trust in Czech.
items.subtitle: A public leaderboard is a map of one task, one prompt population and one scoring method. It is not a verdict on which model is best for Czech work.
