items.body: Section: Justice & law | Technology & AI Author: V Reading time: ~27 min Sources and further reading: 22 items Topics: operator, data retention, traffic data, location data, privacy, criminal proceedings SEO / working title: How long does an operator retain data about your phone? How long does an operator retain data about your phone? The question sounds simple only until we notice that we are not comparing one thing. Six months may apply to traffic data and the content of a call may still be missing. Two months of billing at one operator in 2019 are not a statutory period. The Constitutional Court could bear the rules in 2019 and the Supreme Court in December 2025 could find the same blanket character incompatible with Union law. And a judgment about an apology need not erase a paragraph from the Collection of Laws. The text that follows therefore does not ask what the operator records. It asks which bucket who is requesting, and under which frame lawfulness is measured. 1. In T-Mobile’s testimony two months were heard. In the statute there stand six. In the call there stands nothing. A subscriber asks the operator how long it keeps data about a phone. The operator points to § 97(3) of the Electronic Communications Act: six months of traffic and location data, without the content of messages [1] . A witness for T-Mobile Czech Republic, a.s., in proceedings before the Constitutional Court in 2019 says something narrower: for its own billing and complaint needs it retains data in a narrower scope for two months [4] . A police authority is not asking about an invoice, but about access under § 88a of the Code of Criminal Procedure [10] . And the Court of Justice of the EU is not asking about the convenience of a national rule, but about the blanket character of the interference under Union law [7] [8] . At first glance this is a dispute about half a year, or two months. In fact each person is describing a different bucket. One bucket is statutory data retention. The second is billing and complaints. The third is marketing with consent. The fourth is judicial access to data. The fifth is the constitutional frame. The sixth is the Union frame. Anyone who mixes them easily arrives at the sentence that the operator records calls for half a year. That sentence is wrong. The content of a call does not belong here. § 97(3) expressly says that the content of messages is neither retained nor handed over under this duty [1] . That does not mean that metadata are banal. The Constitutional Court has already said of telephone data that even numbers called, time, duration of a call and base stations fall under the protection of Article 13 of the Charter [14] . It means only that content and a traffic datum are not the same thing. The dossier about a phone in police hands is another text. There the subject is a seized device, stored content and § 113a. Here the subject is network metadata at the operator. Device, network and invoice meet in one user experience. Legally they stand in different columns. Six months at the operator is not the content of a call. Billing is not data retention. — Jiný Kontext 2. Data at the operator have at least six layers The first layer is network metadata. Who called whom, when, for how long, from which cell, with which identification of a device or subscriber. Decree No. 357/2012 Coll. spells out the scope of retained and handed-over traffic and location data, including identification of source and addressee, time, manner and duration of communication [2] . For e-mail protocols it does not aim at the body of a message. It aims at a traffic trail. The second layer is the operator’s own operations. Billing, complaints, network operation, customer care. That may require some data, but another scope and another period. In the sources we have a firmly documented figure of two months only as T-Mobile’s testimony in Pl. ÚS 45/17, for its own needs and in a narrower scope [4] . It is not the statute. It is not the whole market. It is not 2026. The third layer is statutory holding for the state. § 97(3) requires persons who provide a public communications network or a publicly available electronic-communications service to retain data for six months [1] . This figure measures the legal data-retention duty, not the existence of call content and not every firm’s billing practice. The fourth layer is the judicial lock on access. In criminal proceedings that lock is § 88a. It does not regulate retention itself at the operator. It regulates when and how data on telecommunications traffic may be requested [10] . An older form of § 88a was itself the subject of Constitutional Court intervention in Pl. ÚS 24/11 [11] . The fifth layer is the European ceiling. From Digital Rights Ireland through Tele2 to La Quadrature du Net the Court of Justice of the EU rejects general and indiscriminate retention of traffic and location data for the fight against crime, with narrow exceptions [6] [7] [8] . That is a different plane of review from the question of what currently stands in the Czech statute. The sixth layer is the Czech pendulum. The Constitutional Court in 2011 annulled the old rules [3] . After adjustments the legislature rebuilt them on six-month retention. The Constitutional Court in 2019 dismissed an application to annul [5] [13] . The Supreme Court in December 2025 found a conflict with Union law and ordered the state to apologise [9] . As of the September 2026 research cut, however, the paragraph still stands in the text of the statute. 3. The best diagnosis is the one that first names the bucket A bad diagnosis does not begin with ill will. It begins with the word data. Invoice data, traffic data, marketing data, interception data, data in the phone, data at a chat service. In ordinary speech they fit into one sentence. In law they do not. Type of failure What it looks like How to test it What limits the harm Content as retention An expectation that the operator holds a recording of the call Read the sentence in § 97(3) on the ban on content Content is § 88, not retention Billing as statute “Two months” is cited as a ZEK period Point 34 of Pl. ÚS 45/17: one operator, year 2019 At another operator, check its own rules Constitutional Court 2019 as EU 2025 “It is constitutional, therefore also Union-law compliant” Separate Pl. ÚS 45/17 from Tele2 and the Supreme Court 2025 Two frames, two results Apology as annulment A civil judgment is read as a derogating finding Compare Pl. ÚS 24/10 with Supreme Court 30 Cdo 2556/2025 A paragraph in the Collection of Laws may still stand § 88a as everything A request without a threshold and a purpose Read the threshold and conditions of the Code of Criminal Procedure An individual order is not a blanket sieve Interpretive scheme: One telephone trail may be an invoice for the user, a traffic record for the operator, data retention for the state and an interference with fundamental rights for a court. The dispute will not be solved by the word “data”. It will be solved by naming purpose and regime. That is the practical value of precision. We do not ask whether the operator has something. We ask why it has it, in what scope, for how long, who wants to get to it and under which law lawfulness is tested. Only then does an answer make sense. One more distinction is often hidden. The existence of a datum is not the same as an authorisation to hand it over. A datum may arise for network operation, remain for billing, be retained from a legal duty, or be processed with consent. Each path has a different title and a different addressee of review. When the state requests an extract, it is not enough to know that a datum is somewhere. It must be clear why it exists and under which provision it is opened. 4. The content of a message is neither traffic nor location data § 97(3) of the Electronic Communications Act is hard precisely where the public picture often errs. It requires retention of traffic and location data for six months, but at the same time provides that the content of messages must be neither retained nor handed over [1] . A call, the text of an SMS or the body of an e-mail are not data retention under this provision. That does not mean that metadata are an innocent trifle. From times, numbers, cells and IP addresses one can sometimes read movement, the rhythm of a life, a circle of contacts and moments of crisis. The Constitutional Court in II. ÚS 502/2000 extended the protection of Article 13 of the Charter also to numbers called, time, duration and base stations [14] . Protection is therefore not reserved only for the words inside a call. The difference is still decisive. If someone requests the content of future communication, we look at interception under § 88. If someone requests traffic and location data at the operator, we look at § 88a and at § 97 ZEK. If someone reads a stored chat in a seized phone, we look elsewhere. Precision is not academic. It determines the threshold, the judicial filter and the consequences of error. That is why the sentence “the operator has half a year of my calls” is imprecise in two directions. It may have, for the statutory period, data about a call. It is not supposed to have the content of a call from data retention. And it may have other data for other purposes, for example billing, but that is not the same bucket. 5. Data retention is not billing. Billing is not marketing. In testimony in Pl. ÚS 45/17 a figure was heard that tempts a shortcut. A T-Mobile witness stated that for its own needs, that is billing and complaints, it retains traffic and location data in a narrower scope for two months [4] . That is documented. But its precise meaning is narrower than the public slogan. Two months are not statutory data retention. The statutory duty in § 97(3) speaks of six months and of persons who provide public networks or publicly available electronic-communications services [1] . Two months were one operator’s testimony in 2019 about its own need in a narrower scope. This is billing and complaints, not the whole of state retention. Billing is also not marketing. The same point of the judgment states that marketing purposes occurred only with consent and that retention for six months concerned approximately 70 percent of the customers of this one company in 2019 [4] . This figure measures a state described in testimony at one operator. It does not measure the Czech market in 2026 and it does not measure the legal duty of all operators. The practical conclusion is simple. If you read two months, ask: two months of what, at whom and when? If you read six months, ask: six months under which provision and without the content of what? Without those riders the numbers are precise only in appearance. 6. Retention at the operator is not interception. Nor examination of a phone. Interception under § 88 of the Code of Criminal Procedure aims at the content of future telecommunications traffic. That is a different interference from data retention. The operator does not, under § 97(3), stockpile the content of calls. If the content of future communication is to be captured, the path of interception and its conditions must be taken. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Examination of a phone is another different world. A seized device in police hands, its stored content and, from 1 January 2026, § 113a of the Code of Criminal Procedure are not the operator’s network. A phone may contain messages, photographs and a history of communication. An operator may retain traffic and location data. These layers may concern the same person and the same day, but legally they are not identical. Confusion arises when one practical story is told with one verb. “The police watched the phone.” That may mean interception, an extract of traffic data, a location datum, examination of the device, or a combination of several acts. Each has a different threshold. Each has a different document. Each has a different possibility of defence. It does not follow that one act never follows on another. An investigation may work with more than one source. It does follow that one act must not retroactively legalise another. An extract from the operator is not permission to read a phone. A seized phone is not statutory data retention. And interception is not billing. 7. The decree spells out IMSI, IMEI and cells. It does not spell out the body of a message. The statute names a category. Decree No. 357/2012 Coll. spells out the scope. It works with data needed to trace and identify the source and addressee of communication, with date, time, manner and duration, with identification of a device and with location data [2] [19] . On a mobile network that means, among other things, IMSI, IMEI and data about cells. These are words that sound technical. Their legal meaning is, however, intelligible. They do not say what you said. They say when and from where communication passed through the network, who was identified as a subscriber or a device and what the technical context of the connection was. That is precisely why they can be sensitive even though they are not content. For e-mail protocols the difference is still clearer. A traffic datum may show an address, a time or technical parameters. The body of a message is something else. If ordinary debate says that e-mails are retained, it is necessary to stop. A traffic trail is retained, not, as a matter of law, the whole text of an e-mail inside data retention. The decree therefore does not extend § 97 to content. It specifies which traffic and location data are retained, handed over and destroyed. It is a map of the bucket’s scope, not a secret list of recordings. 8. Constitutional conformity in 2019 is not the same as Union conformity in 2014-2025 The Constitutional Court in 2011 annulled the old Czech data-retention rules. Judgment Pl. ÚS 24/10 of 22 March 2011, promulgated as No. 94/2011 Coll., annulled the then § 97(3) and (4) and Decree No. 485/2005 Coll. for a lack of safeguards [3] . That was a derogating finding. The paragraph disappeared. The legislature then recast the rules, shortened the period and tightened the conditions. When the new rules came before the Constitutional Court again, the result was different. Judgment Pl. ÚS 45/17 of 14 May 2019 dismissed the application to annul and described six months as a period that is not manifestly disproportionate [5] [13] . That, however, is not the end. The Court of Justice of the EU was meanwhile deciding under the Union frame: Directive 2002/58, the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU and its articles on privacy, protection of personal data, freedom of expression and the limits of restrictions of rights [12] [17] . That is a different reference frame from the domestic constitutional test. That is why the results can diverge. The Constitutional Court in 2019 could say that the Czech rules stand in the test it applied. The Supreme Court in 2025 could say that blanket and preventive retention of practically all users will not stand against Union law [9] . That is not a logical error. It is a clash of two planes of review. 9. The CJEU annulled a directive. Then it barred blanket holding for criminal cases. Then it left narrow exceptions. The first large cut came on 8 April 2014. The Court of Justice of the EU in joined cases C-293/12 and C-594/12, Digital Rights Ireland, declared Directive 2006/24/EC on data retention invalid [6] . This was not about a Czech statute. It was about a Union directive that imposed a duty of blanket retention on Member States. The second cut came on 21 December 2016. In cases C-203/15 and C-698/15, Tele2 Sverige and Watson, the CJEU interpreted Article 15(1) of Directive 2002/58 as precluding a national rule that, for the fight against crime, provides for general and indiscriminate retention of traffic and location data of all subscribers and registered users [7] . The third step came on 6 October 2020 in cases C-511/18, C-512/18 and C-520/18, La Quadrature du Net [8] . The CJEU confirmed the ban on general and indiscriminate retention for the fight against crime, but admitted narrow possibilities, in particular in a serious threat to national security, and targeted or time-limited regimes. That is not a return to a blanket preventive store. It is a map of exceptions. The following line on national security, for example Privacy International or Commissioner of An Garda Síochána, belongs in the same context [16] . It shows that the European ceiling is not a simple “never”. It is “not this blanket way for this purpose”. The difference matters. It allows targeted regimes to be built, but not a general sieve to be hidden behind the word security. 10. The Supreme Court found a conflict. The paragraph in the Collection of Laws as of September 2026 still stands. The Supreme Court, by judgment of 30 December 2025, file No. 30 Cdo 2556/2025, according to a press release of 8 January 2026, dismissed the state’s appeal on a point of law and confirmed the unlawfulness of blanket retention of electronic-communications data [9] . The reason was a conflict of § 97(3) ZEK with Union law, because it aims at preventive indiscriminate retention of the data of practically all users. The decision was not, however, a derogating finding of the Constitutional Court. The Supreme Court decided a civil dispute about an apology. It ordered the state to apologise. It did not erase the paragraph from the Collection of Laws. That is an uncomfortable, but fundamental, distinction. As of the September 2026 research cut, therefore, two sentences stand side by side. The text of § 97(3) in the statute still stands [1] . The Supreme Court at the same time found its conflict with Union law [9] . Operators and the state thus stand in a vice: on one side a domestic duty, on the other directly effective Union limits and case-law that rejects the blanket character. That is not a stable state. But it is a state that cannot be simplified either to “everything is in order” or to “the paragraph no longer exists”. The precise sentence reads: the paragraph still stands in the text of the statute; its blanket duty is, according to the Supreme Court, in conflict with Union law. 11. A judgment about an apology is not a derogating finding The difference between annulment and an apology is practical. In 2011 the Constitutional Court annulled the then § 97(3) and (4) and the implementing decree [3] . That created a gap that the legislature had to address with new rules. That is a derogating operative part. In 2025 the Supreme Court dealt with the state’s liability for an incorrect official procedure or an unlawful interference in civil proceedings about an apology. It found a conflict of blanket retention with Union law and confirmed a duty to apologise [9] . That is a strong legal signal. But it does not have the same technical effect as annulment of a statute by the Constitutional Court. Caution is therefore in place even in a media sentence. “The Supreme Court annulled data retention” is imprecise. “The Supreme Court confirmed the unlawfulness of blanket retention and the state is to apologise” is closer. And “§ 97(3) as of the research cut still stands in the statute” completes the picture. A judgment about an apology is not a derogating finding. A paragraph may still stand. — Jiný Kontext 12. A request under § 88a is not a request for everything the operator has § 88a of the Code of Criminal Procedure governs an order to establish data on telecommunications traffic [10] . It is not a universal demand “give us everything”. It has a threshold, a purpose and a procedural regime. As worded toward 2026 it aims at an intentional offence with an upper prison term of at least three years and at further listed cases [10] . This figure measures the threshold of access to data, not a duty of the operator to create data. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Access to data is not the same as their retention. ZEK provides what is retained on a blanket basis and for how long [1] . § 88a provides when an authority in criminal proceedings may request data. These two provisions meet, but they do not have the same function. User consent may, under § 88a(3), replace the order [10] . Even that does not make it a boundless authorisation. Consent has its scope and its subject. If someone consents to the provision of a particular extract, that does not mean consent to interception, to the content of a phone or to an indefinite hunt through all data. Older history shows that even the access paragraph had to pass constitutional review. The Constitutional Court in Pl. ÚS 24/11 of 20 December 2011 annulled the then § 88a [11] . That is a reminder that it is not enough to have data stored. There must also be reviewable and proportionate access. 13. Two months at one operator in 2019 are not a 2026 market standard Two months are a useful figure precisely when the reservation stays with them. In point 34 of Pl. ÚS 45/17 a T-Mobile witness stated that the operator, for its own billing and complaint needs, retains traffic and location data in a narrower scope for two months [4] . That is a precise claim. Its limits are part of the claim. It is not a statutory period. It is not a claim about all operators. It is not a figure about 2026. It is not even the whole data-retention bucket. If someone rewrites this sentence as “operators keep data for two months”, they discard the source, the period, the population and the purpose. At another operator its terms, information duties under the GDPR, records of processing activities and answers to a concrete request have to be read. The GDPR matters here not as a further figure, but as a language of purposes: legal obligation, legitimate interest, consent [22] . Each title may mean other data and another period. The public record in the sources does not allow the sentence that all operators in 2026 bill from the same two-month window. The precise sentence is longer. But that is exactly why it is precise. 14. The first three months as the most frequent window are testimony. Not a statutory maximum. The same point of Pl. ÚS 45/17 states that authorised authorities most often request data for the first three months from the origin of the datum [4] . That is interesting. It says something about operational practice described by a witness in 2019 toward one operator. It does not say that the statutory maximum is three months. The statutory maximum of data retention under § 97(3) is six months [1] . After that period the data are to be destroyed, unless the statute provides otherwise. Six months measure the retention duty. Three months measure a most frequent request window described in testimony. Two months measure a narrower billing need. Three figures. Three buckets. The Constitutional Court in Pl. ÚS 45/17 cited partial operational estimates and testimony. That is not an open complete dataset of all police requests or all authorised authorities. The sources contain no public state statistic that could be passed off as a total number and a success rate of extracts. That is why it is good to treat the figure three with the same care as the figure two. It helps describe practice. It must not replace the statute. And it must not at all create the impression that after three months no datum under retention can exist. 15. The Czech pendulum 2011-2026 did not erase the vice between a duty and the Union ceiling The Czech data-retention story is not a straight line. In 2011 the Constitutional Court annulled the old rules [3] . In 2012 the legislature adopted a new construction, including a six-month retention period. In 2019 the Constitutional Court dismissed an application to annul [5] [13] . In 2025 the Supreme Court said that blanket preventive retention of practically all users conflicts with Union law [9] . Meanwhile European case-law moved and tightened the ceiling. Digital Rights Ireland annulled a directive [6] . Tele2 rejected national general and indiscriminate retention for the fight against crime [7] . La Quadrature du Net described narrow exceptions and targeted regimes [8] . The Czech text of the statute has not, as of the research cut, changed into a form that would remove this tension. That is legal uncertainty, not only an academic dispute. An operator has to read the Czech statute. A court has to read Union law as well. An individual has a right to protection of privacy and personal data. Authorities active in criminal proceedings want a tool for investigation. All have a piece of the truth if they describe their own layer. A shared decision is, however, wrong if it ignores the blanket character. The thesis of this article would be weakened by an amendment that replaced blanket six months with a targeted, geographically and temporally limited regime within Union limits. It would also be weakened by a new Constitutional Court judgment that, after the Supreme Court judgment, annulled § 97(3). As of the September 2026 research cut that is not in the sources. 16. Diagnosing the bucket will say more than the sentence “the operator keeps it for half a year” A practical test does not begin with how to get rid of data. It begins with what data are at issue at all. That is the difference between a legal diagnosis and advice on evasion. What needs to be tested The first question reads: are you requesting content, statutory retention, billing, marketing with consent, or access under § 88a? The content of a call or an SMS is not § 97(3). Either it is interception of future communication, or the operator is not supposed to have it from statutory data retention [1] . An extract of connections and cells for the last half-year is another bucket. Items from an invoice are another again. The second question reads: is the request individual, or blanket? An individual order under § 88a and general retention of the data of practically all users are not the same interference. Precisely the blanket and indiscriminate character is the core of the European reservation [7] [8] [9] . Three tests — content, retention, billing First test: are you requesting the words inside a call, the text of an SMS or the body of an e-mail? Then we are not in § 97(3). Second test: are you requesting traffic and location data that the statute requires to be retained for six months? Then we are talking about data retention and about access under the relevant legal title. Third test: are you requesting only data needed for an invoice or a complaint? Then you are looking at the contractual and accounting layer, not at state retention. Before a request for an extract of connections After six months statutory retention is destroyed, unless the statute provides otherwise [1] . Billing may have ended earlier. Marketing may have rested on consent and another scope. A backup in the phone, a cloud service or a chat application lives outside ZEK. A GDPR title at the operator may be a legal obligation, a legitimate interest or consent [22] . Three different reasons are not one bucket. The test therefore does not say how to delete data. It says how to ask, so that the answer is not deceptively short. 17. The hidden cost is the blanket character that the text of the statute still names Six months is at first glance an answer. In fact it is only an answer to one layer. The statute provides six-month retention of traffic and location data without content [1] . T-Mobile’s testimony in 2019 speaks of two months of billing in a narrower scope [4] . The CJEU speaks of the inadmissibility of general and indiscriminate retention for criminal cases [7] [8] . The Supreme Court speaks of a conflict of the Czech blanket duty with Union law and of an apology by the state [9] . All of that can be true at the same time, if we do not pretend that it is the same thing. The content of a call is not metadata. Billing is not retention. Marketing is not a legal duty. Access under § 88a is not retention itself. The Constitutional Court 2019 is not the CJEU 2016. And a civil judgment about an apology is not the annulment of a paragraph. The most hidden cost of the Czech rules is not only the period of six months. It is the blanket character. The duty applies to the traffic and location data of practically all subscribers of the obliged services, in advance and without suspicion. Precisely this property turns a technical archive into an interference with privacy. And precisely this property ran into Union case-law and then into the Supreme Court. The question is therefore not how long an operator retains data about your phone. It is: which bucket who is requesting — content, billing, marketing, or six months of blanket retention — and under which frame it is to be measured whether that will still stand, when the text of the statute remains and the Union ceiling has already said no? Related texts in this series May the police search your mobile phone? — a thing and memory, not six months at the operator. How does police location of a mobile phone work? — who may request data retention and what follows from a cell. Supreme Court judgment 30 Cdo 2556/2025 (30. 12. 2025) finds a Union conflict; the paragraph in ZEK as of September 2026 still stands.

items.title: Pervitin is not one thing. Brand, clandestine lab, dose, file and death do not add up to a single fate.
items.subtitle: The evidence lets a pharmaceutical name, a detected clandestine lab, lifetime experience, high-risk injecting, a seizure and a death be kept apart. It does not let them be assembled into one Czech fate, nor into a method for making the substance.

items.body: The question is: what is pervitin in the Czech Republic — from production through use to the ends of people on it? It sounds simple only until we notice that we are not comparing one thing. A brand from a pharmacy of the thirties is not today’s detected clandestine lab. The lifetime experience of four to five percent of adults is not thirty-eight thousand people in the estimate of high-risk use. One hundred and eighty-four clandestine labs is not a map of production. Twenty-seven deaths in which a special register in 2024 found pervitin or amphetamine is not an annual account of addiction. Only when these four things are separated can one read what the National Monitoring Centre, the National Drug Headquarters and the courts actually measure for 2024 and 2025 — and what still does not follow about an “end”. 1. The epidemiologist, the police officer and the field see the same substance in three statistics Imagine a table on which five files lie and no substance to photograph. An epidemiologist from the National Monitoring Centre for Drugs and Addiction puts down an estimate: in the Czech Republic there are 47.5 thousand people who use drugs in a high-risk way, of whom 38.2 thousand use pervitin. He says this is a multiplication from service clients, not a count of bodies in the street. He is right about the unit his report can carry [1] [2] . Beside him sits a criminal investigator from the National Drug Headquarters. He says that among stimulants in the Czech Republic pervitin has the greatest health, social and criminogenic effects, that production and distribution are changing, and that the price in the regions runs in the order of thousands of crowns per gram. He is right about the market he sees in files and seizures. He does not measure the same thing as the epidemiologist’s estimate of 38.2 thousand [4] . A field worker from a low-threshold programme puts down a third file. In 2024, 41.0 thousand drug users were in contact with low-threshold services, of whom 30 thousand with pervitin and 36 thousand by injection. That is contact with a service. It is not prevalence in the population and it is not the number of detected clandestine labs [1] [2] . A psychiatrist adds an outpatient return: among patients with illicit drugs, “other stimulants” — pervitin and amphetamines — are a strong group, but polydrug use is larger. A public prosecutor sees § 283. A family sees a person who does not sleep, loses weight and loses work. Each is a little right. No one, however, is adding the same unit. At first glance this is a dispute about “how bad pervitin is in the Czech Republic”. In fact each is defending a different object: an estimate of high-risk use, a police picture of the market, the clientele of services, a diagnosis, the elements of an offence, a household. They can therefore all be partly right and the shared sentence “pervitin will destroy the Czech Republic” still wrong. The first rule is therefore not: believe the worst figure. It reads: write one sentence that the figure is supposed to prove. A brand from a pharmacy is not a Czech clandestine lab. — Jiný Kontext 2. Pervitin has at least six layers An epidemiologist at the window with a bundle of reports: each folder measures a different layer of the same word. The word pervitin looks like one object. In a file, at school, on television and at the family table it is used for a substance, a person, a criminal offence and a death. In fact it is a bundle of layers that do not add up. The first layer is the name and the chemical identity. The active substance is methamphetamine. In vernacular: pervitin, piko, perník. The pharmaceutical brand Pervitin from Berlin in the thirties is the history of a medicine. Today’s illicit market is a different regime [16] [4] . The second layer is supply. For 2024 the NMS records 184 detected clandestine labs, seizures of powder and of tablets with (pseudo)ephedrine, and the coincidence of domestic production with imports. That is a police and monitoring picture. It is not a recipe, and this text does not supply one [1] [4] . The third layer is use in the population. Lifetime experience, use in the past twelve months, school ESPAD, the estimate of people who use drugs in a high-risk way, injecting and a metabolite in wastewater measure four to five different things [1] [8] [6] . The fourth layer is harm to the body. Infection, non-fatal intoxication, injury, a traffic accident, dual diagnosis, the special mortality register. Each series has a different denominator [1] [2] . The fifth layer is law. Manufacture and other handling under § 283 of the Criminal Code is not possession for one’s own use under § 284 and is not a misdemeanour under the Addictive Substances Act. A quantity greater than small is case-law, not an impression of the weight on a kitchen scale [10] [12] [13] . The sixth layer is care and what people call an end: contact with a low-threshold service, psychiatry, a therapeutic community, prison, debt, loss of housing, death. An end is several accounts. It is not one fate that can be read from one statistic. This layering is not an academic detail. It decides whether a figure belongs in a sentence at all. If we are talking about a brand, we cannot make it a map of Czech clandestine labs. If we are talking about ESPAD, we cannot make it the estimate of 38.2 thousand. If we are talking about a death in the register, we cannot make it a biography of everyone who has ever taken the substance. 3. The best reading is the one whose swap you can bear An article about pervitin usually breaks into one of five errors. Either pharmaceutical history is made into an explanation of today. Or a lifetime “sometime” is made into a youth epidemic. Or a detected clandestine lab is made into proof that “everyone cooks it”. Or injecting is made into HIV. Or a death with the substance in the toxicology is made into a verdict that pervitin kills more than opioids because it is Czech. The table is not a ranking of horror. It is a map of swaps that the text has to bear before it builds a conclusion from them. Type of failure What it looks like How to test it What limits the harm Brand as today Temmler and the Wehrmacht as a guide to a Czech clandestine lab Separate the history of the medicine from the police picture of 2024 Do not cite a wartime tablet as epidemiology Experience as addiction 4–5% of adults = 38.2 thousand high-risk users Ask about the period, the threshold and the method Do not add “sometime in life” to a multiplier Lab as production 184 = how much is produced Detected sites vs. the unknown remainder Do not convert a count of labs into kilograms of consumption Seizure as consumption 164 kg = the annual market The share of small seizures; one piece of 93 kg Do not leave the weight to one case Injection as HIV 89% of high-risk users inject, therefore an HIV epidemic 6 new injecting HIV vs. 668 VHC Name the infection by name Death as a mono-account 27 = “they die of pervitin” Combinations; opioids 30 of the same 52 Read the register as toxicology, not as biography Low-threshold as treatment 30 thousand clients = 30 thousand cured Contact ≠ abstinence Do not read a service as the conclusion of therapy Illustrative scheme: Six columns — name, supply, prevalence, body, file, care — can, for the same word pervitin, move up and down independently. The stamp “the end of people on it” is an attempt to add what cannot be added. It does not follow that the harm is small. It follows that the harm a sentence can carry must sit on the layer the sentence names. 4. A brand from a pharmacy is not a Czech clandestine lab An empty 1939 Pervitin tablet case: a pharmaceutical name, not a Czech clandestine lab. Jan Wellen, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 . A historic Temmler medicine case. It is not today’s market and it is not a method. Pervitin is so settled a word in Czech that it looks like a domestic invention. Chemically it is methamphetamine. The brand Pervitin was put on the market in 1938 as a stimulant by the Berlin firm Temmler-Werke after a patent of 1937. In Germany the preparation later became prescription-only; the Deutschlandmuseum records availability on prescription until 1988 [16] . The military issuing of tablets to the Wehrmacht is a historical file about another country, another regime and another legality. TIME cites the historian Steinkamp in connection with blitzkrieg; that is a debate about wartime pharmacology, not about Czech low-threshold services in 2024 [17] . In 2025 the NPC says expressly that methamphetamine is traditionally called pervitin in the Czech Republic and that the Czech market is specific in Europe by a historically rooted model of community production and a high share of high-risk users [4] . That is a description of a market. It is not proof that today’s illicit methamphetamine is a Temmler tablet. Nor is it a method for making the substance. It does not follow that the name is an accident. It follows that the name has survived regimes and that today’s reader lumps a medicine, a wartime tablet, a kitchen clandestine lab and imported industrial methamphetamine into one word. The first distinction of the article is therefore not moral. It is nominal: when you say pervitin, say which of these four things you mean. 5. A lifetime four to five percent is not thirty-eight thousand high-risk users The summary of the Report on Illicit Drugs 2025 states that 4–5 percent of persons over 15 report experience with pervitin in their lifetime. Ecstasy 5–7 percent, cocaine 5 percent. Cannabis sometime in life 29–34 percent. That is the general population and the threshold “at least once” [2] . The 2023 national survey in the face-to-face part showed a lower point: pervitin sometime in life 2.3 percent. Another wave of the same research year gave 3.8 percent. The NMS therefore works in the summary with a band of 2024 studies, not with one magic percentage [1] . Neither of these values is the estimate of 38.2 thousand people who use pervitin in a high-risk way. The NMS defines high-risk use in the European tradition: injecting and/or long-term or regular use of pervitin and opioids. That is a different threshold from “I tried it at a party in 2011” [1] . The rate of pervitin use in the general population is, according to the NMS, stable over the long term. For cocaine, by contrast, prevalence in the past twelve months is rising. Stability in the general population and growth in the high-risk estimate for pervitin can hold at the same time, because they do not measure the same density of use [2] . It does not follow that an experiment is without risk. It follows that the sentence “every other person takes it” does not follow from a lifetime four percent. And the sentence “we have 38 thousand addicts” does not follow from the same four percent either. Addiction as a diagnosis is a further threshold that these two series do not open by themselves. 6. ESPAD among sixteen-year-olds is not a map of adult clandestine labs The European school study ESPAD 2024 in the Czech Republic worked with 6,845 questionnaires, of which 2,977 were from students born in 2008. At least once in their life 25.1 percent of sixteen-year-olds had used an illicit drug, most often cannabis (23.9 percent). Pervitin and amphetamines alike 1.4 percent lifetime. Cocaine 1.9 percent. In the past twelve months, use of pervitin, amphetamines, cocaine and heroin moved at about 0.8 to 1.3 percent [1] [8] [9] . The NMS states that the rate of pervitin use among Czech sixteen-year-olds in 2024 was the same as the European average. Hallucinogens and ecstasy were above average. That is an inconvenient sentence for a headline that wants to make the Czech Republic a country where pervitin begins at secondary school [1] . The NMS dates the decline in lifetime prevalence of pervitin among students already from 1999; in the past ten years the series has been stable. That is not proof that the adult high-risk market is disappearing. A sixteen-year-old at school and a twenty-eight-year-old in the high-risk estimate are two populations [1] [9] . It does not follow that a school needs no prevention. It follows that ESPAD does not measure clandestine labs in the Moravian-Silesian Region and does not measure 30 thousand low-threshold clients. Anyone who makes a map of Czech production out of 1.4 percent is adding a school questionnaire to a police site. 7. A multiplier from low-threshold work is not a count of people in the street The estimate of 47.5 thousand people who use drugs in a high-risk way and 38.2 thousand for pervitin stands on a multiplication method from data on clients of harm-reduction services. Injecting 42.5 thousand, about 90 percent of high-risk users. For opioids and pervitin, injecting about 89 percent [1] [2] . That is a strong figure and it already has a reservation in the method. We do not see everyone who uses. We see those who pass through the network, and from them the whole is estimated. When the network thickens, the estimate can rise without the hidden market rising by the same share. When the network thins, the estimate can fall without the harm falling. In low-threshold programmes in 2024 41.0 thousand users, 30 thousand for pervitin, 9 thousand for opioids, 36 thousand by injection. The NMS notes a long-term rise in the number of pervitin users in this clientele [2] . Contact of 30 thousand and an estimate of 38.2 thousand are related series. They are not the same. The first is recorded contact. The second is a model. In prison in 2024, 62 percent of sentenced persons in the survey reported experience with an illicit drug before entry; pervitin lifetime 47 percent, in the last thirty days before entry 31 percent. In prison 27 percent had ever used a drug, most often pervitin (16 percent). The share of people who use drugs in a high-risk way in the prison population of the survey rose to 44 percent, an estimate of 7,900 persons [1] . That is a prison layer. It is not the estimate of 38.2 thousand carried behind the wall. 8. A detected clandestine lab is not a map of production In 2024, 184 pervitin clandestine labs were detected in the Czech Republic, in 2023 189. Small domestic labs predominate: 57 percent with a capacity usually lower than 50 grams per cycle. The number of labs in the order of hundreds of grams up to half a kilogram per cycle is rising. Large-volume production intended mainly for export was, according to the NMS, found most often in the north-western borderland and in the Central Bohemian Region. The most detections: Moravian-Silesian Region 35, South Moravian 32 [1] . In its annual report for 2024 the NPC gives around two hundred laboratories and for 2024 specifically 192. That is not proof that the NMS is counting wrongly. They are two outputs of two records. They do not merge into one “true” count unless a report says they are the same set [5] [1] . The text may say what detections measure: sites the police found. It must not make 184 into a sentence about how many labs in the country are running. It must not make the cycle capacity of those detected into a method. The main precursors remain, according to the NMS, ephedrine and pseudoephedrine from medicines imported chiefly from Poland and Serbia; in 2024, 97.6 thousand tablets and 80.4 kg of powder were seized. That is a seizure of raw material, not a recipe [1] . Pervitin production in the Czech Republic, according to the NMS, supplies the domestic market to a considerable extent. At the same time large-volume production is moving abroad — Poland, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium [1] [4] . Both sentences can hold. The first describes where part of domestic production goes. The second describes where a more industrial grade moves when criminal pressure at home rises. 9. Domestic production is not the same as imported industrial methamphetamine In 2025 the NPC describes a coincidence that a headline likes to erase. Traditional community production in small laboratories, often in flats and farm buildings, with an output in the order of tens of grams per cycle, stands beside the import of large-volume methamphetamine made in Western Europe and beside cases in which the imported substance is further processed at home or mixed with domestic production [4] . The European drug agency and UNODC both point to a shift of synthetic stimulants into industrial laboratories. The NPC mentions the Netherlands, Belgium and the Baltic states. A global branch toward Afghan ephedra is the context of the world market. It is not a description of a Czech kitchen clandestine lab, and this article does not make it a domestic scenario [4] [21] [15] . It does not follow that the “Czech path” has disappeared. The 184 detected clandestine labs in 2024 contradict that. It follows that the user at the end of the chain does not measure which of these supplies arrived in the bag, and that purity and adulterants are therefore not one property of “Czech pervitin”. Mixing of domestic and imported product, according to the NPC, on the contrary increases the variability of composition [4] . Distribution, according to both the NMS and the NPC, is moving from the street into online groups, parcel services and dead drops. That changes the trail for the police. It does not change the definition of the substance and it does not authorise the article to make an encrypted group into a buying guide [1] [4] . The environmental burden — toxic waste and the risk of fire — is a repeated layer of supply in police reports. It is harm at the site and in the water, not proof of the number of users [4] . 10. One hundred and sixty-four kilograms of seizures is not the country’s consumption In criminal proceedings in 2024, 884 seizures of pervitin amounting to 163.8 kg of powder were recorded. In total the NMS gives 164.9 kg. In misdemeanour proceedings, 1,542 seizures of 1.1 kg. Most criminal cases, 72 percent, were seizures weighing less than 10 grams. The largest seizure was 93.0 kg [1] . Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext That is important geometry. The median seizure and the sum of kilograms tell two stories. The sum is pulled by one large piece. The number of cases is pulled by small gram amounts. Anyone who makes 164 kg into “the Czech Republic’s annual consumption” ignores that a seizure is what was found, not what was consumed, and that one case can weigh more than hundreds of small ones. Cannabis remained the most frequently seized drug (1,022 seizures of herbal material, 609 kg in criminal proceedings). Pervitin was second in the order of seizures. The order of seizures is not the order of harms. The NMS and the NPC alike place the greatest health and social weight of a stimulant precisely on pervitin, while the seizure statistic in kilograms can look different [1] [4] [2] . 11. The purity of a sample is not the safety of a dose In 987 analysed samples of pervitin in 2024 the average share of the active substance was 68.8 percent, the minimum 0.1 percent, the maximum 81.8 percent. The ten-year average moves between 64 and 70 percent and the NMS records a rising trend. The price was known in 387 cases: most often CZK 2,000 per gram, a range of 500 to 5,000 CZK [1] . In its 2025 annual report the NPC gives the purity of seized methamphetamine as a rule between 70 and 80 percent and a price by region most often CZK 1,000 to 2,500 per gram, approaching cocaine [4] . That is not proof that one of the figures is lying. They are two outputs on different sets and in a different language of rounding. The article must not average them into a “true purity”. High purity in a police laboratory does not say that a particular dose on a table is predictable. The minimum of 0.1 percent in the same set of 987 samples is a reservation against the sentence that “Czech pervitin is always pure”. The maximum of 81.8 percent is a reservation against the sentence that adulterants protect the user. Neither is a method of use. Both are an argument why the eye and a dealer’s reputation are not toxicology. The NPC links the closing of the price with cocaine to polydrug use. That is a market observation. It is not proof that every low-threshold client alternates the two substances [4] . 12. Injecting is not an HIV epidemic About 89 percent of people who use opioids or pervitin in a high-risk way inject. That is the main route of transmission of infections in this population. It is not automatically a Czech HIV epidemic [1] [2] . In 2024, 269 new HIV cases were reported, of which 6 by transmission through injecting drug use and in a further 15 injecting was in the history. Since 1985 the NMS records 179 cases of HIV transmission by the injecting route. The share has long been low [2] . Viral hepatitis C is another account: 1,445 new cases, 668 (46 percent) among people who inject drugs. Hepatitis B: 40 cases, of which 6 in PWID. Hepatitis A in 2024: 634, of which 20 in PWID; by 5 October 2025 already 1,842 VHA cases in the general epidemiology, which the NMS gives as context for a rise, not as a pervitin series [2] . In 2024, 9.1 million syringes were issued, 213 pieces per injecting user. The NMS reads this as the WHO high-coverage band for HIV prevention [1] [19] . That measures harm-reduction material. It does not measure whether a particular person used a syringe once. The NMS reports psychiatric comorbidity in 30–60 percent of clients of addictology services; among patients in opioid-agonist treatment a dual diagnosis of 57 percent. Toxic psychosis is present in the clinical description of services. It is not a national register of “madness from pervitin” with one percentage [1] [2] . Naloxone (Nyxoid) in 31 programmes: 982 doses, 218 reported uses that averted opioid overdoses. That is an opioid safeguard. It does not transfer to a stimulant [2] . Anyone who makes a low-threshold success with opioids into proof that a pervitin overdose is solved has confused the substances. 13. Twenty-seven deaths with pervitin in the register are not an annual account of addiction A consultation in a surgery: the end a family sees is not the same as a line in the special register. The special mortality register recorded in 2024 a total of 73 fatal overdoses of illicit drugs, volatile substances and benzodiazepines. Illicit drugs and volatile substances were identified in 52 cases: opioids 30 (including 6 heroin/morphine), pervitin or amphetamine 27, benzodiazepines 21 — the most in a decade. Combinations of substances are rising [1] [2] . Twenty-seven is therefore not the sentence “twenty-seven people died of pervitin”. It is the sentence: in 27 of 52 cases with an identified illicit drug or volatile substance, the toxicology found pervitin or amphetamine, often in a landscape where substances add up. Opioids in the same denominator of 52 cases have 30. Anyone who wants to make pervitin the Czech number-one killer must first bear that the register in this year shows opioid traces more strongly, and that benzodiazepines are rising. Non-fatal intoxications: 675 cases, 380 in connection with illicit drugs; among them stimulants including pervitin and unspecified drugs. Hospitalisations for injuries with an illicit drug: 467 (3 percent of injuries under the influence of addictive substances). Traffic: 415 accidents under the influence of illicit drugs (0.45 percent of all accidents), 12 dead; 101 cases of a combination of alcohol and drugs in the person at fault [2] . These are ends that healthcare and transport record. They are not all the ends a family calls an end: loss of children, housing, teeth, work, a relationship. The NMS captures those in part in the social chapter — unstable housing, debts in the order of hundreds of thousands among low-threshold clients, an estimate of the social costs of illicit drugs of CZK 5.6–6.7 billion against tens to hundreds of billions for alcohol and tobacco, household spending on illicit drugs around CZK 10 billion (0.3–0.5 percent of spending) [2] . Billions are a macro-account. They are not a biography. Twenty-seven deaths with a substance in the register are not a map of all ends. — Jiný Kontext 14. Paragraph 283 is not paragraph 284 and is not a misdemeanour A code on a windowsill: manufacture, possession and a misdemeanour have three different ceilings. In 2024, 4.2 thousand primary drug offences were registered, two percent of all detected criminal offences. Most often manufacture and distribution of pervitin under § 283. Of those detained for a primary drug offence, about 47 percent had a link to pervitin, about 35 percent to cannabis. The share of those detained for possession for their own use under § 284 rose to 21 percent [1] [2] [10] . Convicted of a primary drug offence were 2,545 persons, most often for manufacture and distribution of pervitin or cannabis. Main sanction: a suspended sentence 53 percent, unsuspended 26 percent. Under the influence of illicit drugs, 5,628 criminal offences (36 percent of offences under the influence of addictive substances), most often endangerment under the influence (§ 274) and intoxication (§ 360) [2] [10] . Misdemeanours in connection with illicit substances: 10,369. The NPC records 9,644 persons in misdemeanours of unlawful handling; 76 percent cannabis, 17 percent pervitin, a year-on-year fall for pervitin of 403 persons [1] . As a quantity greater than small for pervitin, the criminal division of the Supreme Court treats more than 1.5 grams of the drug, which must contain at least 0.5 g of methamphetamine as base or 0.6 g of the hydrochloride. Below this threshold, without signs of distribution, it is as a rule not § 284 but a misdemeanour under the Addictive Substances Act. Indicative values are in the annex to opinion Tpjn 301/2013; a particular case may need toxicology [12] [13] [11] . An amendment effective from 1 January 2026 releases cannabis within statutory bounds for persons over 21. Methamphetamine does not become lawful by this amendment. Mixing “partial legalisation of cannabis” with pervitin is another layer of law [4] [10] . It does not follow that possession under 1.5 grams is without consequence. It follows that the sentence “for pervitin one goes to prison” without the offence and without the quantity is a map without a scale. 15. Contact with a low-threshold service is not a cure The NMS divides addictology services into prevention, harm reduction, outpatient care, short-term stabilisation, residential care and aftercare. In 2024 there were 15,059 persons with dependence on illicit drugs in outpatient psychiatric care. Return A013: 13,796 users of illicit drugs and volatile substances, of whom 3,584 other stimulants (26.0 percent) and 4,735 polydrug (34.3 percent). For pervitin in outpatient care the age 30–39 dominates [1] [2] . Applicants for treatment: 5,339 persons named methamphetamine. Therapeutic communities supported by the Office of the Government: of 343 people using drugs, 234 had primary pervitin, mean age 31 years. Aftercare with sheltered housing: pervitin primary in 587 of 743 (78.8 percent) [1] . That is a strong concentration of pervitin in the treatment network. It is not proof that 38.2 thousand passed through a community. 234 places in eleven communities is a bottleneck against the high-risk estimate. Opioid-agonist treatment (1,991 persons in the NRLUD in 2024) is an opioid track. For pervitin there is no comparable substitution in these figures. That is why the stimulant appears elsewhere in the network: low-threshold work, outpatient care, community, prison units (571 voluntarily, 208 protective treatment in 11 prisons) [2] . State spending on addictology services CZK 1,054.3 million in 2024, with regions and municipalities 1,631.1 million. VZP for disorders from illicit drugs CZK 527.4 million, of which 380.3 million for combinations of substances. That is a payer’s account. It is not an account of “how much pervitin cost” [1] [20] . As of September 2025, 220 addictology services had certification. The map of services on drogy-info.cz is a practical output of this layer. It is not a promise that a person who enters the map will leave the substance [2] [3] [14] . 16. Wastewater measures a metabolite in a city. It does not measure a person’s fate The central treatment plant on Císařský ostrov: the inflow measures a metabolite in the city, not a person’s fate. ŠJů, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 . Prague is one of seven Czech cities in the SCORE campaign. Wastewater analysis in the SCORE project has run in Europe since 2011. For the Czech Republic the partner is the T. G. Masaryk Water Research Institute. In the 2024 campaign the NMS lists seven cities: Prague, České Budějovice, Plzeň, Karlovy Vary, Ústí nad Labem, Brno and Ostrava. The results confirm above-average concentrations of methamphetamine against other European cities and a year-on-year rise against 2023 for methamphetamine, MDMA and cocaine [1] [7] . EUDA as of 18 March 2026 summarises the 2025 campaign: about 115 cities in 25 countries, weekly composite samples at the inflow of treatment plants. Methamphetamine in Europe is historically concentrated in the Czech Republic and Slovakia, with signals elsewhere as well. Unlike cocaine and MDMA, the methamphetamine load is spread through the week, not only the weekend. The load in a city is not a resident’s diagnosis. Industrial inputs and the uncertainty of the method belong among the reservations that EUDA itself carries for the method [6] . It does not follow that wastewater “has no value”. It follows that a ranking of cities measures a metabolite at the inflow, not the number of people who end in the mortality register, and not the number of clandestine labs in a region. Ústí or Budějovice at the top of a European comparison are an argument about the geography of consumption. They are not an argument about the name of a particular person. 17. Three questions say more than the word pervitin A headline asks for a story from supply to death. The evidence asks three questions that can bear a mistake. What needs to be tested before you say “they cook it in the Czech Republic” Whether you are talking about the 184 detected clandestine labs of 2024, about the seizure of 97.6 thousand tablets of (pseudo)ephedrine, or about the import of finished methamphetamine, which the NPC places beside domestic production. Whether you separate the site the police found from the production they did not find. This test ends at the source. It does not begin with a method. Three tests before a sentence about an end First: which end. Death in 27 items of the register, prison, dual diagnosis, loss of housing, debt. Second: which substance in the body. Pervitin, an opioid, a benzodiazepine, a combination. Third: which population. A sixteen-year-old in ESPAD, a low-threshold client, an applicant for treatment, a sentenced person, a deceased person in the special register. Before looking for a method An article that promises production, use and ends in one take tempts a third, forbidden layer: how to do it. That layer is not here. It is not a gap in the reporting. It is a condition for the text to be able to stand beside justice and public health, and not beside a method. For a person close to someone, the practical step is a map of certified services and low-threshold work, not a discussion forum [3] [14] . Interpretive scheme: One sentence of the reader — “they cook it”, “the young take it”, “people die of it”, “we have HIV” — and one column of the source. If the sentence and the column do not sit, the sentence is not used. 18. The question is not how bad it is. It is which layer you are adding Pervitin in the Czech Republic is heavy enough not to need exaggeration. 38.2 thousand in the estimate of high-risk use. 30 thousand in low-threshold work. 184 detected clandestine labs. 5,339 applicants for treatment with methamphetamine. 47 percent of prisoners in the survey with lifetime experience. An above-average load in wastewater. 668 new VHC among people who inject. 27 deaths in whose toxicology there is pervitin or amphetamine, beside 30 opioid ones. The hidden cost is not that figures are missing. The hidden cost is when they are added into one curve and the curve becomes a fate. A brand from 1938, a kitchen clandestine lab, an imported kilogram, a school 1.4 percent, a multiplier, a seizure of 93 kg, a purity of 68.8 percent, a syringe, a file under § 283 and a death in a combination of substances then look like one substance that “takes people”. In fact they are six layers that can tell the truth about one person only separately — and about a country as a whole need not tell a fate at all. The right question is therefore not: how do people on pervitin end. It is: which layer you are adding now, which denominator can carry your sentence, and which end — body, file, service, death — you are willing to bear when it turns out that you added wrongly. Related texts in this series This article stands outside twenty texts on AI, data and proof. It shares with them the discipline of layers. It does not add the series on power and law into the same sum: there the unit is the power of an official and a statement about punishment; here prevalence, a clandestine lab, a seizure and a death. Anyone who reads about what a photograph can carry as evidence is reading a related question: which object you measure before you make it a fate. Power and law 01 — “Up to five years threatened” is not the correct punishment Power and law 02 — Money that arrived for a purchase is not operational cover Power and law 03 — Three grams off duty are not the same as revealing a patrol 12 — A genuine image can deceive without editing

items.title: A familiar number on the display is not an identity. An authorisation you confirmed yourself is no longer an “unauthorised payment”.
items.subtitle: A scam is not recognised because a number or a header looks like a bank. It is recognised because the channel asks for an action: a datum, a code, a transfer or remote access, without verification through a second, previously known channel.
