items.body: The question is what happened when a Rychnov police officer procured pervitin and reported where patrols were standing — and whether the punishment was what it should have been. It sounds simple only until we notice that we are not comparing one thing. Three to three and a half grams off duty are not the same as the movement of patrols on duty. An aggregate of eighteen months punished both at once, not "only the drug". Sixty thousand and a five-year ban are executed even with a suspended sentence. And "faced up to five years" is again not a judgment, it is a ceiling. Only when these four things are separated can one read what the District Court in Rychnov nad Kněžnou finally imposed on 21 February 2022 — and what still does not follow from that about "a police officer always takes". 1. A dealer, a driver without a licence and a court measure three things Imagine a table after finality. A reader hears "a police officer and pervitin" and sees a pocket. He is right about one branch of the act. He is not right about the other. GIBS described that the man, at least three times from October 2020 to May 2021, off duty, procured for a civilian each time three to three and a half grams of pervitin for roughly ten thousand crowns. The civilian was to use the substance, or to distribute it further — the inspection leaves both [13] [12] . Next to him sits a driver who lost his licence and drove anyway. He says he needed to know where the patrol was. From December 2020 to May 2021 the police officer on duty, according to the indictment, told him that — and one more person in the same situation. He is right about what the account calls abuse of authority. He is not measuring grams [13] [3] . The judge lays down a third file. Guilt on both misdemeanours. Aggregate: eighteen months of imprisonment with a suspension for four years, 60 thousand crowns, a ban on activity in the security corps for five years, forfeiture of a thing. Finality 21 February 2022. Faced up to five years [13] [7] . At first glance this is a dispute about "whether for drugs in uniform a suspended sentence fell". In fact each person is defending a different object: a substance off duty, a key on duty, an aggregate, money, a ban. That is why they can all be partly right and the shared sentence "he got little, because it was only three grams" still wrong. The first rule is not: add the grams. It is: write which act the punishment is supposed to prove. A defence lawyer at the table would say that off duty the man was not in a patrol and that three handovers to one person are not a trade. A prosecutor would say that service knowledge of the movement of vehicles is not a private message. A judge would say that the aggregate punishes both, and that five years of a ban is a longer punishment on the key than how many bars eighteen months promise in a headline. A reader would say that a suspended sentence is zero. Four sentences. The law can bear the first three. The fourth it can bear only when a suspension is turned into an acquittal — and that is what § 81 does not do [7] [13] [3] . Three grams off duty are not the same as leaking a patrol. — Jiný Kontext 2. The case has at least six layers Two folders on one table: substance and patrol met in the judgment, not in the act. The word Rychnov in this case looks like one drug case. In fact it is a bundle. The first layer is the person. A former police officer of Territorial Department Rychnov nad Kněžnou. The regional directorate said in February 2022 that he had been released from the performance of duty. The account after the judgment says "former". Public sources at the core do not carry a name. This text does not supply one [12] [13] . The second layer is § 283: procuring pervitin for another, three times, off duty, 3–3.5 g, in the account a total value of 10 000 Kč for those three handovers as Nguyenová described them in February, and "roughly 10 thousand" in the April report on the judgment. The figures read as the same order, not as two different trades. This text does not add them into thirty thousand, because the account did not carry that unambiguously [12] [13] [2] . The third layer is § 329: information about the movement of vehicles and patrols to two people without a driving licence, on duty, the same half-year window [3] [13] . The fourth layer is a find at a search: before the judgment iDNES cited seven plants and crumble, 64.6 grams of cannabis, 3.14 grams of active substance. After the judgment GIBS says that forfeiture of a thing applies to the cannabis. That is an accessory punishment, not the core of the two misdemeanours in the press sentence about guilt [12] [13] . The fifth layer is the punishment and the stage: a charge in May 2021, an indictment in January 2022, judgment and finality on 21 February, a GIBS press briefing in April [13] [7] . The sixth layer is the service relationship and the public impression. A five-year ban. Dismissal after intent. The headline again carries a suspended sentence as zero. The law carries an aggregate, money and a ban [8] [13] . The regional directorate in February 2022, still before the publication of finality, refused details and said only a release from performance. That is a service measure, not a punishment. Release from performance means that at that moment the man did not have the key on him on a shift. It does not mean guilt. Guilt came only with the judgment. Anyone who fuses both sentences is punishing a person twice with the same verb. The law punishes them once criminally and once in service, in another regime and at another time [12] [8] [9] . GIBS was created outside the corps precisely so that someone could bear this double sentence. The case did not end with a deputy. It ended at a district court. That is part of the answer to "they watched themselves". They did not. The inspection submitted the matter to a prosecutor, the prosecutor an indictment, the court an aggregate [1] [13] [15] . 3. The best reading is the one whose mix-up you can bear Five mistakes here are almost those of a corps. Either grams become the whole guilt. Or patrols become a "friendly service". Or an aggregate becomes a punishment "only for drugs". Or a suspended sentence becomes the claim that 60 thousand and a ban do not run. Or one man becomes the claim that a police officer always takes. Type of failure What it looks like How to test What limits the harm Grams as the whole guilt "A suspended sentence for three grams" Separate § 283 and § 329 Read both misdemeanours in one GIBS sentence A patrol as a kindness "He only wrote where the radar stands" The signs of § 329 A key on duty is not an SMS to a friend An aggregate as one branch A comparison with Příbram only by grams A different concurrence Do not add terms across paragraphs A suspended sentence as zero "He walked away" § 81(2) Money and a ban are executed The man as a corps "The police cover drivers without papers" One person, two civilians Do not add to Domašov From that it does not follow that both acts are equally heavy. It follows that a sentence about leniency must bear both, otherwise it measures a pocket and issues it as a key. The best reading is the one that survives when it turns out that eighteen months punished the patrols as well. A bad reading is the one that turns a suspended sentence into zero and zero into proof that the corps sells patrols. The damage from the first mix-up falls on the judgment. The damage from the second falls on people this account did not convict. 4. Three grams off duty are not a patrol on duty The account expressly divides time and regime. Procuring pervitin: off duty. Information about patrols: in a period when he let people who drove without a licence know — and iDNES places that "directly on duty" [12] [13] . That is not an academic division of shifts. It is a division of a protected interest. § 283 protects society from handling a substance. § 329 protects the exercise of the authority of an official. Anyone who fuses them into "he took something into his pocket" loses exactly the branch that makes the case a case of power, not only a case of gram weight [2] [3] . Off duty a police officer is not relieved of criminality for production and procurement. On duty he additionally carries a key. The account punishes both. A text that wrote only about pervitin would turn Rychnov into Příbram without a key. A text that wrote only about patrols would turn it into Domašov without a judgment. It is a concurrence. A concurrence is punished in an aggregate with one term, not two rankings. From that it does not follow that procurement off duty is a "private matter". It follows that a private shift does not lift § 283 and a service shift adds § 329. Anyone who reads only the first branch is reading Příbram without a key. Anyone who reads only the second is reading Domašov without a judgment. Rychnov is both in one aggregate. That is why the part exists as a third, not as a repetition of the second [2] [3] [13] . 5. Three times three to three and a half grams is not a map of a market Three handovers. Each time 3–3.5 g. One civilian. The period October 2020 to May 2021. GIBS: for his own use, or for further distribution. It does not know which. This text does not supply that [13] . A quantity greater than small for pervitin is, in the case law of the Supreme Court, more than 1.5 grams of the drug with at least 0.5 g of base. Three grams are above this indicative threshold — as a threshold of criminality for possession, not as proof that it was a large extent. A large extent is another paragraph. The account does not name it for Rychnov. The basic range "up to five years" matches that [19] [20] [2] [13] . Article 21 may carry seizures in kilograms and an estimate of 38.2 thousand risky users. This case does not assemble that estimate from nine to ten and a half grams in three doses. It assembles three acts of one person. Before the judgment iDNES wrote that the police officer "bought" pervitin and handed it over. After the judgment GIBS writes procured and handed over. The difference of the verb is not a trifle: a purchase for oneself is another branch than procuring for another. The criminal sentence the indictment bore is the second. This text therefore does not turn the man into a map of his own use, even if a reader would expect that. Use is not the core in the account of guilt. The core is a handover to a civilian and the key of a patrol. Anyone who assembles from a headline about a purchase "he took and therefore reported" has joined two motives that the court did not join in the aggregate by a public sentence [12] [13] [15] . Three handovers to one person are also not proof that it was an organised group. § 283(2) knows a group as a qualification. The account does not name it. The basic range and "up to five years" match that. We do not write a qualification into the file, even if from "dealer" in colloquial Czech it seemed ready to hand [2] [13] . 6. Ten thousand crowns are not a trade from Kroměříž Jakubec sold in 2016 and 2017 in the Kroměříž and Přerov districts, the judge said a trade, plus a bribe of 30 thousand for a burglary, a punishment of three years on five years and a ten-year ban. Rychnov carries in the account an order of ten thousand at three handovers to one civilian. Adding them into "a police officer traded in pervitin" is a truth about a substance and a lie about extent and about a bribe [14] [13] . Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Ten thousand is, in the account, a price the inspection assigned to the handovers. It is not a "considerable" property benefit in the sense of a qualification this text may infer. It is not proof that it was a gift either. It is a figure that keeps the case on the ground: it is not tonnes, it is not zero. Jakubec waived appeal at court. The Rychnov account is silent about an appeal and places finality on the day of pronouncement. That usually means that no one challenged the judgment in the statutory period, or that they waived the right. The text does not finish that for the parties. It says only that a review by a second instance is not in the public source. The question "it should have been harsher" therefore had here no appellate senate that would carry it [14] [13] . 7. Cannabis at a search is not the core of an indictment iDNES on 9 February 2022, therefore before the judgment, cited a find: seven small plants, green-brown crumble, 64.6 g, 3.14 g of active substance. The April report on finality says that the punishment of forfeiture of a thing applies to the cannabis [12] [13] . Forfeiture is a punishment on a thing. It is not a second range of imprisonment. Anyone who turns the plants into a "grow-op" misses a threshold the account did not carry. Anyone who leaves them out misses that the court added to the aggregate one more visible punishment that a suspension under § 81(2) will not postpone [7] . The core of guilt in the GIBS press sentence remains: § 283 and § 329. Cannabis is an add-on that the account itself ranks with a search and with forfeiture. 8. Leaking patrols is section 329, not a friendly service An official who, with the intent of procuring an unauthorised benefit for another, exercises authority contrary to a regulation, exceeds it, or fails to fulfil a duty, fulfils § 329. The basic range: one year to five years or a ban on activity. Information about where a patrol is, to people who drive without a licence, is in the account exactly that key: the benefit is avoiding a check, the authority is service knowledge of movement [3] [13] . The point is not that "he wrote to a friend to drive carefully". It is that two people without a driving licence kept driving and the information, according to GIBS, helped them escape checks. The period overlaps with procuring pervitin, but the regime is different. One was off duty. The other carried service knowledge. Driving without a licence is in itself an infraction or a criminal offence of the person behind the wheel. This part does not know the punishments of those two civilians. It knows that the benefit the account assigns to § 329 consisted in avoiding a check. An official did not sell a gram here. He sold a map. A map is, in traffic, as practical as a substance in a pocket, only it photographs worse into a headline [3] [9] [13] . A reliability test, which the act on GIBS knows as a tool, is not expressly in the Rychnov account. The text therefore does not write it into the act. It says only that the inspection led the case in criminal proceedings as far as an indictment. The Regional Public Prosecutor's Office in Hradec Králové filed the indictment on 11 January 2022. Between the charge in May 2021 and the February judgment there is less than a year. That is not proof that justice hurried. It is a date without which the April press briefing would look like the day of guilt [1] [13] [15] . Domašov in the series punishes — so far only at the stage of a prosecution — a motorway bribe and abuse. Rychnov punishes a leak. The same section, another act, another guilt. Adding them into "traffic police are for sale" is a map without a stage and without a judgment [3] . 9. An aggregate of eighteen months punished both acts at once The court did not impose eighteen months "for three grams" and separately nothing for patrols. It imposed an aggregate punishment for both misdemeanours. An aggregate is a punishment for more criminal offences in one proceeding, not a sum of statutory ranges and not a comprehensive sentence for an act uncovered later. Eighteen months therefore cannot be divided into "twelve for drugs and six for patrols", because the account did not carry such a division. One can say only that guilt stood on both definitions and that the term of punishment carries both [13] [5] . Eighteen months are under the ceiling of three years where § 81 allows a suspension. A four-year probationary period is long against eighteen months; the law requires that the probationary period not be shorter than the sentence, the upper limit of a probationary period is five years. The court therefore chose, for the suspension, the upper half of the interval of one to five years, while for the term of imprisonment it chose the lower third of the range. That is not a contradiction. It is two levers. Anyone who measures only the first sees leniency. Anyone who measures the second sees that the hypothesis about rehabilitation is to run longer than the punishment that was suspended [7] [13] . Příbram has a higher term of imprisonment (two years) and a shorter published probationary period (thirty months) and is silent about a ban. Rychnov has a lower imprisonment term, a longer probationary period and a visible ban and money. The ranking "who got more" breaks according to the axis. The law carries both axes in one judgment [21] [13] . From that it does not follow that eighteen months is little for a concurrence. It follows that the sentence "he got nothing for patrols" is an untruth. The aggregate contains the patrols. It only does not separate them onto a second line a reader would like to see. 10. Sixty thousand and five years of a ban are executed now § 81(2): permission of a conditional suspension does not apply to the execution of other punishments imposed beside a prison sentence. A fine of 60 thousand is paid. A five-year ban on activity runs. Forfeiture of cannabis is executed. Anyone who says "he only got a suspended sentence" must add to the sentence three punishments that do not survive the suspension as zero [7] [13] . Five years of a ban from the corps is longer than eighteen months of imprisonment and longer than the remaining part of a four-year probationary period after the first year and a half. For a person whose power stood on a service relationship, that is a punishment on that power. The act on the service relationship adds to that, after a final intentional conviction, mandatory dismissal. The account already before the judgment describes the man as released from performance and after the judgment as former [8] [22] [12] . A ban on activity in the security corps is not the same as a driving ban, which at Pankrác supplemented influence behind the wheel. Here the account did not carry a driving ban for the police officer. It did not carry either whether the civilians finally lost a driving licence and whether a further punishment for driving awaits them. A gap is again not zero. It is the boundary of a source. What the text may say without inventing: a five-year corps ban punishes a key, not a wheel. The wheel the account punished otherwise: information about a patrol fell under § 329, not under a driving ban [7] [3] . § 38 again: a less intrusive sanction has priority. Eighteen months with a suspension plus money plus a ban is a bundle, not zero. Anyone who turns it into "a soft punishment because he did not go to prison" must first bear that the law treats a ban and a fine as a punishment, and a suspension as a suspension of execution, not as a cancellation of guilt. Proof of conduct under § 83 the account did not carry. The case in public space ends with the finality of February 2022, not with proof of conduct in 2026 [5] [7] . 11. Finality in February is not an April press release The District Court in Rychnov nad Kněžnou, Svatohavelská: finality is 21 February 2022, not an April press briefing. Krvesaj, Wikimedia Commons, public domain. The court building. It is not a map of patrols. The court pronounced the judgment on 21 February 2022, when it became final. GIBS repeated that publicly in April, iROZHLAS on 19 April. CNN Prima cited the same press release. The charge was in May 2021, the indictment on 11 January 2022 [13] [1] . Four dates block the sentence that "the case fizzled out into a press briefing". The judgment is a February one. April is an account. Anyone who reads only April has the impression that a punishment fell in spring as news. It fell in winter and became final at once. That usually means that no one appealed, or that an appeal is not in the account. The text does not invent an appeal. It says that finality is the date of the judgment, not the date of an article. Two months between a judgment and a press release are, in police cases, common and costly for a reader. Anyone who in March 2022 looked for "what he got" may have had the impression that the matter was still hanging. It was hanging only in an editorial calendar. The court finished in February. The inspection repeated in April. CNN Prima and iROZHLAS copied the same GIBS. That is not three audits of a punishment. It is one spokesperson in three windows. Honest citation therefore does not go by the number of headlines, but by the February judgment and by one Nguyenová [13] [16] [15] . 12. Up to five years is again not a judgment Before the indictment and after the judgment the account carries "faced up to five years". That is the ceiling of the basic paragraphs of both misdemeanours, not a middle and not a promise. The court gave eighteen months with a suspension. Between the floor of one year and the ceiling of five, eighteen months are closer to the floor of the term — and at the same time a ban runs on the upper half of what § 329 itself can impose as a ban on activity beside a range of imprisonment [2] [3] [5] [13] . Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext The law knows aggravation by a uniform. Mitigation by a first sentence too. The public account did not carry the senate's reasons the way ČT carried them for Jakubec. Without them the sentence "the court should have gone to five because of the patrols" is a politics of punishment. The sentence "the court stayed in the corridor of § 81 and besides that imposed a five-year ban" is a citation of a source [14] [7] . 13. Off duty and on duty do not add into one bowl For the year 2024 GIBS counted 36 police officers whose criminal activity fell into the performance of duty or working hours, and 29 in whom abuse of position was involved. Rychnov 2020/21 does not belong in that table by year. It belongs by a distinction: one branch of the act is expressly off duty, the other carries service knowledge. Adding both into "36" would be an anachronism. Adding both into one pocket is an error of layer [10] [13] . A practical consequence: anyone who wants to punish "a police officer on pervitin" is punishing the first branch. Anyone who wants to punish "a police officer who sold a key" is punishing the second. The court punished with an aggregate. The public hears the first. The part exists so that the second is heard as well. The figure of 36 from the year 2024 says one more thing about the unit. GIBS there counts persons prosecuted in the performance of duty, not grams and not patrols. Rychnov cannot be put back into that figure, because it is from another year and because one of its branches is expressly off duty. Anyone who turns Rychnov into proof that "36 is little when even patrols are sold" is adding a prosecution to one final aggregate. Anyone who turns 36 into proof that Rychnov is ordinary is doing the same from the other side. Both sentences need the same table and the same stage. They do not have them [10] [13] . 14. A civilian with pervitin is not convicted in the account Pervitin went to one civilian. Two civilians received patrols. A colleague in the 2024 database-check case is being prosecuted — another case, another stage. Here the account did not carry the civilians' punishments. The text therefore does not supply them. That is not protection. It is a gap in a source. The case in public space is the case of an official. Grams at a civilian may be § 284, an infraction, or nothing published. Speculation that "the dealer walked away" needs a file the newspapers do not have [13] [18] [19] . That is not an argument that a civilian escaped punishment. It is an argument that this part measures an official, because only for him does the account carry a judgment. A series that turned silence about civilians into "the police cover their customers" would turn a gap in a source into an act. A gap may stay visible. It must not be filled with a guess that would read better in a headline than an aggregate. 15. What the account does not say about the punishment We do not know the prosecutor's proposal. We do not know whether the accused confessed. We do not know the reasons, how many of the eighteen months the senate "assigned" to patrols. We do not know the civilians' punishments. We do not know whether the probationary period carried supervision or proportionate duties under § 82 [7] [13] . We know an aggregate, money, a ban, forfeiture, finality, two misdemeanours, three handovers, two persons at the patrols, a find of cannabis. That is enough for a distinction. It is not enough for the sentence that the court "should have gone to an unsuspended punishment because". That sentence needs reasons the account did not carry. The gap of the prosecutor's proposal is here the same as in Příbram and different from Vogel. In Vogel's case the account carries the proposal, and therefore one can say the prosecutor asked for a suspended sentence under a headline of ten years. In Rychnov that cannot be said. One cannot turn that into the claim that the prosecutor asked for five years of execution and the court reduced it. One cannot turn that into the opposite. A missing mark is not counted as mitigation for the senate or as proof that "they covered their own" [13] [17] . What needs to be tested The stage. Two paragraphs, not one. Aggregate versus a branch. Money and a ban beside a suspension. Headline versus GIBS. The sixth mark — the prosecutor's proposal — is missing again. 16. Three tests before the sentence that he should have sat for patrols Three tests before a sentence about leniency The first test: guilt stood on both misdemeanours. Finality is there. It is not Domašov [13] . The second test: eighteen months are in the corridor of a suspension. A five-year ban and 60 thousand are not in the corridor of a suspension — they are executed. Anyone who measures only bars is measuring the narrowest part of the judgment [7] . The third test: a comparison with Příbram. There production, here procurement plus a key. A higher imprisonment term there, more visible accessory punishments here. A ranking on one axis lies [12] [13] . Before a comparison with a driver without papers A civilian who drives without a licence did not carry § 329 as an official. He did not carry a corps ban. He did not carry GIBS. "For the same thing" again needs the same thing. The fourth test is the regime of the shift. Off duty one can procure a substance and it will still be § 283. On duty one cannot give a map of a patrol and pretend it was the same. The distinction is not moralising. It is why the part exists beside Příbram. There the account did not carry a key. Here it carries one. Adding both cases into "a police officer and pervitin, a suspended sentence" is convenient and imprecise [21] [13] . The fifth test is the civilian. One person at the pervitin, two at the patrols, punishments unpublished. The sentence "he covered a dealer and they still let him go" needs their judgments. Without them it is an impression. An impression may stay in a discussion. It must not enter a sentence this text issues as documented [13] . The dishonest answer assembles three grams, a suspended sentence and a ceiling of five years into an anger that for patrols "there was nothing". The aggregate contains the patrols. It only does not carry them on a separate line. A practical test has six marks. Finality: 21 February 2022. Two definitions, not one. An aggregate of eighteen months with a suspension for four years. A fine of 60 thousand. A five-year ban. Forfeiture of cannabis. Anyone who of the six leaves only the first two and a suspended sentence gets a sentence the account did not bear. Anyone who leaves all six gets a bundle the law treats as a punishment even without bars [13] [7] . 17. The question is not whether he failed. It is which act you assign to the punishment A winter square of a small town: the aggregate punished two acts, the public hears one. The public question from the opening sounds just. A person with authority who procures pervitin and at the same time sells the movement of a patrol to people without a licence has broken two things, not one. The law knows that. The court punished it with one aggregate. The hidden cost is not that a punishment is missing. Eighteen months, four years of a probationary period, 60 thousand, five years of a ban and forfeiture in February 2022 finally are there. The hidden cost is when "only a suspended sentence for three grams" is assembled from them. The grams were off duty. The key was on duty. Money and a ban run now. The ceiling of five years was again not a promise. The right question is therefore not whether he failed. The public source bore that. It is: which act you are assigning to the punishment just now — substance, patrol, aggregate, ban — and which dislike you are willing to bear when it turns out that you assign to the punishment only a pocket. Part 1 said that a suspended sentence is not an acquittal. Part 2 showed that a headline can turn a suspension into bars. Part 3 shows a third mix-up: an aggregate punishes two acts, the public hears one. Anyone who after Rychnov still says "a suspended sentence for three grams" has not read the second misdemeanour. Anyone who says "nothing for patrols" has not read the aggregate. Anyone who says "he walked away" has not read 60 thousand and five years of a ban. The aggregate punished both acts. The public hears only pervitin. — Jiný Kontext Related texts in this series 01 — "Up to five years" is not the sentence imposed 02 — Running out of money to buy is not operational cover 21 — Pervitin is not one thing

items.title: An email in a leak is not the same as a password in a leak. And a password in a leak is not yet someone else’s login.
items.subtitle: Have I Been Pwned can say whether an address or a password hash has appeared in a known file. It cannot say that the account is now safe, nor delete data from the internet.
items.perex: Have I Been Pwned can say whether an address or a password hash has appeared in a known file. It cannot say that the account is now safe, nor delete data from the internet.

Before a complaint to the ÚOOÚ

items.body: Section: Technology & AI Author: V Reading Length: ~27 min Sources and further reading: 22 items Topics: password leak, Have I Been Pwned, Pwned Passwords, k-anonymity, credential stuffing, GDPR, ÚOOÚ SEO / Working Title: How to find out whether your password or email has leaked? How to find out whether your password or email has leaked? The question sounds simple only until we notice that we are not comparing one thing. An email in a leak is not a password in a leak. A password in a corpus is not “your” password. A hit in an index is not someone else’s login. And an empty result is not proof that no leak occurred. The article is therefore not looking for a safety button. It is looking for which layer you are measuring just now, and what still does not follow from it. 1. A Have I Been Pwned notification is not a message that someone has just logged in In the morning an email arrives: your address has appeared in a new Have I Been Pwned record. The reader opens the page, sees the name of a service and categories of data. In the head that joins into one sentence: someone has my password and is just getting into my inbox. A colleague from IT says not to panic and first to separate the address from the password. A lawyer reminds the controller of the 72-hour period under the GDPR. A banker talks about credential stuffing on other sites. The operator of a service says that it has sent users a notice. At first glance this is one leak. In fact each person is describing a different problem. The reader reads the hit as a live session. IT treats the occurrence of a secret in a corpus. The lawyer speaks of the controller’s duty towards the authority and data subjects. The banker means a repeated password on another service. The operator asks whether its incident creates a risk that must be notified. That is why they can all be partly right and a shared decision still wrong. One error leads to panic and an unnecessary reset into a weaker password. The other leads to calm from an empty result and to further use of the same password on ten sites. HIBP is not an alarm about a login happening now. It is an index of known files and incidents, with its own limits and date. 2. One address has at least six layers The word “leaked” is used for a dump from a compromised service, a paste on a website, a stealer log from a victim’s computer, a stuffing list and a controller’s notice. These words are not interchangeable. When we swap them, we react badly: we change a password where the problem was reuse elsewhere, or we write a complaint where there is no identifiable controller under the GDPR regime. Six layers of one address: Raw material: a dump from a compromised service, a stealer log, a stuffing list or a paste. Each type arises differently. Index: Have I Been Pwned, Sentinel, a password manager or an internal check by a service. Each index has a different corpus and a different latency. Hit: an address, a password, or an address-plus-password pair on the attacker’s side. HIBP does not join a citizen’s address and password. Misuse: credential stuffing on other sites, phishing for a reset, sale of a log or a login to an account. Controller’s duty: Articles 33 and 34 GDPR, documentation of the incident, notification to the ÚOOÚ and, where required, notice to data subjects [13] . Account holder’s response: a unique password, a change where it was reused, a more resilient second factor, a check of sessions and the handling of harm. An index is not raw material. A hit is not misuse. A controller’s duty is not a citizen’s duty. And the user’s response should be proportionate to the layer they are seeing just now. A person does not need to know how stuffing is done. They need to know why a repeated password gives an old dump a new life. This layering also changes the language. “I have an email in a leak” is the right start, not the end of a diagnosis. It is necessary to add whether it was a service the person used, what categories of data are listed, whether a password was there, whether the password was unique and whether it was reused somewhere. Only then comes the response. Without that middle sentence, security turns into a ritual: click, take fright, change something, calm down. An email in a leak is not the same as a password in a leak. And a password in a leak is not yet someone else’s login. — Jiný Kontext 3. The best response is the one whose error will not lock you out and will not open stuffing A good security response is not the loudest. It is a response that lowers risk and does not create a new one. An unnecessary reset of one service is a cheap error. A reset into a short, repeated or forgettable password is worse. Entering a full password into a random “checker” is itself a leak. And calm from an empty index can be expensive if the same password is used elsewhere. Type of failure What it looks like How to test What limits the harm False alarm The address is in HIBP, but the password was unique and MFA holds Read the service and the data categories, not only the word breach Change only where there was a reason False calm HIBP shows nothing, but the password is the same on more sites A k-anonymous password check and a password manager Unique passwords and notifications Leak into a checker The full password leaves for an unknown service Use only official Pwned Passwords or a password manager Never send a secret by email Confusion of stuffing and phishing A historical hit is handled, but the person enters a detail to a fraudster Separate an old dump from a live channel Verification off the link and more resilient MFA Wrong addressee A complaint goes to the ÚOOÚ without a relation to the controller Ask who the controller is and what they were supposed to do Art. 34, Art. 77 and documents This table is not meant to replace a healthy fear. It is meant to make it more precise. The safety of an account does not arise from one web answer. It arises from the fact that a secret is not repeated, that the second factor is not only an easily copied code in every situation, that sessions can be checked and that a person knows when it is no longer an index but a suspicion of someone else’s entry. A response should also have an order. First, access to the account is secured, so that the person does not lock themselves out. Then the password is changed where there is a reason. Then it is checked whether the same password lived elsewhere. Finally, notifications and a second factor that makes sense for the given service are turned on. When the order is reversed, a person can lose a recovery channel, overwrite the password with a variant of the old one, or settle a historical index and leave a live session open. 4. An email in the index is not a password in the index Have I Been Pwned separates a search for an email address in a breach from the Pwned Passwords service. For an address a person sees services and categories of data. They do not see their password next to the address. HIBP explains in the FAQ that passwords are not stored in a way that would join them to addresses for public search [4] . That is a security boundary of the service, not a cosmetic detail. As of 1 September 2026 the HIBP homepage listed 17 796 310 183 indexed accounts and 1 033 pwned websites or incidents [1] . These numbers are live counters of a global service. They measure accounts or addresses in the index, not unique people and not the number of victims in the Czech Republic. One person can have more addresses. One address can be in more incidents. One incident can contain only an email and another a broader set of categories. The practical question is therefore not “am I hacked?”. It is: which service is listed, what categories of data are given for it, and whether I used a password there that was also reused elsewhere. If so, the problem does not lie only with the old service. It lies in all the places where the same secret opened the same door. Data categories also matter because an email is often only an identifier for further attacks. By itself it need not open an account. It can, however, help convincing phishing, reset communication or pairing with another leak. It does not follow that every found address means harm. It follows that an address in the index has a different weight from a password in a corpus and a different weight from a confirmed session of someone else. 5. A password in Pwned Passwords is not “your” password Pwned Passwords measures the occurrence of a secret in a corpus of known leaked passwords. When a password is found, that does not mean the service knows it belonged to you. It means that the same secret appeared somewhere in the corpus. If you have ever used it, it is to be treated as public and unfit for further use. As of 1 September 2026 the Pwned Passwords page listed traffic of more than 18 billion requests a month, a cache hit above 99.9% and 335 edge locations [2] . That measures the operation of the service and the integration of password managers, registration forms and manual checks. It does not measure the number of new leaks or the number of people whose password was misused. The difference between “the password was found” and “someone logged in” is fundamental. The first is the state of a secret. The second is an event in a particular account. The state of a secret is handled by a change everywhere the password was reused, and by a new unique password. An event in an account is handled by sessions, login logs, the support of the service and, in case of harm, the bank or the police. One layer must not swallow the other. 6. A stuffing list is not the leak of one firm Credential stuffing is the misuse of already known pairs of login data against other services. OWASP distinguishes it from brute force and from password spraying [17] . The point is not to guess one password over and over. The point is the reuse of old secrets where people used the same password more than once. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext Troy Hunt described the Synthient Credential Stuffing Threat Data corpus added to HIBP in November 2025. He lists 1 957 476 021 unique email addresses, roughly 1.3 billion unique passwords and 625 million passwords that HIBP had not seen before [6] . The HIBP record for this corpus describes it as stuffing data, not as the leak of one firm [7] . The same text lists 32 million domains and 394 million addresses on the gmail.com domain, that is approximately 20% of the addresses in this corpus [6] . That is not a leak of Gmail. It is a sign that a large freemail domain appears in recycled login pairs. Whoever reads this number as a compromise of Google has confused the denominator. It does not follow that this is a guide to an attack. It follows a defensive rule: an old password must not be reused. If it was reused, it is changed everywhere it was used, not only at the service named in the notification. The new password is not to be a variant of the old one. A password manager is not extra comfort. It is a way to stop the recycling of secrets. Stuffing also explains why old leaks do not leave a life only because the old service has vanished. The value of an address-and-password pair does not lie only in the original site. It lies in the possibility that the person used the same secret elsewhere. Defence therefore does not consist in hunting the original culprit at all costs. It consists in the fact that reuse is removed and future logins do not rest on the same secret. 7. A stealer log is not the same as an operator leak A stealer log arises differently from a leak of an operator’s database. Malware on a victim’s device can collect stored login data, cookies or other data from the user’s environment. Compromise of a firm means a failure at the controller of a service. Both results can end in the same market for data. Cause, responsibility and response are, however, different. Verizon, in the DBIR 2025 supplement, states that compromised data were the initial vector in 22% of breaches out of 9 891 incidents with a known vector, outside the Error and Misuse categories [16] . The same material, for 14 742 infostealer devices, states a median of 49% unique passwords across services, which means that in this population of malware victims there was a median of 51% repeated passwords [16] . This is a Verizon dataset, not the Czech population and not all users. Verizon also states that in SSO logs credential stuffing formed a median of 19% of authentication attempts at 2 301 organisations [16] . That is a measurement in organisations and logs, not the number of logins to your account. It still shows a mechanism: a repeated password turns an old leak into ongoing pressure on other services. A stealer log adds one more lesson. Sometimes it is not enough to change the password at the service that appeared in the index. If the problem was on the device, the person must deal with the device. Updates, removal of malicious software, a check of the browser and of sessions belong to a different layer from an email hit. This text does not give a procedure for obtaining logs or using them. It only separates the cause: a failure at the operator is not the same as an infected user device. 8. K-anonymity measures a prefix. Not trust in a random checker Pwned Passwords uses a k-anonymous search model. The client computes a SHA-1 hash of the password and sends only the first 5 hex characters. There are 1 048 576 possible prefixes, because 16^5 [5] . The server returns the matching suffixes and counts of occurrence. The full password does not leave the device as readable text or as a whole hash. HIBP API v3 describes range search and the preservation of the partial-query principle [3] . The server therefore does not see the whole password. It sees only the prefix of the hash. That does not mean you should send a password anywhere the word “checker” appears. It means that a concrete, safer mechanism exists, used by official Pwned Passwords and by some password managers. NIST SP 800-63B recommends checking chosen passwords against lists of known compromised values [8] . That is a recommendation for proper password management. It is not a universal Czech legal duty of all controllers to use HIBP in particular. And it is not an excuse for collecting full passwords into a random web form. K-anonymity here plays a modest role. It does not say that a password is strong. It does not say that an account is safe. It says whether the given secret has appeared in a known corpus. A weak but as yet unleaked password can still be a bad choice. A strong and unique password that once entered a public corpus is to stop being used. A leak check is one brake, not the whole security system. How to test a password without sending the secret Use official Pwned Passwords or a password manager that performs the check by k-anonymity. Do not enter a full password on an unknown page, do not send it by email and do not test other people’s combinations. The purpose is to find out whether your secret is no longer a secret. Not to check whether someone else’s combination can be used to enter somewhere. 9. Sentinel is not the same as Have I Been Pwned CZ.NIC described Sentinel View as a tool that allows passwords to be checked against data from the Turris Sentinel network and uses the principle of a partial hash [18] . Another CZ.NIC text joins the rules for making a password with the Turris Sentinel Report [19] . It is a close defensive idea: not to send the whole secret, but to compare it with a corpus of known occurrences. Sentinel is not, however, HIBP. It has a different data source, a different scope and a different mission. An empty result in Sentinel does not clear HIBP. An empty HIBP does not clear Sentinel. Neither index can promise that a password has never leaked or that no one is just now trying a login. Absence of a hit is only absence of a hit in the given corpus. That is why indexes should not be used as a contest of authorities. One can catch a password from its own environment, another a global public dump, a third a check inside a password manager. A contradiction between them need not mean an error. It often means a different source, a different timing and different rules of inclusion. The defensive conclusion is then simple: a found password is retired, an unfound password is still not reused. For a Czech user the value of Sentinel is that it offers another defensive view without the need to work with attack lists. If the service reports an occurrence, the password is not used. If it reports nothing, uniqueness of the password and a second factor still apply. Security must not rest on one empty page. 10. A notification to the ÚOOÚ is not a data subject’s complaint Article 33 GDPR says that the controller shall notify a personal-data breach to the supervisory authority, if possible within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons [13] . The ÚOOÚ has its own information and form for this [11] . This period is a duty of the controller. Not of the citizen. In its annual report for 2024 the ÚOOÚ lists 336 notifications of personal-data breaches [9] . In the annual report for 2025 it lists 392 notifications, the highest number since the GDPR took effect [10] . These numbers measure notifications by controllers to the Czech supervisory authority. They do not measure the number of leaked passwords of citizens, the number of records in HIBP or the size of particular dumps. A data subject’s complaint is a different thing. In the report for 2025 the ÚOOÚ lists 3 854 submissions, of which 2 514 were complaints and 1 340 initiatives, 68% more than in 2024 [10] . This is a mix of GDPR agendas, not only password leaks. A complaint under Article 77 requires a relation to a particular controller and, at the ÚOOÚ, an authenticated procedure [12] [13] . A hit in HIBP by itself need not say whom and what can be blamed. 11. Notice to data subjects is not the same as the HIBP index Article 34 GDPR regulates notice of a personal-data breach to the data subject if the breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons [13] . The EDPB and the original WP29 issued the WP250 guidelines on this [14] . This notice comes from the controller. It is to say what happened, which data concern the person and what they should do. HIBP is a different institution, in quotation marks and without them. It indexes known publicly leaked files and incidents. It can show an address in an old dump. It need not have a non-public incident that the controller notified to data subjects. And it can have a historical record with which the controller no longer communicates. Being in one does not mean being in the other. Before a complaint to the ÚOOÚ First ask three questions. Who is the controller? Which duty was supposed to have been breached? What document do you have: a notice, a communication, a refusal of a request, or only a public index? Article 78 paragraph 2 GDPR works with informing the complainant of the progress or result of the complaint within three months [13] . It is not a period for erasure from HIBP. 12. A hit in the index is not proof of someone else’s login. An empty result is not a clean account The HIBP FAQ expressly works with the limit of absence of evidence: absence of evidence is not evidence of absence [4] . When an address is not found, we do not know that it never leaked. We know only that it is not in the given index. When it is found, we do not know that someone has just logged in. We know that it appeared in a known file or incident. Redakční ilustrace · Jiný Kontext This double negation is unpleasant, but liberating. It does not give certainty, but it prevents a wrong conclusion. A hit leads to a check, not to panic. An empty result leads to keeping good habits, not to repeating passwords. An index is not a guardian of sessions. It does not see a current login to a bank, an email or a social network. If there is a suspicion of someone else’s login, the procedure changes. Sessions, signed-in devices, mail-forwarding rules, password changes, the second factor and notices from the service are checked. In case of harm or an attempt at financial misuse, the bank, the operator of the service and, according to the circumstances, the police are involved. That is no longer an article about an index of leaks. A password manager’s warning should be read with the same care. When a password manager reports that a password is compromised, it usually does not say that someone opened a particular account. It says that the secret matches a known compromised value or a record in a monitored service. It is a reason to replace the secret and remove reuse. It is not, by itself, proof of harm. An empty result is not a clean account. A hit is not a login in progress. — Jiný Kontext 13. MFA lowers stuffing. It does not stop phishing into which you enter the password yourself A second factor lowers the impact of a repeated password. If an attacker knows an old pair of email and password, a second factor can prevent a login. That is why MFA makes sense even years after old leaks. It is not, however, a bulletproof shield against every channel. Phishing in which a person themselves enters a password and a further code into a fraudulent interface is a different mechanism from the historical occurrence of a password in a corpus. This text does not describe techniques of circumvention or an attack in real time. The distinction is enough: HIBP shows a historical hit in known data. Phishing is a live channel that can bypass a good habit if a person follows the wrong link. From that follows a sober rule. After a hit, the password, reuse and MFA are handled. On a suspicious link, verification off the link, direct entry of the service address and contact through a known channel are handled. One defence does not replace the other. A password in Pwned Passwords is not proof of phishing, but a repeated password cheapens the consequences of phishing. 14. A sensitive breach is not the same as a publicly searchable dump HIBP distinguishes sensitive breaches that are not publicly searchable without verification of ownership of the mailbox. As of 1 September 2026 the FAQ listed a total of 87 sensitive breaches and 2 retired breaches [4] . That measures a classification inside HIBP, not the sensitivity of every real leak in the world. The reason is simple. Some incidents themselves disclose sensitive information merely by the fact that a person was in the service. A public answer “yes, this address is in this incident” could cause new harm. That is why the service has a mode in which ownership of the mailbox must be verified. An index is therefore not only a database. It is also a decision about what may be shown to whom. The same FAQ states plus-aliasing at approximately 0.03% of addresses and explains that the service does not fully respect it [4] . A small number can have a large practical impact. If a person uses an address of the type name+service@domain, a hit or a non-hit can be read wrongly. Again this is not a clean account. It is a technical rule of the index. 15. ENISA’s sixty percent of phishing is not the Czech share of leaked passwords ENISA in Threat Landscape 2025 states that phishing formed approximately 60% of observed cases as an intrusion vector in the period from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025 [15] . At the same time the material states that 77% of incidents in the dataset were DDoS and that, among intrusions, 8.9% concerned credential theft [15] . These numbers have different denominators. That is why they must not be added into a sentence about Czech passwords. ENISA measures the European threat landscape and categories of incidents in its dataset. HIBP measures known breaches and addresses in the index. The ÚOOÚ measures notifications by controllers and complaints. Verizon measures its incidents and organisations. Each number can be true and still unusable for another conclusion. NÚKIB can be a useful context for Czech organisations, but the number of incidents in the report on the state of cybersecurity is not a proxy for the number of citizens with a password in HIBP [21] . Europol, in turn, describes the market in compromised accounts and the crime around them [22] . That helps in understanding the motivation of attackers. It is not a guide and it is not an individual audit of a mailbox. 16. A short exposure test does not promise safety The point of the test is to find exposure, not to obtain other people’s data and not to try whether an account can be broken. That must remain visible even in the small steps. One’s own email is checked on official HIBP. One’s own password is checked through Pwned Passwords or a password manager with k-anonymity. Other people’s combinations are not tried. Stuffing lists are not downloaded. Three tests of a hit The first test is the address. Enter your own email into official HIBP and read the results by services and categories of data. Do not look for the feeling “I am hacked”. Look for whether it was an email, a phone, a password hash, profile data or another category. Set notifications only for your own mailbox. The second test is the password. Check it only by k-anonymity. If it is found in the corpus, treat it as public. Change it everywhere it was reused, and do not use a variant of the old password. This sentence is not an attack. It is the closing of a stuffing path. The third test is the account. If the service shows someone else’s sessions, unknown devices, changes of settings or financial harm, HIBP is no longer the main tool. It is about the running of the account. A change of password, signing out of sessions, a check of the second factor, contact with the service and, in case of harm, the bank or the police take precedence over a further search in the index. Optionally, Sentinel View can be added as another corpus [18] . If a notice from the controller under Article 34 GDPR arrives, follow it. If the controller does not communicate or breaches rights, a complaint under Article 77 is handled, not a request that the ÚOOÚ erase a public index [12] [13] . Write the result of the test in three columns: address, password, account. For the address belong the service and the categories of data. For the password belongs the decision where it was reused and where it is changed. For the account belong sessions, the second factor and unknown changes. This table is not spectacular. It is, however, better than the vague sentence “it leaked on me”, because each row shows a different step. 17. The question is not whether it leaked. It is which layer you are measuring The safety of an account is not a property of an index. An index can be useful and still limited. It will show a known occurrence of an address or a password. It will not unlock an account, it will not delete data from the internet, it will not confirm a live login and it cannot prove that nothing leaked. That is not a weakness of one service. It is the boundary of the measured layer. The hidden cost of the word “leak” is the loss of distinction. When an email in a breach, a password in a corpus, a stuffing list, a stealer log, a controller’s notice and someone else’s session fall into one sentence, the response becomes random. Once it overshoots. Once it misses. And sometimes it opens exactly the path it was meant to close. Distinction helps even when nothing was found. An empty result does not release anyone from password management. It only says that the given index has no matching record. A unique password, a password manager, a meaningful second factor and a check of sessions remain the rule even without a red warning. Security is not to wait for a hit. In the same way a hit is not to determine a single emotion. It is to determine the next step. An address leads to a reading of data categories. A password leads to a change of the secret. A controller’s notice leads to its instructions. A session leads to protection of the account. Whoever separates these steps need not guess whether to be calm or in panic. The right question is therefore not only: “Did my password leak?” The right question is: “Which layer have I just measured: a known dump, a password hash, a stuffing list, a controller’s notification, or someone else’s session, and what still does not follow from it?” Only then does it make sense to change a password, read a notice, check sessions or file a complaint. Not because panic is a weakness. Because an imprecise response is a further risk. A good answer is therefore neither “everything is all right” nor “everything is lost”. A good answer is smaller and more precise. An email in the index is read as a trace in a known file. A password in Pwned Passwords is read as a secret that is no longer fit to use. A stuffing list is read as a warning against reuse. A controller’s notice is read as a legal and practical instruction for a particular incident. And someone else’s session is handled as the running of an account, not as a further search on the web. It does not follow that indexes have no value. It follows that they have value only when the right layer and the right step are bound to them. Have I Been Pwned, Sentinel View or a notice from the ÚOOÚ then cease to be one red button. They become a map. A map is not a lock. But without a map the lock is changed blindly. Related texts in this series How to recognise a fraudulent email, SMS or phone call? — attack channel vs. leak index. What is a digital footprint… — HIBP is one layer, not the whole internet.

items.title: War Looks Clean on a Map. In Reality, It Has No Straight Lines.
items.subtitle: What does it mean to control territory on a military map—and why are a line, colour, arrow or percentage not the front itself, but a reduced model of a complex reality?
items.perex: What does it mean to control territory on a military map—and why are a line, colour, arrow or percentage not the front itself, but a reduced model of a complex reality?
headings: 01 What does it actually mean to “control territory”?
One territory, eight different answers
02 A model is not a lie. A model is a reduction.
03 A line that has to run somewhere
04 Zoom in, and the front dissolves into a system

Many kilometres, little change to the network

The same space, three different questions

09 What a map can do—and what it can never tell us
10 A straight line above an uneven reality
